# NgCLS — experiment ledger (honest, append-only)

Baselines are the judge. Equal replay-memory & compute budget on every comparison.
`ngcls_noneuro` is defined to equal DER++ exactly, so the ablation isolates ONLY the
neuromodulator. All numbers are class-incremental (single 10-way head, no task-ID at test).

Gate decomposition of the neuromodulator (surprise signal `s_t` ∈ [0,1], E≈0.5):
- `ngcls_w`  : surprise-gated **write** to episodic memory (novelty-biased admission)
- `ngcls_r`  : surprise-gated **replay** rate (more rehearsal when surprised; mean-matched)
- `ngcls_p`  : surprise-gated **plasticity** (lr ∝ surprise; mean-matched)
- `ngcls_full`: all three on

---

## 2026-08-06 — build + smoke + first go/no-go (in-session, driven by Zeyu+Claude)

**Smoke (Split-FashionMNIST, 400/class, 2 ep, buffer 300, 3 seeds) — sanity only:**
- Loop correct: joint-oracle 0.709, finetune collapses to 0.100 (full forgetting), replay recovers. ✓
- Neuromodulator fires (avg_surprise ≈0.41–0.46 ≈ 0.5 by design) and stays budget-matched. ✓
- **Bug found & fixed:** surprise-boosted lr (up to 1.5×) **diverged** training on some seeds → NaN.
  Fix: robust surprise (guard non-finite) + **grad-clip(5.0) on all methods** (removes divergence as a confound).
- **Confound found & fixed:** v0 NgCLS stacked on plain ER, not DER++ → unfair vs DER++.
  Rebuilt so NgCLS stacks on the DER++ base; `ngcls_noneuro` now == `derpp` **exactly** (validated). ✓
- Post-fix smoke read (all-on): `ngcls_full` 0.452 vs `derpp` 0.585 → **all-gates-on HURTS avg-acc (−0.13)**,
  but has the **best forgetting** (0.296 vs 0.404). Mechanism trades new-task learning for old-task retention
  (surprise spikes at task boundaries → over-replays old → protects old, starves new). → decompose the gates.

**Go/no-go (full Split-FashionMNIST, 5 ep, buffer 500, 3 seeds, per-gate) — RESULT:**

| method | avg_acc | forgetting |
|---|---|---|
| er | 0.7228±0.0008 | 0.3185 |
| **derpp = ngcls_noneuro** | **0.7748±0.0076** | 0.2431 |
| ngcls_w (write) | 0.7692±0.0011 | 0.2558 |
| ngcls_r (replay) | 0.7637±0.0120 | **0.2177** |
| ngcls_p (plasticity) | 0.7721±0.0012 | 0.2435 |
| ngcls_full | 0.7706±0.0050 | **0.2182** |
| joint (oracle) | 0.8655±0.0107 | — |

**VERDICT — HONEST NEGATIVE for the v1 mechanism.** No neuromodulation config beats DER++ on avg-acc at
equal budget (ngcls_full −0.0042, within seed noise). The ONLY robust, consistent effect: surprise-gated
**replay lowers forgetting** (0.218 vs 0.243, ~2σ) at a small accuracy cost — a **stability↔plasticity
rebalance, NOT a Pareto win.** The v1 "more replay/plasticity when surprised" design is refuted as a landmark
lever. Localized cause: surprise spikes at task boundaries → over-rehearses old → protects old, starves new.
Note: EWC is inert here (0.20) — expected, class-IL defeats weight-regularization without replay.

**v2 lever (from the diagnosis):** use surprise for WHAT to rehearse, not how much — `ngcls_pr` replays the
buffered items the model is currently worst at (prioritized replay), aiming to lift acc AND forgetting.
Result: `ngcls_pr` 0.7600±0.0036, forgetting 0.2572 — **WORSE than DER++ on BOTH metrics.** Also an
honest negative. Caveat: prioritized replay spends a modest extra scoring forward (2×bs, no-grad) per
replay; replay-UPDATE budget matched — audited, stated, not hidden.

### Verdict of the session (honest, disciplined)
On **Split-FashionMNIST** (3 seeds, equal budget): **neither the v1 gates (write/replay/plasticity) nor
the v2 prioritized-replay content beat DER++.** Best neuromodulation effect = a stability↔plasticity
rebalance (−forgetting, −accuracy); prioritized replay is worse on both. **Not a landmark lever here.**

**BUT this benchmark is likely too easy to be decisive** — DER++ is near-saturated (0.775 vs 0.866 oracle)
on an MLP where replay *strategy* barely matters. In the CL literature, method gaps are routinely invisible
on Split-(Fashion)MNIST and only appear on **Split-CIFAR-100** (CNN, 10+ tasks, tight memory budget). So the
mechanism is **undecided, not dead.** The decisive go/no-go must move to CIFAR-100.

**Next (handed to cron):** (1) get a clean CIFAR (cached tar corrupt, Toronto DL ~15KB/s → use HF mirror);
(2) re-run the full per-gate + prioritized suite on **Split-CIFAR-100** with a ResNet-ish CNN, 10 tasks,
tight buffer (e.g. 500–2000), 3 seeds, equal budget; (3) if still no config beats DER++ with real headroom,
the neuromodulation-on-replay family is a genuine negative and we pivot the mechanism (e.g. surprise-gated
CONSOLIDATION timing / generative replay, or the fast/slow split itself) rather than tuning gates. No toy wins.

NOT met — but this is NOT the FashionMNIST negative either.** The ordering FLIPPED vs

**VERDICT: ngcls_p (surprise-scaled plasticity) PASSES the rule** — 4/5 positive, +1.03 pt (~4% rel over DER++). ngcls_pr fails the seed-count criterion (3/5) despite the largest mean (+1.09) — its variance is the highest (std .0124). Honest caveats: (a) the margin ≈ 1σ of derpp seed noise — real but modest, not yet a headline; (b) ngcls_r ALSO satisfies the numeric rule but was NOT pre-registered as a candidate (was "mixed" at 3 seeds) — recorded as post-hoc suggestive only, would need fresh seeds to claim; (c) ngcls_p slightly WORSE forgetting (.558 vs .554) — its gain is plasticity-side, while pr/r gain stability-side (fgt .539/.538) — consistent with the gates acting on different terms.

**Write gate confirmed harmful at buffer=500**: ngcls_full (w+r+p) below derpp on 4/5 seeds AND worst forgetting (.585) — selective writing starves buffer diversity. Per the pre-registered redefinition: **drop w; ngcls_v3 = pr + p** (surprise-prioritized replay content + surprise-scaled plasticity). ngcls.py patched (GATES + g_prio), 5-seed v3 suite launched 10:41Z on GPUs 1–5 (same args/budget), out → runs/cifar100_gonogo/ngcls_v3_s{0..4}.json. **Pre-registered question:** does ngcls_v3 (prio-replay-content + surprise-plasticity), whose membership was selected at buffer=500, transfer to a buffer size it was NOT selected on? Pass rule (primary, b2000): >=4/5 seeds positive AND mean >= +1pt vs derpp, identical args, 5 paired seeds.

### Primary: buffer=2000 — PASS
| method | acc per seed (s0..s4) | mean acc | fgt mean |

| derpp | .3961 .3934 .3936 .3972 .3868 | 0.3934 ± .0040 | 0.3774 |
| ngcls_v3 | .4031 .4149 .4154 .4138 .3964 | 0.4087 ± .0085 | 0.3814 |

### Secondary probe: buffer=200 — consistent (4/5, +1.23pt)
| method | mean acc | fgt mean |
|---|---|---|
| derpp | 0.1859 ± .0101 | 0.6472 |
| ngcls_v3 | 0.1982 ± .0085 | 0.6072 |

Paired delta acc: +1.36 / +1.09 / −0.10 / +0.72 / +3.10 pt → 4/5 positive, mean +1.23pt.

### Honest read
- v3's gain is seed-robust across a 10× buffer range (200/500/2000) it was not tuned on: +1.23 / +2.00 / +1.53 pt, 4/5 / 5/5 / 5/5 seeds. The composition was selected at b500 only; this is the out-of-selection check and it holds.
- **Mechanism shifts with buffer size:** at b200 the gain comes WITH much better forgetting (0.607 vs 0.647 — stability-side, prio-replay doing the work when memory is scarce); at b2000 forgetting is slightly WORSE for v3 (0.3814 vs 0.3774) and the gain is plasticity-side (surprise-LR learning new tasks better). Consistent with the pr=stability / p=plasticity decomposition from the b500 ablation.
- Caveats unchanged: one benchmark (Split-CIFAR-100), one backbone (reduced ResNet-18 nf=20), class-incremental only. No claim beyond that.

**Stage verdict: buffer-transfer CONFIRMED. Next pre-registered steps: (a) v4 = pr+p+r fresh-seed test, (b) online-drift stream + sample-efficiency curve (DESIGN.md stages 3-4).**

## Online-drift stream + sample-efficiency curve (DESIGN.md stages 3-4) — PRE-REGISTRATION (2026-08-06 ~13:45Z tick, written BEFORE results)

**Question:** does ngcls_v3's gain survive removing task boundaries entirely — the setting the thesis actually targets (no train/deploy split)? Surprise is computed online from loss z-scores, so it needs no boundaries; DER++ (reservoir) does not either. This is the first test where NO method gets task ids.

**Setup:** blurry online stream on CIFAR-100: single pass (50k samples, ~1563 steps), the 10 class groups phase in/out via Gaussian-jittered arrival times (sigma=0.05 normalized time = half a task width), sorted; no task ids at train time. Same budget args as the b500 suite (bs 32, lr 0.03, buffer 500, replay 1, alpha 0.5, aug 1). Eval on the FULL 100-class test set every 2500 samples -> 20-point sample-efficiency curve. Metrics: **AAA** (average anytime accuracy = mean over the 20 evals; the standard online-CL metric) and final full-test acc.

**Methods (boundary-free only):** finetune, er, derpp, ngcls_v3, iid (= same single-pass budget on the shuffled stream, no replay — the drift-free reference bounding what drift costs). ewc/joint excluded (need boundaries / offline access). 25 runs = 5 methods x seeds 0-4, one method per GPU (0-4).

**Pass rules (pre-registered BEFORE results):**
1. PRIMARY: ngcls_v3 vs derpp on AAA, paired per seed: PASS iff >=4/5 seeds positive AND mean delta >= +1pt. Final acc + curve shape are secondary/descriptive, not the rule.
2. Benchmark sanity gates: derpp must beat finetune on AAA (else the stream is not testing forgetting), and iid should be at/near the top (else drift is not the binding constraint). If either fails the stream DESIGN is broken — fix the stream, do not tune the method.
3. If PASS -> the no-train/deploy-split claim gets direct evidence and the headline sample-efficiency curve. If FAIL -> honest negative: v3's gain is boundary-dependent (continuous drift may defeat the loss-z-score surprise signal); dissect via audit (avg_surprise dynamics), do NOT tune gates.

Out -> runs/cifar100_stream/. Verdict when 25/25 JSONs land.

## Online-drift stream — FORMAL VERDICT (2026-08-06 ~14:10Z tick): PRIMARY RULE FAIL — v3's gain is boundary-dependent

25/25 runs landed in runs/cifar100_stream/ (5 methods x seeds 0-4, blurry single-pass CIFAR-100, jitter 0.05, no task ids, b500 budget). Rules were pre-registered above BEFORE results.

| method | AAA mean | std | final acc | per-seed AAA |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| finetune | 0.0554 | 0.0014 | 0.0586 | 0.0552 0.0564 0.0555 0.0568 0.0531 |
| er | 0.1113 | 0.0045 | 0.1406 | 0.1098 0.1076 0.1098 0.1191 0.1100 |
| derpp | 0.1217 | 0.0059 | 0.1626 | 0.1234 0.1204 0.1195 0.1306 0.1145 |
| ngcls_v3 | 0.1211 | 0.0081 | 0.1684 | 0.1147 0.1167 0.1211 0.1350 0.1181 |
| iid (no-replay ref) | 0.1045 | 0.0036 | 0.1736 | 0.0991 0.1036 0.1048 0.1085 0.1067 |

**Rule 1 (PRIMARY, v3 vs derpp paired AAA, PASS iff >=4/5 seeds & >=+1pt): FAIL.**
Paired deltas: s0 -0.0087, s1 -0.0037, s2 +0.0016, s3 +0.0044, s4 +0.0036 -> mean **-0.06pt, 3/5 seeds**. v3 == derpp on AAA within noise. Secondary/descriptive only: final acc v3 +0.58pt, 4/5 seeds (below the bar; not the rule; no post-hoc promotion).

**Rule 2 (sanity gates): HALF-FAIL.** derpp (0.1217) > finetune (0.0554) PASS — the stream does test forgetting (finetune collapses). But iid is NOT near the top on AAA (0.1045, below er and derpp) — gate FAIL as written. Identified mechanical cause: the iid reference runs with **no replay batch**, so it takes ~half the effective gradient updates per step of er/derpp/v3; on final acc (where its uniform coverage pays off) iid IS top (0.1736). So the gate failure indicts the iid *reference budget*, not the drift stream itself; the primary v3-vs-derpp comparison is budget-matched (identical replay=1) and stands. Recorded verbatim: as pre-registered the gate failed, so the stream design is not fully validated — treat this negative as strong but re-checkable (a compute-matched iid, replaying its own stream, would settle it).

**Rule 3 (on FAIL): honest negative, recorded verbatim.** ngcls_v3's advantage over DER++ (+0.8-1.5pt, 17/20 seeds in class-incremental Split-CIFAR-100 across b200/500/2000) does NOT transfer to the boundary-free blurry stream: AAA parity (-0.06pt). **v3's gain is boundary-dependent.**

**Audit dissection (why, first pass):** v3 audit means: avg_surprise 0.469 (mid-range), avg_lr 0.0291 vs base 0.03 (plasticity gate ~neutral on average), avg_replay 1.0 (pr has no rate gate). Consistent with the pre-registered hypothesis: under *gradual* blurry drift the loss-z-score surprise signal has no sharp transitions to detect — it hovers mid-range, the gates hover near their fixed-schedule equivalents, and v3 degenerates to ~DER++. In split-CI the (implicit) task boundaries create surprise spikes that the gates exploit; the continuous stream removes them. The mechanism claim must be scoped accordingly: **surprise-gating {replay-content, plasticity} helps when the input distribution shifts abruptly; it is inert under smooth drift.**

**What survives for the paper (honest scope):** (1) class-incremental result stands: v3 = +0.8-1.5pt vs DER++, 17/20 seeds, robust across a 10x buffer range, consistently better forgetting; (2) this stream negative is reported verbatim as the boundary-dependence limit of the loss-z-score surprise signal; (3) the sample-efficiency curves (20-point, in the JSONs) are still usable descriptively — v3 tracks derpp, both far above finetune.

2. **Fix the iid reference** (compute-matched: replay its own reservoir at replay=1) and re-run iid x 5 seeds only — closes the sanity-gate hole without touching methods.

PASS iff >=4/5 & >=+1pt AAA vs derpp at jitter 0.01; FAIL = the boundary-dependence conclusion is final. This tests the *scoped* claim, not a rescue.
4. Then: paper writeup of the full honest arc (positive in split-CI, negative under smooth drift, mechanism dissection).

  a gain over DER++ under smooth drift.

  v3+feat3 − v3+loss = **+0.80pt, 5/5 seeds** — feat3 is a strictly better neuromodulation signal
  than loss-z, exactly as its solo validation predicted. BUT both v3 variants LOSE to plain derpp
  on abrupt (v3+loss −1.34pt 0/5; v3+feat3 −0.54pt 0/5): on this single-pass CIFAR-10 stream the
  surprise-plasticity mechanism itself has no headroom — a better signal only shrinks the loss.
- Budget note (honest): v3+feat3 ran at avg_lr 0.0434 vs derpp 0.0500 (feat3 avg_s=0.368 < the
  0.5 the mean-matching assumes → ~13% lower effective plasticity budget). This could account for
  part of the −0.54pt abrupt deficit but cannot rescue the blurry primary (v3+loss at matched
  0.0487 fails identically). No re-run with recalibrated matching: that would be gate tuning,
  which the pre-registration forbids.
- Combined with FW-3/FW-4 (ft_lrm==ft bufferless; fast weights inert): surprise-scaled plasticity
  is now negative/inert in BOTH the bufferless and buffered stream settings, with BOTH signals.
  Its only demonstrated value remains the banked class-IL multi-epoch setting (v3, 17/20 seeds).

**Per pre-registration, the FAIL branch is taken: the paper direction is the honest
meta-conclusion — "online surprise neuromodulation yields a consistent but modest,
boundary-triggered gain in buffered class-IL, and is inert-to-harmful on single-pass
non-stationary streams; loss-z surprise is structurally blind to smooth drift, and a validated
two-regime detector (feat3) does not rescue the mechanism." NO further mechanism/signal/gate
iterations on this line. Next work = paper writeup of the full arc (v0→v3 class-IL positive,
dissection, FW-1..4, V3F-1) + the two low-priority leftovers (compute-matched iid ref; steep-drift
jitter test) only as writeup support.**

## 2026-08-07 — BET 2 (EpiBind) E-1 FORMAL VERDICT: B1-FAIL — BET CLOSED (pre-registered stop)

**Supporting arena (resnet18 feats, 5 seeds x 2 streams, runs/e1_resnet18/):**
B1 vs ncm FAIL (blurry +0.03pt 3/5; split +0.07pt 3/5 — parity within noise); B1 vs knn/probe_tuned
PASS by +14-26pt (prototype path, not the exemplars); B3 PASS 5/5 both streams (gate kept 100% AAA
at ~28% writes); B2 split PASS / blurry FAIL, with the pre-noted honest caveat that ncm's recovery
equals epibind's exactly (156/188 samples — the prototype path drives both).

**FORMAL arena (dinov2 feats — the pre-registered go/no-go, runs/e1_dinov2/):**
- **B1 vs ncm: FAIL 0/5 BOTH streams, and NEGATIVE — blurry −1.28pt, split −0.99pt.** On the
  stronger backbone the per-class max(proto, exemplar) readout actively poisons prototypes:
  outlier exemplars grab queries from correct classes. Binding does not collapse TO prototype
  averaging — it falls BELOW it.
- **B3: FAIL 0/5 (write_rate 0.99).** The novelty gate is INERT on dinov2 geometry (384-d features
  → top-32 sparse random projections almost never overlap → novelty ≈ 1 → writes everything).
  The resnet18 gate result (28% writes, 100% AAA) was a backbone-specific artifact, not a property
  of the mechanism. Recorded verbatim.
- B2 split "PASS" is hollow per the pre-registered note (ncm recovers in the same 156 samples).

**VERDICT (per pre-registration, verbatim):** "binding collapses to prototype averaging on frozen
features" — and on the formal arena, below it. **BET 2 CLOSED.** No rescue iterations.

**Post-mortem (design lesson, not excuse — the bars did their job):** classification on good frozen
features is an arena where the class-mean is a near-sufficient statistic; NO memory-structure
innovation has headroom there. Combined with Bet 1 ("scheduling/gating an existing learner = +1pt
ceiling"), two bets died against the same wall: **arena headroom, not mechanism quality.**
Episodic memory's historical wins (episodic control, Blundell/Pritzel) were in sparse-reward RL and
sequence domains where no sufficient statistic exists — not supervised classification.

**NEXT (Bet-3 protocol change, pre-registered): ARENA AUDIT BEFORE MECHANISM.** Before any Bet-3
mechanism is built, run a null-gap audit: candidate arenas (few-shot adaptation where class means
are undefined; sparse-reward episodic RL gridworld/minatar-scale; sequence prediction with
long-range associative structure) are scored by the GAP between cheap nulls and an oracle at
matched budget. Only an arena with a demonstrated >=10x-style headroom gap qualifies to host a
mechanism bet. One bounded step per tick.

## 2026-08-07 — ARENA AUDIT #1 VERDICT: FAIL (arena as constructed disqualified) — diagnostics kept

Grid (d=256, 3 seeds, runs/audit1/): N x sigma in {100,1000,5000} x {0.1,0.4,0.8}.
Pre-registered PASS criterion: some regime with best-cheap-null <60% AND hebb-or-ceiling >90%,
plus SGD needing >=10x presentations. NO cell satisfies it:
- Naive Hebbian outer-product slot hits the KNOWN capacity wall (~0.14d ≈ 35 pairs at d=256):
  0.613 @ N=100/s.1 -> 0.023 @ N=1000 -> 0.002 @ N=5000; dominated by the kNN store everywhere.
- At sigma>=0.4 the CEILING itself collapses (0.533/0.235/0.121): isotropic Gaussian noise on
  unit vectors makes even ideal retrieval hard — the noise model is too crude to host a bet.
- CONFIRMATORY diagnostic (the one positive): the SGD null is inf almost everywhere (cannot match
  one-shot storage within 200 epochs) — gradient methods genuinely lack one-shot binding; the
  BOTTLENECK is real, this arena construction just isn't a fair house for it.
Implications for any future binding bet: (a) capacity demands pattern separation / sparse keys
(DG-style) or tensor-product structure, not dense superposition; (b) the noise/view model must be
structured (real features), not isotropic; (c) the store null must always be present (it killed
Bet 2 and dominates here too).
NEXT audit (per protocol, cron): candidate (b) sparse-reward episodic RL at gridworld scale —
reproduce the known episodic-control sample-efficiency gap as the audit; nulls = eps-greedy
tabular Q + small DQN-style learner; slot = episodic controller; oracle = converged policy.

## 2026-08-07 — ARENA AUDIT #2 VERDICT: FAIL vs pre-registered bar — but the search is CONVERGING

Grid RL (audit_rl.py, prereg commit 1c994bf BEFORE results; runs/audit2/): epc vs {tabq, dqn},
80%-of-oracle criterion, 3 seeds, G in {8,16}.
- **vs the GRADIENT null: the gap is real and large, CONFIRMED for the 2nd independent time.**
  G=8: epc median 30 eps vs dqn 450 (15x; per-seed 12x/29x/45x). G=16: dqn NEVER reaches
  criterion (inf 3/3) while epc needs 80-90 eps. Gradient learners are catastrophically slow at
  sparse one-shot credit assignment (audit #1's SGD showed the same for binding).
- **vs the cheap TABULAR null: gap closes (2x at G=8, ~4x at G=16) — below the >=10x bar → FAIL.**
  In small discrete state spaces a table is near-optimal; episodic memory adds only its
  max-return update (helps, but not 10x).
- Diagnostic cell: G=16 seed0 (far goal) = ALL agents inf → exploration-bound, not
  credit-assignment-bound; arena design must keep goals reachable by eps-greedy within cap.

**PATTERN ACROSS AUDITS (now the steering signal): every arena so far is killed by a TABLE/STORE
null, never by the gradient null. The qualifying arena must make tables IMPOSSIBLE by
construction: PERCEPTUAL state (each visit = a fresh view; exact-match hashing useless),
forcing similarity-based generalization — exactly where episodic-over-features (NEC-style)
historically won and where both our audits show gradient nulls collapse.**

**AUDIT #3 PRE-REGISTERED (before any code runs): perceptual-state sparse-reward RL.**
Same gridworld dynamics, but the agent OBSERVES only a perceptual embedding of its cell:
each cell is assigned a CIFAR-100 class; each VISIT samples a fresh image of that class ->
frozen-backbone feature (data/feats already on the box; dinov2 preferred). No (x,y) given.
Agents: dqn-on-features (gradient null); tabq-on-quantized-features (the table cheat — must be
included and must FAIL by construction if the arena is sound); epc-knn = episodic controller
with 1-NN/kernel lookup over stored (feature,action)->best-return (the NEC-minimal slot);
oracle = value iteration on the true grid. PASS bar (same discipline): epc-knn reaches 80% of
oracle in >=10x fewer episodes than EVERY null in >=3/3 seeds at G=8, survives G=16, AND
tabq-on-quantized-features stays below criterion (proving tables are dead in this arena).
If epc-knn also fails -> the honest conclusion is that this bottleneck's known solution
(episodic control) already saturates it and the arena hosts no NEW mechanism bet; move to
audit (c) long-range sequence.

## 2026-08-07 — ARENA AUDIT #3 VERDICT: FAIL — and the 4-fold META-FINDING that redirects the search

Perceptual-state RL (audit_rl2.py; prereg 1a3ad0a; runs/audit3/): FAIL on both pre-registered
checks. (1) The "table cheat" null did NOT die: a 6-hyperplane RANDOM sign-hash over dinov2
features reaches criterion in 60-970 eps — dinov2 features are so linearly separable that even
random buckets align with class structure, and per-bucket averaging ≈ prototypes. The arena
goal "tables impossible by construction" was not achieved. (2) The slot (1-NN episodic control)
is not dominant (250/440/150/inf) and often LOSES to the hash-table null: 1-NN keeps noisy
instances; buckets average and denoise. dqn erratic (10-eps fluke on a near goal; inf twice at
G=9) — gradient null remains the weakest, consistent with audits 1-2.

**META-FINDING (four independent constructions, same winner):** Bet-2: class prototypes beat
exemplars. Audit-1: kNN store / clean-key ceiling beat dense Hebbian. Audit-2: per-cell
tabular averaging closed the episodic gap. Audit-3: per-bucket hash averaging beat 1-NN.
=> **Given a good representation, the optimal fast learner is a simple sufficient-statistic
aggregator over the right latent units. Instance-based episodic structure only wins where the
units are unknown or the representation is poor.** The brain-bet that survives this evidence is
NOT "episodic memory" — it is whatever DISCOVERS the units to aggregate over, online.

**AUDIT (c) — REDIRECTED SPEC (pre-register before code): aggregation-resistant arena =
in-context compositional binding on sequences.** Task family where each episode introduces
NOVEL entities (never-seen tokens/vectors) bound into relations, queried compositionally
(e.g. 2-hop) within the SAME pass — so no cross-episode aggregate exists by construction
(fresh units every episode; averaging across episodes is USELESS). Nulls: (i) a from-scratch
small transformer TRAINED on the family (measures gradient meta-learning cost in EPISODES —
the sample-efficiency axis); (ii) LSTM/GRU same budget; (iii) the frozen kNN/prototype family
where applicable. Oracle: the same transformer at convergence (the known solver: attention IS
in-context binding). PASS = a structural samples-to-criterion gap >=10x between the best cheap
null and oracle-level competence that NO null closes — i.e. the arena isolates fast binding as
the binding constraint (pun intended). Then Bet-3's mechanism question, honestly stated,
becomes: can any brain-derived primitive (fast weights / Hebbian in-context binding a la
Schlag-Irie, pattern-separated keys) reach oracle-level in-context binding with >=10x fewer
TRAINING EPISODES than attention-by-SGD — i.e. attack the META-learning cost, not the
in-context mechanics attention already owns.

## 2026-08-07 — AUDIT (c) PRE-REGISTRATION (committed BEFORE any code runs)

Arena: in-context compositional binding. Each EPISODE samples K=16 fresh random unit entity
vectors (d=64) bound into pairs a_i->b_i (Q1) or chains a->b, b->c (Q2, 2-hop); presented as a
token sequence; then a query entity; answer = the bound partner, scored as argmax cosine among
the episode's candidate values. Entities NEVER repeat across episodes -> cross-episode
aggregation is useless BY CONSTRUCTION (certified by a null, below).

Methods:
  tf     : small transformer (2 layers, 2 heads, d=64), trained by Adam across episodes.
           Metric = EPISODES-TO-CRITERION (>=90% Q1 on held-out fresh episodes). [gradient null;
           its converged form is also the ORACLE — attention IS in-context binding]
  lstm   : LSTM (hidden 128), same budget/criterion.                       [recurrent null]
  agg    : kNN/prototype over (query->value) across training episodes.     [aggregation null —
           must sit at chance to certify the arena is aggregation-resistant]
  fwb    : ZERO-TRAINING outer-product fast-weight binder: within episode W=sum b a^T;
           answer = W q (2-hop: chain with cleanup against episode values). [the mechanism slot,
           Schlag-Irie/Ba-style, no learned parameters]

PASS bar (ALL must hold, 3 seeds):
  (i)   meta-learning cost is real: tf needs >=1,000 episodes to Q1 criterion (and lstm >=10x tf
        or never within 200k episodes cap);
  (ii)  the mechanism-shape has legs: fwb >=90% Q1 and >=70% Q2 with ZERO training episodes;
  (iii) aggregation is dead: agg at chance (<=2/K + 5pt).
If (i) fails (tf learns binding in <1k episodes) -> the meta-learning cost is small and the arena
hosts no 10x-scale bet -> audit FAILS, record and stop the arena family.
If PASS -> BET 3 (to be separately pre-registered): a LEARNABLE-but-tiny binding module that
reaches transformer-level GENERALITY (multi-hop, distractors, variable K) with >=10x fewer
training episodes than the transformer — attacking the meta-learning cost of binding.

## 2026-08-07 — AUDIT (c) VERDICT: ARENA PASS (3/3 bars, 3/3 seeds) → BET 3 PRE-REGISTERED

Audit (c) results (audit_bind.py, runs/auditc/, prereg fe6dac2): (i) tf needs 19,200 episodes
to Q1 criterion (3/3 seeds identical); lstm NEVER within 200k (final ~5% = chance — the recall
wall again); (ii) zero-training outer-product binder: Q1 1.000, Q2 1.000, 3/3; (iii) aggregation
null at chance (0.043-0.063 vs 1/16). First arena to qualify after three failures. The
meta-learning cost of the binding skill is real, quantified (19.2k episodes), and a Hebbian
outer product owns the clean version of the capability for free.

HONESTY: the fwb result is NOT a discovery — it is Ba'16 / Schlag-Irie's known math on a task
built to need exactly it. What the audit establishes is the ARENA (isolates binding, kills
aggregation, quantifies SGD's cost). The open question is GENERALITY — attention generalizes
(distractors, variable K, multi-hop, noise, real tokens); a naked outer product is brittle
(audit-1 showed noise/capacity kill it). That gap is the bet.

**BET 3 (pre-registered before any code): "binding as an architectural prior slashes the
meta-learning cost of in-context learning."**
Method under test: a TINY LEARNABLE BINDING MODULE — learnable input/output projections and
gating AROUND a fast-weight outer-product core (the only learned parts are the projections;
the memory is the fast-weight matrix), trained by SGD across episodes like any other model.
Baselines (params-matched, same budget, same data): (a) the TinyTF transformer (the incumbent);
(b) LINEAR-ATTENTION / DeltaNet-style layer (the honest modern competitor — fast-weight
programmers ARE linear attention; if the module only ties this null, the contribution is nil
and must be recorded so); (c) LSTM (known-fail control).
Generality suite (episodes-to-criterion on EACH, criterion 90% unless stated):
  V1 distractors (K pairs + K noise tokens interleaved)
  V2 variable K per episode (4..32; criterion 85%)
  V3 3-hop composition (criterion 70%)
  V4 noisy entity views (sigma 0.2 train and test)
  V5 token-vocab entities (discrete symbols -> learned embeddings, 1000-symbol vocab,
     novel symbols at test; criterion 85%)
PASS (ALL required, 3 seeds): binding-module reaches criterion with >=10x fewer training
episodes than the transformer on >=4/5 variants AND never >2x slower on any variant AND
>= the linear-attention null on >=3/5 variants (else the win belongs to linear attention,
recorded verbatim). FAIL branches recorded verbatim; no post-hoc variant selection; no
criterion tuning after results.

Suite complete (bet3.py, runs/bet3/, prereg d02c19e): 4 models x V1-V5 x 3 seeds, params

**Finding 1 (the deep one): the meta-learning cost of binding lives in learning WHAT to bind
(the projections), not in the binding mechanics.** Wherever both learn, bind == tf on
episodes-to-criterion (V1 28.8k vs 25.6-28.8k; V2 19.2-25.6k vs 22.4k; V5 19.2-28.8k vs
19.2k). Giving the network a perfect fast-weight memory for free does NOT cut the ~20k-episode
cost — because audit (c)'s zero-training binder scored 100% only via HAND-WIRED projections.
SGD pays ~20k episodes to discover the slot structure regardless of the memory substrate.

**Finding 2 (real, modest): the standard linear-attention form (elu+1 features + normalizer)
NEVER learns any of the five binding tasks (15/15 never), while the pure outer-product core
with a chained read learns V1/V2/V5 at transformer-level sample efficiency with 4x fewer
params.** An architectural statement about learnability of binding in the fast-weight family;
would need honest comparison vs DeltaNet/GLA/TTT variants before any external claim.

**Finding 3 (the located frontier): V3 (3-hop composition) and V4 (noisy binding, sigma=.2,
crit 90%) are learned by NOTHING in the family within 200k episodes — including the
transformer.** Within this budget/scale, multi-hop composition and noise-robust binding are
open cells: the first place this whole search has found where the incumbent ALSO fails.
(Caveats: tiny models, 200k cap, V4's criterion may sit above the noisy-retrieval ceiling —
mis-specified-bar risk noted, same class as earlier audit lessons.)

**Per pre-registration, FAIL branch: no rescue iterations of Bet 3 as-formulated. The honest

projection-learning cost 10x (auxiliary objectives? architectural slot priors? curriculum?);

(depth? iterative read? curriculum from 2-hop?), with the same discipline.**

## 2026-08-07 — PRIOR-ART VERDICT on N4 (mandatory check, executed BEFORE any claim): PRECEDENTED

Survey findings: weight-tied depth recursion -> compositional/length extrapolation is an
ESTABLISHED and actively-published result family: Universal Transformer (Dehghani'18, weight
tying over depth); looped transformers with instance-scaled recurrence obtaining strong length
generalization; and 2025-26 papers demonstrating exactly compositional DEPTH extrapolation in
recurrent-depth transformers ("Thinking Deeper, Not Longer", arXiv 2603.21676; "Loop, Think &
Generalize", arXiv 2604.07822 — "dynamic recurrence achieves the strongest generalization").
**Therefore N4 is an independent small-scale REPLICATION of a known principle on a different
substrate (parameter-free recursion over a fast-weight episodic matrix; in-context novel
entities; 33k params), NOT a discovery. The epoch-candidate status of N4 is REVOKED, verbatim,
per the pre-registered discipline.**

What remains honestly ours from the N-series: (1) the head-to-head — at matched tiny budget the
tied fast-weight binder extrapolates while attention fails even trained hops (a clean substrate
comparison the looped-TF papers do not run at this scale); (2) the N2 conjunction finding
(architecture x curriculum, neither alone); (3) the located negative map (linatt never learns
binding; depth-indexed reads don't compose; reads=hops). These are workshop/short-paper-scale
observations at toy scale — not landmarks.

Meta-observation for the record: the search machine, starting from brain principles and running
pre-registered elimination for one day, independently converged onto the SAME territory the
field's 2025-26 frontier occupies (recurrent-depth composition). That validates the machinery's
direction-finding; it also means this lane is occupied. NEXT (cron, pre-register first): the

## 2026-08-07 — ARENA-AUDIT #4 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): the VALUE-FUNCTION family

The last untouched pillar of the original analysis (Sutskever Nov-25: human sample efficiency
rides on a robust internal VALUE function). New family per the standing protocol: headroom
certification BEFORE any mechanism bet.
Arena: NOVEL-WORLD sparse-reward RL — every episode a FRESH procedurally-generated gridworld
(G=12; random goal in far half; random wall pattern: 2 straight walls with gaps), so per-world
tables must start from scratch (the killer of audits 2-3 is structurally neutralized: nothing
transfers except a PRIOR over where reward lives / how to explore).
Meta-protocol: agents interact with a stream of worlds, N_ep episodes per world; metric =
episodes-to-first-reward and episodes-to-solve (reach 80% oracle return) IN FRESH WORLDS,
averaged over 20 test worlds, after any meta-learning has happened on 200 training worlds.
NULLS (this audit implements ONLY these + oracle; mechanism slot comes later if headroom
certifies): (a) random walk; (b) count-based novelty bonus (per-world state counts, no
cross-world learning); (c) tabular Q per world from scratch (audit-2's winner, reset each
world); (d) ORACLE = value iteration on each world's true MDP (upper bound).
HEADROOM BAR (fixed now): the family qualifies iff the best null needs >=10x the oracle's
effective cost AND >=30 episodes-to-solve median in fresh worlds (i.e. real room for a
transferable value-prior to cut). If the count-based null already solves fresh worlds in <10
episodes, the arena has no headroom -> family disqualified, record verbatim.
Mechanism slot (ONLY if certified, separate prereg): a meta-learned value/progress prior
(obs -> proximity-to-reward estimate, trained across worlds) guiding exploration.

**THE MARATHON'S DEEPEST THROUGH-LINE (cross-family convergence, now twice-confirmed):**
Two independent families bottomed out on the SAME bedrock. N-series: networks at this scale
do not LEARN multi-hop chaining as an algorithm — they unroll it (only weight-tying, i.e.
architecturally EXECUTED recursion, extrapolates). M-series: networks do not LEARN shortest-
path fields — they fit pattern maps that break on fresh topology. In both cases the missing
capability is **learned algorithm execution** — not memory, not gating, not signals, not
substrate. Where the algorithm is executed by construction (tied recursion; true BFS shaping)
everything works; where it must be LEARNED from data, everything at this scale fails.
This names the real target any future epoch-bet must hit: a primitive that makes ALGORITHM
ACQUISITION as natural for networks as pattern acquisition. (Known adjacent lanes: neural
algorithmic reasoning (Velickovic), graph nets, looped TF — a future family must enter via

## 2026-08-07 — A-2 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): structure DISCOVERY by differentiable selection

A-1 isolated structure (routing + semiring) as the load-bearing element. A-2 = the first
structure-DISCOVERY mechanism bet, minimal honest version: a DIFFERENTIABLE STRUCTURE SELECTOR.
The tied step is a soft-min-plus combination over a BASIS of routing atoms {identity, shift-up,
shift-down, shift-left, shift-right, global-mean} with learned atom logits alpha (6), learned
per-atom cost fields (tiny conv on walls), and learned semiring temperatures (tau -> 0 = exact
min-plus). The model must DISCOVER "route from the 4 neighbors, combine by min" from the same
200 G=12 worlds (K=24 tied iterations, same training as A-1).
PRIOR ART NAMED NOW: selection-over-basis = DARTS-shaped; task framing = NAR. The delta under
test: whether selected structure is ALGORITHMIC (semiring+routing) and therefore SIZE-INVARIANT.
BARS (fixed now, 3 seeds):
 (i)  fresh G=12: downstream median <= 30 (matching the hand-built ceiling's regime);
 (ii) **SIZE EXTRAPOLATION G=20, never trained: downstream median <= 30** — the decisive bar;
      pattern-fitting cannot pass it, a discovered size-invariant structure can;
 (iii) ablation isolates discovery: uniform-FROZEN alpha (no structure selection, costs still
      learned) must FAIL (i) or (ii);
 (iv) interpretability check (descriptive): learned alpha mass on the 4 directional atoms.
PASS = (i)+(ii)+(iii). FAIL branches recorded verbatim; no rescue without new prereg naming
the confound. If PASS: a pre-registered micro-existence-proof that gradient descent can
DISCOVER algorithmic structure from a basis and that the discovered structure extrapolates
across scale — the first rung of the structure-discovery ladder (open-ended basis = future).

## 2026-08-07 — A-4 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): SUBSET commitment — the type error in A-3

Sharper diagnosis of A-3: the softmax-over-atoms parameterization forces COMPETITION among
COMPLEMENTARY atoms — BFS needs the SUBSET {up,down,left,right}, but softmax can only commit
to ONE category; winner-take-all greediness was induced by the parameterization's TYPE.
A-4 = independent per-atom gates g_r = sigmoid(beta_r) (no normalization), soft-min-plus over
gated atoms, L1 sparsity on gates (weight .01) to prune useless atoms. Everything else as A-3
(same training, G12; eval K=2G).
BARS (3 seeds): PASS iff G12 <= 30 AND G20 <= 30 AND the gate pattern is CORRECT (all 4
directional gates > 0.5 AND identity+gmean gates < 0.5 — the algorithm's true support
recovered). If PASS -> the ladder concludes: structure discovery over a basis requires
COMMITMENT OF THE RIGHT TYPE (subset, not category) — selection+subset-commitment suffices at
micro-scale (open-ended basis remains the epoch problem). If FAIL -> the anti-greedy
requirement escalates to genuinely combinatorial search; A-series final.

## 2026-08-07 — A-4 VERDICT: FAIL (uniform shrinkage) — A-SERIES FINAL with four named failure modes

runs/a4/ (prereg 27a508b). Independent sigmoid gates + L1: gates hover 0.31-0.42 (3/3 seeds) —
neither commitment nor pruning; L1 shrinks indiscriminately while cost-fields compensate;
nothing breaks the useful/useless atom symmetry. G12 degrades (52-130 median vs 20). G20 inf.
The TYPE-error hypothesis is refuted as sufficient: fixing the commitment type (subset) without
a symmetry-breaking / exploration mechanism still fails.

**A-SERIES FINAL. The complete ladder of pre-registered failure modes for gradient-local
structure choice:**
  A-1 : structure is load-bearing (executed skeleton perfect; iteration useless)
  A-2 : softmax selection -> NO commitment (soft mixture, DARTS-collapse)
  A-3 : annealed softmax -> GREEDY commitment (locks a partial heuristic)
  A-4 : independent gates + L1 -> UNIFORM SHRINKAGE (no symmetry breaking)
**Conclusion (definitive at this scale): every gradient-local parameterization of structure
choice fails in its own named way; structure DISCOVERY requires genuinely non-local /
combinatorial search over structures (population, MDL-scored proposal, symbolic enumeration) —
gradient descent optimizes within a structure; it does not find one.** This is the search's
terminal, teachable finding — the precise mechanistic reason the missing primitive
(algorithm/structure acquisition) resists the current paradigm's core tool.

open problem. FAIL (selection picks the wrong structure) would mean the validation signal
itself cannot identify correct structure — a deeper negative, recorded verbatim.

## 2026-08-08 — T-1 THEORY NOTE (pre-registered BEFORE R-2's rank data lands): the quantitative curse

Zero-compute analytic step, recorded before the experiment it predicts.
(1) The two-point extrapolation is EXACTLY v_inf = 2*v10 - v5 (unique a+b/t fit through
t=5,10). Hence Var(v_inf) = 4*sigma_v^2 + sigma_v^2 = 5*sigma_v^2: **the estimator AMPLIFIES
evaluation noise by sqrt(5) ~ 2.24x** — the mechanistic root of the winner's curse the moment
|candidate space| grows.
(2) Rank-inflation law: with candidate true losses L_i and independent noise N(0, sigma_inf^2),
E[rank(true)] = 1 + SUM_i Phi((L_true - L_i) / (sqrt(2)*sigma_inf)) — rank inflation grows with
the DENSITY of near-competitors times sigma_inf; at n=1023 the near-shortcut mass dominates.
(3) FALSIFIABLE PREREGISTERED PREDICTIONS (testable by R-2 and a future R-3):
  P1: R-2's measured true-support rank will be >> 16 (consistent with R-1's cut failure) and
      its magnitude will indicate sigma_inf via the law in (2).
  P2 (R-3 design, derived not tuned): a THREE-point fit (t=5,10,15; least-squares a+b/t)
      reduces the variance factor from 5 to ~1.9 (weights w=(A^T A)^{-1}A^T on [v5,v10,v15]:
      a-row ~ [-0.463, 0.257, 1.206] -> SUM w^2 ~ 1.74; +50% eval cost) — i.e. sigma_inf drops
      ~1.7x, and by (2) the true rank should drop SUPERLINEARLY (through the Phi tail).
      R-3 = the 3-point cut at the same keep-K; PASS iff measured rank improves by >= the
      factor predicted from R-2's implied sigma_inf (exact bar computed from R-2's numbers
      when they land — the PREDICTION is registered now, the bar instantiates it).
This converts the recipe's scaling boundary from a named phenomenon into a QUANTITATIVE,
predictive law — the ledger's first theory-ahead-of-data entry.

## 2026-08-08 — T-1v PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): testing T-1's own independence assumption

T-1's sqrt(5) amplification assumed Var(v_inf)=4V10+V5 with INDEPENDENT v5,v10 — but both come
from the SAME training trajectory (strong positive correlation): true Var = 4V10+V5-4Cov(v5,v10),
possibly far below 5*sigma_v^2. If correlation rescues the estimator, the curse's mechanism must
be REVISED (candidate: a+b/t CURVATURE MISMATCH on shortcut learning curves — shortcuts plateau,
so their v_inf is UNDER-estimated systematically, a BIAS not a variance effect).
T-1v (LOCAL box, zero server load): home arena (63-subset machinery), 6 candidate structures
(the true one + 5 spanning shortcut types), R=10 repeats each with different torch seeds;
measure empirical V5, V10, Cov, Var(v_inf), the amplification factor vs sigma_v; ALSO measure
per-candidate BIAS: E[v_inf] - L_converged (L from one 60-epoch run each) — separating the
variance story from the bias story.
BARS: none needed (a measurement, not a bet); the outcome REFINES T-1: (a) amplification >= 2x
-> T-1 variance mechanism stands; (b) amplification < 1.5x AND shortcut bias E[v_inf]-L < 0
by >> noise -> the curse is a BIAS (curvature mismatch) phenomenon -> R-3's design changes from

## 2026-08-08 — TT-SERIES OPENED (user directive: follow the TRANSFORMER TEMPLATE)

Strategic reset, registered: the 2017 attention result was not a compute story — it beat the
incumbent (RNN/LSTM) at MATCHED-OR-LESS compute on the community's own benchmark (WMT), and
its structural advantage made scaling worthwhile afterwards. Our search so far has run only on
self-built arenas. The TT-series adopts that format: community benchmark, established
baselines, matched parameters AND matched training budget, seed-robust margin — and only then
scaling.
ASSET WE BRING (measured, S1/S2): a weight-tied fast-weight binder with a chained read learns
novel-entity multi-hop binding that transformer blocks (static or looped, with PE, up to 839k
params = 30x ours) NEVER learn at the same budget; and standard linear attention (elu+1 +
normalizer) failed 15/15 on the same family while the pure outer-product core learned it.
Those are exactly the two incumbents on the community's measuring stick for this capability.

**TT-1 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): MQAR (multi-query associative recall)** — the standard
benchmark of the efficient-architecture literature (Zoology/Arora et al.; used by Based, Mamba,
DeltaNet). Sequence = N key-value token pairs followed by Q queries; the model must emit the
value bound to each queried key. REAL token vocabulary (learned embeddings), not our synthetic
vectors; identical data for all models.
 Models, PARAM-MATCHED to within +-10% (target ~250k, d_model tuned per family):
   tf     : causal Transformer, 2 layers, learned positional embeddings   [the incumbent]
   linatt : linear attention (elu+1 feature map + normalizer), 2 layers   [efficient-arch null]
   gru    : GRU                                                           [recurrent null]
   fwb    : OUR tied fast-weight binder (outer-product write, chained read, no softmax)
 Protocol: identical optimizer/LR/batch/token budget; 3 seeds; two difficulty settings
   (N=8 pairs / seq 64, and N=32 pairs / seq 256) with vocab 8192.
 METRICS: (i) steps-to-criterion (>=90% query accuracy on held-out sequences), (ii) final
   accuracy at a fixed budget, (iii) wall-clock and param count reported for honesty.
 BARS (registered now): TT-1 PASSES iff fwb reaches criterion in >=2x FEWER steps than the
   transformer in >=2/3 seeds at BOTH settings, OR (if tf never reaches criterion) fwb reaches
   it while tf does not, 3/3. Any other outcome = FAIL, recorded verbatim (including "linatt
   or gru wins" — that would mean the wedge does not transfer to real tokens).
 If TT-1 PASSES -> TT-2 (pre-registered separately): real-text language modeling
   (WikiText-103 subset, already on the box) at matched params/tokens, reporting perplexity
   vs the same baselines — the actual scaling-law entry point.
 HONEST SCOPE NOTE: MQAR is the community's synthetic measuring stick for in-context recall,
 not real-world data; a win there is a real but bounded claim, and TT-2 is what makes it a
 language-model claim. Prior art to cite either way: Zoology/Based (linear attn + recall),
 DeltaNet/fast-weight programmers (Schlag-Irie), Mamba's recall analyses.

## 2026-08-08 — TT-1 SELF-AUDIT: OUR OWN CONFOUND FOUND (registered before any claim)

Fair-baseline table, easy sd0: fwb 400 steps / 1.000 (90k non-emb) vs tf-at-best (warmup +
LR sweep + 3x budget) 15800 steps / 0.907 (470k non-emb) — 39.5x fewer steps, 5x fewer
non-embedding params, 59x less wall-clock. The transformer DOES solve the task (post-phase-
transition), so it is no longer a strawman.
**BUT the fwb implementation reads `kpos = even positions, vpos = odd positions, queries =
positions after 2N` — the task's structure is HARD-CODED into our architecture, while
tf/linatt/gru must infer it from data. This asymmetry plausibly explains most of the gap and
would (correctly) be the first thing a reviewer strikes. Recorded as OUR confound, found by
self-audit, before any claim was made.**
FIX (registered): `fwb_causal` — a standard causal fast-weight layer with NO positional
privilege: at every timestep t compute k_t, v_t, q_t from the token embedding (plus the
previous token's embedding for the write), write F += v_t k_t^T online, read r_t = F q_t,
predict at every position; loss taken only at query positions (same supervision as all
baselines). Everything else identical. TT-1's verdict will be read from fwb_causal, not from
the privileged version; the privileged number stays in the ledger as an upper bound and as the
audit record.

## 2026-08-08 — CHUNKED-PARALLEL KERNEL: math-identical, 6.7x faster/step — the wall-clock gap CLOSES

tt1k.py implements the chunked-parallel form of the causal fast-weight read (intra-chunk masked
matmul + inter-chunk running state), the standard trick of the linear-attention family.
VERIFIED math-identical to the sequential implementation: max|seq - chunked| = 1.97e-6 on
identical weights/inputs (fp32 noise). Speed at batch 64, easy setting: sequential 0.269 s/step
-> chunked 0.040 s/step (6.7x); the transformer measures 0.075 s/step under the same isolated
conditions => **we are now ~1.9x faster PER STEP than the incumbent, on top of 13.2x fewer
steps.** Projected time-to-criterion: ~48 s (ours) vs ~1185 s (tf) ~ 25x.
NOT YET A CLAIM: these are micro-benchmarks plus a projection. The registered next step is a
CLEAN full re-run (all 4 models, 3 seeds, both settings, no CPU contention, wall-clock recorded
per model) — only those numbers may be quoted. Earlier wall-clock figures were taken under
contention and are hereby marked non-comparable.

(below gpt at >=2/3 late checkpoints AND <=0.7x tokens-to-gpt-final): FAILED outright.**
Also: on GPU the transformer's fused SDPA/flash kernel runs 3x faster per step than our chunked
kernel — the TT-1 wall-clock advantage was a CPU artifact (no fused attention kernel there) and
does NOT survive on accelerator hardware. Recorded verbatim.

**HONEST CONCLUSION (the project's most important scoping statement to date):**
the fast-weight binder is a SPECIALIST, not an architecture. On associative recall (MQAR, the
community's recall benchmark) it is ~13x more sample-efficient than attention at half the
non-embedding params; on general next-token prediction it is worse than both attention and a
GRU at matched params. That is the classic specialist/generalist trade-off, and it means:
 - no Transformer-replacement claim is available, and none will be made;
 - the honest home for this mechanism is as a RECALL MODULE inside a hybrid stack — precisely
   the design space the literature already occupies (Based, Griffin, Jamba, DeltaNet hybrids);
 - "then we do scaling laws" is OFF the table on this mechanism as a standalone architecture.
NEXT (registered, if the line continues): a HYBRID test — replace only k of n layers' attention
with the binder and measure (a) LM loss vs pure-gpt at matched params, (b) MQAR-style recall
retained; that is the only configuration in which our measured strength and measured weakness
are both respected. TT-1 hard remains informative for characterising the strength's range.

The literature's answer to exactly this profile is hybridisation (Based / Griffin / Jamba).
TT-3 tests it in the only form our own data licenses: keep attention, replace the LAST k of 4
layers with the binder (placement fixed a-priori, NO search over placements — searching would
invite the selection artifacts this project has documented repeatedly).
Arms (identical stack/data/optimizer/params as TT-2): gpt (4 attn) | hyb1 (3 attn + 1 binder) |
hyb2 (2 attn + 2 binder) | fwbc (4 binder, from TT-2) — 2 seeds, 3000 steps, 24.58M tokens.
BARS: TT-3 PASSES iff some hybrid reaches val loss <= gpt's (within 0.01 nats) on 2/2 seeds
AND retains a large recall advantage (to be measured by running the SAME hybrid on MQAR-easy
under TT-1's protocol: criterion in <=0.5x gpt's steps). Anything else = FAIL, recorded:
a hybrid that merely interpolates between the two (LM worse than gpt, recall better) is NOT a
contribution — it is the trivially expected outcome and will be labelled as such.

## 2026-08-08 — TT-3 VERDICT: FAIL — hybrids interpolate; the TT line closes with an honest scope

Real-text LM, identical stack/params (16.10M / 3.16M non-emb), 24.58M tokens, 2 seeds:
  gru   6.7384                      (ppl  844)
  gpt   6.8250 / 6.8206  mean 6.823 (ppl  918)   <- incumbent
  hyb1  6.8079 / 6.8948  mean 6.851 (3 attn + 1 binder)
  hyb2  6.8851 / 6.8785  mean 6.882 (2 attn + 2 binder)
  fwbc  7.0231 / 7.0196  mean 7.021 (4 binder)

interpolation between the two endpoints. Per the registered wording this is "NOT a

**TT LINE CLOSED. The honest, complete statement of what we have:**
 (1) On the community's recall benchmark (MQAR-easy), the weight-tied fast-weight binder with a
     chained read reaches criterion in 1000-1400 steps vs an at-its-best transformer's 15800
     (13.2x), at half the non-embedding params, with no tuning on our side — replicated 3/3.
 (2) On real-text language modelling at matched params, the same mechanism is WORSE than
     attention (7.02 vs 6.82) and worse than a GRU (6.74); mixing it into attention only
     interpolates. On GPU, fused attention is also 3x faster per step than our chunked kernel.
 (3) Therefore: a genuine, replicated, specialist result about associative recall — and a
     clear negative about general language modelling. No Transformer-replacement claim, no
     scaling-law programme on this mechanism. That is the whole truth of the TT series.
This is the shape of an honest short paper (recall-specialist mechanism + its measured
boundary), not of an epoch-making algorithm — recorded as such, per the project's standard.

## 2026-08-08 — TT-4 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code/results): LONG CONTEXT, the untested variable

TT-2/TT-3 tested context 256 — the regime most favourable to attention (quadratic cost still
cheap, KV cache small). The fast-weight family's entire raison d'etre is O(1) state vs O(T)
cache and O(T) vs O(T^2) compute; that variable was never varied. TT-4 varies exactly it,
nothing else, on the SAME real-text LM setup (OpenWebText -> WikiText-103, matched params).
Arms: gpt vs fwbc vs hyb1 at context T in {256 (done), 1024}; 2 seeds; TOKEN-MATCHED training
(same total tokens: steps adjusted so steps*bs*T is equal), same optimizer/data order.
MEASURED: val loss at equal tokens; wall-clock/step; peak GPU memory (the KV-cache axis).
BARS (registered now):
 (a) SCALING-DIRECTION bar: the gap (fwbc - gpt) in val loss must SHRINK from T=256 to T=1024
     in 2/2 seeds. If it shrinks materially (>=50% of the 0.20-nat gap), the mechanism's
     disadvantage is context-dependent and long-context is the honest home; if it does not
     shrink, our disadvantage is intrinsic and the TT line is finished for good.
 (b) COST bar (descriptive, always reported): wall-clock/step and peak memory vs gpt at 1024.
This is the last registered experiment of the TT series either way: shrink -> the honest claim
becomes "recall specialist whose LM gap closes with context, cheaper memory"; no-shrink -> the
mechanism is simply worse at LM and the series ends with that recorded flatly.

                  T=256              T=1024            gap (fwbc - gpt)
  gpt             6.823              7.239              --

  hyb1            6.851              7.256              (hyb1 - gpt): +0.028 -> +0.017

BOTH come out against us at this scale: our peak memory is HIGHER than attention's (22.85 vs
21.29 GB — the chunked kernel's intermediates outweigh the KV cache at T=1024), and we are
2.6x SLOWER per step. The O(1)-state advantage is real only asymptotically; at 1024 tokens with
a fused flash-attention baseline it has not arrived.

**TT SERIES CLOSED (TT-1..TT-4), final honest statement:**
 - REAL, replicated: a 13.2x sample-efficiency advantage over an at-its-best transformer on the

 - REAL, replicated: worse than attention AND worse than a GRU on real-text language modelling;

 - CONCLUSION: an associative-recall specialist with a precisely measured boundary — a legitimate

## 2026-08-08 — TT-5 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): STRATIFIED evaluation — is the recall win invisible in aggregate PPL?

The TT series produced two facts: 13.2x sample-efficiency on associative recall, and a flat
loss on aggregate LM. The direct implication (untested): our mechanism helps on the SUBSET of
tokens that require long-range exact recall, and that subset is too small to move corpus PPL.
This is testable on the models ALREADY TRAINED — no new training, no new tuning.
METHOD: take the TT-2 checkpoints' architecture/config, retrain once per arm (2 seeds, same
protocol, 3000 steps) while EVALUATING the val set stratified into:
  (S1) RECALL tokens: positions whose target token appeared earlier in the same context at
       distance > 64, and whose preceding bigram also appeared earlier (an induction-style
       exact-copy event) — the canonical "induction head" subset;
  (S2) ALL other tokens.
Report per-stratum loss for gpt / fwbc / hyb1. BARS (registered):
 - PRIMARY: fwbc's S1 loss < gpt's S1 loss in 2/2 seeds AND the S1 margin is at least 3x the
   (negative) S2 margin in magnitude — i.e. the mechanism genuinely trades general prediction
   for recall, rather than being uniformly worse.
 - If fwbc is worse on BOTH strata, the "specialist" reading DIES: the MQAR win would then be
   an artifact of that synthetic task's structure, not a property that survives natural text.
   That is the harsher, and entirely possible, outcome — and it must be recorded as such.
This is the experiment that decides whether "recall specialist" is a real characterisation of
the mechanism on natural language, or only a story about a synthetic benchmark.

## 2026-08-08 — TT-5 VERDICT: the "recall specialist" reading DIES on natural text

Stratified evaluation on WikiText-103 val (induction-style long-range exact-recall tokens,
n=9748, ~4% of positions; vs all others, n=236012), 2 seeds, matched params:
             recall tokens (S1)        other tokens (S2)
  gpt        7.4628 / 7.6527           6.7816 / 6.7726
  fwbc       7.7806 / 7.7839           6.9801 / 6.9724
**fwbc is WORSE than attention on BOTH strata (S1 +0.22 nats, S2 +0.20 nats), 2/2 seeds.**
The pre-registered PRIMARY bar (better on S1, with the S1 margin >=3x the S2 margin) fails
outright; the harsher branch that was registered in advance is the one that occurred:
**the mechanism is not a recall specialist on natural language — it is uniformly worse, by
essentially the same margin on recall-heavy and ordinary tokens alike (0.22 vs 0.20).**
CONSEQUENCE, stated flatly: the MQAR 13.2x advantage does NOT transfer to natural text in any
stratum. It is a property of that synthetic task's structure (clean, unambiguous, exactly
repeated key-value pairs with no distributional competition), not a transferable capability.
The "specialist" framing offered after TT-2 is hereby RETRACTED — it was a hypothesis, it was
pre-registered as falsifiable, and it has been falsified by our own experiment within hours.
**FINAL POSITION OF THE TT SERIES:** a synthetic-benchmark result with a measured failure to
transfer. The only honest artifacts are (i) the MQAR number itself with its scope limit
attached, and (ii) this negative transfer result, which is arguably the more useful of the two
for anyone else building on fast-weight/linear-attention recall mechanisms.

## 2026-08-08 — TT-6 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): CROSSTALK as the cross-domain explanation

Two independent lines in this ledger now report the same failure of outer-product memory on
CORRELATED representations: N6/N7 (vision — hand-wired ideal binder + cleanup reaches only
h1=0.18 on dinov2 features; sparse expansion to dk=16384 does not rescue it) and TT-5
(language — fwbc uniformly worse than attention on every token stratum). MQAR, where we win
13.2x, uses random near-orthogonal keys. HYPOTHESIS (registered): the binder's disadvantage is
governed by RETRIEVAL CROSSTALK, which is a function of key correlation, and attention's
softmax is precisely a competitive normalisation that suppresses it.
MEASUREMENT (no training needed beyond existing runs): for a trained fwbc and a batch of real
text, build the memory F over a context and compute, at each position t,
   SNR_t = <F q_t, v_t*> / mean_{j != t*} |<F q_t, v_j>|
i.e. signal (the intended stored value) over mean interference from all other stored values.
Report median SNR for: (a) natural text (WikiText val), (b) MQAR sequences, (c) natural text
with keys RANDOMISED (orthogonalisation control). Same statistic for attention's post-softmax
weights as the reference.
PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS:
 P1: SNR(MQAR) >> SNR(natural text) for fwbc — the win/loss flip tracks crosstalk, not task
     semantics. (If natural-text SNR is comparable to MQAR's, the crosstalk story is FALSE and
     the loss must be explained otherwise — recorded as such.)
 P2: attention's effective SNR on natural text is substantially higher than fwbc's, isolating
     competitive normalisation as the differentiator.
 P3 (quantitative): randomising/orthogonalising the keys on natural text raises fwbc's SNR
     materially (>=2x), confirming correlation as the causal variable.
If P1-P3 hold, the TT series ends with a MECHANISTIC, cross-domain explanation of why linear
associative memories underperform attention on natural data — a more useful result than the
MQAR number. If they fail, the explanation is wrong and gets recorded as wrong.

## 2026-08-08 — TT-6 VERDICT: ALL THREE PREDICTIONS CONFIRMED — crosstalk explains the whole TT series

Measured retrieval SNR (signal to mean interference), same trained architecture, layer 0:
  fwbc on natural text (WikiText val)        SNR = 0.869   <-- signal BELOW interference
  fwbc with random near-orthogonal keys      SNR = 20.274  (the MQAR-like condition)
  attention on the SAME natural text         SNR = 2.589   (post-softmax winner vs rest)
  key correlation |off-diag|: natural 0.0750 vs random 0.0497
P1 CONFIRMED (23.3x): the same mechanism that wins 13.2x on MQAR is operating at SNR<1 on
natural text — the win and the loss are two ends of ONE variable, not two task properties.
P2 CONFIRMED (3.0x): competitive normalisation (softmax) buys 3x the signal-to-interference on
identical data; that is the isolated differentiator.
P3 CONFIRMED (direction): natural keys are 1.5x more correlated; because crosstalk accumulates
over T=256 stored items, a modest correlation increase compounds into the 23x SNR collapse.
CROSS-DOMAIN: this is the SAME bedrock the vision line hit independently (N6/N7: hand-wired
ideal binder + cleanup = 0.18 on dinov2 features; sparse expansion to dk=16384 did not rescue
it). Two domains, two independent routes, one mechanism: **linear associative memory is
crosstalk-limited on correlated natural representations; attention's softmax is precisely the
competitive normalisation that resolves it.**
HONEST CAVEATS: 16M-param models trained 24.6M tokens; SNR is our own construction measured at
layer 0; the random-key condition queries its own key exactly (an upper bound, favourable to
that condition); P3's raw correlation gap is modest (1.5x).
**THIS is the TT series' real deliverable** — not the MQAR number, and not a new algorithm: a
measured, cross-domain, mechanistic account of WHY the fast-weight / linear-attention family
underperforms attention on natural data, with a quantity (retrieval SNR) that predicts it.

## 2026-08-08 — TT-7 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): is retrieval-SNR a PREDICTOR of architecture quality?

TT-6 established crosstalk as the mechanism. The useful corollary, and the convergence with the
A-series' central question (what cheap signal predicts final quality?): **if crosstalk governs
performance, then retrieval SNR measured AT INITIALISATION, without any training, should rank
sequence mixers by their eventual LM loss.** That would be a design tool for exactly the family
(linear attention / fast weights) where the field currently trains-and-prays.
ARMS (>=5 mixers, same stack/params/data as TT-2): softmax attention (gpt); fwbc (ours);
linatt (elu+1 + normaliser); delta (delta-rule write F += (v - F k) k^T — the DeltaNet-style
error-correcting update, which SHOULD reduce crosstalk by construction); fwbc-l2 (values
L2-normalised, a cheap crosstalk mitigation).
PROTOCOL: (1) measure SNR at INIT on natural text for each (no training, seconds);
(2) train each 1500 steps, 2 seeds, identical everything; (3) record final val loss;
(4) compute Spearman rank correlation between init-SNR and final loss.
BARS (registered): TT-7 PASSES iff Spearman |rho| >= 0.8 with the correct sign (higher SNR ->
lower loss) across all arms, 2/2 seeds. A pass means an untrained, seconds-cheap measurement
ranks architectures; a fail means SNR explains our own mechanism but does not generalise into
a predictor, and gets recorded as such.
SECONDARY (descriptive, registered): does `delta` — the error-correcting write, which the
crosstalk account predicts should help most — actually close the gap to attention? That is the
crosstalk theory's own prescription being tested on the LM task.

## 2026-08-08 — TT-7 part 1: init-time SNR measured for 5 mixers (+ a self-audit of the measure)

Retrieval SNR at INITIALISATION on natural text (seconds, no training):
  gpt 2.5888 | linatt 1.0091 | fwbc 0.8686 | fwbl2 0.8686 | delta 0.8520
SELF-AUDIT (recorded before the correlation is computed): the statistic depends ONLY on keys and
queries, not on values — so fwbl2, which changes only the value normalisation, is IDENTICAL to
fwbc by construction. The measure therefore captures KEY-SPACE crosstalk only; any value-space
mitigation is invisible to it. That is a ceiling on its predictive power and must be stated
whenever the predictor is discussed. (It also means fwbl2 is, for this predictor, a
tie-prediction — if fwbl2's trained loss differs materially from fwbc's, the measure is
incomplete and the TT-7 bar should be read accordingly.)
Training of gpt/fwbc/fwbl2/linatt (1500 steps, 2 seeds, identical protocol) is running; delta
is deferred/reduced-budget because its per-token Python loop costs ~3.75 s/step (deviation
recorded, not hidden). Spearman correlation to be computed when the losses land.

## 2026-08-08 — TT-7 VERDICT: bar PASSED on the letter (rho = -1.000) — but the substance is a 2-GROUP separation, not a ranking

init-SNR (seconds, untrained) vs final val loss (1500 steps, 2 seeds, matched params):
  gpt    SNR 2.5888 -> loss 7.1683
  linatt SNR 1.0091 -> loss 7.1700
  fwbl2  SNR 0.8686 -> loss 7.2097
  fwbc   SNR 0.8686 -> loss 7.2415
Spearman rho = -1.000 (bar: <= -0.8, correct sign) => PASS as registered.
**THREE CAVEATS THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THE NUMBER (self-audited before any claim):**
 (1) n = 4 arms; a perfect rho arises by chance with p = 1/24 = 4.2%. Suggestive, not conclusive.
 (2) fwbc and fwbl2 have IDENTICAL SNR by construction (the statistic ignores values — flagged
     in advance); their relative order was decided by an arbitrary tie-break, so the honest
     count is 5/6 concordant pairs, not 6/6.
 (3) gpt vs linatt differ by 0.0017 nats — an order of magnitude below seed noise (~0.02).
     That pair's "correct" ordering is meaningless.
**HONEST READING: the statistic separates TWO GROUPS — un-normalised fast-weight memories
(SNR ~0.87, loss 7.21-7.24) from competitively-normalised mixers (SNR 1.0-2.6, loss ~7.17) —
which is exactly what the crosstalk account predicts (a normalisation term, softmax or
elu+1-denominator alike, is the dividing line). It does NOT demonstrate fine-grained ranking
power, and the fwbl2 blind spot shows where it is structurally incomplete.**
USABLE FORM OF THE RESULT: "measure retrieval SNR before training; if it is <1 (signal below
interference) your mixer is in the crosstalk-limited group and will underperform a normalised
one" — a cheap screening rule with a stated failure mode, not an architecture-ranking oracle.
TT SERIES NOW COMPLETE (TT-1..TT-7). Deliverables, in order of value:
 1. the crosstalk account + SNR screening rule (mechanism + tool, cross-domain with N6/N7);
 2. the negative-transfer result (MQAR 13.2x does not survive natural text, in any stratum);
 3. the MQAR number itself, only ever quoted with (2) attached.

## 2026-08-08 — TT-8 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): the crosstalk account's OWN PRESCRIPTION — key decorrelation

TT-6/7 measured the mechanism (SNR<1 from correlated keys) and identified competitive
normalisation as attention's fix. But normalisation is not the only way to raise SNR: the
crosstalk term is driven by KEY CORRELATION, so decorrelating the keys should raise SNR at
O(d^2) cost — with NO dependence on sequence length, unlike softmax's O(T^2). This is the
prescription our own measurement implies, and it has not been tested.
ARMS (identical stack/params/data/protocol as TT-7; 1500 steps, 2 seeds):
  fwbc      : baseline (SNR 0.869, loss 7.2415)
  fwbc-cent : keys centred by a running mean key (removes the dominant shared component —
              the single largest crosstalk source), then re-normalised
  fwbc-white: keys standardised per-dimension by running mean/var (a cheap diagonal whitening)
  gpt       : reference (SNR 2.589, loss 7.1683)
MEASURED: init SNR for each new arm + final val loss.
BARS (registered): TT-8 PASSES iff some decorrelated arm (a) raises init SNR above 1.0 AND
(b) reduces final val loss vs plain fwbc by >=0.02 nats (one seed-noise unit) in 2/2 seeds.
A FULL pass — reaching gpt's loss (within 0.01) at O(d^2) cost — would be a genuine
architectural result derived from our own diagnosis. A partial pass (SNR up, loss improved but
short of gpt) is exactly the honest middle outcome and will be reported as such. If SNR rises
but loss does NOT improve, the crosstalk account is INCOMPLETE as a design principle — the
sharpest possible negative, and it must be recorded that way.

## 2026-08-08 — TT-8 SELF-AUDIT: TT-6's headline 23.3x was CONFOUNDED — retracted pending re-measurement

TT-8 tested the crosstalk account's own prescription and found key decorrelation INERT at the
SNR level: fwbc 0.8686 -> centring 0.8647 -> diagonal whitening 0.8562 -> FULL ZCA whitening
0.8673. If crosstalk were driven by key correlation, full whitening had to move it. It did not.
That null forced a re-examination of TT-6, and the confound is ours:
**In TT-6's "random key" control I set the query EQUAL to its own key (qr = kr), so the signal
term was 1.0 by construction. In the natural-text condition the query and key are DIFFERENT
learned projections (wq vs wk) of the same hidden state, so the signal term is small by
construction. The 23.3x "MQAR-like vs natural" ratio therefore compares a best-case control
against a realistic condition — it is not an apples-to-apples measurement of key correlation.**
CONSEQUENCE (recorded now, before any re-measurement): TT-6's P1 headline (23.3x) is RETRACTED.
P2 (attention 3.0x higher effective SNR than fwbc on identical data) used a different statistic
for attention (post-softmax winner vs rest) and is ALSO not strictly comparable — flagged.
The only TT-6 element that survives unchallenged is the raw observation that fwbc's natural-text
signal-to-interference is < 1 with q,k as trained projections.
CORRECTED MEASUREMENT (registered, running next): identical statistic for both conditions —
keep wq/wk fixed and replace only the INPUTS with random vectors (so q,k remain different
projections in both arms). This isolates input-correlation from projection-mismatch. Whatever
it shows will be reported, including that the crosstalk account may be substantially weaker
than TT-6 claimed.

## 2026-08-08 — TT-9 VERDICT: the crosstalk account is FALSIFIED. TT-6 and TT-7 are RETRACTED.

Corrected measurement (identical statistic in every arm; q and k always distinct projections):
  fwbc, natural text inputs      SNR 0.8686   key |corr| 0.0750
  fwbc, RANDOM inputs            SNR 0.8571   key |corr| 0.0701   -> input effect 0.99x
  gpt, raw q.k (no softmax)      SNR 0.8595                        -> 0.99x vs fwbc
**Both TT-6 claims collapse:**
 (1) "natural-text key correlation causes the crosstalk that sinks our mechanism" — FALSE.
     Replacing the inputs with pure random vectors leaves the SNR unchanged (0.99x). There is

     whitening and full ZCA whitening were all inert (TT-8).
 (2) "attention wins because its retrieval SNR is higher" — FALSE. Measured with the SAME
     statistic and no softmax granted, attention's q.k geometry is indistinguishable from ours
     (0.99x). Attention's advantage comes ENTIRELY from the softmax competition itself, not
     from any representational property our measurement can see.
**RETRACTIONS: TT-6 (crosstalk account, P1/P2/P3) is retracted in full. TT-7's rho = -1.000
"SNR predicts architecture quality" is retracted with it — its ranking signal came from a
statistic that, correctly measured, does not distinguish the architectures at all.**
WHAT SURVIVES THE WHOLE TT SERIES, honestly: (i) the MQAR sample-efficiency result with its
measured non-transfer to natural text (TT-1, TT-5); (ii) the flat negative that our mechanism
is worse than attention and than a GRU on real-text LM, at matched params, at 256 and 1024
context, alone or hybridised (TT-2/3/4); (iii) this methodological record: three self-caught
confounds (positional privilege, contended wall-clock, and now the query=key control) each
found and retracted by our own pre-registered follow-ups, twice overturning a headline result
within hours of producing it.
No mechanism, no predictor, no algorithm. The honest yield of the TT series is one clean
negative-transfer result and a demonstration of how fast an unexamined control can manufacture
a 23x effect that does not exist.

## 2026-08-08 — TT-10 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): is COMPETITION-BY-ITERATION the missing ingredient?

TT-9's surviving positive statement: attention's advantage is the softmax COMPETITION itself,
not representational geometry (raw q.k geometry is identical, 0.99x). The brain's own way of
implementing competition is not all-pairs comparison but recurrent lateral inhibition /
attractor iteration — and our fwbc already contains exactly ONE step of it (the chained read
r2 = F normalize(r1), i.e. a Hopfield-style pattern-completion step).
TEST: sweep the READ-ITERATION DEPTH n_read in {1, 2, 4, 8} (n_read=2 is current fwbc), cost
O(n_read * T) — still linear in sequence length, never O(T^2). Everything else identical to
