{1,2,4,8} in 2/2 seeds AND the best depth reaches within 0.02 nats of gpt (7.168).
PARTIAL: monotone improvement that plateaus above gpt = competition helps but is not
sufficient; recorded as a bounded positive with the plateau value stated.
FAIL: no monotone improvement = iteration is not the mechanism, and the "competition is the
whole story" reading of TT-9 is itself wrong — which would be the third headline this series
has overturned, and must be recorded with the same bluntness as the previous two.

## 2026-08-08 — TT-10 VERDICT: FAIL — competition-by-iteration is NOT the missing ingredient. TT-9's surviving claim falls too.

Read-iteration depth sweep (identical stack/params/data, 1500 steps, 2 seeds):
  n_read=1  7.2469 / 7.2591   mean 7.2530
  n_read=2  7.2305 / 7.2516   mean 7.2411   (the fwbc baseline depth)
  n_read=4  7.2381 / 7.2277   mean 7.2329
  n_read=8  7.2736 / 7.3177   mean 7.2957   <- WORSE
  gpt reference                     7.1683
**NOT monotone (8 is the worst), improvement from 1->4 is ~0.02 nats = one seed-noise unit, and
every depth stays ~0.06-0.13 nats above attention. Registered bar (monotone AND within 0.02 of
gpt) FAILED on both clauses.**
CONSEQUENCE: TT-9's surviving positive statement — "attention's advantage is the softmax
competition, which a cheaper competition mechanism could capture" — is itself refuted in the
form we could test. Attractor iteration inside the compressed state does not recover it.
The reading that survives is information-theoretic rather than mechanistic: softmax compares
against ALL STORED ITEMS (O(T) evidence per query), whereas our iteration recirculates a single
O(1) state vector — whatever the write compressed away cannot be recovered by re-reading it,
no matter how many times. Competition is not a bolt-on to a compressed memory; it needs the
uncompressed set. (That is the same compression-vs-retrieval conservation law recorded at the
very start of this project's SSM analysis, arrived at here from the opposite direction.)
**THIRD HEADLINE OVERTURNED IN THIS SERIES** (after positional privilege and the query=key
control). Running tally of the TT series: 10 experiments, 1 replicated synthetic win that does
not transfer, 4 flat negatives, 3 self-retractions, 0 mechanisms that survived contact with a
proper control. Every retraction was produced by our own pre-registered follow-up, and each
took hours, not months.

## 2026-08-08 — TT-11 PRE-REGISTRATION: quantify the conservation law (state size vs retrieval quality)

TT-10's surviving reading is a law, not a mechanism: a fixed O(1) state cannot recover what its
write compressed away; competition needs the uncompressed set. If that law is real it must be
QUANTITATIVE — LM loss should fall monotonically with the fast-weight state's capacity, and
should only approach attention when the state approaches the size of what attention keeps
(the KV cache).
DESIGN: sweep the fast-weight state size via dk in {64, 128, 256, 512} (state = dk x dk matrix
per layer, i.e. 4k / 16k / 65k / 262k numbers) against attention, whose per-layer KV cache at
T=256, d=256 holds 2*T*d = 131k numbers. Everything else identical (stack, data, optimizer,
1500 steps, 2 seeds). Note honestly: changing dk changes parameter count, so BOTH loss and
params are reported and the comparison is loss-vs-state-size, not iso-parameter.
BARS (registered):
 (a) MONOTONICITY: loss must fall monotonically with dk in 2/2 seeds — if not, the law's
     quantitative form is wrong and it stays a slogan (recorded as such).
 (b) CROSSING POINT: report the state size at which fwbc's loss reaches gpt's 7.168. The law
     predicts this occurs near attention's own cache size (~131k numbers, i.e. dk ~ 362).
     A crossing far BELOW that would falsify the law (we would be beating the bound); a
     crossing far above, or no crossing, bounds how much worse compression-with-competition is.
This converts the project's oldest thesis (compression vs retrieval, first written in the SSM
analysis at the very beginning) into a measured curve on real text — the most defensible
artifact available from this whole line.

## 2026-08-08 — TT-11 VERDICT: state capacity is NOT the binding constraint — the conservation law's quantitative form FAILS

State-size sweep (fast-weight state = dk x dk numbers per layer; attention's KV cache at
T=256,d=256 holds ~131k numbers), 1500 steps, 2 seeds, real text:
  dk=64   state    4k   loss 7.2081 / 7.2139   mean 7.2110
  dk=128  state   16k   loss 7.2137 / 7.2670   mean 7.2404
  dk=256  state   65k   loss 7.2097 / 7.2733   mean 7.2415
  dk=512  state  262k   loss 7.3191 / 7.2465   mean 7.2828   <- 2x attention's cache, WORSE
  gpt reference                                       7.1683
**Bar (a) monotonicity: FAILED — the curve is flat-to-rising. Bar (b) crossing point: no
crossing exists; even a state 2x LARGER than attention's entire KV cache does not reach it.**
A 64x range of state capacity (4k -> 262k numbers) moves the loss by less than seed noise.
CONSEQUENCE: the conservation-law reading inherited from TT-10 is WRONG in its quantitative
form. Our deficit versus attention is not a capacity deficit at all — it is qualitative. Three
independent, pre-registered routes now converge on the same conclusion:
  TT-9  : attention's raw q.k geometry is identical to ours (0.99x) — the advantage is softmax.
  TT-10 : more read-iterations do not recover it (non-monotone, 8 worst).
  TT-11 : more state does not recover it (flat over a 64x capacity range).
**What is left standing is a single, sharp, thrice-triangulated statement: the gap between
linear associative memory and attention is the COMPETITIVE (softmax) READOUT itself — not the
representation, not the depth of recurrent completion, and not the size of the memory. Nothing
we can add to a linear readout recovers it; the competition has to be there.**
That is the honest terminal finding of this entire line. It is a negative result about a whole
mechanism family, triangulated three ways, with every intermediate hypothesis (crosstalk,
SNR-prediction, competition-by-iteration, capacity) pre-registered and then falsified by our own
follow-ups. It is not an algorithm and it never became one.

## 2026-08-08 — PROJECT SYNTHESIS: what ~200 pre-registered commits across 30+ families jointly imply

Five constraints, each established by its own pre-registered line, each surviving its own
follow-ups:
 C1 COMPETITION IS IRREDUCIBLE. The gap between a linear associative read and attention is the
    competitive (softmax) readout. Not representation (TT-9: 0.99x on identical statistics),
    not completion depth (TT-10: non-monotone, deepest worst), not capacity (TT-11: flat over a
    64x state sweep reaching 2x attention's KV cache), not key decorrelation (TT-8: centring,
    diagonal and full ZCA whitening all inert).
 C2 GRADIENT OPTIMISES WITHIN A STRUCTURE; IT DOES NOT FIND ONE. Four parameterisations of
    structure choice each failed in their own named way (A-2 no commitment, A-3 greedy,
    A-4 uniform shrinkage, A-5 short-horizon mis-selection); only enumeration + converged
    inner training recovered the true support, at 63x compute.
 C3 GIVEN A GOOD REPRESENTATION, AGGREGATION OVER THE RIGHT UNITS BEATS INSTANCES. Four
    independent constructions (Bet-2 prototypes vs exemplars; audit-1 store vs dense Hebbian;
    audit-2 tabular vs episodic; audit-3 hash-bucket vs 1-NN) returned the same winner.
 C4 NETWORKS LEARN PATTERNS, NOT ALGORITHMS. Executed skeletons solve instantly what learned
    ones never acquire (N-series, M-series, A-1).
 C5 THE BRAIN'S RETRIEVAL ADVANTAGE MAY BE SUBSTRATE, NOT ALGORITHM — massively parallel
    content-addressable storage, which von-Neumann hardware must pay O(T) or O(T^2) to emulate
    (the project's opening neuromorphic thread, and the reason attention is what it is).
**JOINT IMPLICATION — the only shape consistent with all five: a primitive that DISCOVERS THE
UNITS OVER WHICH TO COMPETE.** Not competing over every token (attention, quadratic), not
compressing before competing (the fast-weight family, refuted here), but learning what to group
so that competition runs over a small number of the right units. C1 says competition must be
present; C3 says it should run over aggregated units, not instances; C2 and C4 say those units
will not fall out of gradient descent on an unstructured parameterisation — the grouping must
itself be a first-class, discovered object.
**THIS IS REGISTERED AS THE NEXT FAMILY (family U, "unit discovery"), and it inherits the
standing protocol: an ARENA AUDIT FIRST (a task where the right units are unknown, unavailable
by hand, and where a hand-given grouping demonstrably wins — the headroom that C3's arenas
lacked), then a mechanism bet, then falsification.**
Honest statement of status: this is a coordinate derived from ~200 pre-registered experiments,
not a result. No epoch-making algorithm has been found in this project. What has been produced
is: two submission-ready papers (one on neuromodulatory gating, one on this mechanism family),
a search map with every dead end diagnosed, and a machine that has retracted its own headline
four times within hours of producing it.

## 2026-08-08 — FAMILY U, ARENA AUDIT U-1 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code)

Family U asks for a primitive that DISCOVERS the units over which to compete. Per the standing
protocol the arena must be certified first, and this audit's bar is deliberately the one the
three previous audits failed: a HAND-GIVEN grouping must demonstrably beat both no-grouping and
instance-level baselines by a wide margin. If it does not, the arena has no headroom for unit
discovery and is discarded without a mechanism ever being proposed.
ARENA (latent-unit sequence prediction): tokens are emitted by K hidden LATENT CLASSES; each
class has its own transition statistics over a shared vocabulary; class identity NEVER appears
in the input and cannot be read off a single token (classes share tokens, differing only in
their transition structure). Sequences switch class at random points. Predicting the next token
well REQUIRES pooling statistics over tokens that belong to the same latent class — the units
are real, unknown, and not hand-specifiable from surface form.
ARMS (identical budget/params/data):
  oracle-group : given the TRUE latent class of each position, aggregate per-class statistics
                 (the hand-given grouping — the headroom probe)
  no-group     : one global aggregate over all history (the no-grouping baseline)
  instance     : k-NN over individual past tokens (the instance-level baseline, which won
                 audits 1-3 and killed them)
  ngram        : plain bigram/trigram statistics (a cheap surface null)
METRIC: next-token cross-entropy on held-out sequences, 3 seeds.
HEADROOM BAR (registered): the arena QUALIFIES iff oracle-group beats BOTH no-group and
instance by >= 0.30 nats in 3/3 seeds, AND ngram does not come within 0.10 nats of oracle-group.
Anything less = no headroom = arena discarded, recorded, and family U pauses until a better
arena is found. NO mechanism will be proposed in this experiment; this audit only asks whether
knowing the right units is worth anything here.

## 2026-08-08 — U-1 VERDICT: ARENA QUALIFIES (first one in this project) + U-2 MECHANISM BET registered

U-1 (prereg 7216082, runs_local/u1.json): oracle-group beats no-group by 0.798/0.818/0.815 nats
and beats the instance (kNN) baseline by 1.501/1.669/1.686 nats, 3/3 seeds; trigram trails
oracle by 0.712-0.848. All three registered bars cleared with large margins.
**This is the first arena in ~200 pre-registered experiments to certify headroom for unit
structure. Audits 1-3 all died because instance/table baselines matched the structured approach;
here, knowing the right units is worth 0.8-1.7 nats.**
REGISTERED LIMITATION, stated before the mechanism is built: this arena was CONSTRUCTED by us to
contain latent-class structure, so a mechanism that recovers latent classes winning here is close
to tautological. The arena certifies that unit-discovery CAN pay; it does not show that it pays
anywhere real. Therefore U-3 (natural text) is registered NOW as MANDATORY and gating: no claim
of any kind may be made from U-2 alone.

**U-2 MECHANISM BET (registered before code): online competitive unit discovery.**
Mechanism: maintain M unit slots, each holding aggregated next-token statistics. At each
position compute a responsibility over slots (softmax competition — C1) from the recent context,
update the winning slots' statistics online (aggregation over discovered units — C3), and
predict by the responsibility-weighted mixture. Units are never given; M is a hyper-parameter
fixed a-priori at M=K=6 AND also tested at M=12 (over-provisioned) to check it is not
K-dependent tuning. No gradient descent is used for the units themselves (C2/C4: structure is
not something gradient finds — here it is found by competition + online aggregation).
ARMS: unit-discovery (M=6, M=12) vs the U-1 baselines (oracle-group as the CEILING, no-group,
instance, ngram), 3 seeds, identical data.
BARS: U-2 PASSES iff unit-discovery beats no-group AND instance by >=0.30 nats in 3/3 seeds at
BOTH M, AND reaches within 0.15 nats of the oracle-group ceiling. Partial (beats baselines but
far from ceiling) is recorded as partial. Failure to beat no-group = the mechanism does not
discover the units and the family closes.

## 2026-08-08 — U-2 VERDICT: FAIL — online competitive unit discovery recovers ~12% of the available headroom

Arena U-1 certified 0.80 nats of headroom between no-group and oracle-group. The registered
mechanism (M slots, softmax competition over context signatures, online soft aggregation of
per-slot bigram statistics, no gradient) delivers:
  M=6 : beats no-group by 0.113 / 0.076 / 0.067 nats; gap to ORACLE 0.685 / 0.742 / 0.748
  M=12: beats no-group by 0.169 / 0.108 / 0.094 nats; gap to ORACLE 0.629 / 0.710 / 0.721
**Registered bar: beat no-group AND instance by >=0.30 AND come within 0.15 of oracle. FAILED
on both clauses at both M.** It beats the instance baseline comfortably (0.82-0.97 nats) — but
so does the trivial no-group aggregate, so that margin carries no information about unit
discovery. Against the baseline that actually matters (no-group), the mechanism recovers only
0.07-0.17 of the 0.80 nats on the table: **~12-21% of the available headroom, i.e. it is
finding at best a faint shadow of the latent units.**
DIAGNOSIS (recorded, not rescued): the competition operates on a bag-of-tokens context signature,
but in this arena the latent classes differ ONLY in transition structure over a SHARED
vocabulary — the classes are近 indistinguishable in token-frequency space, which is exactly what
the arena was designed to enforce. The mechanism therefore competes over the wrong feature of the
context. That is a real failure of the mechanism, not of the arena: the arena's own oracle proves
0.80 nats are recoverable by something that knows the units.
STATUS: family U's first mechanism bet FAILS at its first honest test, in the FIRST arena this
project ever certified as having headroom. The arena stands (it is now a validated testbed with
a known ceiling and four baselines); the mechanism does not. Per protocol no rescue iteration is
permitted without a new pre-registration naming the confound — which here would be: the
competition must run over TRANSITION statistics, not token-occurrence statistics.

## 2026-08-08 — U-3 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): compete on PREDICTIVE LIKELIHOOD, not on feature similarity

U-2's named confound: the slots competed on a bag-of-tokens context signature, while the arena's
latent classes differ ONLY in transition structure. The fix that the confound names: slots must
compete on HOW WELL THEY PREDICTED THE OBSERVED TRANSITIONS — a likelihood, not a similarity.
MECHANISM (U-3): M slots, each holding transition statistics p_m(next|cur). Responsibility over
slots is a temporally-smoothed posterior:
    r_t ∝ (r_{t-1}^gamma) * prod_{i in window} p_m(x_{i+1} | x_i)      (online, no gradient)
i.e. Bayesian filtering over which unit is currently generating the stream, with a stickiness
exponent gamma that encodes the arena's slow class-switching. Slots are updated by
responsibility-weighted counts, exactly as in U-2 (the aggregation half is unchanged, so the
comparison isolates the competition signal).
ARMS: U-3 at M=6 and M=12, against the same fixed baselines (oracle-group ceiling, no-group,
instance, ngram) and against U-2 (the failed similarity-based competition), 3 seeds, same data.
BARS (registered): U-3 PASSES iff it beats no-group by >=0.30 nats in 3/3 seeds at BOTH M AND
closes to within 0.15 nats of the oracle ceiling. PARTIAL = beats no-group by >=0.30 but stays
>0.15 from oracle (report the fraction of headroom recovered). FAIL = <0.30 over no-group, in
which case the "compete on likelihood" fix is refuted and family U's competition half is closed.
STANDING LIMIT (unchanged, restated): this arena is synthetic and built to contain latent units;
U-4 on natural text remains MANDATORY and gating before any claim of any kind.

## 2026-08-08 — U-3 VERDICT (prereg 3793fd6): PARTIAL. The named fix works, and does not suffice.

Changing ONLY the competition signal — feature similarity (U-2) -> sticky predictive likelihood
(U-3), with the aggregation half byte-identical as registered — roughly tripled the recovered
headroom:
                        vs no-group (3 seeds)     gap to ORACLE        headroom recovered
  U-2 sim  M=6      0.113 0.076 0.067        0.685 0.742 0.748        12% 9% 8%
  U-2 sim  M=12     0.169 0.108 0.094        0.629 0.710 0.721        21% 13% 12%
  U-3 lik  M=6      0.375 0.257 0.316        0.423 0.561 0.498        47% 31% 39%
  U-3 lik  M=12     0.457 0.422 0.423        0.340 0.396 0.392        57% 52% 52%
Registered bar was: >=0.30 over no-group in 3/3 at BOTH M, AND within 0.15 of oracle. Held
against it honestly: M=6 MISSES the first half (seed1 = 0.257 < 0.30); M=12 MEETS the first half
3/3 but BOTH M miss the second half by a wide margin (0.34-0.40 vs 0.15 bar). Verdict PARTIAL,
carried entirely by M=12. Roughly half of the 0.80-nat unit headroom is still unrecovered.
WHAT THIS DOES ESTABLISH: U-2's diagnosis was correct and was the binding constraint. The unit
discovery problem in this arena is a competition-signal problem, and the right signal is a
predictive likelihood, not a representational similarity. That is a mechanism result, and it was
obtained by fixing the confound the previous verdict named, with no other change.
WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH: that competitive aggregation can reach the oracle. Half the headroom
is unexplained and the mechanism is untested on natural data.

## 2026-08-08 — U-4 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): where does the residual 0.35-0.40 nats live?

U-3 leaves ~48% of the headroom on the table. Two failure sites are confounded in that number:
TRAIN-time clustering (slots end up impure) and TEST-time inference (the filtered posterior does
not identify the active unit fast enough after a switch). A 2x2 decomposition separates them by
swapping in the TRUE latent class on one side at a time, aggregation code otherwise unchanged:
   A (filt-train, filt-test) = U-3 itself      B (true-train, filt-test)
   C (filt-train, true-test)                   D (true-train, true-test) = sanity, must ~= oracle
REGISTERED READING, fixed now: if B closes to within 0.15 of oracle and C does not, the residual
is TRAIN-time clustering. If C closes and B does not, it is TEST-time inference. If both close
(each alone nearly sufficient), the two errors compound and neither alone is the bottleneck. If
NEITHER closes, the aggregation half itself is lossy and the competition story is not the whole
story. D failing to land within 0.05 of the U-1 oracle invalidates the decomposition and I report
that instead of the split.
PRE-REGISTERED FIX, committed BEFORE seeing the decomposition so it cannot be chosen to fit it:
E = two-pass EM (a second sweep re-estimating slot statistics under the converged slot params,
online filtering unchanged). EM is the standard remedy for single-pass online responsibility
estimation regardless of which cell dominates. E PASSES iff it beats U-3 at matched M by >=0.10
nats in 3/3 seeds AND lands within 0.15 of oracle; anything less is reported as its measured
value with no further iteration on this arena.
STANDING LIMIT (restated, unchanged since U-1): this arena is synthetic and was constructed to
contain latent units. U-5 on natural text remains MANDATORY and gating before any claim of any
kind leaves this family.

## 2026-08-08 — SELF-CAUGHT CONFOUND 5, in U-4's own diagnostic (arm C). Before any reading of U-4.

U-4 arm C ("filtered training, TRUE class supplied at test") returned NEGATIVE headroom:
0.961/1.115/1.047 nats WORSE than the oracle and worse than not grouping at all. A diagnostic
that hands the mechanism MORE information and makes it worse than chance is a broken diagnostic,
not a result. The bug: arm C sets r = one-hot(te_c[i]), i.e. it assumes slot index m corresponds
to latent class m. That identity holds only in the train_oracle arms, which assign by construction.
Under filtered training the slot indices are an arbitrary permutation of the classes at best, and
in general a soft many-to-many mixture. So arm C as written did not supply perfect test-time
identification; it pointed at an unrelated slot. The printed line "NEITHER closes -> the
aggregation half is itself lossy" was produced by that bug and is RETRACTED before it was used.
CORRECTION, registered before running: arm C' supplies the true class and then decodes it into
slot space with the best class-conditional mixture estimated ON TRAIN — R[k] = mean responsibility
over train positions with tr_c == k, and r_test = R[te_c[i]]. This is the honest "test-time
identification is perfect" cell: no filtering lag, no assumed index alignment.
Bars for C' unchanged from prereg 72917f5 (closes iff within 0.15 of oracle, 3/3 seeds), and the
same four-way reading of B/C' stands as registered. Arm B is unaffected by this bug (it assigns
by construction on both sides) and its numbers carry over unchanged.

  B  TRUE-train / filt-test               0.259 0.258 0.243      68% 68% 70%
  C' filt-train / TRUE-test  M=6          0.341 0.502 0.426      57% 39% 48%
  C' filt-train / TRUE-test  M=12         0.290 0.384 0.399      64% 53% 51%

PRE-REGISTRATION MISS, recorded as such: my registered branch labels did not anticipate this cell.

The branch fired and its LABEL is wrong. I report the measured decomposition above and mark the

Diagnosis (not an excuse): the second sweep re-estimates responsibilities under the converged
parameters on the SAME stream, so it reinforces whatever partition pass one found; with a sticky

## 2026-08-10 — RE-AIM, and W-1 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): natural-data audit of TEST-TIME ADAPTATION

STATED PLAINLY: after ~200 pre-registered experiments across 30+ families, this project has
produced no epoch-making algorithm. It has produced two defensible negative/diagnostic papers and
one methodological contribution. I am not adding rescue rounds to family U; its ceiling is visible
and the adjacent live ground (gradient-learned representations with competitive routing) is already
occupied by MoE and sparse attention, so even a positive result there would be a rediscovery.
THE DRIFT, recorded: the founding motivation of this program was sample efficiency -- a child
learns to drive in thirty minutes, a machine needs a corpus. The work drifted into architectural
mechanism ("why does a linear associative memory lose to softmax"), which is a clean line but is
NOT that bet. The founding bet has never once been tested at matched compute against an incumbent.
W-1 re-aims at it, and follows the rule U-5 bought us: certify headroom on NATURAL data first.
QUESTION (audit only, no mechanism proposed): on natural text, how much is left on the table by a
model that does not adapt at test time -- above and beyond what the ALREADY-KNOWN adaptation
methods extract?
ARMS: (1) STATIC: dev-smoothed bigram/trigram, frozen at test. (2) CACHE / DYNAMIC EVALUATION --
THE BINDING BASELINE: the same model interpolated with a unigram+bigram cache over the test
prefix, interpolation weights dev-selected. This is Grave et al.'s neural cache and Krause's
dynamic evaluation in count form; it is the trigram of this arena and the reason audits 1-3 and
U-5 died. (3) ORACLE-ADAPT (ceiling): a model that has already been fit on the entire test
document, i.e. an upper bound on what ANY test-time adaptation scheme could possibly extract.
DATA: WikiText-103 (real article structure and burstiness) and OpenWebText documents, GPT-2 BPE,
three disjoint splits, documents delimited by EOT. Report per-document, not just aggregate.
BARS: the arena QUALIFIES iff ORACLE-ADAPT beats the CACHE baseline by >=0.30 nats in 3/3 splits.
It FAILS if the cache is already within 0.10 nats of the oracle -- which would mean test-time
adaptation on natural text is a solved problem and the founding bet is closed too. Any outcome in
between is reported as the measured headroom with no mechanism claim attached.
NO MECHANISM IS PROPOSED HERE. If and only if this arena qualifies do I get to bet on one, and
that bet needs its own pre-registration naming its baseline in advance.

## 2026-08-10 — W-2 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): neural TTA-headroom audit on TRUE documents

Registered as the follow-up audit W-1 named as legitimate, fixing W-1's recorded deviations

limit (4) count-family-only. This is still an ARENA AUDIT. NO mechanism is proposed; a mechanism
bet is permitted only if this arena qualifies, and would need its own pre-registration.

QUESTION (unchanged from W-1, now at neural scale on real documents): how much does a model that
does not adapt at test time leave on the table, above what the ALREADY-KNOWN test-time-adaptation
methods extract?

DATA: WikiText-103 raw, downloaded via hf-mirror (HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com, no proxy),
tokenized with GPT-2 BPE locally. TRUE documents = articles (heading-delimited). Before any
training, hold out 120 articles of >=2,000 tokens each from the TRAIN shard: 30 = DEV (all
hyperparameter selection), 90 = EVAL as 3 disjoint sets of 30 (the split analogue of W-1).
The static model never sees any held-out article. FALLBACK, fixed now: if the WT103 download is
infeasible from the box, the fallback is OWT documents ONLY IF the existing bin contains EOT
(50256) delimiters; if it does not, W-2 is recorded as BLOCKED — no silent substitution of
fixed-size windows (that was W-1 deviation (3b), not to be repeated).

ARMS (all sharing one static model):
 (1) STATIC: one small causal transformer (~4 layers, d_model 256, 8 heads, ctx 256; GPT-2 BPE
     vocab truncated to top-8k on TRAIN + UNK), trained on the WT103 train shard minus holdouts,
     single GPU, fixed budget <=6h wall; the exact config is frozen in w2.py BEFORE launch and
     not revisited. Frozen at test.
 (2) KNOWN-ADAPTATION baseline — THE BINDING BASELINE, named in advance: the BEST per split of
     (a) neural cache (Grave et al. 2017: pointer distribution over test-prefix hidden states;
     interpolation weight and temperature dev-selected on a fixed grid) and (b) dynamic
     evaluation (Krause et al. 2018: SGD updates on the test prefix in fixed-size chunks;
     lr and decay dev-selected on a fixed grid). Taking the max of the two known methods makes
     the baseline as strong as the literature provides; grids are frozen in w2.py before running.
 (3) ORACLE-ADAPT (strict, no target leakage): chunk-level leave-one-out. Each eval article is
     split into 4 contiguous chunks; for chunk c, fine-tune a copy of STATIC on the article's
     OTHER 3 chunks (steps/lr dev-selected to MAXIMIZE the oracle on DEV — being generous to a
     ceiling arm is registered as intended), then score chunk c causally with its preceding
     article context. Target tokens never appear in the fine-tuning data.

BARS (registered now, same thresholds as W-1 for comparability): the arena QUALIFIES iff
ORACLE-ADAPT beats the binding baseline by >=0.30 nats/token (mean over articles) in 3/3 eval
sets. It FAILS iff the margin is <=0.10 in 3/3. Anything between is reported as the measured
headroom, no mechanism claim attached. Per-article distributions are reported, not only means.

ASYMMETRY OF THE ORACLE, registered before running so the reading cannot be chosen post hoc:
W-1's count-LOO oracle was a true within-family upper bound, so its FAIL was sound. W-2's
chunk-LOO fine-tune oracle is an ACHIEVABLE-adaptation reference — a LOWER bound on the true
adaptation ceiling. Therefore: QUALIFY is sound evidence of reachable headroom (a concrete
scheme exists above the known methods); FAIL closes only what this oracle reaches, NOT test-time
adaptation per se, and will be scoped exactly that way.

COMPUTE CAP (registered): everything on ONE idle GPU (box is shared; verify idle first); static
train <=6h; ~360 short fine-tunes for the oracle arm; total <=24h wall. If the cap is hit the
run stops and the partial state is recorded as such.

STAGES (one bounded tick each): (0) download + tokenize WT103, carve holdouts, verify article
lengths; (1) w2.py static train launch (nohup); (2) dev-grid selection for cache/dyneval/oracle;
(3) eval sweep, 3 sets; (4) verdict against the bars verbatim, ledger, commit.

## 2026-08-10 — B1-R1 PRE-REGISTRATION (before any code): does the Bet-1 positive REPLICATE on a
## second PROPER class-incremental benchmark? (Seq-Tiny-ImageNet)

WHY THIS IS PERMITTED UNDER THE PROTOCOL. This is a REPLICATION of an ESTABLISHED positive on a new
benchmark, not a rescue iteration of a refuted mechanism. The protocol forbids the second. The
distinction is load-bearing and I state it before running: nothing here retunes a gate constant,
searches a learning rate, or re-opens a closed verdict. If the mechanism fails to transfer, that is
the finding and it goes in the abstract.
WHY IT IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE RUN AVAILABLE. The paper's load-bearing claim (+0.8..+1.5 pt over
matched DER++, positive on 17/20 seeds across a 10x buffer range it was not selected on) rests on
exactly ONE proper class-incremental benchmark, Split-CIFAR-100. The abstract already concedes
benchmark-dependence, and the benchmark that produced that concession is FashionMNIST -- a
SATURATED SMOKE benchmark, not a real CIL arena. So the honest current state is: one real benchmark,
one smoke benchmark. A reviewer will ask for the second real one. This is that run.

ARENA: Seq-Tiny-ImageNet, 10 tasks x 20 classes, 64x64. Reduced ResNet-18 (nf=20), the same backbone
FAMILY as the banked CIFAR-100 apparatus. Augmentation identical (4-pad random crop + hflip).
EVERY HYPERPARAMETER COPIED VERBATIM from the banked CIFAR-100 config, no exceptions and no search:
n_tasks 10, epochs 10, bs 32, lr 0.03, replay 1, alpha 0.5, aug 1.
ARMS (all share one code path; gates-off arm IS DER++ exactly):
  primary   derpp, ngcls_v3 (prio replay CONTENT + surprise plasticity, no write gate)
            x buffer {200, 2000} x seeds 0-4  = 20 runs
  secondary ngcls_p (plasticity gate alone), ngcls_w (write gate alone)
            x buffer {200} x seeds 0-4        = 10 runs
REGISTERED BUDGET: 30 runs total. No arm is added later.

BARS, fixed now:
  REPLICATES iff at BOTH buffer sizes: (ngcls_v3 - derpp) is positive in >=4/5 paired seeds AND the
    mean delta is >= +0.5 pt average accuracy.
  PARTIAL iff that holds at one buffer and not the other.
  FAILS iff it holds at neither.
  The mean bar is +0.5 pt, DELIBERATELY LOWER than the CIFAR-100 pass rule's +1.0 pt, and I record
  the reason in advance so it cannot be re-motivated later: Tiny-ImageNet absolute accuracy in this
  regime is roughly half of CIFAR-100's, so one accuracy point is a larger RELATIVE effect. I would
  rather commit to a bar I can be held to than pick one after seeing the numbers. A measured delta
  between 0 and +0.5 will be reported as a numeric near-miss, not spun as support.
REGISTERED CONSEQUENCE OF FAIL: the paper's claim is NARROWED IN THE ABSTRACT to Split-CIFAR-100
  specifically. No third benchmark is hunted, no gate constant is retuned, no arm is added. The
  bounded-positive framing becomes a single-benchmark framing and says so.
REGISTERED FALSIFIABLE PREDICTIONS (these are predictions, not extra chances to find an effect):
  P1 ngcls_w <= derpp. The write gate was harmful on CIFAR-100 (starves buffer diversity). If it is
     POSITIVE here, the "write gate is harmful" claim is itself benchmark-specific and the paper
     must soften it.
  P2 ngcls_v3 >= ngcls_p. The gates should compose, as they did on CIFAR-100. If v3 < p, the honest
     method reverts to the single best gate -- exactly the rule applied at b500.
VOID CONDITION (apparatus honesty, registered before running): if derpp average accuracy at
  buffer 2000 is < 8%, this arena is near-floor and cannot discriminate. The run is then VOID and
  reported as an apparatus failure, NOT as a verdict about the mechanism. A void does not count as
  a FAIL and does not trigger the narrowing clause.
SCOPE STATED NOW: same backbone family, same augmentation, same optimiser. This tests BENCHMARK
  transfer only. It says nothing about architecture transfer, and I will not claim otherwise.

## 2026-08-10 — B1-R1 APPARATUS BUG, caught before any B1-R1 result existed

augment() hardcoded the crop side at 32: after reflect-pad 4 it took x[:, :, i:i+32, j:j+32]. On the
64x64 Tiny-ImageNet arena that silently crops TRAIN batches down to 32x32 while EVAL batches stay
64x64 — a train/test resolution mismatch that would have produced a meaningless FAIL and, worse, a
plausible-looking one (accuracy would simply have been bad). Found while reading the apparatus for
the new arena, before a single B1-R1 run was launched.
FIX: the crop side now follows the input (side = x.size(-1)). For the banked CIFAR arenas side == 32,
so the operation is BIT-IDENTICAL there and no CIFAR-100/CIFAR-10/FashionMNIST result is affected or
needs re-running. Stated explicitly because this edit touches code shared with closed series.
DATA: data/tinyimagenet.npz built from the HF mirror (zh-plus/tiny-imagenet) by build_tin.py —
100,000 train / 10,000 val, 200 classes present in both, uint8 HWC, same layout as the CIFAR npz.
Backbone needs no change: ReducedResNet18 ends in AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1), so 64x64 flows through the
nf=20 stack unmodified. "Same backbone family" is therefore literal, not approximate.

## 2026-08-10 — TT-12 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): adversarial audit of TT-1's headline against
## the MODERN incumbents on MQAR (delta rule, gated linear attention)

WHY THIS IS NOT A FORBIDDEN RE-RUN, stated before anything is measured. TT-1..TT-11 are closed and
must not be re-run to hunt a better answer. This is the opposite operation: TT-1's headline — the
single largest effect anywhere in this project (criterion in 1000/1200/1400 steps vs 15,800 for a
tuned transformer, 3/3 seeds, half the non-embedding params) — was measured against a VANILLA
TRANSFORMER and a vanilla linear attention. It was never measured against the methods this
literature actually treats as incumbents. REGISTERED ASYMMETRY: there is NO outcome of TT-12 that
adds a new positive claim to the paper. The best case is that an existing claim survives contact
with real opponents; the worst case is that our opening claim is deleted. An audit that can only
cost us is not a rescue.
I also record the prior expectation now, so a bad result cannot be reframed later as a surprise:
the delta-rule line of work exists BECAUSE vanilla linear attention fails associative recall. A
correctly implemented DeltaNet is expected to be a strong opponent on MQAR, and I expect our margin
to shrink substantially, most likely in the hard setting.

ARENA: MQAR exactly as in TT-1 — vocab 8192; easy (8 pairs, 4 queries, seq 64) and hard (32 pairs,
8 queries, seq 256). Metric: steps to >=90% held-out query accuracy. 3 seeds. Harness tt1c.py/
tt1k.py, now committed (9fe857d).
ARMS: ours = FWBCausal, run UNTUNED exactly as in TT-1 (lr 1e-3, no warmup, TT-1 step budget).
Incumbents = TF, LinAtt (both already in the harness), plus NEW: delta-rule linear attention
(DeltaNet-style) and gated linear attention (GLA-style). Every incumbent receives the same
advantages TT-1 gave the transformer and ours receives none: linear warmup, an LR sweep over
{3e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3}, and 3x our step budget. Non-embedding parameters matched to ours, printed per arm.

*** IMPLEMENTATION VALIDITY GATE — a win over a broken baseline is worth nothing. ***
Earlier today I criticised an external submission whose load-bearing baseline reported identical
mean AND identical standard deviation across a 4x parameter and 3x step change — the signature of a
baseline that was not training. I will not bank the same defect. Before ANY comparison counts:
  (a) delta MUST beat LinAtt on MQAR. That is the published qualitative result this family rests on.
      If my delta does not beat LinAtt, MY IMPLEMENTATION IS PRESUMED BROKEN and no claim is made
      against it — the arm is reported as an implementation failure of mine, not as a defeated rival.
  (b) any arm whose accuracy stays at chance across all three learning rates is reported as NOT
      TRAINING and excluded, with that stated in the verdict. It never counts as a beaten baseline.
  (c) any arm more than 15% below ours in non-embedding parameters is re-sized before it counts.

BARS, fixed now:
  HOLDS    iff ours reaches criterion in <= 1/3 the steps of the BEST valid incumbent (minimum over
           arms and learning rates), in 3/3 seeds, in BOTH settings, at no more non-embedding
           parameters. 3x is a deliberately conservative threshold for "large" given TT-1 claimed
           11-16x; I would rather commit to a bar I can be held to.
  WEAKENED iff ours is still fastest but by less than 3x in either setting.
  REFUTED  iff any valid incumbent matches or beats ours in either setting.
REGISTERED CONSEQUENCE of WEAKENED or REFUTED: the 11-16x number comes OUT of the TT paper's
  abstract and is replaced by the measured comparison against the modern incumbents. The paper's

## 2026-08-10 — TT-12 REGISTERED DEVIATION (before the grid runs): incumbent budget for the two
## SEQUENTIAL arms cut from 60,000 to 12,000 steps

Measured cost from the validity-gate smoke: delta runs at ~48 ms/step on the easy setting (T=20) and
will be roughly 3.5x that on hard (T=72), because the delta rule is written in its literal
sequential form and T is looped in Python. At the registered 3x budget of 60,000 steps this is
25+ GPU-hours for delta and GLA alone.
DEVIATION: delta and gla are capped at 12,000 steps. tf, linatt and gru keep the full 60,000
(they are parallel and cheap: linatt measured 15 ms/step).
WHY THIS COSTS NOTHING IN DECISION POWER, and why it CANNOT manufacture a win — the asymmetry is
the whole justification and I state it before running: the registered bar asks whether ours reaches
criterion in <= 1/3 the steps of the best incumbent. Ours reached criterion at 1000/1200/1400 steps
in TT-1, so the decision point is ~3,600 steps. A 12,000-step cap sits 3.3x ABOVE that point, so
any incumbent capable of beating the bar is fully observed. For runs that exceed the cap, censoring
reports ">12,000" where the truth is a larger number — i.e. censoring UNDERSTATES our advantage and
can only weaken our claim. There is no mechanism by which a lower cap invents an advantage.
REPORTING RULE: censored runs are reported as censored at their cap, never as a finite number and
never dropped. If delta or gla reaches criterion under the cap, the observed value is used.
GATE-(a) NOTE, recorded now so it is not read as a post-hoc excuse: at the 6,000-step smoke neither
delta (acc 0.133) nor linatt (acc 0.111) reached criterion, so gate (a) is UNDECIDED at that budget,
not passed. It will be evaluated on the grid at the caps above. If delta still fails to separate
from linatt there, my delta implementation is presumed broken per the gate and NO claim is made
against it -- the arm is reported as my implementation failure.

## 2026-08-11 — TT-13 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): the TT-12 audit, with an opponent that can
## actually fight and a gate statistic that is valid

TT-12 failed for two reasons that are both MINE: my DeltaNet had one layer against the baselines'
two, no head structure and no short convolution; and my gate compared mean steps-to-criterion across
arms with 5x different censoring caps, which is an invalid statistic and produced a false PASS.
TT-13 fixes the instrument. Under the protocol this is permitted -- repairing a broken measuring
device is not the same act as rescuing a refuted mechanism -- and the same registered asymmetry as
TT-12 applies verbatim: NO OUTCOME OF TT-13 CAN ADD A POSITIVE CLAIM. It can only confirm a narrower
version of an existing claim, or delete it.

FIXES TO THE OPPONENTS (delta and gla both):
  - TWO layers, depth-matched to tf and linatt.
  - Multi-head: 4 heads over the state, the standard construction in this family.
  - Short depthwise causal convolution (kernel 4) on q/k/v. This is standard in published DeltaNet
    and GLA implementations and is known to matter for recall; leaving it out was a real handicap.
  - beta in (0,2) via 2*sigmoid for the delta rule, permitting over-correction as published, rather
    than the (0,1) sigmoid I used.
  - Output normalisation on the read before the output projection.
  Non-embedding parameters are re-matched to ours (234,113) and printed; per registered gate (c)
  any arm more than 15% below ours is re-sized before it counts.
UNIFORM BUDGET: every arm, ours included, gets the SAME cap of 20,000 steps. No arm is censored at a
  different point than another, which removes the defect that produced TT-12's false gate PASS.
  Ours reached criterion at 1000-1400 steps on easy, so 20,000 sits 5.5x above the 3,600-step
  decision point. Baselines keep their warmup and their 3-learning-rate sweep; ours stays untuned.
SETTING: EASY ONLY (8 pairs, 4 queries). Registered reason, stated in advance rather than discovered
  later: the delta rule is written in its literal sequential form, and at T=72 a two-layer version
  costs more wall-clock than the decision is worth. HARD IS DEFERRED, not quietly dropped, and no
  claim about the hard setting will be made from TT-13.

GATE (a), RESTATED WITH A VALID STATISTIC: delta must beat linatt on at least one of
  (i) reaching criterion on >= 2/3 seeds when linatt does, or (ii) best held-out accuracy.
  Evaluated on the accuracy trajectory and on criterion hits, NEVER on mean steps under censoring.
  If delta still cannot beat a vanilla linear attention with depth, heads and a short conv, then the
  failure is mine twice over, I say so, and TT-13 reports NO comparison against the modern
  incumbents -- the question stays open and the paper stays narrow.
BARS (unchanged in substance from TT-12): HOLDS iff ours reaches criterion in <= 1/3 the steps of the
  best VALID incumbent in 3/3 seeds at no more non-embedding parameters; WEAKENED iff ours is fastest
  by less than 3x; REFUTED iff any valid incumbent matches or beats ours.
REGISTERED CONSEQUENCE, unchanged: anything other than HOLDS removes the 11-16x figure from the TT
  paper's abstract in favour of the measured comparison.

## 2026-08-11 — FAMILY D OPENED. D-1 ARENA AUDIT PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): is there headroom
## in the WRITE RULE, above what the delta rule already extracts?

WHERE THIS CAME FROM, so it is not mistaken for a fresh guess. TT-13 showed that what turned my
DeltaNet from "never reaches criterion" into "ties us on a seed" is the ERROR-CORRECTING WRITE:
subtract what the state already associates with k before writing v. Every TT experiment before it
interrogated the READ (competitive softmax vs linear). Independently, B1-R1's P1 was REFUTED: the
surprise-gated WRITE, which was harmful on CIFAR-100, is the best single arm at b200 on
Tiny-ImageNet. Two unrelated lines of this project now point at the write rule rather than the read,
and the two literatures they come from do not cite each other.
THIS ENTRY PROPOSES NO MECHANISM. Per the standing protocol established by Family U, an arena audit
comes first and may close the family immediately.

ARENA: MQAR with REBINDING and DISTRACTORS -- the two things that make a write policy matter and
that plain MQAR lacks. Sequence contains N key-value pairs of which (i) R keys appear twice with
different values, only the LAST binding correct, and (ii) D pairs are never queried. Vocabulary,
criterion (>=90% held-out query accuracy) and the harness are TT-1's, unchanged.
ARMS (audit only, no mechanism):
  ORACLE-WRITE: an additive binder that writes ONLY pairs that will be queried, and for a rebound
    key only its final value. This is the ceiling any write policy could reach.
  ALWAYS-WRITE: the same binder writing everything (our fwbc's rule).
  DELTA: the error-correcting write, i.e. the best write rule currently known to this literature.
BAR, fixed now: the arena QUALIFIES iff ORACLE-WRITE reaches criterion in <= 1/3 the steps of BOTH
  other arms, in 3/3 seeds. It FAILS if ORACLE-WRITE does not beat DELTA by that margin -- which
  would mean the delta rule already sits near the write-policy ceiling and there is NO HEADROOM for
  a better write rule. On FAIL the family closes here with no mechanism bet, and I report it.
  Uniform step cap for every arm; no arm censored at a different point than another.
STATED IN ADVANCE so a null cannot be reframed later: it is entirely possible that the delta rule is
  already near-optimal as a write policy, in which case this audit kills Family D in one experiment.
  That is the outcome the audit is FOR. I am not proposing a mechanism until an arena earns one.
SCOPE: synthetic. Per the lesson registered at U-5 (synthetic certification does not transfer), a
  natural-data gate is MANDATORY before any Family D claim of any kind leaves this ledger.

## 2026-08-11 — D-1 VERDICT (prereg 85d3a2e): ARENA FAILS. And the failure is my arena's, named.

  oracle-write  400 / 600 / 400      always-write  400 / 1000 / 400      delta  600 / 400 / 400
  ratio always/oracle 1.00 / 1.67 / 1.00      delta/oracle 1.50 / 0.67 / 1.00
Bar was oracle <= 1/3 of BOTH in 3/3 seeds. Measured ratios are about 1.0, and delta actually BEATS
the oracle on seed 1. Knowing exactly which pairs will be queried, and writing only those, buys
nothing at all. **ARENA FAILS.**

DIAGNOSIS, and it is a design fault of mine rather than a fact about write rules: the arena has NO
CAPACITY PRESSURE. Eleven associations are written into a 128x128 state -- roughly 16,000 numbers
for 11 bindings. Interference is negligible at that ratio, so no write policy CAN matter, and the
audit could not have discriminated one no matter what it measured. I should have seen this before
running: a write rule is a policy for deciding what to keep when you cannot keep everything, and I
built an arena where everything fits.
Per the registration, Family D closes here UNLESS a new audit names the confound. It is named above,
so D-2 follows -- and I record explicitly that this is the U-2 -> U-3 pattern (fix the confound the
previous verdict named, in a fresh pre-registration), not an unregistered rescue.

## 2026-08-11 — D-2 VERDICT (prereg 813f3df): ARENA QUALIFIES — but the oracle is NON-CAUSAL, and
## that caveat is load-bearing, not decorative.

  oracle-write   600 / 800 / 800    criterion 3/3   best acc 0.999
  delta          censored x3        criterion 0/3   best acc 0.800
  always-write   censored x3        criterion 0/3   best acc 0.658
  ratio vs oracle: always 33.3/25/25,  delta 33.3/25/25.   Bar was >=3x vs BOTH in 3/3. QUALIFIES.
Not VOID: the oracle reaches criterion on 3/3 seeds, so the arena is solvable and discriminating.
The contrast with D-1 is one variable: capacity pressure. At 11 associations into a rank-128 state a
write policy was worth nothing; at 80 associations into a rank-32 state it is worth >=25x. The delta
rule DOES help (0.800 vs 0.658 accuracy) and still never reaches criterion.

THE CAVEAT, stated before any mechanism is proposed, because without it the 25x is empty: THE ORACLE
USES FUTURE INFORMATION. It writes exactly the pairs that will be queried, which requires knowing the
queries before they arrive. No causal mechanism can do that. So what D-2 certifies is a
NON-REALIZABLE upper bound, and the honest reading is "a better-informed write policy has enormous
room" and NOT "a realizable write rule can capture 25x".
This is the same shape as the trap caught at W-1, where an oracle whose counts included the target
token showed ~0.9 nats of "headroom" and was rejected as a vacuous pass. It is not identical: this
oracle does not see the ANSWER, only which associations will be NEEDED -- it still has to store and
retrieve the right value. It is relevance information, not answer leakage. But it is still
information a causal learner does not have, and I record that the difference between "relevance" and
"answer" is a matter of degree, not a clean exemption.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE NEXT STEP: a mechanism bet may only claim the fraction of this headroom that a
CAUSAL policy recovers, and the arena as it stands cannot tell us whether that fraction is large or
zero. D-3 must therefore carry a realizable-baseline arm and a registered expectation, and the U-5
lesson still binds absolutely: a natural-data gate is MANDATORY before any Family D claim leaves this
ledger. On the project's own history the prior is not encouraging -- U-2 recovered 12-21% of a
certified headroom and U-3, after fixing the named confound, 52-57%, and the family then died on
natural text anyway.

## 2026-08-11 — SELF-CAUGHT ARENA CONFOUND 6, in D-2, found BEFORE any mechanism bet was registered

D-2's arena places its structure at FIXED positions: the distractors are the last n_distract slots of
the base block, and the re-bindings are appended after the base block reusing the first n_rebind keys.
A causal write policy could therefore learn "write slots [base..base+n_rebind) and skip slots
[base-n_distract..base)" from POSITION ALONE and capture the certified headroom without learning
anything about associations. That is the same defect I self-caught in TT-1, where our binder read keys
and values from fixed token positions while the baselines had to infer the structure; it cost that
result its 39.5x headline. I am not repeating it one family later.
The D-2 VERDICT ITSELF STANDS: the oracle arm consumes the write mask directly and never looks at
position, so the 25-33x measurement is unaffected. What is affected is the INTERPRETATION -- the
headroom might be reachable by positional pattern-matching, which would make it say nothing about
write rules. That interpretation was the entire motivation for a mechanism bet, so the bet waits.

## 2026-08-11 — D-2a PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): de-confound the arena, then test whether the
## headroom is merely positional

ARENA FIX: re-bindings and distractors are placed at UNIFORMLY RANDOM slot positions, independently
per example, so no fixed offset carries information. Which keys are re-bound and which pairs are
distractors is re-sampled per example. Everything else -- 64 pairs, dk 32, rebind 16, distract 16,
vocabulary, criterion, uniform 20,000-step cap, 3 seeds -- is unchanged from D-2.
ARMS: oracle-write and delta, re-run on the fixed arena, PLUS one new control:
  POSITIONAL: a write policy whose gate is a learned function of SLOT INDEX ONLY (a per-slot scalar,
  no access to the key or value content). On the D-2 arena this arm should be able to capture most of
  the headroom; on the de-confounded arena it should not.
BARS, fixed now:
  The headroom is CONTENT-BASED (and a mechanism bet is licensed) iff, on the de-confounded arena,
  oracle still beats delta by >= 3x in 3/3 seeds AND the POSITIONAL control does NOT reach criterion.
  The headroom is POSITIONAL (and Family D's audit is void, no mechanism bet, family closes) iff the
  POSITIONAL control reaches criterion in 3/3 seeds.
  Anything between is reported as the measured split with no mechanism bet attached.
STATED IN ADVANCE: if the positional control solves it, D-2's QUALIFIES was an artifact of my arena
and I will say so in exactly those words. That is a live possibility and it is the reason this runs
before any mechanism.

## 2026-08-12 — D-2a VERDICT (prereg b3359d7): CONTENT-BASED. The headroom survives de-confounding.
## And a harder caveat than D-2's, found while reading the result: part of it is INFORMATIONALLY
## unreachable, not merely hard.

  oracle      1000 /  800 /  800   criterion 3/3   best acc 0.998
  positional  censored x3          criterion 0/3   best acc 0.323
  delta       censored x3          criterion 0/3   best acc 0.510
  ratio vs oracle: delta 20/25/25, positional 20/25/25.
Registered reading: the position-only gate does NOT reach criterion, and the oracle still beats delta
by >=20x in 3/3 seeds. So the certified headroom is CONTENT-BASED and one mechanism bet is licensed.
CONFOUND 6 CONFIRMED QUANTITATIVELY: delta's best accuracy falls from 0.800 on the fixed-position
arena to 0.510 on the randomised one. Same mechanism, same overload; the only change is that slot
position no longer carries information. The confound I caught was not hypothetical and it was not
confined to some imagined mechanism arm -- it was inflating the strongest REAL opponent by 0.29
accuracy. Any comparison run on the D-2 arena is void for this reason and I am not reusing it.

THE HARDER CAVEAT. In this arena a distractor is statistically identical to a queried pair; the ONLY
thing that makes it a distractor is that it happens not to be queried later. Therefore NO CAUSAL
POLICY CAN IDENTIFY DISTRACTORS, even in principle. The oracle's advantage decomposes into
  (i) handling re-binding correctly -- causally reachable, and what the delta rule already attempts,
  (ii) not spending capacity on pairs that will never be queried -- causally UNREACHABLE here.
So "fraction of oracle headroom recovered" is the WRONG metric for a mechanism, and I am recording
that before proposing one, because using it would guarantee an unfair-looking failure and would also
let a weak mechanism claim credit for an impossible target. The right comparison is against DELTA,
the best causal write rule this literature has.

## 2026-08-12 — D-3 MECHANISM BET PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): capacity-aware error-correcting
## write, gated by novelty rather than by relevance

MECHANISM (one bet, no variants held in reserve): keep the delta rule's error-correcting write, and
scale its strength by a CAUSAL novelty estimate computed from the state itself --
    n_t = 1 - ||S_{t-1} k_t||  (how unbound this key currently is),  beta_t = 2*sigmoid(w . [h_t, n_t])
so the write is strong when a key is genuinely new or genuinely re-bound and weak when the state
already agrees, and the model can learn to spend a finite-rank state instead of overwriting it 80
times. This is the composition the two independent lines of this project pointed at: TT-13's
error-correcting write and B1-R1's surprise/novelty gating, from literatures that do not cite each
other. Nothing else changes: same arena (D-2a, randomised positions), same 20,000-step cap, same
3 seeds, same optimiser, no LR sweep for us.
BARS, fixed now and stated against DELTA, not against the oracle:
  PASSES iff the mechanism beats delta's best accuracy by >= 0.10 absolute in 3/3 seeds, OR reaches
    criterion in any seed where delta does not.
  PARTIAL iff it beats delta by >= 0.05 in 3/3 seeds.
  FAILS iff it is within 0.05 of delta, or worse. On FAIL, Family D closes: the write rule is not the
    lever, the D-2a headroom is dominated by the unreachable component, and I report exactly that.
REGISTERED PRIOR, so a null is not later reframed as a surprise: on this project's record, mechanisms
derived from a certified arena have recovered 12-21% (U-2) and then 52-57% (U-3) of their headroom,
and that family still died on natural text. I expect a small positive at best here.
STANDING GATE, unchanged and absolute: a natural-data gate is MANDATORY before any Family D claim
leaves this ledger, whatever D-3 returns.

Arena D-2a (de-confounded, randomised slot positions), identical cap, seeds, optimiser and parameter
count (111,363 vs delta's 111,201 non-embedding). Numbers from runs/d3/novelty.json and
runs/d2a/delta.json, none from memory.

  delta    (registered comparison)  acc 0.491 / 0.510 / 0.502    criterion 0/3
  novelty  (the mechanism)          acc 0.508 / 0.507 / 0.514    criterion 0/3
  per-seed delta:  +0.017 / -0.003 / +0.012      mean +0.009
Registered bar: PASS >= +0.10 in 3/3, PARTIAL >= +0.05 in 3/3, FAIL within 0.05 or worse. Measured is
an order of magnitude below the PARTIAL bar and one seed is NEGATIVE. **FAIL.**
Neither arm reaches criterion; the oracle reaches it in 800-1000 steps. Gating an error-correcting
write by a causal novelty estimate read off the state buys essentially nothing over the delta rule.

REGISTERED CONSEQUENCE, executed verbatim: FAMILY D CLOSES. The write rule is not the lever, and the
D-2a headroom is dominated by the component I identified in advance as causally unreachable -- in this
arena a distractor is statistically identical to a queried pair, so no causal policy can decline to
store it. The oracle's 20-25x is mostly the value of information a causal learner cannot have. I
registered that decomposition BEFORE running the mechanism precisely so this result could not be
re-narrated as a surprise, and it is not one.
WHAT SURVIVES FROM FAMILY D, and it is small but real and causal: capacity pressure is the switch.
At 11 associations into a rank-128 state (D-1) an oracle write policy is worth NOTHING; at 80 into
rank-32 (D-2a) it is worth >=20x. That is a fact about when write policies matter at all, it does not
depend on the non-realisable oracle, and it is reproducible. It also implies the delta-rule
literature's gains should shrink toward zero in the under-loaded regime -- a testable prediction I am
NOT testing here, and which would need its own pre-registration.
NO NATURAL-DATA GATE IS RUN. The standing gate applies to CLAIMS; the family produced none. Running a
natural-text experiment now would be work in search of a claim that does not exist.

## 2026-08-12 — D-4 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): test the falsifiable prediction Family D left
## behind, about an INCUMBENT method rather than one of ours

WHY THIS AND NOT A SEVENTH MECHANISM. Family D closed and its two-arena contrast produced one causal,
reproducible fact: capacity pressure is the switch for whether a write policy matters at all (worth
nothing at 11 associations into rank-128, >=20x at 80 into rank-32). That fact implies a PREDICTION
ABOUT DELTANET, a method this literature actually uses: the delta rule's advantage over a vanilla
linear attention should SHRINK TOWARD ZERO as capacity pressure falls, because its whole contribution
is deciding what to overwrite when you cannot keep everything. I wrote that prediction into the D-3
verdict and explicitly did NOT test it there. This entry tests it. It is a claim about someone else's
method, measured with an apparatus we have already de-confounded (D-2a), and it can be wrong.

ARENA: the de-confounded D-2a generator (random slot positions, re-binding, distractors), n_pairs 16,
n_query 4, n_rebind 4, n_distract 4 -- reduced from 64 so the sweep is affordable -- with the STATE
RANK swept: dk in {4, 8, 32, 128}. That spans ~5 associations per unit of rank down to ~0.16, i.e.
heavily overloaded to heavily under-loaded.
ARMS: delta (error-correcting write) and linatt-style additive write ("always"), identical in every
other respect, same parameter budget except for dk itself, 3 seeds, lr 1e-3, no sweep for either.
METRIC: held-out query accuracy at a FIXED budget of 4,000 steps (not steps-to-criterion, because
several cells will not reach criterion and censoring would obscure the trend the prediction is about).
PREDICTION, registered: gap(dk) = acc_delta(dk) - acc_always(dk) is positive and LARGE at dk=4, and
falls monotonically toward ~0 by dk=128.
BARS: CONFIRMED iff gap(dk=4) >= 3 x gap(dk=128) AND gap(dk=128) <= 0.05 absolute.
  PARTIAL iff the gap shrinks but either condition misses.
  REFUTED iff the gap does not shrink, or is larger at dk=128 than at dk=4.
  A REFUTED here would mean the D-1/D-2a contrast does not generalise the way I claimed it does, and
  I would have to withdraw the one thing Family D left standing. That is the point of running it.

## 2026-08-12 — D-4 VERDICT (prereg 5ac3efb): PREDICTION REFUTED. I withdraw the one claim Family D
## had left standing, in the form I stated it.

State-rank sweep on the de-confounded arena, 20 associations, 4,000-step fixed budget, 3 seeds.
  dk    assoc/rank    delta                 always                gap
   4        5.000     0.001 0.001 0.002     0.001 0.001 0.001     +0.000
   8        2.500     0.015 0.018 0.015     0.009 0.009 0.010     +0.007
  32        0.625     0.955 0.954 0.956     0.829 0.818 0.803     +0.138
 128        0.156     0.998 1.000 0.947     0.938 0.953 0.948     +0.035

I registered: the delta-vs-additive gap is LARGE at the most overloaded rank and falls MONOTONICALLY
toward zero as pressure drops. Measured: the gap is ~ZERO at the most overloaded rank, peaks at
dk=32, and is small again at dk=128. gap(dk=128) EXCEEDS gap(dk=4), which is the pre-registered
REFUTED condition stated verbatim. **REFUTED.**

WITHDRAWAL, executed rather than softened. Family D's closing entry claimed "capacity pressure is the
switch for whether a write policy matters", generalising from a two-point contrast (D-1 at rank 128,
D-2a at rank 32). That two-point contrast is REPRODUCED here -- 0.035 vs 0.138 -- but the claim I
built on it is false as stated, because it fails in the direction I never sampled. Two points cannot
distinguish a monotone trend from the left flank of a peak, and I generalised from two points. That is
the error, and it is a familiar one: it is the same shape as inferring a trend from D-1 and D-2a alone.
WHAT THE DATA ACTUALLY SHOWS, labelled as a POST-HOC OBSERVATION and NOT a conclusion: the
error-correcting write appears to have a SWEET SPOT. At extreme overload (5 associations per unit of
rank) both write rules sit at floor -- 0.001, i.e. nothing a rank-4 linear memory does can represent
20 associations, so deciding what to overwrite is worthless. At mild pressure (0.156) there is little
to decide and the gap shrinks. The gap is largest in between. This is a hypothesis generated AFTER
seeing the data; it has not been pre-registered or tested and I am not entitled to call it a finding.
Testing it would need its own pre-registration with the peak's location predicted IN ADVANCE, which is
the only version of that experiment worth running.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LEDGER: Family D now leaves behind NO standing claim, only a refuted prediction, a
post-hoc observation, and a de-confounded arena that other people could reuse. The honest tally for
this family is one arena-design fault (D-1), one self-caught positional confound (6), one mechanism
failure (D-3), and one self-refuted generalisation (D-4).

## 2026-08-12 — FAMILY E OPENED. E-1 ARENA AUDIT PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): is the TRAINING
## SIGNAL a lever this program has never pulled?

THE NEW COORDINATE, and why it is new rather than a variation. Every one of this program's ~200
pre-registered experiments varied an ARCHITECTURE or an UPDATE RULE at fixed supervision. Families U
and D are both spent, and both were mechanism families. Meanwhile C4 -- "networks learn patterns, not
algorithms", established by showing hand-executed skeletons solve instantly what learned ones never
acquire -- was only ever tested under OUTCOME supervision. If a network fails to acquire an algorithm
because the final loss carries almost no information about the intermediate computation, then C4 is a
statement about the SIGNAL, not about networks, and the whole program has been attributing to
architecture something that belongs to supervision. That is a falsifiable re-reading of our own
central negative, and it costs one cheap experiment to test.

ARENA: 2-HOP LOOKUP. Each sequence contains A->X pairs and X->Y pairs in random slot order; the query
is an A token and the answer is its Y, so the model must chain two retrievals through an unobserved
intermediate X. Vocabulary 8192, random slot positions (the de-confounding lesson from confound 6
applies from the start, not after), 3 seeds, uniform step cap, no learning-rate sweep for any arm.
ARMS (audit only, no mechanism proposed):
  OUTCOME:      loss on Y alone. This is what every experiment in this program has used.
  INTERMEDIATE: loss on Y PLUS loss on the true intermediate X at the query position, equal weight.
                The oracle SIGNAL. Identical architecture, identical parameters, identical data order.
  Both arms are the same model. NOTHING about the network changes between them -- only what it is
  told. That is the point: the comparison isolates supervision.
BAR, fixed now: the arena QUALIFIES iff INTERMEDIATE reaches criterion (>=90% held-out answer
accuracy on Y, measured identically for both arms) in <= 1/3 the steps of OUTCOME, in 3/3 seeds.
It FAILS otherwise, and on FAIL this coordinate closes immediately: the training signal is not the
lever, C4 stands as a statement about networks, and I report that.
MEASUREMENT HONESTY, fixed in advance: both arms are evaluated on Y accuracy ONLY. The intermediate
arm gets extra information during training and NO credit for it at evaluation. If I scored the
intermediate arm on X as well it would win by construction.
REGISTERED PRIOR: process supervision is not a new idea in the literature, so a positive here would
NOT be a novel mechanism -- it would be evidence that this program mis-attributed its own central
negative. That is the claim I would be entitled to, and it is smaller than an algorithm. I record it
now so a positive is not later inflated.
STANDING GATE: the U-5 lesson binds -- a natural-data gate is mandatory before any Family E claim
leaves this ledger.

## 2026-08-12 — E-1 VERDICT (prereg c01ba67): ARENA FAILS. And the same design fault as D-1, twice in
## a row, which is a fact about me and not about the coordinate.

  outcome       1200 / 1200 / 1000 steps   y-acc .999 / .998 / 1.000
  intermediate   800 /  800 /  600 steps   y-acc .971 / .989 / .958
  ratio outcome/intermediate: 1.50 / 1.50 / 1.67.   Bar was >= 3.0 in 3/3. **FAILS.**
Intermediate supervision IS faster -- consistently, on 3/3 seeds -- but by 1.5x, not the 3x I
registered as the threshold for "the signal is a lever here". Reported as measured.

DIAGNOSIS, and it is mine: I built the two-hop structure INTO THE ARCHITECTURE. The Chainer does two
chained reads through the same memory matrix, so the intermediate representation is very nearly forced
to exist whether or not anything supervises it. Outcome supervision then solves the task in 1,200
steps and there is almost no room left for a better signal to demonstrate value. The audit could not
have discriminated.
THE PATTERN THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THIS RESULT: this is the SECOND consecutive family whose first
arena I built too easy for the baseline. D-1 had 11 associations in a rank-128 state -- no capacity
pressure, so no write policy could matter. E-1 has the hop structure hard-wired -- no representational
pressure, so no signal could matter. In both cases I could have seen it before running, and in both
cases the diagnosis was only visible after. That is a regularity in how I design arenas: I instantiate
the mechanism's job into the apparatus and then measure whether the mechanism has a job. I am recording
it as a standing check to run BEFORE any future arena: "does the baseline architecture already contain
the thing I am about to test for?"
COORDINATE STATUS: E-1's registered FAIL clause closes this coordinate as tested. It does NOT settle
the underlying question, because the arena was incapable of settling it -- a distinction I am keeping
explicit rather than banking a clean negative I did not earn. A real test of the training-signal
coordinate needs an architecture WITHOUT the hop structure built in, and it needs its own

## 2026-08-12 — E-2 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): the training-signal audit, on a baseline that does
## NOT already contain the thing being tested

E-1 FAILED because I hard-wired the two-hop structure into the architecture (two chained reads through
one memory), so outcome supervision solved it in 1,200 steps and no signal could matter. The standing
check I wrote after it — "does the baseline architecture already contain the thing I am about to test
for?" — is applied here BEFORE running, which is the point of writing it down.
BASELINE CHANGE: a 2-layer transformer. Nothing in it composes two retrievals; to answer a 2-hop query
it must LEARN to chain one attention lookup into another. That is precisely the algorithm C4 says
networks do not acquire, and it is not built in. Check passes.

ARENA: the E-1 generator unchanged (A->X and X->Y pairs at uniformly random slot positions, query is an
A, answer is its Y, intermediate X never shown at query time), vocab 8192, 3 seeds, uniform 20,000-step
cap, lr 1e-3 for both arms, no sweep.
ARMS, same network, differing ONLY in what they are told:
  OUTCOME       loss on Y alone.
  INTERMEDIATE  loss on Y plus loss on the true X at the query position, equal weight.
Both are evaluated on Y accuracy ONLY. The intermediate arm gets extra information in training and no
credit for it at evaluation.
BAR, fixed now: the arena QUALIFIES iff INTERMEDIATE reaches criterion (>=90% Y accuracy) in <= 1/3 the
steps of OUTCOME in 3/3 seeds. FAILS otherwise.
ADDITIONAL REGISTERED OUTCOME, because this baseline can plausibly fail outright: if OUTCOME never
reaches criterion within the cap while INTERMEDIATE does in 3/3 seeds, that is the STRONGEST form of
QUALIFIES and I will report it as "outcome supervision cannot acquire the algorithm at this budget;
intermediate supervision can, in the same network". If NEITHER reaches criterion, the arena is VOID
(too hard to discriminate) and I report an apparatus failure, not a claim.
CEILING ON THE CLAIM, registered in advance: process/intermediate supervision is NOT new in the
literature. A positive here does not give me a new algorithm. What it would give is evidence that this
program's central negative (C4: networks learn patterns, not algorithms) was partly an artifact of only
ever using outcome supervision — i.e. that we mis-attributed to architecture something belonging to
the signal. That is the entitlement, and it is smaller than an algorithm. Any further step needs the
mandatory natural-data gate per U-5.
