## 2026-08-12 — CALIBRATION PROBE (per the widened check f83a3ee): the baseline is not failing, it is
## guessing — and it guesses at EXACTLY 1/n_pairs

Single seed, outcome arm, 2-layer transformer, 20,000 steps, 2-hop lookup:
  n_pairs  2  ->  y-acc 0.494   (1/2 = 0.500)
  n_pairs  3  ->  y-acc 0.335   (1/3 = 0.333)
  n_pairs  4  ->  y-acc 0.251   (1/4 = 0.250)
  n_pairs  8  ->  y-acc 0.125   (1/8 = 0.125)   [from E-2, 3 seeds: .125/.126/.125]
Four difficulty levels, four exact matches to chance-among-the-in-context candidates.

WHAT THIS IS. The transformer has learned the FORMAT completely -- emit a token from the Y range that
is present in this context -- and the two-hop computation not at all. It is not stuck below chance,
and it is not failing to optimise; it has converged on the surface regularity and stopped. This is C4
("networks learn patterns, not algorithms") in its cleanest quantitative form anywhere in this
project: the pattern is learned perfectly, the algorithm is learned zero.
WHAT IT CHANGES. E-2's VOID diagnosis said the arena was "too hard". That was wrong in an important
way and I correct it here: the arena is not unlearnable, it is UNTAUGHT. Outcome supervision supplies
no signal about the intermediate hop, and the model settles on the best format-only strategy. This is
precisely the regime where intermediate supervision should matter -- and E-2 tested the intermediate
arm ONLY at n_pairs 8, where both arms sit at the format-only plateau and the comparison is
uninformative. The decisive cell -- intermediate supervision at n_pairs 2, where outcome plateaus at
exactly coin-flip -- has never been run.
This entry is an apparatus observation, not a claim about training signals. The claim requires the
registered three-seed audit, which now has a calibrated arena to run in.

## 2026-08-12 — DECISIVE CELL result, and an implementation flaw in my own arm that I am naming
## rather than banking around

  n_pairs 2:  outcome 0.494  ->  intermediate 0.500   (+0.006)
  n_pairs 3:  outcome 0.335  ->  intermediate 0.395   (+0.060)
Intermediate supervision does NOT break the format-only plateau. Both arms remain at
chance-among-in-context-candidates. On its face this says the training signal is not the lever.

WHY I AM NOT BANKING THAT. My "intermediate" arm adds a cross-entropy on the true X at a SECOND HEAD
reading the SAME final representation. That is a MULTI-TASK AUXILIARY LOSS, not process supervision.
Nothing in the architecture makes the Y pathway CONSUME the recovered X: head_x and head_y both read
h (E-2's transformer) in parallel, so supervising X teaches a readout, not a computation Y depends on.
Real process supervision -- the thing the literature means, and the thing that motivated this
coordinate -- GENERATES the intermediate and then CONDITIONS on it: produce X, feed X back, produce Y.
My arm cannot express that. So this result is evidence about auxiliary multi-task losses and says
almost nothing about the coordinate I opened Family E to test.
That is the third apparatus-level miss in this family (E-1 arena too easy, E-2 arena mis-diagnosed as
too hard, and now the treatment arm implementing the wrong intervention). The pattern is consistent
and it is mine: I keep building the test before I have specified precisely what the treatment IS.
STATUS: the training-signal coordinate is STILL UNTESTED. What is now established, and is worth
keeping, is the calibration finding -- an outcome-supervised transformer converges to exactly
1/n_pairs at n=2,3,4,8, learning the format completely and the algorithm not at all. That stands on
its own as the cleanest quantitative instance of C4 in this project.
A REAL test needs a generate-then-condition arm (autoregressive: emit X, then emit Y conditioned on
the emitted X), with the outcome arm free to emit whatever it likes in that slot. That is a different
harness, not a flag on this one, and it needs its own pre-registration written when I can specify the
treatment exactly. I am not writing it inside this entry.

## 2026-08-12 — E-3 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): GENERATE-THEN-CONDITION. The training-signal
## coordinate, instrumented correctly for the first time

Three apparatus misses in this family, all mine, all named in prior entries: E-1 arena too easy
(structure hard-wired), E-2 mis-diagnosed as too hard (actually the format-only 1/n_pairs plateau),
decisive-cell treatment arm implementing an auxiliary multi-task loss instead of process supervision.
The coordinate — does the TRAINING SIGNAL determine whether a network acquires the algorithm rather
than the format — is still untested. This entry specifies the treatment EXACTLY, before any code,
because the pattern across all three misses was building the test before specifying the treatment.

ARENA: the E-1/E-2 generator unchanged (A->X and X->Y pairs at uniformly random slot positions,
vocab 8192, query is an A, answer is its Y, X never shown at query time). Baseline trunk: the e2.py
2-layer causal transformer unchanged (d=128, 4 heads). ONE change to the readout, shared by both
arms: the two parallel heads are replaced by a SINGLE LM head read at two positions (that parallel-
head geometry was exactly the decisive-cell flaw). n_query = 1 per sequence (changed from E-2's
min(4, n_pairs); registered reason: interleaved multi-query rollouts make the feed-back pathway
ambiguous; one query keeps the conditioning chain unambiguous; batch 64 keeps query throughput).

THE HARNESS (identical for BOTH arms — this is the substrate, not the treatment):
sequence = [2P context tokens] [A]. Pass 1: read LM-head logits at the A position -> emitted token
X_hat = argmax, DETACHED (no gradient through the emission, either arm). Append X_hat's embedding as
the next input token. Pass 2: read LM-head logits at the X_hat position -> Y prediction. Greedy,
deterministic, same rollout at train and eval, both arms. Y must be computed THROUGH the emitted
token or not at all — the architecture provides the pathway but not the algorithm; the model still
has to learn (i) to emit the right X and (ii) to chain the second lookup off it.

THE TWO ARMS differ ONLY in the loss:
  OUTCOME   CE on the Y prediction alone. The emission slot is a free scratchpad; nothing trains it
            (argmax is non-differentiable and the emission is detached — the slot's content drifts
            with the shared trunk but receives no directed pressure).
  PROCESS   CE on the Y prediction PLUS CE(emission logits, true X), equal weight — the same weight
            E-2 registered.
NO teacher forcing in either arm, registered reason: feeding the TRUE X into the rollout would leak
the intermediate into the input stream; the outcome arm could then learn a one-hop lookup off the
teacher-forced token and fail at eval only through exposure bias. Own-emission rollout in BOTH arms
makes the supervision signal the ONLY manipulated variable — the single-variable requirement the
decisive-cell arm violated.

SCOPE OF THE COMPARATOR, registered now so a skeptic reads it here first: the OUTCOME arm is
outcome-supervised cross-entropy — the signal every experiment in this program has used. It is NOT
an RL-style arm that assigns outcome credit to the emission (STaR-like sampling); that is a third
signal class, out of scope. A QUALIFIES verdict claims superiority over outcome-CE only.

STANDING CHECK, both directions, applied before running:
 (a) Does the apparatus already contain the tested thing? The tested thing is the SIGNAL. Both arms
     share the architecture including the conditioning pathway. Check passes.
 (b) Difficulty band (widened check f83a3ee): CALIBRATION PROBE MANDATORY before any audit — single
     seed, OUTCOME arm only, n_pairs in {2,3,4,8}, 20k-step cap. A level is IN-BAND iff outcome
     y-acc at cap lies in [1/n_pairs - 0.05, 0.85]. If NO level is in-band the harness is VOID as a
     discriminator. Special case registered: if the outcome arm SOLVES levels (>0.85), the free slot
     became a discovered scratchpad without supervision — reportable as a descriptive finding, no
     claim, and the audit does not run there.

FULL AUDIT (only at in-band levels, at most three): 2 arms x 3 seeds, 20k-step cap, lr 1e-3, batch
64, no sweep, no tuning. Eval = Y accuracy only, greedy rollout, identical for both arms.

BARS, fixed now:
  QUALIFIES        at EVERY in-band level: PROCESS reaches y-acc >= 0.90 within cap 3/3 seeds AND
                   OUTCOME finishes <= 1/n_pairs + 0.10, 3/3 seeds. (Process learns the algorithm;
                   outcome stays on the format plateau.)
  QUALIFIES-WEAK   if OUTCOME also reaches 0.90: PROCESS must hit criterion in <= 1/3 the steps,
                   3/3 seeds, every in-band level (E-2's ratio bar, reused verbatim).
  FAIL             PROCESS plateaus at ~1/n_pairs at any in-band level. The signal is not the lever
                   in this arena; Family E closes with the coordinate answered negative AS TESTED in
                   a correctly-instrumented harness. No rescue without a fresh prereg naming the
                   confound.

MANDATORY VALIDITY GATE — THE CONSUMPTION CHECK (written to kill apparatus miss #4 before it
happens): for every PROCESS seed that reaches criterion, re-evaluate with the fed-back emission
replaced by a random X-range token. y-acc must fall by >= 0.30. If it does not, the Y pathway is not
consuming the emission, the arm did not implement generate-then-condition, and the result is VOID
regardless of the bars. Run the same check descriptively on any OUTCOME seed that leaves the plateau.

FALSIFIABLE MECHANISTIC PREDICTION P1 (descriptive, not a gate): in PROCESS seeds that reach
criterion, emission accuracy (X_hat vs true X) crosses 0.90 BEFORE y-acc leaves the plateau —
the intermediate becomes correct first, then the chaining is learned off it.

CEILING ON THE CLAIM, restated from the E-2 prereg: process supervision is not new (CoT training,
STaR, process reward models). A QUALIFIES does not produce an algorithm. It produces evidence that
C4 — networks learn patterns, not algorithms, this program's central negative — is partly an
artifact of outcome-only supervision, which re-scopes several of this project's own negatives. The
U-5 natural-data gate remains mandatory before any claim leaves this toy arena.

BUDGET, exact: probe 4 runs (1 seed x 4 levels, outcome arm) + audit <= 18 runs (2 x 3 x <=3
levels). CPU-or-one-idle-GPU scale, minutes per run at this model size. NOTHING else is authorized
by this prereg: no extra arms, no extra seeds, no teacher-forcing variant, no RL arm.
IMPLEMENTATION: e3.py, NEW file, generator imported from e2.py unchanged. Next tick: implement +
run the calibration probe; audit only at levels the probe certifies.

## 2026-08-12 — E-4 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): the treatment I failed to implement last time —
## GENERATE-then-CONDITION, with the intermediate actually consumed

WHY THIS EXISTS. E-3's "intermediate" arm was a multi-task auxiliary CE on a parallel head reading the
same final representation. Nothing forced the answer pathway to CONSUME the recovered intermediate, so
that experiment tested auxiliary losses and not process supervision. I named that flaw in the ledger
rather than banking its negative, and said the real test needed its own pre-registration written once I
could specify the treatment exactly. This is that specification.

ARENA (calibrated, per the widened check f83a3ee): the 2-hop lookup, A->X and X->Y pairs at uniformly
random slot positions, X never shown at query time, vocab 8192. n_pairs in {2, 3} — the two settings
where the probe established that an outcome-supervised transformer sits at EXACTLY 1/n_pairs (0.494 and
0.335), i.e. it has learned the format completely and the algorithm not at all. Maximum room for a
signal to show, and a baseline that is neither solving the task nor at absolute floor.

MECHANICS, identical in both arms — this is the part E-3 got wrong:
  Pass 1: forward on [context, query_A]; the last position emits a distribution over the INTERMEDIATE.
  Feedback: the SOFT embedding of that distribution, sum_v p(v) emb(v), is appended as the next input
    position. The intermediate is therefore generated and then conditioned on, differentiably, in BOTH
    arms. This is the mechanism, not the supervision, and it is held constant.
  Pass 2: forward on [context, query_A, soft_intermediate]; the last position emits the ANSWER.
ARMS differ ONLY in the loss:
  OUTCOME  CE on the answer alone. The intermediate slot is unsupervised — the model may put anything
           there, and gradient reaches it only through the answer.
  PROCESS  CE on the answer PLUS CE on the true X at the intermediate slot, equal weight.
EVALUATION, identical: hard argmax feedback (no soft embedding, no teacher forcing) and scoring on
FINAL-ANSWER accuracy only. The process arm receives extra information during training and zero credit
for it at test.
3 seeds, uniform 20,000-step cap, lr 1e-3 both arms, no sweep, same 2-layer transformer as E-2.

BARS, fixed now:
  QUALIFIES iff PROCESS reaches criterion (>=0.90 answer accuracy) in 3/3 seeds while OUTCOME does not,
    OR reaches it in <= 1/3 of OUTCOME's steps in 3/3 seeds.
  FAILS if PROCESS does not clear the format-only plateau (answer accuracy within 0.05 of 1/n_pairs).
  VOID if neither arm clears the plateau — apparatus failure, not a claim, and I will say so.
CEILING ON THE CLAIM, registered in advance and unchanged from E-2: process supervision is NOT new in
the literature. A positive here is NOT a new algorithm. What it would establish is that this program's
central negative — C4, "networks learn patterns, not algorithms" — is partly an ARTIFACT OF SUPERVISION
FORM, because every one of the ~200 experiments behind C4 used outcome supervision only. That would
require re-examining the C4 evidence, which is a large and specific consequence, and it is still not an
algorithm. The mandatory natural-data gate (U-5) applies before anything leaves this ledger.

## 2026-08-12 — E-4 VERDICT (prereg 83a4e72): QUALIFIES in the STRONGEST registered form at n_pairs 2,
## FAILS at n_pairs 3. Both reported; I did not register an aggregation rule and I am not choosing one now.

n_pairs 2
  outcome  steps None/None/None   acc 0.469 0.355 0.518   (criterion 0/3)
  process  steps 10400/4600/10400 acc 0.996 0.908 0.947   (criterion 3/3)
n_pairs 3
  outcome  steps None/None/None   acc 0.004 0.004 0.012   (criterion 0/3)
  process  steps None/None/None   acc 0.328 0.344 0.287   (criterion 0/3, at the 1/3 plateau)

VERDICT AT n=2: the registered strongest form -- OUTCOME never reaches criterion in 20,000 steps while
PROCESS reaches it in 3/3 seeds. Identical network, identical data, identical generate-then-condition
mechanism, identical hard-argmax evaluation scored on the final answer only. The ONLY difference is
whether the intermediate slot carries a loss. This is the first strongest-form QUALIFIES in this
session and the first time in this project that a TRAINING SIGNAL, holding architecture fixed, has
decided whether an algorithm is acquired at all.
VERDICT AT n=3: FAILS by the registered bar -- process sits at 0.320 mean, within 0.05 of 1/3. So the
effect does not survive going from two pairs to three. Whatever process supervision buys here, it buys
it in a very narrow regime, and I am not going to describe an n=2-only result as a general one.
PRE-REGISTRATION GAP, named: I registered per-arena bars and ran two arenas without registering how to
combine them. Both verdicts are therefore reported side by side. Picking either as "the" verdict after
seeing them is exactly the move the protocol exists to prevent.

AN INDEPENDENT FINDING, cleaner than the headline. At n=3 the OUTCOME arm collapses to 0.004 -- far
BELOW the 0.335 that the single-pass transformer reached on the same arena in the calibration probe.
The generate-then-condition mechanism, unsupervised, is WORSE THAN NOT HAVING IT: the soft-embedding
feedback carries noise the model then conditions on. Mechanism alone hurts; mechanism plus signal is
what works. This is a statement about architecture-vs-signal that does not depend on the n=2 win, and
it is the part I would defend hardest.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT ENTITLE ME TO, per the ceiling registered before the run. It is NOT a new
algorithm; process supervision is not new. What it does is put a crack in C4 ("networks learn patterns,
not algorithms"): at n=2, on this arena, the network's failure to acquire the algorithm was an artifact
of SUPERVISION FORM, not of architecture -- and every one of the ~200 experiments behind C4 used outcome
supervision only. C4 is not refuted; it is now known to be confounded with supervision form in at least
one arena, which means the C4 evidence has to be re-read rather than cited. The n=3 failure bounds how
excited to be. The U-5 natural-data gate still applies absolutely before any of this leaves the ledger.
NEXT, named and deliberately NOT registered tonight: find where between n=2 and n=8 the effect dies, and
whether it dies because of the arena or because soft-embedding feedback degrades with more candidates.
That needs the calibration probe first, per f83a3ee.

## 2026-08-12 — E-5 BOUNDARY PROBE: a CLIFF, not a gradient. And a CORRECTION to my own E-4 framing,
## written one hour after I wrote it.

Process arm, 1 seed, 20,000 steps, same harness:
  n=2  0.996 / 0.908 / 0.947  CRITERION 3/3        (1/n = 0.500)
  n=3  0.328 / 0.344 / 0.287  plateau              (1/n = 0.333)
  n=4  0.258                  plateau              (1/n = 0.250)
  n=5  0.201                  plateau              (1/n = 0.200)
  n=6  0.000                  collapsed
n=3, 4 and 5 sit on EXACTLY the format-only plateau -- the same place outcome supervision lands. So
beyond two pairs, process supervision buys NOTHING. The reading criterion for cliff-vs-gradient was
fixed in the transcript BEFORE these numbers existed, and it says cliff: the n=2 result is a toy regime.

CORRECTION TO E-4 (2de08e4), which I wrote an hour ago. There I said the n=2 result "puts a crack in
C4" and that C4's evidence "has to be re-read rather than cited". That is too strong and I withdraw the
strength of it. The reason is mechanistic and the probe makes it visible: at n=2, once the intermediate
X is emitted correctly -- and the process arm is DIRECTLY SUPERVISED to emit it -- recovering Y is a
choice between TWO candidates. The model does not need to compose two retrievals; it needs one
supervised emission plus a coin-flip-sized lookup. That is why it does not survive n=3. What supervision
bought at n=2 was not "the two-hop algorithm"; it was the first hop handed over for free plus a
near-trivial second step.
So the honest statement is much narrower than the one I banked: in one arena, at the smallest
non-trivial size, supervision form decided acquisition of a near-degenerate task. C4 is NOT shown to be
confounded with supervision form in any interesting regime. The E-4 verdict entry stands as written --
I do not edit history -- and this entry is the correction that supersedes its framing.
WHAT SURVIVES, and it is not nothing: (1) the calibration finding, an outcome-supervised transformer
converging to EXACTLY 1/n_pairs at n=2,3,4,8 -- format learned completely, algorithm learned zero, four
independent points; (2) the mechanism-alone-hurts finding, unsupervised generate-then-condition at 0.004
versus single-pass at 0.335 on the same arena. Both are quantitative, both reproduce, neither depends on
the n=2 win.
FAMILY E CLOSES. The training-signal coordinate is now TESTED, with a correctly implemented treatment,
on a calibrated arena, and the answer is that it does not lift the algorithm-acquisition failure beyond
a degenerate size. No further arm, size or variant is registered. I am not hunting for a larger n where
it might work -- that is the rescue-iteration move this protocol forbids.

## 2026-08-12 — STANDING MANDATE (user directive): continuous autonomous exploration toward an
## epoch-making algorithm. Cron cadence raised to every 2 hours.

The user has instructed that the search continue autonomously and not stop at the absence of a result.
Recorded here because the cron tick treats THIS FILE'S TAIL as its source of truth, not the prompt file.
WHAT THE LOOP IS AND IS NOT. It is a standing mandate to advance ONE bounded, pre-registered step every
tick. It is NOT a promise that an epoch-making algorithm will be produced, and no tick may report one
that has not passed the three gates. Twelve pre-registered experiments on 2026-08-11/12 produced none;
that record stands and must not be softened in any summary.
THE FIVE DISCIPLINES, each bought with a specific failure this project made, now binding on every tick:
  1 pre-register bars + FAIL consequence + predictions in the ledger and commit BEFORE code; commit the
    scorer before reading data;
  2 no rescue iteration without a fresh prereg naming the confound — if numbers tempt a config change,
    record the temptation and change nothing;
  3 a two-sided calibration probe before any full audit — the baseline must neither solve the arena nor
    sit at floor (three audits were wasted for want of this);
  4 define the intervention exactly before building the test (E-3 measured an auxiliary loss while
    claiming to measure process supervision);
  5 report as measured; retract your own headline when a control kills it; never substitute a post-hoc
    favourable statistic for a registered bar.
THE THREE GATES, in order, before anything is called a result: (i) a de-confounded arena that certifies
headroom, with any NON-CAUSAL oracle advantage identified and excluded; (ii) beat the real incumbent the
literature uses — an opponent that fails to reproduce its published qualitative behaviour means MY
implementation is broken and no claim is made against it; (iii) a natural-data gate, then a
matched-compute win over a capable incumbent on an established benchmark. Gate (iii) has never been
reached by anything in this project.
SPENT COORDINATES, not to be recycled under new notation: unit discovery; the memory write rule; the
training signal (closed at E-5 — a cliff, nothing beyond n=2); test-time adaptation in the count-model
family; fast-weight memory as an attention replacement.
ESCALATION CLAUSE, so the loop cannot degenerate into motion: if three consecutive ticks end without a
new pre-registration because no legitimate new coordinate exists, the tick writes ONE escalation entry
here, drops to idle-check, and stops registering. Choosing a new direction is the user's decision.
Inventing a mechanism to keep a streak alive is forbidden.
OUTWARD-FACING actions remain the user's alone: paper submission, repo visibility, the W-3 go/no-go, and
revoking the exposed GitHub PAT.

## 2026-08-12 — FAMILY P PRE-REGISTRATION (P-1, before code): PARALLELISM AS A FIRST-CLASS CONSTRAINT.
## User directive: the GPU-parallelism advantage is what made backprop and the Transformer win.

WHY THIS IS A GENUINELY NEW COORDINATE and not a recycled one. The spent list is: unit discovery, the
write rule, the training signal, count-family TTA, fast-weights-as-attention-replacement. All five were
scored on STEPS-TO-CRITERION or accuracy at a fixed step budget. NONE was ever scored on WALL-CLOCK at
matched hardware, and in none of them was PARALLELISABILITY a design constraint. That axis is untouched.

## 2026-08-12 — P-1 RESULT: chunked-parallel delta rule VERIFIED and BENCHMARKED. And it convicts my
## own TT-13 of handicapping the opponent.

IDENTITY CHECK (float64, five configurations incl. C=T and T not divisible by C):
  worst max|sequential - chunked| = 2.7e-15  (bar was 1e-4). IDENTITY HOLDS. Derivation is in p1.py --
  the delta rule's within-chunk dependency is a LOWER-TRIANGULAR system in the update vectors,
  (I + diag(beta) tril(K K^T,-1)) U = diag(beta)(V - K S_0^T), one triangular solve per chunk. Exact.
GPU WALL-CLOCK (A800, B=64, dk=dv=128, C=32, ms per forward):
   T=20   seq  2.46  chunk 0.40   6.1x
   T=72   seq  8.54  chunk 1.07   8.0x
   T=128  seq 15.13  chunk 1.39  10.9x
   T=256  seq 30.58  chunk 2.73  11.2x
   T=512  seq 60.46  chunk 5.44  11.1x
The speedup GROWS with sequence length and plateaus near 11x. This is the user's point made
quantitative on our own hardware: the same mathematics, reorganised to use the parallel units, is an
order of magnitude cheaper -- and cost is what decides how much data a method sees per unit of time.

WHAT THIS CONVICTS, and it is against our own interest so it is reported first. In TT-13 I registered a

I registered that a wall-clock win cannot revive a steps verdict. This is the mirror case and the same
principle forces the opposite action: a wall-clock finding that shows I UNDER-RESOURCED THE OPPONENT

## 2026-08-12 — P-3 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): the design principle sharpened, and the primitive
## it implies. PARALLEL DEPTH, not FLOPs, not steps.

THE PRINCIPLE, in the form I will actually design against. What backprop, the CNN and the Transformer
share is not fewer FLOPs -- it is SHORT SEQUENTIAL DEPTH with wide parallel work. Attention INCREASED
cost from O(T) to O(T^2) and won anyway, because the Transformer paper's own motivation is that an RNN's
length-T dependency "precludes parallelization within training examples". FLOPs are cheap; critical-path
length is expensive.
THIS CONVICTS MY OWN CHOICE OF METRIC. Every audit in this project scored STEPS-TO-CRITERION -- sample
efficiency. That is not what the Transformer won on. TT-1's headline was that our binder beats a
transformer by 11-16x in STEPS on MQAR: that is precisely the LSTM's position -- cheaper per step,
sequential depth O(T), and it loses at scale. I have been optimising the metric that historically loses.
P-1 gives the principle its number on our own hardware: identical mathematics, reorganised for the
parallel units, is 6-11x cheaper and the advantage GROWS with T.

THE GAP THIS PRINCIPLE POINTS AT, which this session's own results establish: a 2-layer transformer
CANNOT LEARN two-hop composition on the E-4/E-5 arena. It converges to EXACTLY 1/n_pairs at n=2,3,4,8 --
format learned completely, algorithm learned zero -- and process supervision does not rescue it beyond a
degenerate n=2 (E-5: a cliff). Two-hop retrieval needs depth 2 and is not acquired at depth 2.

THE PRIMITIVE, specified exactly (discipline 4 -- no harness until the treatment is written down):
  inputs H (B,T,d). Projections W_q, W_k, W_v, W_k2, W_v2.
  A1 = softmax( (H W_q)(H W_k)^T / sqrt(d) + causal_mask )      # where to hop FIRST
  A2 = softmax( (H W_k2)(H W_k2)^T / sqrt(d) + causal_mask )    # from there, where to hop NEXT
  O  = A1 @ A2 @ (H W_v2)
Sequential depth in T: ZERO -- two dense matmuls, no recurrence, no per-step loop. Cost: two T x T
matmuls, i.e. 2x attention, same asymptotic class. Both hops keep a COMPETITIVE softmax readout, which
is the one thing the TT series established as irreducible (C1). The composition is BUILT IN rather than
left to be learned, which is the direct response to C4.
INCUMBENT: a 2-layer causal transformer at MATCHED non-embedding parameters -- the exact model E-5 showed
converges to 1/n. OUTCOME SUPERVISION ONLY for both arms: the point is that a correct primitive should
remove the NEED for process supervision, not require it.
ARENA: the E-4 generator unchanged, n_pairs in {3, 4, 6} -- deliberately EXCLUDING n=2, the degenerate
size where a supervised emission plus a coin flip already sufficed. 3 seeds, 20,000-step cap, lr 1e-3,
no sweep for either arm.
BARS, fixed now:
  QUALIFIES iff the primitive reaches >=0.90 answer accuracy in 3/3 seeds at n=3 AND n=4, while the
    param-matched transformer stays within 0.05 of 1/n.
  PARTIAL iff it clears 1/n by >=0.20 absolute in 3/3 seeds at n=3 without reaching criterion.
  FAILS iff it lands within 0.05 of 1/n like the transformer -- in which case building the composition
    in does not help either, C4 survives this attack, and the coordinate closes.
  n=6 is reported as a scaling observation, not as part of the bar.
PRIOR-ART OBLIGATION, registered before results: multi-hop / higher-order / attention-over-attention
variants EXIST in the literature. I am not entitled to a novelty claim without a prior-art check, and a
QUALIFIES result licenses only "this design principle predicts a primitive that works where the
param-matched incumbent provably fails", not "we invented it". The natural-data gate and the
matched-compute win over a capable incumbent still stand between this and any result.

## 2026-08-12 — P-3 VERDICT (prereg 919e4d0): FAILS, decisively, and the diagnosis refines the
## principle rather than the principle refuting itself.

two-hop primitive, outcome supervision, 3 seeds, non-emb 467,456 (vs incumbent 470,272):
  n=3  0.000 / 0.172 / 0.178   mean 0.117   1/n = 0.333   single-pass transformer reference 0.335
  n=4  0.123 / 0.000 / 0.201   mean 0.108   1/n = 0.250   reference 0.251
  n=6  0.000 / 0.000 / 0.000   mean 0.000   1/n = 0.167
The primitive is 0.217 BELOW chance-among-in-context-candidates at n=3 and below the plain single-pass
transformer everywhere. Three of nine runs collapsed to EXACTLY 0.000, which is optimisation
instability, not merely insufficient expressiveness. Registered bar: FAILS.

DIAGNOSIS, and it was stated BEFORE the final numbers landed (see transcript): I wrote the second hop as
A2 = softmax(K2 K2^T), which is QUERY-INDEPENDENT. Every query gets the same hop-2 table; row i of A2
depends only on key i and not on who is querying it. But in two-hop retrieval WHERE THE SECOND HOP GOES
DEPENDS ON WHERE THE FIRST ONE LANDED. Matrix-multiplication associativity let me write A1 @ A2 @ V and
call it two hops; what I actually built was "one global hop-2 table, re-weighted by the hop-1
distribution". The selectivity of the second hop was thrown away, and the product of two softmaxes is
also badly conditioned -- hence the collapses.

WHAT THIS DOES TO THE PRINCIPLE. It does NOT refute it. Parallel depth remains the right SELECTION
criterion -- P-1 measured its value on our own hardware at 6-11x, growing in T. What P-3 establishes is
that parallel depth is NECESSARY BUT NOT CONSTRUCTIVE: it tells you which mechanisms to disqualify, not
how to build one. And it has a price that attention does not pay. Attention buys O(1) depth with O(T^2)
cost LOSSLESSLY -- softmax(QK^T)V is exactly content-based retrieval. My construction bought O(1) depth
with 2x O(T^2) cost LOSSILY, by dropping query-conditioning. That asymmetry is the actual lesson, and it
is sharper than "use the parallel units".
THE OPEN QUESTION, now precisely stated, and deliberately NOT registered tonight: can (a) O(1) sequential
depth, (b) a competitive softmax readout, and (c) a second-hop selection CONDITIONED ON THE FIRST HOP'S
RESULT be had simultaneously? A2 would have to depend on A1's output while remaining a matmul rather than
a loop. I do not currently know whether that is possible, and per discipline 4 I will not build a harness
until I can write the treatment down exactly. Writing it down is the next step, not running anything.

FOURTH APPARATUS ERROR OF THE SESSION, named. P-3's prereg specified as incumbent "the exact model E-5
showed converges to 1/n" -- that is the SINGLE-PASS transformer in e2.py. I wired in TFGenCond, the
TWO-PASS generate-then-condition model from E-4, which without process supervision collapses to 0.004.
So the incumbent column of P-3 is VOID: it is a crippled opponent and I will not use a 0.004 baseline to
flatter a 0.117 result. The verdict above is taken against the single-pass reference from the calibration
probe (0.335 / 0.251), which is the honest comparison and the one that condemns my primitive.
This is the fourth time this session I built the test wrong (E-1 arena too easy, E-2 mis-diagnosed, E-3
wrong treatment, P-3 wrong incumbent). The rate is the finding: my failure mode is apparatus
specification, not idea generation, and no amount of new coordinates fixes that.

## 2026-08-13 — P-4 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): the P-3 open question written down exactly
## (discipline 4) and registered as the sanctioned follow-up with the confound named (discipline 2).

CONFOUND NAMED: P-3's second hop was QUERY-INDEPENDENT — A2 = softmax((H Wk2)(H Wk2)^T) gave every
position the same hop-2 table, discarding hop-1's selection entirely. P-4 fixes exactly that and
nothing else: hop-2's query is computed FROM hop-1's output.

THE NAMED QUESTION, DISSOLVED FIRST. P-3 left open whether (a) O(1) sequential depth in T, (b) a
competitive softmax readout, and (c) hop-2 selection conditioned on hop-1's RESULT can coexist as
matmuls. Written down exactly, the question splits: conditioning on hop-1's discrete LANDING SITE is
an argmax — nonlinear in state, the same shape as every NO line in parallelism_audit.md — and is NOT
matmul-expressible. Conditioning on hop-1's returned VALUE MIXTURE is trivially expressible: hop-1
completes in one round of matmuls and its output is an ordinary tensor from which hop-2's queries are
projected. Depth in T stays zero; depth in LAYERS is 2, constant, which is all the P-1 principle asks.
Early in training the mixture is smeared across candidates, so the hop-2 query is smeared too. P-4
therefore tests one real, unknown thing: is the incumbent's 1/n failure a COMPOSITION-DISCOVERY
problem (fixable by hard-wiring the pathway) or a MIXTURE-BOOTSTRAP problem (no wiring fixes it; the
smeared gradient is the wall)?

TREATMENT, EXACTLY (discipline 4). Arena tokenization was READ BEFORE REGISTERING (e4.py make_batch):
pairs span TWO positions (lhs token at even slot 2s, rhs token at odd slot 2s+1), queries appended at
the end; a content-addressed hop lands on the MATCHED position, so retrieving the successor token
requires a FIXED next-position value shift. Without it the treatment cannot express the task at all —
catching this now, not post-hoc, is discipline 4 doing its job (it would have been apparatus error
five). The shifted-value hop IS the previous-token-head + induction-head decomposition of Elhage et
al. 2021 / Olsson et al. 2022, hard-wired; NO novelty claim is available, registered now.
  Inputs: e4.py token stream unchanged; token embedding + positional embedding, H in R^{B x T x d}.
  Hsh = roll(H_tok, -1) along T, zero at last position (next-position token content; legitimate —
        every attended position is in the causal past of the query position).
  Hop 1: A1 = softmax((H Wq1)(H Wk1)^T / sqrt(d) + causal mask);  O1 = A1 (Hsh Wv1)
  Hop 2: Q2 = O1 Wq2;  A2 = softmax((Q2)(H Wk2)^T / sqrt(d) + causal mask);  O = A2 (Hsh Wv2)
  Logits = head(O) at query positions only; cross-entropy on Y only; OUTCOME supervision only.
Q2 is a function of O1 ONLY — no residual path into it, no MLP, no mixing with H. The composition
pathway a generic transformer must DISCOVER through its residual stream is here the only pathway that
exists. Six d x d projections + shared emb/pos/head, two softmaxes, zero recurrence in T.

INCUMBENT: TFChainer in e2.py (single-pass 2-layer transformer, d=128, heads=4), the model behind the
P-3 calibration reference (0.335 at n=3, 0.251 at n=4). GATE-(ii) GUARD, after P-3 wired the wrong
incumbent: at launch the incumbent must land within 0.05 of 1/n at n=3 AND n=4 under this harness. If
it does not (EITHER direction), P-4 is VOID — apparatus failure recorded, no claim made by anyone.

PARAMETER CONVENTION, registered as a deviation from P-3's matching and hostile to us: treatment uses
the SAME d=128 and identical embedding/positional/head shapes as the incumbent, and NO param matching
is attempted. Treatment non-emb-non-head = 6d^2 = 98,304 vs incumbent ~470k (4.8x FEWER, our
disadvantage, accepted). Reason: widening the treatment to match would change embedding width and
introduce a capacity confound; the hostile direction needs no adjustment and leaves no excuse
available to us. Exact counts reported at launch.

STAGE 0 — CAPACITY GATE before any training (the P-1 no-unverified-arm rule applied to our own arm):
zero-training hand-wired construction with FROZEN RANDOM embeddings — Wq Wk^T = tau * I (embedding-
space matcher; tau is the single free scalar, nothing else tuned), value path = pass-through of the
shifted stream, both hops. Gate: Y accuracy >= 0.95 at n=3. If the construction cannot pass, P-4
STOPS as an apparatus failure and no comparison is run.

PROTOCOL: harness copied verbatim from p3.py (BATCH 64, CRIT 0.90, EVAL_EVERY 200, EVAL_BATCHES 8,
same eval); n_pairs in {3,4,6}, n=2 stays excluded as degenerate (E-5); 3 seeds x {treatment,
incumbent}; 20,000-step cap; lr 1e-3 fixed; NO sweep for either arm; outcome supervision both arms.
n=6 is a scaling observation, not part of any bar. Scorer score_p4.py committed BEFORE any run

BARS, fixed now on final eval accuracy at cap:
  QUALIFIES iff treatment >= 0.90 in 3/3 seeds at n=3 AND at n=4, with the incumbent gate holding.
  PARTIAL   iff treatment >= 1/n + 0.20 absolute in 3/3 seeds at n=3, short of full criterion.
  FAILS     iff treatment lands within 0.05 of 1/n or below at n=3, OR any seed at n in {3,4}

## 2026-08-13 — P-4 STAGE-0 VERDICT (prereg aa1e900; code+scorer committed BEFORE data at
## 85e723d): the capacity gate FAILS at 0.0016 vs 0.95. P-4 STOPS as an apparatus failure,
## per the registered branch. No comparison is run and no claim is made by anyone.

Stage 0 ran the registered zero-training construction (frozen random embeddings, Wq Wk^T =
tau*I both hops with the sqrt(d) scale folded into tau, value pass-through of the shifted
stream, nearest-token-embedding readout) at n=3 over a 20-point tau sweep 0.001..2.0, 9,600
queries per tau, CPU only. Best Y accuracy 0.0016 at tau=0.015. Gate 0.95. FAIL at every tau,
by three orders of magnitude.

THE TWO WALLS, measured, not conjectured (attention-mass diagnostics were in the committed
stage-0 code, not added after):
(i) HOP-1 SELF-MATCH. At the query position the query token matches ITSELF: with H = e_tok +
    e_pos the self score is ||e_tok||^2 + ||e_pos||^2 ~ 256 against ~128 for the true context
    match, so softmax mass goes to self at any tau sharp enough to separate match from noise.
    Measured: hop-1 self-mass rises 0.09 -> 1.000 across the sweep while true-match mass peaks
    at 0.123 (tau=0.01) and then collapses. The self position's shifted value is junk (the
    next query token) or zero, so O1 never carries X.
(ii) HOP-2 DOUBLE OCCURRENCE. X appears twice in every sequence — rhs of the A->X pair (odd
    position) and lhs of the X->Y pair (even position) — and a content matcher scores them
    IDENTICALLY. Measured: hop-2 mass on the two occurrences is equal at every tau (0.072 vs
    0.072 ... 0.022 vs 0.022, exactly), a structural 50/50 with only the even one carrying Y.

NON-REGISTERED ORACLE CONTROL (p4_diag.py, run after the FAIL to falsify the implementation-
bug hypothesis, consumed by no gate): the SAME frozen machinery with the two walls oracle-
masked — diagonal masked in hop-1; hop-2 restricted to lhs positions — scores 0.998-0.9995 at
tau>=0.05. Masking only the self-match gives 0.507-0.508, the exact coin flip wall (ii)
predicts. The failure is therefore fully accounted for by the two named walls and the
apparatus (shift, embeddings, readout, harness) is sound. My implementation is not the
explanation; the registered construction is.

REGISTERED CONSEQUENCE EXECUTED: "If the construction cannot pass, P-4 STOPS as an apparatus
failure and no comparison is run." Stopped. The trained-comparison bars (QUALIFIES / PARTIAL /
FAILS) are never evaluated; the FAIL branch's consequence (the open question closing, the
mixture-bootstrap conclusion) does NOT fire — that branch belonged to the trained comparison
only. The open question from P-3 remains NAMED AND UNREGISTERED.

APPARATUS ERROR FIVE, named. The P-4 prereg read the arena tokenization before registering
and recorded that doing so "would have been apparatus error five." The error was one layer
deeper: the tau*I matcher was registered without computing its self-match term and without
noticing that X occurs twice per sequence. E-1 arena too easy, E-2 mis-diagnosed, E-3 wrong
treatment, P-3 wrong incumbent, P-4 stage-0 construction inexpressive: five apparatus errors,
and the rate remains the finding. What is different this time: the registered gate caught it
BEFORE training — minutes of CPU, zero GPU, no contaminated comparison, no headline to
retract. That is the P-1 no-unverified-arm rule doing exactly what it was bought to do.

SCOPE OF THIS VERDICT, stated precisely so it cannot inflate later: stage 0 establishes that
the registered HAND-WIRED CONSTRUCTION cannot express the task. It does not establish that
the trained architecture cannot: the oracle control shows the missing ingredients are two
position-decodable structures (self-suppression in hop-1; even/odd parity selection in hop-2)
which trained projections over learned embeddings could in principle supply. Whether the
trained treatment would actually learn them is exactly the question P-4 was built to answer,
and per the registered branch it stays unanswered here.

TEMPTATION RECORDED (discipline 2): the fix is obvious — mask the diagonal, or move the shift
to the KEY side, which is the actual Elhage/Olsson previous-token composition and has no
self-match by construction, and which the oracle control all but validates. Nothing is
changed and nothing is run. A P-4b would require a fresh pre-registration naming these two

## 2026-08-13 — P-4b PRE-REGISTRATION (before code; discipline-2 rescue with the confound named):
## the confound is the P-4 STAGE-0 HAND-WIRED CONSTRUCTION, not the architecture, arena, or
## question. One term changes in the construction; trained arms, arena, harness, bars are P-4
## VERBATIM. Rescue depth is bounded: no P-4c exists.

CONFOUND NAMED (discipline 2). P-4 stopped at stage 0 because the registered matcher
(Wq Wk^T = tau*I, value pass-through of the shifted stream) cannot express the task: (i) hop-1
SELF-MATCH — the query token matches itself, self score ~ tau*(||e_t||^2 + ||e_p||^2), ~2x the
true match; (ii) hop-2 X DOUBLE-OCCURRENCE — X at odd (rhs of A->X) and even (lhs of X->Y)
positions, scored identically, structural 50/50. The non-registered oracle control scored 0.999
with both walls masked (0.507 masking self alone), so the machinery is sound and the
construction is the whole failure. P-4b fixes exactly the construction and nothing else.

THE TEMPTATION-NOTE FIXES, COMPUTED BEFORE REGISTERING (the apparatus-error-five lesson applied:
never register a matcher without computing its terms). Both proposals in the P-4 temptation note
are insufficient on their own:
- DIAGONAL MASK alone removes wall (i) only; hop-2 still splits 50/50 across X's two
  occurrences. The oracle control already measured this branch: mask-self-only = 0.507.
- KEY-SIDE SHIFT (K_i = H_{i-1}) removes the hop-1 self-match by construction, but with full-H
  values it makes wall (ii) DETERMINISTIC: O1 = e_X + e_p(2s+1), and the key at i = 2s+2 matches
  on BOTH content (t_{2s+1} = X) AND position (e_p(2s+1) inside the shifted key) -> score
  ~2*tau*nu vs ~tau*nu at the true continuation i = 2u+1 -> mass goes to the junk continuation,
  ~0.00 predicted. With token-only K/V it reverts to the 50/50 coin flip. Registering either fix
  naively would have been apparatus error six.

THE REGISTERED FIX: POSITIONAL INHIBITION OF RETURN — one term, same form in both hops. The two
walls are one wall: a content matcher RE-FINDS THE POSITION IT CAME FROM. Hop-1's query carries
its own positional code and re-matches it (self). Hop-2's query O1 = Hsh value = H_{2s+1} =
e_X + e_p(2s+1) carries the positional code of hop-1's landing site and re-matches THAT (the rhs
X occurrence). One suppression term kills both:
  score(q, k_i) = tau * (q . k_i) - 2*tau * (q^T S_hat k_i),
  S_hat = (1/nu_hat) * sum_j e_p(j) e_p(j)^T,  nu_hat = mean_j ||e_p(j)||^2,
computed from the frozen positional embedding table only — no task data, no training, no tuning;
the 2x multiplier is WIRED, not swept; tau remains the single free scalar with the P-4 sweep
verbatim (20 points, 0.001..2.0). Computed margins: hop-1 self ~ 2*tau*nu - 2*tau*nu ~ 0 vs true
match ~ tau*nu (margin = one full content match); hop-2 rhs occurrence ~ 2*tau*nu - 2*tau*nu ~ 0
vs lhs occurrence ~ tau*nu (same margin). Correct matches are untouched (their positional cross
terms are O(noise)). Values (shifted full-H stream), readout (nearest token embedding), n=3,
9,600 queries, gate 0.95: all VERBATIM from P-4 stage 0. Reliance stated: the construction
assumes X occurs EXACTLY twice per sequence, which P-4's committed diagnostics measured (two
masses, exactly 50/50 at every tau); any violation fails the gate and is covered by it.

PRIOR ART / NOVELTY: none claimed. Diagonal suppression in attention is standard practice; the
biological gloss (inhibition of return, Posner) is motivation only; the circuit remains the
previous-token + induction-head decomposition of Elhage et al. 2021 / Olsson et al. 2022,
already named in aa1e900.

EXPRESSIBILITY IN THE TRAINED ARM, verified before registering: tau*I - 2*tau*S_hat is a plain
d x d matrix, and Wq1 Wk1^T / Wq2 Wk2^T are unconstrained d x d products, so the construction
lies strictly inside the trained treatment's function class. THE TRAINED ARMS GET NOTHING NEW —
no diagonal mask, no inhibition term, no wiring change; treatment and incumbent are P-4 verbatim
(85e723d) — because the registered question is whether SGD DISCOVERS the circuit given the
pathway, not whether we can hand it more of the answer. Temptation recorded and declined
(discipline 2): no architectural mask is added to the trained treatment.

REGISTERED FALSIFIABLE PREDICTIONS for stage 0, both directions: at the passing tau, hop-1
self-mass (1.000 in P-4) drops below 0.05; hop-2 mass on X's two occurrences (exact 50/50 in
P-4) breaks to >= 0.90 on the lhs occurrence; the gate passes >= 0.95 at some tau in the

THE RUN (registered protocol verbatim): 20-point tau sweep 0.001..2.0, n=3, 9,600 queries per
tau, frozen random embeddings (seed 1234), same eval stream every tau (erng 77), CPU, minutes.
Best Y accuracy 0.5049 at tau=2.0, a saturated plateau (0.502-0.505 at every tau >= 0.15).

REGISTERED PREDICTIONS SCORED, both directions (discipline 5):
(1) hop-1 self-mass < 0.05 at the passing tau: CONFIRMED, and stronger — self-mass 0.000 from
    tau >= 0.07 (P-4 measured 1.000), and the SAME term kills the hop-2 return wall: rhs-X mass
    0.017 at best tau (P-4 measured an exact 50/50). The inhibition-of-return term did exactly
    what it was registered to do on BOTH named walls; the one-wall diagnosis was correct.
(2) hop-2 lhs-mass >= 0.90: REFUTED — 0.499 at best tau, saturating at ~0.50.
(3) gate >= 0.95 at some tau: REFUTED — no tau reaches 0.51.

TWO IMPLEMENTATION DISCLOSURES, made in the committed code BEFORE the run (1a8cc3d), each
resolving a prereg ambiguity in the only direction consistent with the registered margins:
(i) S_hat sums the T USED positions, not the full 512-row table — the full-table sum gives
    S_hat ~ (512/d) I = 4I, so I - 2*S_hat ~ -7I, a sign-flipped ANTI-matcher contradicting
    every margin computed in the prereg. (ii) Values = shifted FULL-H stream, as the prereg's
    own central formula (O1 = Hsh value = H_{2s+1} = e_X + e_p(2s+1)) requires — its
    cross-reference calling the values "verbatim from P-4 stage 0" was factually WRONG about
    p4.py's committed hsh (token-only), under which hop-2's query carries no positional code,
    the IOR term cannot act on wall (ii), and the 50/50 stands by construction. Both alternative
    readings fail trivially; the run used the most favorable faithful reading of the
    registration and still failed by 44 points. No reading of the prereg passes the gate.

APPARATUS ERROR SIX, named exactly: the registered margin computation was done at leading order
(means only) and omitted the VARIANCE the inhibition term itself injects. Measured, in the
pre-committed diagnostics: hop-1 true-match mass saturates at 0.683 as tau -> 2.0 — at argmax
sharpness ~32% of queries lose the true content match to a noise key DETERMINISTICALLY (frozen
embeddings; the eval stream is fixed). The arithmetic account (stated as analysis, not
separately measured): the -2*S_hat term roughly doubles per-key score noise via specific
positional cross-terms while shaving the content margin by the factor (1 - 2T/d); at d=128 with
~T=15 competing keys, the max over noise keys reaches the single-content-match margin for
roughly a third of queries per hop. Two hops compound: 0.683 x ~0.74 = 0.505, the measured
plateau. Same error class as apparatus error five — a hand-wired matcher registered without
computing all of its terms: five omitted the mean of a term it forgot (the self-match); six
omitted the variance of the term it added.

REGISTERED CONSEQUENCE EXECUTED VERBATIM: apparatus error six is named above; the P-4 family
CLOSES PERMANENTLY — rescue depth was bounded at one, there is NO P-4c under any framing; the
open question (O(1) sequential depth + competitive readout + value-conditioned composition:
composition-DISCOVERY vs mixture-BOOTSTRAP) stays NAMED AND UNREGISTERED, reopenable by the
USER only; empty-tick counting resumes with no credit from the P-4b registration.

TEMPTATION RECORDED (discipline 2), nothing changed, nothing run: the fixes are visible — wider
d (content margin grows ~sqrt(d) against the noise), a multiplier below the wired 2x,
orthogonalized positional embeddings (kills the cross-term noise entirely), T-normalized S_hat.
Every one is a rescue iteration on a family whose bounded rescue depth is spent. Recorded and
declined.

WHAT THE CLOSED FAMILY LEAVES BEHIND (descriptive, no claim): the two-hop machinery is sound
(P-4's oracle control scored 0.999); the return-inhibition principle did what it claimed (both
named walls died; prediction 1 confirmed both hops); what failed twice is the same thing —

built to run was never licensed by either construction and remains UNRUN; whether SGD discovers
the composition circuit given the hard-wired pathway stays unknown. Reopening that question is

## 2026-08-14 — FAMILY Q PRE-REGISTRATION (Q-1, before code). Registration RESUMES: the 2026-08-13
## escalation stopped for a USER DIRECTION DECISION and the user has now supplied one.

LICENCE. The escalation entry (af35227) stopped registration and stated "choosing a new direction is
the USER's decision, not this loop's". The user has directed: exploit GPU parallelism, produce a new
algorithm. That is the direction decision the clause was waiting for. Registration resumes for this
family only; the spent-coordinate list and all five disciplines remain binding.

THE EMPTY CELL, derived from OUR OWN parallelism audit (parallelism_audit.md, 480d40f) rather than
from inspiration. Its reference lines give two boundaries:
  attention        write trivial (concatenation), read SOFTMAX-COMPETITIVE, parallel, state GROWS with T
  DeltaNet/linear  write LINEAR IN STATE, read LINEAR, parallel, state FIXED
  ---> nobody occupies: FIXED state + write linear in state (hence chunk-parallel) + COMPETITIVE read.
Each ingredient is supported by this project's own evidence: C1 says the competitive readout is the
irreducible thing attention has (TT-9/10/11 eliminated representation, depth, capacity, decorrelation);
the audit's law says a mechanism parallelises iff its recurrence is LINEAR IN STATE with all
nonlinearity in the READ path; and P-3 says competition bought by discarding query-conditioning fails
below chance. The crux the law makes visible: READ-PATH NONLINEARITY IS FREE for parallelism, because
the read does not recur. The only hard constraint is that the WRITE GATE MUST DEPEND ON THE INPUT ONLY,
never on the state — which is exactly where D-3 died.

MECHANISM, specified exactly (discipline 4). State = M slots, each S_m in R^{dv x dk}, fixed size.
  routing (input-only):   r_{t,m} = softmax_m( k_t . a_m / tau )        a_m learned slot addresses
  write (per slot):       S_m,t = S_m,t-1 + beta_t r_{t,m} ( v_t - S_m,t-1 k_t ) k_t^T
  read (competitive):     o_t = sum_m softmax_m( q_t . a_m / tau ) ( S_m,t q_t )
The write is the delta rule with a per-slot scalar coefficient c_{t,m} = beta_t r_{t,m} that depends
ONLY on the current input, so per slot it is LINEAR in S_m and P-1's triangular-solve chunking applies
verbatim with beta replaced by c_{:,m}:
  U_m = (I + diag(c_m) tril(K K^T,-1))^{-1} diag(c_m) (V - K S_{m,0}^T);  O_m = Q S_{m,0}^T + tril(QK^T,0) U_m;
  S_m <- S_{m,0} + U_m^T K.   The competitive read is applied pointwise afterwards.
DISTINCTION FROM THE NEAREST RELATIVE, stated up front: multi-head linear attention gives each head its
own state and CONCATENATES them. This COMPETES over them. C1 says competition, not concatenation, is
the operative thing — this mechanism is the minimal test of that sentence at fixed parallel form.

IDENTITY GATE, mandatory before any comparison: the chunked implementation must match a literal
sequential implementation to max|seq - chunked| < 1e-4 (P-1 standard; observed 2.7e-15 there). If it
fails, Q-1 STOPS and is reported as an implementation failure. No comparison against any opponent is
run with an unverified kernel — apparatus errors five and six were both hand-wired constructions that
skipped this.
CALIBRATION PROBE, mandatory before the full audit (discipline 3): single seed, short budget; the
incumbent must neither already solve the arena nor sit at floor.
ARENA: MQAR easy (8 pairs, 4 queries) and hard (32 pairs, 8 queries), vocab 8192, 3 seeds, ours untuned
at lr 1e-3 cap 20k; incumbents get warmup 500, LR sweep {3e-4,1e-3,3e-3}, cap 60k — the same asymmetry
in their favour used in P-2.
PRIMARY INCUMBENT = delta2c (the P-1 verified chunked DeltaNet), at MATCHED non-embedding parameters
and MATCHED TOTAL STATE SIZE (M x dv x dk for ours must equal dv' x dk' for it). That isolates exactly
one variable: whether the read competes. Attention is reported as a reference ceiling only.
MANDATORY ABLATION, registered now so it cannot be dropped: M=1. At M=1 the softmaxes are degenerate
and the mechanism reduces to DeltaNet plus a scalar. IF M=1 MATCHES M>1, the competition is doing no
work and I report that as the finding, whatever the headline number says.
BARS: QUALIFIES iff, with the identity gate passed and state size matched, ours reaches criterion in
<= 1/2 the steps of best-LR delta2c in 3/3 seeds in BOTH settings AND M>1 beats M=1 by >= 2x in 3/3.
PARTIAL iff it holds in one setting. FAILS otherwise, and on FAIL the empty cell is reported as tested
and closed — no re-parameterisation, no third variant.
PRIOR ART OBLIGATION: mixture-of-experts routing, multi-head linear attention, and gated/selective
state-space models are all relatives. A QUALIFIES licenses only "this cell, which our own audit showed
empty, is occupiable and beats the fixed-state incumbent" — never a novelty claim before a literature
check. The natural-data gate and a matched-compute win over a capable incumbent on an established
benchmark still stand between this and any result.

## 2026-08-14 — Q-1 REGISTERED DEVIATION (before code), and it makes the test HARDER for us

The identity gate passed at 1.4e-15 over six configurations including M=1 and C=T, so the registered
mechanism chunks exactly. But on reading the incumbent I found a strictly sharper instantiation and I
am switching to it, recording the deviation rather than quietly taking the easier one.
WHAT I NOTICED: Delta2Chunked is a 2-layer MULTI-HEAD DeltaNet. It ALREADY maintains H independent
fixed-size states -- and it CONCATENATES them. So the sentence this family exists to test ("multi-head
concatenates, C1 says competition is the operative thing") has a minimal instantiation: slots = heads,
and change NOTHING except the read.
DEVIATION: instead of adding M new slots with their own input-routed writes, Q-1 now keeps the
incumbent's write PATH BYTE-IDENTICAL (per-head delta rule, already linear in state, already chunked,
already verified) and replaces ONLY the output combination:
    incumbent   o_t = W_o [ head_1(t) ; ... ; head_H(t) ]          (concatenate, then project)
    ours        o_t = W_o sum_m softmax_m( q_t . a_m / tau ) head_m(t)   (compete over heads)
State size is identical BY CONSTRUCTION, the write is identical, the parallel form is identical, and
the only new parameters are H x dh slot addresses. One variable changes: whether the read competes.
WHY THIS IS THE CONSERVATIVE CHOICE AND NOT THE CONVENIENT ONE: I give up the extra write-routing
flexibility the registered version had, and I hand the incumbent exact parity on everything except the

## 2026-08-14 — Q-1: a confound in my own H-sweep control, caught BEFORE the control ran

Instantiating slots as heads means dh = dk/H, so TOTAL STATE = H * dh^2 = dk^2 / H. Measured:
  H=2  state/layer 2 x 76 x 76 = 11,552      non-emb 276,628 (-0.11% vs incumbent)
  H=4  state/layer 4 x 38 x 38 =  5,776      non-emb 277,240 (+0.11%)
  H=8  state/layer 8 x 19 x 19 =  2,888      non-emb 278,464 (+0.55%)
More slots means a SMALLER total state, by 4x across the sweep. So comparing ours at H=2 against ours
at H=8 would confound "more competing slots" with "less memory", and an advantage that grew with H
could be either. The registered control as written would not have controlled.
FIX, before any control run: the trend is taken over PAIRED DIFFERENCES, not raw numbers. At each H,
slotcomp(H) and delta2c(H) have IDENTICAL state and near-identical parameters, so their difference
isolates competition at that H; the state shrinkage hits both arms equally inside a pair. The
prediction stands in the corrected form: the PAIRED ADVANTAGE should grow with H, because competition
over two slots is nearly no competition. If the paired advantage is flat in H, the win is not from
competition and I report that whatever the headline says.
This is the seventh apparatus problem I have caught in this project and the first one caught before
the run it would have spoiled rather than after. The two-sided calibration discipline (f83a3ee) is
what made me look at the state column at all.

## 2026-08-17 — FAMILY O PRE-REGISTRATION (O-1, before code): does the benefit of spiking depend on
## whether the architecture is SPATIOTOPIC or DISTRIBUTED?

ORIGIN. Advisor-assigned project (N. Imam, 2026-08-16): adapt the non-spiking network of Wang, Sun,
Axel, Abbott & Yang (Neuron 2021, "Evolving the olfactory system with machine learning") to a spiking
network and demonstrate why the brain uses spikes.
WHY NOT THE OBVIOUS VERSION. "Convert to spikes, count synaptic operations, report an energy ratio" is
close to tautological: a sparsity-exploiting method wins on sparse input by construction, and the
operation-count proxy is exactly the measure this project already criticised in the spiking-LLM
literature. It would produce a number and no mechanism.
THE SHARPER QUESTION, which comes from putting two results side by side. Imam et al. (Sci Adv 2026)
separate cortical systems into SPATIOTOPIC (vision/audition/somatosensation: spatial-order index
0.90/0.89/0.86, receptive-field locality 0.97/0.99/0.84) and DISTRIBUTED (olfaction: 0.11 and 0.00) --
and show localized priors HELP the first group while imposing locality on olfaction sharply degrades
it. Independently, this project's parallelism audit (2026-08-13) found that a mechanism parallelises
iff its recurrence is linear in state with all nonlinearity in the read path; spiking is a write-path
nonlinearity and therefore forfeits batch parallelism.
Those two combine into a prediction neither makes alone: LOCALIZED ARCHITECTURES ARE PRECISELY THE ONES
THAT PARALLELISE WELL, so they have the most to lose by going event-driven. The benefit of spiking
should therefore be LARGER in a distributed architecture than in a spatiotopic one at matched task
difficulty. Olfaction is not merely a convenient test case for spikes -- on this account it is the
architecture where spikes cost least.

ARENA: odour classification in the Wang et al. structure -- ORN layer (one unit per receptor type),
convergence to glomeruli/PN layer, expansion to a sparse high-dimensional KC layer, linear readout.
Odours are sparse random mixtures over receptor activations with lognormal concentration and additive
noise. I am reconstructing this from the published description of the circuit, NOT from the paper
itself, which is paywalled at Cell and blocked at bioRxiv; every structural choice I could not verify
is listed in the code header as a reconstruction assumption, and the comparison is internal (my
architectures against each other), never a claim to reproduce their numbers.
ARMS -- a 2x2, which is the whole point:
  architecture: DISTRIBUTED (PN->KC connectivity global, non-local, as in olfaction)
                SPATIOTOPIC (PN->KC connectivity restricted to a local neighbourhood, matched fan-in
                and matched parameter count, so the ONLY difference is locality)
  neuron:       RATE (continuous activation)  vs  SPIKING (LIF, surrogate-gradient trained)
COST METRIC, fixed now and hardware-neutral: accuracy at matched SYNAPTIC EVENTS (non-zero
presynaptic activations x fan-out), reported alongside plain accuracy. I am not reporting a joules
estimate; this project has already recorded that operation-count energy claims are the weak link in
the spiking-LLM literature and I will not add another.
BARS:
  PREDICTION CONFIRMED iff (spiking - rate) accuracy-at-matched-events is greater in the DISTRIBUTED
    architecture than in the SPATIOTOPIC one, in 3/3 seeds, with the gap >= 0.05 absolute.
  REFUTED iff the difference is <= 0 in the same comparison, i.e. spikes help the localized
    architecture at least as much. That outcome would break the proposed link between Imam's duality
    and the parallelism boundary, and I would report it as such.
  INCONCLUSIVE otherwise, reported as the measured numbers with no mechanism claim.
CALIBRATION PROBE FIRST (standing discipline from 2026-08-13): single seed, short budget, confirming
the rate model on the distributed architecture neither saturates nor sits at chance. No full audit
until that passes.
SECOND, REGISTERED MANIPULATION (only if the probe passes): input regime. Sparse/event-driven
(intermittent plume-like presentation, low rate) vs dense/synchronous (all receptors driven every
step). The email to Imam states this prediction, so it is on the record: the spiking advantage should
appear in the sparse regime and vanish in the dense one.
STANDING GATES UNCHANGED: nothing here is an algorithm claim, and no result leaves this ledger without
the natural-data gate. This is an advisor-assigned mechanistic question, not a bid for the /goal.

## 2026-08-17 — O-2 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): does the spiking cost disadvantage INVERT under
## sparse, event-driven input? This is the mechanism test for "why the brain uses spikes".

WHAT O-1 LEFT. At dense synchronous input, spiking costs 2.75x the synaptic events of the rate model
AND is less accurate, at identical parameters. That is the half where parallelism has value. The
advisor's question -- why does the brain use spikes -- requires the other half, and it has not been run.
WHY THE O-1 REGIME WAS UNFAIR TO SPIKES, stated as the confound this prereg names: in O-1 the stimulus
was a single static analog vector. The rate model reads it ONCE; the spiking model must rate-code
magnitude across T=12 steps, so it pays a 12x temporal cost for information the rate model gets free.
That is not a property of spiking, it is a property of presenting a static stimulus to a temporal code.
THE FAIR VERSION, and the actual biological case: the stimulus is TEMPORALLY EXTENDED and INTERMITTENT
-- an odour plume, not a step function. Then BOTH models must integrate over T steps, and the question
becomes which one pays less per step.
MECHANISM PREDICTION: at low duty cycle the rate model still performs dense arithmetic on every step
(its activations are continuous and non-zero wherever input is non-zero), while the spiking model moves
only events. So the events ratio (spiking / rate) should DECREASE MONOTONICALLY as duty cycle falls,
and cross 1.0. If it never crosses, the "spikes are cheaper because the world is sparse in time"
argument does not hold in this apparatus and I will say so.

ARENA: O-1's odour classification, unchanged (100 classes, 4-receptor signatures, noise 1.0), but the
stimulus is delivered as a temporal stream over T=12 steps with DUTY CYCLE p: at each step, each
receptor independently emits its analog value with probability p and 0 otherwise. p = 1.0 reproduces a
synchronous presentation; p sweeps {1.0, 0.5, 0.3, 0.15}. Both arms see the SAME stream and must
integrate over all T steps -- the rate model accumulates its ReLU activations, the spiking model
integrates in its LIF membrane. Identical parameters, identical fan-in, distributed (olfactory)
architecture only, since O-1 found architecture does not matter (measured +0.0037 against a 0.05 bar).
COST METRIC unchanged and hardware-neutral: synaptic events = non-zero presynaptic activations x
fan-out, summed over all T steps. No joules estimate.
BARS, fixed now:
  INVERSION CONFIRMED iff the events ratio (spiking/rate) falls monotonically across the four duty
    cycles AND is < 1.0 at p <= 0.3 in 3/3 seeds, while spiking accuracy stays within 0.03 of rate at
    that duty cycle. Both conditions required: cheaper at the cost of accuracy is not an inversion.
  REFUTED iff the ratio stays >= 1.0 at every duty cycle tested in 3/3 seeds.
  PARTIAL iff the ratio crosses 1.0 but accuracy falls more than 0.03 behind, which I will report as
    "cheaper only by giving up accuracy" and NOT as a mechanism for why the brain spikes.
CALIBRATION PROBE FIRST (standing discipline): single seed at p=1.0 and p=0.15, confirming the rate
  model is neither saturated nor at floor at BOTH ends of the sweep. A regime where the task becomes
  impossible at low duty cycle would make the comparison vacuous, and that is the failure mode this
  probe exists to catch.
REGISTERED PRIOR: I expect the ratio to fall, because the arithmetic is straightforward -- but I do not
  know whether it crosses 1.0, because the rate model's activations also sparsify when its input is
  zero. If both sparsify at the same rate, there is no inversion and the argument fails. That is a real
  possibility and it is why this is worth running rather than asserting.

## 2026-08-17 — O-2 VERDICT (prereg 9b6b9be, scorer 8580d27 committed before the sweep finished):
## PARTIAL by the letter of the bar, and MY PREDICTION IS BACKWARDS. The ratio moves the wrong way.

Distributed architecture, identical parameters, both arms consuming the identical event stream and
integrating over T=12. 3 seeds per cell.
  duty  rate acc  spk acc   d_acc     rate ev   spk ev   ratio spk/rate
  1.00   0.4002    0.3657   -0.0345    3083.6    739.1    0.240
  0.50   0.3508    0.2736   -0.0773    1221.9    433.6    0.355
  0.30   0.3120    0.2016   -0.1105     467.0    296.1    0.634
  0.15   0.2561    0.1223   -0.1337     175.3    180.7    1.032
Registered bar required the ratio to fall MONOTONICALLY and cross below 1.0 at p<=0.3 with accuracy
within 0.03. Measured: the ratio RISES monotonically (0.240 -> 1.032), and the accuracy gap widens
(-0.035 -> -0.134). The formal verdict is PARTIAL only because the ratio is < 1 at p<=0.3 -- but it is
< 1 EVERYWHERE and largest in the DENSE regime, which is the opposite of the mechanism I registered.
Per the prereg's own clause, "cheaper only by giving up accuracy" is NOT an inversion, and here it is
not even the direction claimed.

MY PREDICTION WAS WRONG, AND THE REASON IS MEASURABLE. I registered: as input sparsifies, the rate
model keeps doing dense arithmetic while the spiking model moves only events, so the ratio should fall
and cross 1.0. The data say the rate model sparsifies FASTER: its events drop 17.6x (3083.6 -> 175.3)
while spiking drops only 4.1x (739.1 -> 180.7). The reason is straightforward once measured -- a ReLU
rate unit is exactly zero wherever its input is zero, so it costs nothing on silent channels, whereas
part of the spiking cost is membrane integration and threshold traffic that does NOT vanish with input
sparsity.
WHAT THIS OVERTURNS, stated as the substantive finding: the widely-repeated argument that "the world is
sparse in time, therefore spikes are cheaper" does not hold in this apparatus, and its direction is
reversed. Spiking's cost advantage here comes from BINARISATION under DENSE drive (0.240x events at
duty 1.0), not from temporal sparsity, and that advantage is erased exactly as the input becomes the
sparse event stream the argument invokes. I did not expect this and I am reporting it against my own
registered prediction.
CAVEAT THAT LIMITS THE CLAIM, and it is real: at low duty the task itself degrades for both arms
(rate 0.400 -> 0.256), so the low-duty cells are measured in a regime where less information is
present. The ratio comparison is still internally valid -- both arms see the identical stream -- but the
accuracy gap at p=0.15 is partly a harder-task effect and should not be read as spiking failing to
learn. A cleaner version would hold task difficulty constant while varying only temporal spread, and
that is a different experiment.
STATUS: two measured results now exist for the advisor's project -- the dense-regime cost picture
(O-1) and this duty-cycle reversal. Neither is an algorithm and neither has passed a natural-data gate.
The next step, unregistered, would be the difficulty-controlled version named in the caveat.

## 2026-08-17 — O-3 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): the difficulty-controlled experiment O-2's own
## caveat named — vary TEMPORAL SPREAD at constant task information.

WHY. O-2's manipulation confounded temporal sparsity with task difficulty: lowering the duty cycle
removed stimulus frames, so the low-duty cells measured a harder task (rate accuracy fell
0.400 -> 0.256 across the sweep). The folk argument O-2 tested — "the world is sparse in time,
therefore spikes are cheaper" — is a claim about temporal ARRANGEMENT, not about how much signal
exists. O-3 isolates arrangement.

DESIGN. Hold the number of stimulus-bearing frames fixed at K=12 (O-2's densest cell) and embed them
at uniformly random positions in a window of T in {12, 24, 48, 96}, so duty falls 1.00 -> 0.125 while
the stimulus content per sample is IDENTICAL across cells. Everything else is o2.py verbatim:
distributed (olfactory) architecture, identical parameters in both arms, both arms consuming the
identical stream, the rate arm accumulating its ReLU activations and the spiking arm integrating in
its LIF membrane over all T frames. Whatever policy o2.py applies to non-stimulus frames (noise or
silence) is kept byte-identical — the intervention is the placement schedule and NOTHING else.
3 seeds per cell. COST METRIC unchanged and hardware-neutral: synaptic events = non-zero presynaptic
activations x fan-out, summed over all T frames. The T=12 cell reproduces O-2's duty-1.0 cell
(measured ratio 0.240) and serves as a consistency anchor.

CALIBRATION PROBE FIRST (standing discipline): single seed at T=12 and T=96. The difficulty control
HOLDS iff rate accuracy at T=96 is within 0.05 absolute of rate accuracy at T=12, and neither cell is
saturated or at floor. If the control fails — if spreading the same 12 frames over 96 steps degrades
the rate arm by more than 0.05 — then this arena cannot separate arrangement from difficulty either;
I report that verbatim and STOP, no redesign inside this registration.

BARS, fixed now (ratio_T = spiking events / rate events at window T):
  FOLK ARGUMENT SUPPORTED iff the ratio falls monotonically over the four windows AND ratio at
    T=96 < 1.0 in 3/3 seeds AND spiking accuracy is within 0.03 of rate at T=96, with the difficulty
    control holding.
  REVERSAL CONFIRMED iff ratio at T=96 > ratio at T=12 in 3/3 seeds, with the difficulty control

## 2026-08-17 — O-2 LIMITATION, added after the verdict: my cost metric is not neutral between the
## two arms, and the conclusion is metric-dependent.

Prompted by the question "in which apparatus?", I re-examined my own measure and found a defect that
bounds the O-2 conclusion rather than decorating it.
THE METRIC AS DEFINED: synaptic events = non-zero presynaptic activations x fan-in (7), summed over
T=12, computed IDENTICALLY for both arms. That identical treatment is exactly the problem. A rate
arm event is a MULTIPLY-ACCUMULATE; a spiking arm event is an ACCUMULATE, because the presynaptic
value is binary. Counting them as equal-cost silently charges the spiking arm the rate arm's price.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE HEADLINE: the O-2 claim was that the events ratio rises with sparsity and reaches
1.032 at duty 0.15, i.e. spiking's advantage is erased. Under any weighting that charges a multiply
more than an add -- which every real substrate does -- the 1.032 crossing moves back below 1.0 and the
erasure may not occur. So the honest statement is narrower than what I wrote:
  measured: under a metric that counts multiply-accumulate and accumulate as equal, the relative cost
  advantage of a RATE-CODED spiking network vanishes as input sparsifies.
  NOT established: that spiking loses its advantage in the sparse regime on any hardware-weighted
  measure.
The direction of the ratio (rising, 0.240 -> 1.032) stands as measured and is still the opposite of
what I pre-registered. What does not stand is the stronger reading that the sparse-world argument is
refuted; it is refuted only under an unweighted event count.
TWO FURTHER LIMITS OF THIS APPARATUS, recorded in the same place so the scope is in one entry:
 (1) The network is a RECONSTRUCTION from the published description of the Wang et al. circuit, not the
     paper's model (Cell paywalled, bioRxiv Cloudflare-blocked). All comparisons are internal.
 (2) Only ONE spike code was tested: rate coding via Bernoulli sampling of the PN layer. Temporal codes
     (time-to-first-spike, phase) are the ones most plausibly able to exploit temporal sparsity, and
     they were not tested at all. "Spiking" in O-1/O-2 means "rate-coded spiking", not spiking in general.
WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: re-score the existing runs under a weighted cost (multiply = k x add, k swept),
report the crossing duty as a function of k, and separately implement a time-to-first-spike arm. Both
are cheap; neither is registered. The weighted re-score in particular uses data already on disk.

## 2026-08-17 — O-2W PRE-REGISTRATION (before computing): weighted re-score of the O-2 data, to test
## whether the "erasure" I reported is an artifact of my own unweighted metric.

CONFOUND NAMED (c87ba2f): my synaptic-event count treats a rate-arm event and a spiking-arm event as
equal cost. They are not. A rate synaptic operation is a MULTIPLY-ACCUMULATE (the presynaptic value is
continuous); a spiking synaptic operation is an ACCUMULATE (the presynaptic value is binary, so w*1 = w).
WEIGHTING, fixed before computing. Let k = cost(MAC) / cost(AC) in the same units. Weighted cost is
  rate    : events_rate    * k
  spiking : events_spiking * 1
k is swept over {1, 2, 3, 5, 7}. Justification for that range, so it is not chosen to suit the answer:
k=1 is the degenerate case equivalent to my original metric's assumption, and the upper end reflects
commonly cited CMOS figures where a 32-bit float MAC is roughly 5x a float add and an INT8 MAC roughly
7x an INT8 add. I am not claiming those constants are exact for any specific substrate; the point of
the sweep is to find the k at which the conclusion flips, and to report it.
REGISTERED READING, fixed now:
  If the weighted ratio (spiking/rate) is < 1.0 at EVERY duty cycle for all k >= 2, then the O-2
    headline claim -- that spiking's advantage is ERASED in the sparse regime -- is VOID as an artifact
    of the unweighted metric, and I will retract that sentence in the ledger rather than soften it.
  If the ratio still reaches >= 1.0 at duty 0.15 for k in the 3-7 range, the O-2 claim survives with
    the weighting made explicit.
  Either way the DIRECTIONAL result stands as separately measured: the unweighted ratio rises with
    sparsity (0.240 -> 1.032), contrary to my original pre-registered prediction. Weighting changes the
    level, not the slope, and I will state which of the two claims each number supports.
NO NEW RUNS. This re-scores JSONs already on disk (runs/o2/), so nothing about the underlying
measurement changes. The scorer is written before the numbers are read.
