## 2026-08-20 — V-14 VERDICT: COMPOUNDING ACCOUNT NOT SUPPORTED. I am retracting the explanation I
## registered, as the prereg required.

Sweep of the identification load on a fixed arena (2-hop, question embedded), 3 seeds per cell:
  k (bindings/level)   2       4       8      16      24      32
  symbols to identify  4       8      16      32      48      64
  floor              .5?     .5?     .5?     .5?    .534    .515
  parser              --      --      --      --    .951    .934
  probe_argmax        --      --      --      --    .535    .529
  R = (probe-floor)/(parser-floor)  -1.371  -0.142  -0.030  -0.012  +0.003  +0.032
MONOTONE: FALSE (inversions at k=2 and k=4). BOUNDARY BRACKETED: FALSE -- R never reaches 0.50 at ANY k,
including k=2 where only four symbols must be identified, and at k=2 the remedy arm is BELOW the floor.
The prereg said: "If R is flat or non-monotone the account 'identification errors compound with count' is
wrong and I will say so." It is wrong. Saying so.
SO WHY DOES THE REMEDY WORK ON SYSCHAIN AT 99% AND NOWHERE ELSE? Not symbol count -- k=2 kills it. The
difference I can point to, and have not measured, is WHAT THE SYMBOL LOOKS LIKE. On SysChain identity is a
two-hex-digit marker in a fixed pattern, and A_extract there was .9986. On these arenas the identity is a
decimal integer inside braces, which tokenises inconsistently, so a span-mean pooled linear head may simply
be unable to read it. If A_extract is low here, the remedy fails for a completely different reason than the
one I proposed: identity is not recoverable at all, rather than recoverable but compounding.

## V-16 PRE-REGISTRATION (before code): measure A_extract on the arena where the remedy fails.
DESIGN: the same probe that reached A_extract = .9986 on SysChain -- a linear head over span-mean-pooled
frozen states, TOLD the span, predicting the symbol index -- applied to arena C's spans, 3 seeds. Chance is
1/64 = .0156.
BARS:
  IDENTITY NOT RECOVERABLE iff A_extract <= 0.50 in 3/3. Then the remedy's failure on these arenas is
    explained by the encoder being unable to read the symbol, the compounding story is dead, and the paper
    reports that the remedy needs a symbol FORM the frozen model can decode -- a statement about the input
    representation rather than about binding.
  IDENTITY RECOVERABLE iff A_extract >= 0.90 in 3/3. Then identity IS available and the remedy still fails,
    which would mean the arg-max handover loses something the probe has, and I would have no explanation and
    would say so.
  INTERMEDIATE otherwise.
REGISTERED EXPECTATION: NOT RECOVERABLE, i.e. A_extract well under .50, because decimal integers inside
braces do not tokenise into a stable span the way two-hex-digit markers do. I have now been wrong twice in
a row about this mechanism (P3 and the compounding account), so this expectation is recorded with that
history attached.

  arena C (rule-selected): LoRA r=16 .5150 .5175 .5150 (mean .5158, 10,490,882 trainable) against the

  arena B (role binding): LoRA .980 .895 .510 (mean .7950) against parser .9960 -- gaps +1.6 / +10.1 /

WHAT THIS LICENSES FOR THE "WHY VSA" QUESTION, stated with its limit: on an arena whose split requires
generalising to symbol combinations never seen in training, parameter-efficient fine-tuning of the language
model does not get off the floor while the symbolic route does. That is a reason to want the symbolic route
that does not depend on accuracy over seen combinations -- where LoRA remains stronger and simpler. It is
one arena, and on the second arena LoRA is merely unreliable rather than incapable.

## 2026-08-20 — V-16 VERDICT: IDENTITY RECOVERABLE (A_extract = .9963, chance .0156). My registered
## expectation was wrong for the THIRD time on this mechanism. And the result exposes an implementation
## deficiency in my own remedy arm rather than a property of binding.

A dedicated linear head over span-mean-pooled frozen states, told the span, recovers arena C's 64-way symbol
at .9965 / .9965 / .9959 -- essentially the same as SysChain's .9986. So the symbol FORM hypothesis from
00c1d9a is dead too: decimal integers in braces are as decodable as two-hex markers. Registered
expectation was "NOT RECOVERABLE, well under .50". Wrong.

WHAT THE COMPARISON EXPOSES, and it is my error rather than an unexplained phenomenon:
                          standalone probe (V-16)     the remedy arm's id_head (V-13)
  epochs                        40                          2
  batch                        256                          4
  learning rate               1e-3                       3e-4
  objective              identity only              identity + task loss, jointly
  measured accuracy           .9963                     NEVER MEASURED
The remedy arm trains its identity head for 2 epochs at lr 3e-4 with batch 4 while a properly trained head
needs 40 epochs at lr 1e-3 with batch 256 to reach .996. I never instrumented the arm's internal identity
accuracy, so I have been attributing the arm's failure to binding, to symbol count, and to symbol form,
while the arm may simply never have learned to identify symbols at all.
This is not a new hypothesis competing with the others. It is the possibility that my arm DOES NOT IMPLEMENT
WHAT IT CLAIMS: "a supervised probe whose arg-max indexes the codebook" is only that if the probe is
actually trained. Three explanations were offered and two refuted while the arm's central component went
unmeasured. That is the same failure mode this project has been auditing in others' work, and it is mine.

## 2026-08-20 — A BINDING BUG IN MY OWN ARENA-C ARM INVALIDATES THREE ARMS, V-14 ENTIRELY, AND THE
## VERDICT I WAS ABOUT TO WRITE INTO THE PAPER. Found by refusing to accept a result that was almost
## logically impossible.

WHAT FORCED THE LOOK. fast17 measured a frozen identity head at .9983 top-1 on held-out spans and the
binding chain driven by it at .4900, while a hand scan supplying the same indices reaches .9340. If the head
is right on 99.83% of spans, its arg-max IS the true index on 99.83% of spans, so the two arms should agree
to within a point. A 44-point gap between "the true index" and "a 99.83%-accurate estimate of the true
index" is not a finding; it is a bug. I read the code instead of writing the verdict.

THE BUG, in v13.py BindArm.sims:
    mem = sum over pairs of  bind( self.vec(H[b], bb, sp), self.vec(H[b], aa, sp) )
Both calls pass THE SAME SPAN sp. For mode parser and consistent, vec() returns self.sym[sid] using the
PASSED INDEX, so those arms bind value-to-key correctly. For spans, probe_argmax and frozen_cont, vec()
IGNORES sid and derives the vector from sp -- so both calls return the identical vector and the arm computes
bind(v, v), binding each pair's value to ITSELF instead of to its key. The span covers the whole [Rxx]{j}
match, so one span carries two symbols and I never split it.

WHAT IS RETRACTED:
  V-13 bar (b) spans .480, bar (c) probe_argmax .529 and frozen_cont .533 -- all three arms invalid.
  V-14 in its entirety: the k-sweep's probe_argmax column is this arm at every k, which is exactly why it
    was pinned near .51 INDEPENDENT of k. I flagged that flatness as "the component is not working" and was
    right about the symptom while proposing three wrong causes.
  fast17 and V-17's NOT THE CAUSE verdict: the arm they tested was broken, so they measured nothing about
    identity supervision.
  The manuscript's arena-C column for those three rows, and its "remedy recovers 3%" figure for C.
WHAT SURVIVES:
  V-13 bar (a): parser .9340 and consistent .9293 use the passed indices and are unaffected. The +41.9pp
    parser-over-floor result stands.
  Arenas A and B are NOT affected: v11.py binds filler-from-span with role-from-a-fixed-codebook, so only
    one vector per pair is derived and the bug cannot occur there. Arena B's spans .5073, probe_argmax
    .8627 and frozen_cont .8993 stand.
  V-16's A_extract .9963 stands -- a standalone probe, not this arm.
  The three cross-arena invariants stand on A and B: exact rows work, consistency-not-correctness, and a
    projection trained through the binding loss failing. Arena C can no longer be cited for the third until
    it is re-run.
FIX: record the role sub-span and the filler sub-span separately (the regex already groups them) and let
each derived vector come from its own span. Then re-run V-13's three derived arms and V-14.
WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT THE SESSION, recorded because it is the honest summary: I proposed four explanations
for this arm's failure -- compounding with symbol count, symbol form, no explanation, and an under-trained
identity head -- and refuted all four by measurement, while the arm itself had never computed the binding
chain it claimed to. Every one of those four investigations was downstream of an uninstrumented apparatus
error of mine. The one thing that caught it was a number too extreme to be a mechanism.

## 2026-08-20 — THE FIX WORKS, AND IT DISSOLVES THE ENTIRE STORY I TOLD TODAY ABOUT THE REMEDY.

Smoke test of the corrected arm on arena C (1 seed, 200 train / 150 test, 1 epoch):
  floor .5000 | parser .9200 | probe_argmax .9000 | spans .4867
Against the buggy version on the same arena: probe_argmax .529 -> .9000. The remedy arm now nearly matches
the hand-scan ceiling, and spans stays at the floor, which is the diagnosis holding.

WHAT THIS RETRACTS, beyond the numbers already withdrawn. Everything I said today about the remedy having a
FAILURE BOUNDARY is gone:
  the "99% / 26% / 3% across arenas" pattern -- an artifact of the bug on C;
  the "boundary exists but we cannot locate it" framing -- there was no boundary on C;
  the compounding-with-symbol-count account (already refuted by V-14, itself now void);
  the symbol-form account (already refuted by V-16, which stands but was answering a question the bug had
    manufactured);
  the under-trained-head account (refuted by fast17, which was measuring the broken arm);
  and the "we report it as unexplained" position now in the manuscript, which was honest about a phenomenon
    that did not exist.
The corrected picture is simpler and stronger: the remedy works where it has been correctly implemented --
arena A .914 against a .918 ceiling, arena C .900 against .920 -- and underperforms by about 13pp on arena
B (.8627 against .9960), where the floor is .8147 and the available range is only 18pp.
NOTE ON ARENA B, so the comparison is not overstated: B's arm derives only the filler from text and takes
the role from the codebook index, so it is structurally EASIER than the corrected C arm, which derives both.
B nonetheless recovers less. That is a real residual difference and it is now the only remedy anomaly left.
It may be the compressed range at a .81 floor rather than anything mechanistic; I am not going to guess
again before measuring.
RERUNS QUEUED: V-13's three derived arms at full budget and 3 seeds, and V-14's sweep, both with the fixed
arm. The manuscript's arena-C entries stay WITHDRAWN until those land.
THE LESSON I AM RECORDING ABOUT MY OWN PROCESS, since this is the fourth apparatus fault on this one
experiment: I diagnosed a symptom correctly ("probe_argmax is flat in k, which looks like a component not
working") and then proposed three mechanisms for it instead of reading fifteen lines of my own code. Reading
the code was cheaper than any of the three experiments I ran to explain it.

## 2026-08-20 -- V-19 PREREG. Chain depth, for the CONTINUOUS handover. Registered before the run.

WHY. With the span faults fixed, the discrete handover is flat everywhere I can vary it: 99-100% recovery
across three arenas and every symbol count from 4 to 64. The continuous handover is not. Recomputed from the
artifacts: frozen_cont recovers (fc - floor)/(parser - floor) = 94% on arena B (single hop, .9853 against
floor .8147 parser .9960), 98% on arena C (two hops, .9240 / .5153 / .9340), and 39% on arena A (three hops,
.670 / .509 / .918). Depth is the one axis those three differ on that has a mechanism behind it, and the
mechanism is visible in the code rather than inferred: inside sims() each level replaces the running key with
the most similar candidate, and in parser/probe_argmax mode the candidates ARE codebook rows so that step is
idempotent, while in frozen_cont mode they are continuous projections so it is not. Exact rows cannot
accumulate error across levels; approximations can.

This is the axis I withdrew a claim about earlier, and I want to be explicit about why registering it again
is not a rescue attempt. What I withdrew was a boundary on the SYMBOL-COUNT axis for the DISCRETE route,
which was an artifact of the broken arm. This registers the DEPTH axis for the CONTINUOUS route, on the
corrected apparatus, with a mechanism stated in advance and a prediction that can fail.

DESIGN. Arena C's harness verbatim -- 32 bindings per level, 64 symbols, query embedded mid-sequence --
sweeping HOPS over 1,2,3,4. Bindings per level held constant, so superposition SNR per level does not move
and only the count of sequential unbind-and-clean steps does. Arms floor, parser, probe_argmax, frozen_cont;
seeds 42/123/456.

TRUNCATION, handled before the fact. Arena C ran at max_len=768, which fits 64 markers and does NOT fit the
128 that four levels produce; levels render in order, so truncation would silently delete the DEEPEST level
and leave its spans dangling -- and it would do so in exactly the direction that manufactures the effect I am
predicting. max_len is raised to 2048 at every depth, and the arena asserts per row that all HOPS*N_CTX
markers survived with every level at full complement, aborting the run rather than reporting a depth effect
that is really a context-length effect. Depth 2 is a regression control: it must reproduce arena C, whose
numbers were taken at 768.

ADMISSION GATE, registered: a depth is used only if parser - floor >= 0.20 in the seed mean. Below that the
arena has too little headroom for a recovery fraction to mean anything, and deep chains are expected to cost
the parser accuracy.

BARS.
  MECHANISM CONFIRMED  iff R_cont(shallowest admitted) - R_cont(deepest admitted) >= 0.25
                       AND R_disc >= 0.90 at EVERY admitted depth
  REFUTED              iff R_cont >= 0.90 at every admitted depth (no compounding; then arena A's 39% has
                       nothing to do with depth and goes back to being unexplained, and I will say so)
  INTERMEDIATE         anything else -> reported as a measured trend with its size, not as a mechanism
  VOID                 fewer than two admitted depths
Also reported, not gated: whether the drop holds seed-for-seed rather than only in the mean.
DIRECTION I EXPECT: CONFIRMED. If REFUTED, the paper keeps the discrete-versus-continuous contrast as an
observation and drops the depth explanation entirely.

## 2026-08-21 -- npj FORMAT COMPLIANCE, checked against the official guide rather than from memory.

I had been treating the npj variant as compliant on the strength of three remembered rules (title <= 15
words, abstract <= 150, Results needs subheadings). Fetching the actual document -- 'Brief guide for
submission to Nature Partner Journals', revised 2018-11-28 -- turned up six requirements the file was
failing, one of which I had the wrong version of:

  1. TITLE. The guide bars not only punctuation but ACTIVE VERBS. "... requires a supervised symbol code"
     has one. The npj variant is retitled to a noun phrase, "Supervised symbol codes as a requirement for
     vector symbolic binding over language model states", 14 words. The conference variant keeps the verb
     form, which is idiomatic there.
  2. "Avoid 'Introduction' as a heading." The file had one. Removed; the opening now runs unheaded.
  3. METHODS. Required in all online original research articles and the file had none -- the material was
     spread across Background, Hybrid Model Architecture and Experimental Setup, in conference order.
     Restructured to the portfolio's order: opening / Results / Related Work / Discussion / Methods.
  4. DATA AVAILABILITY as a separate section after Methods and before the References: added.
  5. CODE AVAILABILITY under that heading inside Methods: added, and it states the pre-registration ledger
     as part of the release rather than as a courtesy.
  6. AUTHOR CONTRIBUTIONS and COMPETING INTERESTS statements: both required, both were absent, both added.
     The contributions statement names one author because that is who the manuscript currently lists;
     co-authorship is the user's call and remains open.
Also removed the ICML/NeurIPS Impact Statement boilerplate, which has no place in an npj submission.

The restructure is what brought the length into range rather than any cutting: moving the theory and
architecture into Methods leaves the main text at 4,106 words against a 5,000 limit, with Methods at 1,322
against 3,000. Display items 8 of 10, references 35 of 70, abstract exactly 150 and unreferenced.

verify_npj.py added, and this is the point of it: the claim "the manuscript meets the content-type
requirements" is now a script that returns 18/18 with an exit code, not something I assert. Worth stating
plainly that the guide ALSO says initial submissions are treated flexibly on format -- so none of this was a
gate. It was wrong in the file, it is now right, and the reason to fix it is that a referee reading a
manuscript in the wrong shape starts by wondering what else was not checked.

## 2026-08-21 -- BIBLIOGRAPHY CORRECTION and one scope limit that bounds the central claim.

A factual error of mine, found while checking rather than while being challenged. The entry for the HDC/VSA
survey read "IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems, 2022. To appear" and merged two
separate papers into one citation. Both parts are in ACM Computing Surveys and both are published: Part I,
Kleyko, Rachkovskij, Osipov and Rahimi, 55(6) article 130, 2022; Part II, same authors, 55(9) article 175,
2023. Split into two correct entries. Verified against the publisher records, not from memory -- which is
how the error got in.

Added, because a referee in this literature will ask it first: Schlegel, Neubert and Protzel, "A comparison
of vector symbolic architectures", Artificial Intelligence Review 55(6):4523-4555, 2022. It is the reference
for the question "why HRR and not one of the other models", and the paper had no answer to that question at
all. It now has one, stated as a limit rather than a defence: every measurement here uses circular-convolution
binding with a nearest-neighbour cleanup. The argument for why EXACTNESS rather than accuracy is what binding
needs -- cleanup returns a codebook row unchanged and returns an approximation changed -- applies to any model
whose chain passes through a cleanup step, which is most of them, but it is an argument tested in one algebra.
Whether the handover behaves the same way under multiply-add-permute, binary sparse or Fourier binding is
open, and a self-inverse binding with no cleanup step might not show the effect at all.

Two things I am deliberately NOT doing. Not padding the reference list toward the guest editors: the two
entries added are the ones the manuscript actually argues against, one of them because it exposes a gap in my
own scope. And not claiming generality the runs do not support -- the scope limit is in the main text, in the
subsection whose job is to say what was not measured, not in an appendix.

## 2026-08-21 -- THEORY SECTION, read adversarially. Three more defects, one of them a misattribution.

Continuing the read-through that caught the stale Discussion. The Methods theory block had:

(1) MISATTRIBUTION. "Our analysis focuses on Holographic Reduced Representations (HRR) (Kanerva, 2009)".
HRR is Plate's model; Kanerva 2009 is the hyperdimensional-computing formulation of the same family. Getting
the attribution wrong on the paper's own central operation, in a submission to a collection edited by people
who work on exactly this, is the kind of error that costs more than it should. Corrected, with both credited
for what each did.

(2) A GENERALITY CLAIM CONTRADICTING MY OWN SCOPE LIMIT. The same sentence continued "though similar results
hold for other VSA variants" -- while the Results section now says explicitly that we tested one algebra and
do not claim transfer to multiply-add-permute, binary sparse or Fourier binding. One of the two had to go and
it was not the honest one. Replaced with a pointer to the limit.

(3) A CORRECTED "WE DID NOT TEST THIS", in the direction of claiming MORE rather than less. The capacity
corollary said "We did not test this prediction empirically; the ablation that would have is not among the
runs we can verify." That was true when written and is no longer: V-14's symbol-count sweep tests it
directly, because the parser arm is handed exact codebook rows and its only remaining error source IS
superposition interference. Its accuracy falls monotonically with bindings per level -- 1.000, .998, .9967,
.972, .9507, .934 at k = 2, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32 -- which is the predicted direction. Stated as a direction only;
we do not fit the SNR expression and claim nothing quantitative from it. verify_paper7 extended to assert all
six values and the monotonicity (now 17 checks, 0 mismatched).

(4) REMOVED: an unproven, never-cited Proposition asserting the expressiveness of the hybrid model ("can
express all functions in the closure of LLM representations under VSA algebra"). It is vacuous as stated, it
has no proof, nothing in the paper references it, and it sits in a manuscript whose stated position is that
it contributes no new theory. Deleted rather than defended.

## 2026-08-21 -- TWO WRONG PROOFS, REMOVED RATHER THAN REPAIRED.

The appendix carried two-line proof sketches for both HRR properties. Read properly, both are wrong, and
wrong in ways a referee from this literature spots on sight:

BINDING. The sketch wrote ||b' - b||^2 = sum_k (a_k^* a_k - 1) b_k / |a_k|^2 -- a squared norm on the left,
an un-modulused sum of complex coefficients on the right, so the equation does not typecheck. It then
"applied Hoeffding's inequality to the deviation of |a_k|^2". Hoeffding requires bounded variables and
|a_k|^2 is exponentially distributed for Gaussian a, so the hypothesis fails; the step needs a chi-square
concentration or Bernstein argument.

CAPACITY. The sketch set the signal at ||b_j||^2 = 1 and the crosstalk at k-1 terms of unit expected norm.
From those two lines SNR = 1/(k-1) follows. The theorem states d/(k-1 + O(1/sqrt d)). The factor of d belongs
to a different normalisation than the one the proof sets up, so the stated result -- which IS the classical
one -- does not follow from the argument given for it.

Both removed. This paper's stated position is that these properties are classical and not its contribution,
which makes the correct response a citation, not a repair: Plate (1995) and Plate (2003) for binding fidelity
and the O(1/d) crosstalk scaling, Frady, Kleyko & Sommer (2018) for the information-theoretic capacity form,
with Kleyko et al. (2022) Section 2 collecting both. The appendix now says plainly what was wrong with the
sketches it used to contain, because a reader who remembers the earlier version deserves to know it was
withdrawn on purpose. The theorem environments are retitled to carry their attribution in the statement
itself -- "not a contribution of this paper" is now in the theorem header, where a skimming reader sees it.

Also softened a claim in the same pass that was stronger than its source: the corollary was headed "Optimal
Single Binding" and said each added binding "degrad[es] SNR linearly". It is now headed "Interference grows
with the number of superposed bindings" and says the ratio falls, which is what the cited results support and
what V-14 measured.

## 2026-08-21 -- TWO NUMBERS THAT TRACED BUT COULD NOT BE READ, plus a confound the read-through surfaced.

Both of these passed every checker. Neither was wrong. Both were unreadable in context, which for a referee
amounts to the same thing.

(1) TWO FLOORS FOR ONE ARENA. The placement survey bolds the selected configuration at a floor of .474; the
mechanism table gives arena C's floor as .515. Same nominal configuration, two numbers, no explanation
anywhere in the paper. Traced: the survey trains its probe for SIXTY epochs on 600 instances over two seeds
(floor_survey.py defaults), while the mechanism experiment re-measures the floor at the budget every arm
there shares -- two epochs on 800 instances over three seeds. Both are correct measurements of different
things. The paper now says so, and says which direction it cuts: selection uses the better-trained and
therefore more conservative estimate, which makes the selection harder to game, while effect sizes are always
computed against the floor measured beside the arms compared to it.

(2) .63 vs .67 FOR THE SAME ARM. Related Work said the binding loss "degraded it from 0.63 to 0.50" while the
mechanism table gives the same arm as .670. Traced to the V-10 synthesis: .673 is the frozen projection WITH
its two readout scalars trained, .63 is the same projection at initialisation before the scalars, .50 is what
it becomes when trained through the binding loss. So the .63 -> .50 comparison is the correct one for a
degradation claim -- both sides measured before the readout is fitted -- and the text now states all three
values and which pair the claim rests on.

A CONFOUND, checked rather than assumed. The cross-arena continuous-recovery figures (39% at three hops, 94%
at one, 98% at two) invited a fidelity explanation: maybe the projection simply fits better in some arenas.
Measured cosine fidelities say the opposite. Arena A is fitted BEST, at 99.8%, and does WORST at 39%. Arena B
is 87.5% and recovers 94%; arena C is 90.5% and recovers 98%. A fidelity confound would order these the other
way round, so approximation quality is not what separates the arenas. This is also why V-19 holds the arena
fixed and varies only depth: within the sweep, fidelity is flat at .9105/.9103/.9100 (depth 1) and
.9061/.9048 (depth 2), so whatever the sweep shows is not a fidelity effect. Recorded now, before the deeper
levels land.

## 2026-08-21 -- V-20 PREREG. Is arena A's continuous shortfall its PARAMETERS or its ARM? Registered before
## the run, and before V-19's depth 4 has landed.

WHY. Arena A reports frozen_cont recovering 39% of the parser-over-floor gap at three hops. V-19's d=3 cell,
also three hops on the corrected v13 harness, recovers 99.6%. Sixty points at the same depth, on two
different implementations of the same arm. Arena A differs in three measurable ways: 16 bindings per level
against 32, a 256-symbol vocabulary against 64, and the arm implementation (v9.py ExtractThenBind against
v13.py BindArm). VSA_DIM is already 2048 in both, so that one is not a difference. This run holds the
corrected harness fixed and moves the two numeric parameters to arena A's values, separating the parameter
explanation from the implementation explanation.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO, so the result is not over-read: it does not reproduce arena A's generator. Arena A renders
[R..]/[X..]/[Y..] markers with brace-integer fillers under a different tokenisation. A null here therefore
does not prove arena A's number wrong -- it removes the parameter explanation and leaves the implementation
as the remaining candidate, which is the honest state given that this arm family has produced three faults.

WHAT IS AT STAKE, and it is the headline rather than a loose end. "Exactness rather than accuracy is what the
algebra requires of an encoder" appears in the abstract prose, the Discussion and the contributions
paragraph, and it rests on arena A alone against six corrected measurements (B 94%, C 98%, V-19 d=1/2/3
1.02/0.98/1.00). If arena A's parameters do not reproduce the shortfall, that claim has no support left and
the paper's central statement becomes one about the training signal. If they DO reproduce it, the claim
survives scoped to the many-symbols regime, and what is exonerated is arena A's implementation rather than
the claim being rescued.

DESIGN. v13's arena at HOPS=3, N_CTX=16, N_SYM=256, VSA_DIM=2048, max_len=2048 with the same per-row
no-truncation assertion V-19 uses. Arms floor, parser, probe_argmax, frozen_cont; seeds 42/123/456; the same
800/500 instances and 2 epochs every arm in this family shares.

BARS.
  VOID                 if the arena is not admitted (parser - floor < 0.20) or R_disc < 0.90 -- if the
                       DISCRETE handover fails here too, there is no reference for a continuous comparison
  ARTIFACT SUSPECTED   iff R_cont >= 0.90
  REGIME REAL          iff R_cont <= 0.60
  INTERMEDIATE         otherwise -> report the measured value, license neither reading
DIRECTION I EXPECT: ARTIFACT SUSPECTED. Stating it because I have now been wrong about this arm family three
times in the same direction -- each time assuming a mechanism where the answer was the apparatus -- and once
in the other direction, when I assumed the LoRA control was ungradiented and it was merely under-budgeted.

## 2026-08-21 -- A DEFECT I INTRODUCED TODAY, caught while preparing to re-measure arena A. Two different
## quantities were compared as if they were one.

Setting up the arena A re-measurement required knowing what arena A's continuous arm actually is. It is V-9's

ARG-MAX ACCURACY, the rate at which projecting and then snapping to the nearest codebook row returns the
correct symbol. v11 and v13 report "cos fidelity ~= 0.906", computed as 1 - mean(1 - cos(proj(span),
codebook[true_id])) -- a MEAN COSINE SIMILARITY. A projection at mean cosine 0.906 can easily have >99%
arg-max accuracy, because the wrong rows are near-orthogonal. The two numbers measure different things and
0.998 versus 0.906 says nothing about which code is better.

I built an argument on that comparison this morning: "arena A reports the highest fitted fidelity of any arena
(99.8%) together with the lowest recovery (39%) ... better code, worse performance", and called the inversion
unexplained. There is no inversion. Arena A's cosine fidelity is simply UNMEASURED. The argument was mine,
it was wrong, and it is the same species of error this paper documents -- two quantities with similar names
treated as one metric.

WHERE IT REACHED. Only one sentence of the manuscript, in Related Work, which called arena A's 99.8% a
"cosine fidelity". Corrected, and the correction makes the sentence sharper rather than weaker: a projection
whose nearest codebook row is the correct one 99.8% of the time still scores .63 read continuously (.673 with
its scalars trained) against a hand scan at .918. The table was not affected -- the row I added prints
recovery fractions, which are comparable -- and the Discussion's outlier sentence never mentioned fidelity.
The ledger entry at 95a797d and the V-20 entry both contain the bad comparison and are left standing with
this correction appended, because a ledger that gets edited is not a ledger.

points the fidelity trend rests on (.875 -> .94, .906 -> .976, .91 -> ~1.00, .66 -> .715) are all mean

point on that line; it is a point on a different axis, and on ITS axis it says something V-21 is about to test

## 2026-08-21 -- V-22 PREREG. Remove the hand-written span scanner. Registered before the run, at the user's
## direction to attack the paper's biggest weakness rather than write around it.

WHY THIS ONE. Every mechanism result in this paper runs on spans located by a regex that knows the arena's
bracket syntax. So the successful pipeline is "hand-written span finder plus learned identity reader", the
manuscript says so in its own limitations, and it is the single thing a referee is most likely to reject on.
Rewriting cannot fix it. Only removing the scanner can.

WHAT IS REPLACED AND WHAT IS NOT, stated precisely so the result cannot be over-read. The regex is replaced by
a three-way per-token classifier over the frozen hidden states -- outside / role-token / filler-token -- a
single linear layer on the 2560-dimensional states, trained on labels the generator already provides. At
evaluation its arg-max is grouped into contiguous runs, each run is a span, and each role-run is paired with
the next filler-run in text order. This removes the scanner's knowledge of the bracket syntax and of where
symbols sit in the string. It KEEPS two things: one ordering convention (a role precedes its filler), and
generator supervision, which the paper already discloses as a limitation of the identity head. This is not
unsupervised span discovery and will not be described as such. What it buys, if it works, is that nothing in
the pipeline reads the input string any more -- every symbol and every boundary comes out of the model's own
states.

TWO STAGES, because a failure must be attributable. Stage 1 measures span detection alone on the held-out
split: precision, recall, F1 against the true spans, and the fraction of instances whose FULL span set is
recovered exactly. Stage 2 runs the binding chain on the discovered spans and compares against probe_argmax
(hand-written spans, learned identity) only if stage 1 passes. Without stage 1, a chain failure cannot be told
apart from a detection failure, and that ambiguity is how the earlier arena-B "26% recovery" survived for days.

BARS.
  STAGE-1 GATE     F1 >= 0.90 in 3/3 seeds to proceed. If it fails, the finding is that SPAN DISCOVERY ITSELF
                   is the obstacle -- a real and reportable result, and the honest end of this line rather
                   than a reason to tune the detector until it passes.
  STAGE 2, if reached:
  SCANNER REMOVABLE      iff learned-span chain >= probe_argmax - 0.10 x headroom in 3/3
  SCANNER LOAD-BEARING   iff learned-span chain <= floor + 0.20 x headroom in 3/3
  INTERMEDIATE           otherwise -> report the measured value, license neither reading
Arena: HOPS 2, N_CTX 32, N_SYM 64 -- arena C's configuration, the one the mechanism results are stated on.
Detector budget 6 epochs at lr 1e-3, fixed in advance and not tuned against the gate.

DIRECTION I EXPECT: stage 1 passes and stage 2 lands at SCANNER REMOVABLE or close to it. The reasoning is
that these markers are lexically regular, so a linear probe on contextual states should find them easily --
and if that reasoning is right, the interesting content of the result is not that it works but that it closes
the paper's largest hole. If stage 1 FAILS, that is a more interesting paper and a worse one: it would mean
the frozen states support symbol IDENTITY at .9986 while not supporting symbol LOCALISATION, which I would
report as the finding and would not try to rescue.

## 2026-08-21 -- V-22 STAGE 1 PASSES, and two holes in my own check that nearly let me skip stage 2.

Learned span detection, three-way per-token classifier on the frozen states, arena C's config: precision,
recall, F1 and exact-span-set all 1.0000 in 3/3 seeds. STAGE-1 GATE: PASS. The hand-written scanner is
replaceable -- and the reason it is replaceable so easily is that these markers are lexically regular, which
is a property of our synthetic arenas and not a claim about natural text. That limitation goes in the paper
with the result.

I was about to call stage 2 arithmetic on the strength of exact-set = 1.000 and skip it. Two holes:
  (1) "exact set" compares the SET of spans, not the PAIRING. Perfect detection with a wrong role-to-filler
      pairing scores 1.000 there, and the pairing is what the chain consumes.
  (2) The three-way detector carries no LEVEL information and the arena is layered. Assigning discovered
      pairs to levels by "the first N_CTX pairs are level 0" would smuggle back exactly the hand-written
      convention this experiment exists to remove.
Stage 2 therefore uses a 1 + 2*HOPS-class detector, so level membership is learned too, and it measures
pairing exactness explicitly. The only knowledge left outside the model is that a role precedes its filler.

Also fixed before running: identity targets for discovered spans are now aligned to true spans by TOKEN
OVERLAP rather than by position. Positional alignment would mislabel silently whenever the detector's order
differs from the generator's -- and measuring pairing exactness is precisely how we find out whether it does.
A discovered span overlapping nothing keeps id 0 and is scored on the consequence.

## 2026-08-21 -- V-23 PREREG. Remove the IDENTITY supervision. Registered before the run.

WHY. After V-22 nothing in the pipeline reads the input string, but the identity targets still come from the
task generator, which keeps the remedy a diagnostic rather than a deployable method. That is now the
load-bearing objection to the paper, and a referee is entitled to ask what was shown if everything was
supervised.

WHY THE PAPER'S OWN RESULT SAYS THIS IS ATTACKABLE. The `consistent` arm shows that relabelling EVERY symbol
consistently costs under a point -- .994 against .996 on arena B, .929 against .934 on arena C. The algebra
needs a code stable across occurrences, not one that matches the generator's names. An unsupervised clustering
of the span representations returns precisely that: a permutation of the true identities, using no
per-instance labels. So k-means at k = vocabulary size, fitted on TRAIN spans only and applied to eval spans
by nearest centroid, is a label-free identity mechanism that our own existing measurement predicts should
work. This is not a new idea bolted on; it is the consequence of a result already in the manuscript.

DESIGN. Arena C's config. Every span is relabelled by the same map -- context roles, context fillers, the
query role, and the candidate filler. Relabelling the context while leaving the query at its true id is the
V-11 candidate bug and would break the comparison by construction rather than measure anything. The arm is
`parser` mode, so the only thing that differs from the parser reference is where the ids come from.

APPARATUS CHANGE, disclosed. v13's Arena did not record spans for the query or the candidate: the query
renders as "Q [Rxx] {cand} ?" with a space between ] and {, and PAT requires \]\{, so it never matched.
Added QPAT and q_span/cand_span. Verified before use rather than trusted -- on 20 instances, zero degenerate
fallbacks, and the recorded spans decode to '0E' and '16' for a row whose q is 14 and cand is 16. Existing
arms do not read these fields and are unaffected.

STILL SUPPLIED: span boundaries (V-22's detector needs span labels) and k. NOT SUPPLIED: any symbol identity,
at training or evaluation.

BARS.
  DEPLOYABLE             iff the unsupervised-code arm >= parser - 0.10 x headroom in 3/3
  SUPERVISION REQUIRED   iff <= floor + 0.20 x headroom in 3/3
  INTERMEDIATE           otherwise -> report the measured value, license neither reading
Reported and NOT gated: cluster purity and adjusted Rand index against the true symbols, on both splits. A
failure at high purity means the chain is the obstacle; a failure at low purity means the clustering is.
Without both they are indistinguishable, which is how arena B's anomaly survived for days.

DIRECTION I EXPECT: DEPLOYABLE, or close. If purity is high and the arm still fails, the interesting reading
is that the algebra needs more than a consistent permutation -- which would contradict the `consistent` arm
and would be the most surprising result in the line. I am recording that so it cannot be reinterpreted later.

RESULT, arena C, 3 seeds, k-means at k=64 on 104,000 train spans, applied to eval by nearest centroid, every
span relabelled by the same map including the query role and candidate filler:
  unsupervised codes  .554 / .490 / .536  mean .5267
  floor .5153   parser .9340   consistent (a HANDED permutation) .9293   headroom .4187
  cluster purity, eval: .3581 / .2945 / .3397     ARI: .2923 / .2418 / .2845
VERDICT: SUPERVISION REQUIRED. The arm sits at the floor.

I predicted DEPLOYABLE. That is the fourth registered prediction of mine to fail today, after the depth
mechanism (V-19 REFUTED), the arena-A parameter explanation (V-20 INTERMEDIATE) and my own mis-specified
exactness bar (V-21). I am recording the count because the ratio matters: the predictions that failed were all
mine, and the ones that held were the paper's existing measurements.

THE DIAGNOSTIC DID ITS JOB, and this is why it was registered ungated. Purity is LOW -- .33 against 64
symbols -- so the failure is attributable to the CLUSTERING, not to the chain. Had purity been high and the
arm still failed, the reading would have been the opposite and far more surprising, because it would have
contradicted the `consistent` arm.

WHAT THIS ACTUALLY ESTABLISHES, and it is a result rather than a limitation restated. Symbol identity is
linearly decodable from these frozen states at .9986 with supervision, and k-means on the same span-pooled
states recovers only ~.33 purity. So the symbol code IS present and is NOT salient: it does not lie along the
dominant variance structure of the representation, which is presumably dominated by position and local
context. That supplies a MECHANISM for the paper's central negative result, which until now was an
observation. The binding objective does not induce a codebook because a gradient through a downstream loss
has no more access to a low-variance identity direction than k-means does. Nothing that fails to target
identity explicitly will find it.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PAPER. The supervision limitation is now MEASURED rather than disclosed -- we tried to
remove it and report what happened -- which is stronger content than a caveat. But it confirms the objection
rather than removing it, so it does not raise my estimate of acceptance; it raises the paper's honesty and its
explanatory power. The next thing that would follow from it is a direct measurement of how much variance the
symbol-discriminating direction accounts for, which would turn "not salient" into a number.

## 2026-08-21 -- V-24 PREREG. Turn "the code is not salient" into a number. Registered before the run.

WHY. V-23 established that identity is linearly decodable from span-pooled frozen states at .9986 with
supervision while k-means on the same states reaches only ~.33 purity. The natural reading is that the symbol
code is present but does not lie along the dominant variance structure. That reading is currently a sentence.
If it is right it supplies a MECHANISM for this paper's central negative result -- a binding objective does not
induce a codebook because any objective that does not target identity explicitly optimises what dominates the
variance, and the code is not in it -- and a mechanism is worth more than the observation it explains.

## 2026-08-21 -- V-28 PREREG. Can the algebra reduce error where it matters -- after abstention? Registered
## before the run, at the user's request to make hallucination reduction a contribution.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING, and why it has to be said first. The user asked for VSA to reduce hallucination and
improve accuracy. Every matched comparison in this paper says a VSA module does NOT improve accuracy: it loses
to a linear probe by 3.20/4.18/4.65pp across four admitted arenas and loses to LoRA where the tasks admit it.
Designing a run in the hope of reversing that is exactly how the earlier draft got its headline, and I will not
do it. So the accuracy claim is not what this tests.

WHAT THE ALGEBRA ACTUALLY PROVIDES that a softmax does not: the chain can be unbound and its retrieval compared
against the codebook, so the cosine between the retrieved vector and the row it cleans up to is a STRUCTURAL
confidence signal rather than a trained score. If that signal ranks the system's own errors better than a
classifier's confidence does, then at any coverage the answered subset carries less error. That is the
operational sense in which hallucination can be said to fall, and it is the sense that matters for deployment.

TASK CHANGE, deliberate and disclosed. The comparison uses the RETRIEVAL the chain actually performs -- name
the endpoint symbol, 64 ways -- rather than the binary verification used elsewhere in the paper. This is
chosen because it is a task a pooled-state probe CANNOT do (it requires composing two hops), so the comparison
is not rigged in the probe's favour by asking only what the probe can answer. It also means the accuracy
comparison here is not the one reported elsewhere and must not be quoted as though it were.

  (A) probe baseline  64-way classifier on the pooled frozen state; confidence = max softmax
  (B) binding chain   unbind through levels, clean up; confidence = cosine(retrieved, cleaned row)
Both read the same frozen states. The chain's identity comes from a supervised probe, which is the supervision
the paper already discloses; the baseline gets the answer label directly, which is a different and arguably
larger supervision budget, and that asymmetry is stated rather than hidden.

METRICS: top-1 accuracy, AUROC of confidence for detecting the system's own errors, and selective accuracy at
50/70/90 percent coverage, all for both systems, three seeds.

BARS.
  CONFIDENCE BETTER  iff chain AUROC >= probe AUROC + 0.05 in 3/3 AND chain sel@70 >= probe sel@70 + 0.05 in 3/3
  NO BETTER          iff chain AUROC <= probe AUROC + 0.01 in 3/3 -> the structural signal does not beat a
                     trained one, and the claim is dropped rather than softened
  INTERMEDIATE       otherwise -> report both curves, license neither reading

DIRECTION I EXPECT: the chain wins on accuracy here because the probe cannot compose two hops, and the
confidence comparison is the open question. Seven of my predictions have failed today, so that expectation is
worth exactly what the bar says. If the verdict is NO BETTER, the honest outcome is that the paper gains
nothing on hallucination and I will report that to the user rather than reframing it.

operational measure is worse still -- the chain answers at .8720 and abstaining on half the data raises that
to .8840, so discarding 50% of the input buys 1.2 points. On this evidence the algebra does not supply a
confidence signal worth having, and the claim that VSA reduces hallucination is not supportable.

accuracy and one at 2% is not meaningful. With the baseline at chance its confidence ranks nothing, so the
