## V-35 prereg: how good must the mention partition be? Registered before any code is written.

**Why this and not "remove the supervision".** Reading v30.py changed the question. On bAbI the identity labels are
`persons[word]` and `locs[word]` -- indices assigned by surface form over the corpus, not values handed over by a
generator. So on natural text the supervision the algebra needs is already a *mention partition* obtainable from the
text, and the standing objection "all supervision comes from the generator" does not apply there. What is untested,
and what a practitioner actually needs, is how good that partition must be: a real coreference signal is imperfect
(pronouns, aliases, ambiguity), and the paper currently says nothing about tolerance.

**Why it is a test and not a decoration.** The paper's central claim is consistency, not correctness. That claim makes
a falsifiable asymmetry prediction. Corrupting the partition two ways:
  MERGE (under-splitting): two distinct symbols are given one code. The mention-to-code map stays a function of the
    symbol -- consistent, not injective. Unbinding returns a superposition of both fillers.
  SPLIT (over-splitting): mentions of one symbol are given different codes. The map is no longer a function of the
    symbol -- consistency is broken. A key bound with one code and unbound with another fails outright.
"Consistency, not correctness" predicts SPLIT hurts more than MERGE at equal rate. If SPLIT is not worse, the
paper's framing is challenged and I report that, not the framing.

**Setup.** bAbI task 1, the v33 configuration (query spans included in the identity head's training data, HRR,
Phi-2, seeds 42/123/456), nothing else changed. Reference points already banked: chain 1.0000 with the uncorrupted
partition; six-way linear probe floor .7713. So H = .2287 and floor+0.90H = .9771, floor+0.10H = .7942.
Corruption rates r in {0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.40}, applied to the TRAINING partition only; evaluation uses the true
partition, because the question is what a noisy supervisor costs, not what a noisy evaluator measures.

**Bars.**
(a) VALIDITY: at r = 0 the chain must reach >= .9771 in 3/3, reproducing V-33. If it does not, the run is void and
    I report it void rather than reading the curve.
(b) ROBUST iff chain >= .9771 (floor + 0.90H) at r = 0.10 in 3/3, for the family in question.
(c) BRITTLE iff chain <= .7942 (floor + 0.10H) at r = 0.10 in 3/3, for the family in question.
(d) Otherwise GRADED: report the curve and license neither reading.
(e) ASYMMETRY CONFIRMED iff chain(split, r) < chain(merge, r) at r = 0.10 in 3/3. ASYMMETRY REFUTED iff
    chain(split, 0.10) >= chain(merge, 0.10) in 3/3, which contradicts consistency-not-correctness and gets
    written up as contradicting it. Anything else is INCONCLUSIVE on the asymmetry.
(f) Monotonicity is an expectation, not a bar: I expect both curves to fall monotonically in r. Non-monotone output
    is reported as measured and not smoothed.

**Predictions, on the record.** SPLIT catastrophic by r = 0.10; MERGE graded and still above the floor at r = 0.10;
asymmetry confirmed. Thirteen predictions tested today and twelve failed, so these are worth the bars and nothing
more.

**What each outcome does to the manuscript.** ROBUST on MERGE plus asymmetry confirmed turns the deployability
limitation into a quantified requirement -- the supervision the algebra needs is a mention partition, it must be
consistent rather than correct, and here is the tolerance. BRITTLE on both turns it into a sharper limitation than
the one now written, which currently asserts no tolerance either way. ASYMMETRY REFUTED is the outcome that costs
me the framing, and it is the reason this is worth running.

## V-35 GRADED / GRADED, ASYMMETRY INCONCLUSIVE -- and my prediction was refuted in direction

**Numbers (bAbI task 1, v33 configuration, 3 seeds, corruption on the training partition only, evaluation against
the true label; capacity held constant at a 20-row id space in every cell).**

  rate    MERGE chain                   SPLIT chain                  MERGE cons.  SPLIT cons.
  0.00    [1.000 1.000 1.000] 1.0000    (shared validity cell)        1.0000       --
  0.05    [1.000 1.000 1.000] 1.0000    [.992 .974 .978] 0.9813       1.0000       0.9847
  0.10    [.706 1.000 .868 ] 0.8580     [.964 .956 .918] 0.9460       1.0000       0.9573
  0.20    [.844 .568 .718 ] 0.7100      [.842 .818 .814] 0.8247       1.0000       0.8633
  0.40    [.432 .606 .830 ] 0.6227      [.466 .528 .552] 0.5153       1.0000       0.5973

**Verdicts, by the bars at cab4405.** Validity OK (uncorrupted chain 1.0000 in 3/3, reproducing V-33). MERGE at
r=0.10 GRADED. SPLIT at r=0.10 GRADED. ASYMMETRY INCONCLUSIVE -- the seeds disagree, so I license neither reading
even though the means run the other way. Both curves monotone in r, as expected.

**My prediction was wrong in direction.** I registered "SPLIT catastrophic by r=0.10, MERGE graded, asymmetry
confirmed". The means say the opposite at r=0.10 and r=0.20: breaking consistency costs LESS than losing
injectivity (.946 vs .858, .825 vs .710). The ordering flips again at r=0.40 (.515 vs .623). Fourteen predictions
tested today, thirteen failed.

**Why, and what it does to the paper's central sentence.** The consistency column is the mechanism: MERGE holds
code-consistency at exactly 1.0000 at every rate while SPLIT drives it from .9847 to .5973 -- and yet MERGE is
the more damaging family at moderate rates. The reason is that the identity head is a FUNCTION OF THE STATE, so
identical mentions receive identical codes at inference no matter how inconsistently they were labelled in
training; per-mention noise is averaged away. A merge, by contrast, is a systematic relabelling the head learns
faithfully. So consistency was never the fragile property -- it is free for any deterministic encoder. The
fragile property is INJECTIVITY: distinct symbols must receive distinguishable codes. This reads on the paper's
"consistency, not correctness" as underdetermined rather than wrong: the `consistent` arm permutes the codebook,
which is injective, so it satisfies both readings and cannot separate them.

**I am not writing that into the manuscript yet.** The two data points sit on different substrates -- the
injective-relabelling arm is in synthetic arena C, the non-injective measurement is here on bAbI -- and I have
been wrong thirteen times today by explaining before measuring. V-36 puts both on bAbI.

**Disclosed limitations of this run, not banked as strengths.** (i) With four persons and six locations, r=0.10
merges an expected ONE symbol, so the seed spread reflects WHICH symbol was merged rather than a smooth rate
effect; this is why the per-seed bar came out inconclusive and it is the honest reason to report means with
spread rather than a verdict. (ii) When a LOCATION is merged, the readout runs over true location rows, so the
target row is unreachable by construction and part of MERGE's cost is an evaluation mismatch rather than a
binding failure. V-36 separates persons from locations.

## V-36 prereg: injectivity or consistency? Registered before any code, on the same substrate.

**The question V-35 raised and cannot settle.** V-35's mechanism reading is that consistency is free for any
deterministic encoder and the fragile property is injectivity. The evidence for that is split across substrates:
the injective-relabelling arm (`consistent`, a permuted codebook, costing under a point) is in synthetic arena C,
and the non-injective measurement (MERGE) is on bAbI. A cross-substrate inference is exactly the kind of thing
that has cost me a claim four times today. V-36 puts both on bAbI and separates the confound V-35 disclosed.

**Cells, all bAbI task 1, v33 configuration, seeds 42/123/456, 20-row id space as in V-35.**
  (1) PERMUTED: the codebook rows are permuted -- an injective, wholly incorrect relabelling. Training labels
      untouched, so this is correctness destroyed with injectivity and consistency intact.
  (2) MERGE-PERSONS at r=0.10 and 0.25: aliasing restricted to persons, so the queried symbol can collide but the
      answer row is always reachable.
  (3) MERGE-LOCATIONS at r=0.10 and 0.25: aliasing restricted to locations, where the answer row is by
      construction unreachable for a merged pair. Reported separately precisely because part of its cost is an
      evaluation mismatch rather than a binding failure, which V-35 could not separate.
  Rate 0.25 replaces V-35's 0.20/0.40 because with four persons r=0.25 merges an expected one person, making the
  persons cell interpretable at a stated expected count instead of a rate that rounds to zero or to everything.

**Bars.** Reference points: floor .7713, uncorrupted chain 1.0000, H .2287, so floor+0.90H = .9771 and
floor+0.10H = .7942.
(a) VALIDITY: cell (1) must be run first and the uncorrupted number is already banked at 1.0000; if PERMUTED
    itself lands below .9771 the injectivity framing FAILS on this substrate and I say so.
(b) INJECTIVITY IS THE PROPERTY iff PERMUTED >= .9771 in 3/3 AND MERGE-PERSONS at r=0.25 <= PERMUTED - 0.05 in
    3/3. Then the manuscript's "consistency, not correctness" is replaced by "injectivity, not correctness", with
    the merge number as the price of losing it.
(c) CONSISTENCY SURVIVES AS THE PROPERTY iff PERMUTED < .9771 in 3/3 -- i.e. an injective but incorrect code does
    NOT come free on natural text, which would mean the arena result does not transfer and the existing sentence
    stays as it is, scoped to synthetic markup.
(d) INCONCLUSIVE otherwise: report all cells, change nothing in the framing.
(e) Descriptive, no bar: whether MERGE-LOCATIONS costs more than MERGE-PERSONS at equal rate, which measures how
    much of V-35's merge cost was the unreachable-row artifact.

**Prediction, on the record.** PERMUTED at 1.000 (matching the arena's under-a-point loss) and MERGE-PERSONS
clearly below it, i.e. (b). I also expect MERGE-LOCATIONS to be worse than MERGE-PERSONS. Fourteen predictions
tested today and thirteen failed, so these are worth the bars and nothing more.

**What each outcome does.** (b) sharpens the paper's central sentence from an underdetermined claim to a
measured one, on natural text, at the cost of admitting the earlier phrasing could not separate the two readings.
(c) is the outcome that keeps the current sentence but confines it to synthetic markup, which is a real
limitation I would then have to write. Either way the manuscript ends up saying something it cannot say now.

## V-36 INJECTIVITY IS THE PROPERTY -- and the paper's central sentence was supported by an isomorphism

**Numbers (bAbI task 1, 3 seeds, 20-row id space, corruption on the training partition only).**

  cell                      symbols merged / seed    chain
  permuted (isomorphism)    [0, 0, 0]                [1.000 1.000 1.000]  1.0000
  merge-persons  r=0.10     [0, 0, 0]                [1.000 1.000 1.000]  1.0000   <- VACUOUS, see below
  merge-persons  r=0.25     [1, 1, 1]                [.880  .880  .880 ]  0.8800
  merge-locations r=0.10    [1, 0, 2]                [.812  1.000 .694 ]  0.8353
  merge-locations r=0.25    [1, 3, 2]                [.832  .486  .656 ]  0.6580

**Verdict by the bars at 92fb15c: INJECTIVITY IS THE PROPERTY.** PERMUTED >= .9771 in 3/3 and MERGE-PERSONS at
r=0.25 <= PERMUTED - 0.05 in 3/3. The descriptive comparison also came out as predicted: merged locations cost
more than merged persons at equal rate.

**What must not be claimed from this, and why.** PERMUTED returning exactly 1.000 in 3/3 is not a discovery, it
is confirmation of an analytic argument I made while writing the cell: the codebook rows are i.i.d. random unit
vectors and the permutation is applied uniformly to binding and to the readout, so the permuted system is
ISOMORPHIC to the unpermuted one. Its expected accuracy is identical by construction. Which means the paper's
`consistent` arm in arena C -- "loses under a point when every symbol is consistently relabelled" -- measures
run-to-run noise, not a property of encoders, and the sentence it supports, "what binding needs from an encoder
is consistency and not correctness", is TRUE BUT VACUOUS as stated: when codebook rows are arbitrary random
vectors, "correct" has no referent and every bijection is equivalent. I have been presenting a tautology as a
measurement. A referee finding this before I did would have been expensive.

**What the empirical content actually is.** The cost of losing injectivity, which had never been measured in this
paper: aliasing one of four names costs twelve points, 1.0000 -> .8800 in 3/3. Locations cost more (.6580 at
r=0.25), and part of that is an evaluation mismatch rather than a binding failure, because a merged location's
row is unreachable in the readout -- which is exactly why V-36 separated the two scopes and why the persons cell
is the one that carries the claim.

**Three internal checks that came out right.** The permuted cell hit the uncorrupted value exactly; the
merge-locations seed that merged zero symbols returned exactly 1.000; and merge-persons at r=0.10 merged zero
symbols in all three seeds (four persons at rate .10 is an expectation of 0.4), so that cell is VACUOUS and is
reported as vacuous rather than counted as three seeds of evidence.

**Standing tally.** Sixteen registered experiments today. Fifteen predictions tested, thirteen failed. Five of my
own claims refuted by my own bars, and now one more retired for being unfalsifiable as phrased.

## V-37 prereg: does the discrete handover transfer at DEPTH TWO on natural text? Before any code.

**The gap this closes.** The paper's two-hop evidence is entirely synthetic (arena C, and the depth sweep V-19 at
depths one to four). On natural text it has one task and one hop: bAbI task 1 is a single role-filler unbinding.
A referee asking "does this survive composition on real sentences" currently has no answer in the manuscript.
bAbI task 2 is the two-hop version in English: "Mary took the football there" then "Mary travelled to the
hallway", asked as "Where is the football?", so the chain is object -> holder -> location.

**What task 2 adds that task 1 could not, and what it costs.** Task 2 contains a second thing a superposition
cannot express, on top of recency: "Mary dropped the football" REVOKES a holding relation, and thereafter the
object's location is where it was dropped rather than wherever Mary goes. A bundle has no way to retract a
binding. As in V-30, the ordering rule is therefore supplied from OUTSIDE the algebra -- last event per object,
last movement per person, and for a drop the mover's location at the time of the drop -- and the manuscript must
say so in the same breath as the result. This measures the ENCODING question (does the discrete handover
compose on natural text) and not the expressiveness question, which is already answered negatively.

**Setup.** bAbI task 2, Phi-2, HRR, seeds 42/123/456, the v30/v33 configuration otherwise. Symbols are persons,
locations and objects. Two bundles: mem1 over bind(code(holder), code(object)) for the selected object events,
mem2 over bind(code(location), code(person)) for the selected movements; unbind mem1 by the queried object to get
a holder, then unbind mem2 by that holder to get a location. Arms: floor (linear probe on the pooled frozen
state predicting the location), parser (true ids indexing the codebook), probe_argmax (identity head over spans,
arg-max indexing the codebook -- the supervised discrete handover), spans (a projection trained through the
binding loss).

**Bars.** H = parser - floor.
(a) ADMISSION: parser - floor >= 0.20, else VOID and reported void, because a task whose oracle arm is near its
    own floor cannot separate arms.
(b) TRANSFERS AT DEPTH TWO iff probe_argmax >= floor + 0.90H in 3/3.
(c) FAILS AT DEPTH TWO iff probe_argmax <= floor + 0.10H in 3/3, in which case the manuscript's claim narrows
    from "off synthetic markup" to "off synthetic markup at depth one", which is a real retreat and I write it.
(d) GRADED otherwise: report, license neither.
(e) spans reported with a registered expectation of at or below floor, as in every other arena; if spans instead
    clears floor + 0.50H the through-the-loss route works somewhere it has never worked and that is the finding.

**Predictions on the record.** TRANSFERS, with probe_argmax within a point of parser, and spans at or below the
floor. Fifteen predictions tested today and thirteen failed, so these are worth the bars and nothing more.

**What each outcome does to the manuscript.** TRANSFERS extends the central claim from one natural-text task at
one hop to two tasks and two hops, which is the axis a referee will press hardest and the one where the paper is
currently thinnest. FAILS narrows the central claim to depth one on natural text and is the outcome I would have
to write against my own abstract. Either way the sentence "off synthetic markup" stops being supported by a
single hop of a single task.

## V-37 TRANSFERS AT DEPTH TWO, and SPANS UNEXPECTEDLY WORKS -- my prediction refuted again

**Numbers (bAbI task 2, Phi-2, HRR, 3 seeds; 4 persons, 6 locations, 3 objects, codebook 13; arms compared on
the expressible subset, 235 train / 140 eval; mem1 carries 2.0 objects and mem2 3.6 persons per instance, so
distractors are present).**

  floor         [.4429 .4357 .4714]  0.4500
  parser        [1.000 1.000 1.000]  1.0000
  probe_argmax  [1.000 1.000 1.000]  1.0000
  spans         [.8571 .8571 .8429]  0.8524

Headroom .5500; bars transfers >= .9450, fails <= .5050, spans-works >= .7250.

**Verdicts by the bars at d7e2bde.** TRANSFERS AT DEPTH TWO: probe_argmax equals the parser exactly in 3/3, so
the supervised discrete handover composes on natural text and the central claim now covers two natural-text
tasks and two hops instead of one task and one hop. That prediction of mine held. SPANS UNEXPECTEDLY WORKS:
spans clears half the headroom at .8524, in fact 73% of it. I registered the expectation that spans would sit at
or below the floor, as it does in every synthetic arena, and registered in advance that clearing floor+0.50H
"is the finding". It is. Sixteen predictions tested today, fourteen failed.

**Why the spans result matters more than the one I predicted.** The manuscript says a projection trained through
the loss NEVER works. That is now false as stated on natural text, and this is the second instance, not the
first: bAbI task 1 gave .976 against a .771 floor (86% of headroom) and the manuscript currently reports it as a
result it cannot account for, with V-34a having eliminated symbol count as the explanation. Two natural-text
tasks at two depths now show the continuous route working where every synthetic arena shows it failing. The
lone unexplained outlier has become a replicated phenomenon, which is a better paper and a narrower claim.

**The confound that could kill it, and which I am testing before writing any of it.** Candidate-set size. mem2
here offers about 3.6 candidate locations; synthetic arena C offers 32. An inexact continuous code can still
win an arg-max against 3.6 distractors and lose against 32. V-34a already ran arena C at N_CTX=8 and spans sat
at the floor there (.5140 at 64 symbols, .5347 at 10), so 8 candidates is not enough to rescue it -- but 3.6 is
below 8 and the gap is untested. V-38 runs arena C at N_CTX=4. If spans still fails there, candidate count is
eliminated and natural text is the factor; if it works, this new story collapses and I say so.

**Prereg/implementation discrepancy, disclosed rather than quietly kept.** The prereg's oracle rule says that
for a DROP the object's location is "the mover's location at the time of the drop". The code implemented the
weaker rule -- the holder's LAST movement overall, regardless of when the drop happened. Consequence: the
measured expressiveness ceiling, 31.4% of eval instances answerable by the oracle bundle and 68.6% not, is a
LOWER bound on expressibility, and part of that 68.6% is my weaker rule rather than the algebra's limit. The
arm comparison itself is unaffected, because every arm sees the identical subset and the identical bundles.
V-37b reruns with the registered rule and the ceiling will be restated from that.

## V-38 prereg: is the continuous route's natural-text success just a small candidate set? Before any code.

**The claim at risk.** V-37 and the bAbI task-1 result together say the through-the-loss projection works on
natural text (.8524 at 73% of headroom; .976 at 86%) and fails in every synthetic arena. Before that goes into
the manuscript, the obvious alternative has to be killed: bAbI task 2 offers about 3.6 candidate locations per
instance and arena C offers 32. An inexact continuous code can win an arg-max against four distractors and lose
against thirty-two, in which case the factor is candidate count and the phrase "natural text" is decoration.

**What is already known.** V-34a ran arena C at N_CTX=8 with spans at .5140 (64 symbols) and .5347 (10 symbols),
both at the floor. So eight candidates does not rescue the continuous route. The untested region is below eight,
which is where bAbI sits.

**Setup.** Arena C, HRR, Phi-2, seeds 42/123/456, everything as the mechanism table, N_CTX swept over {4, 6} at
N_SYM = 64, arms floor / parser / spans. Nothing else changed.

**Bars.** Per cell, H = parser - floor, with admission H >= 0.20 or the cell is void.
(a) CANDIDATE COUNT EXPLAINS IT iff spans >= floor + 0.50H in 3/3 at N_CTX = 4. Then the natural-text framing is
    withdrawn before it is ever written, the bAbI results are attributed to candidate count, and the
    manuscript's unexplained .976 gets that explanation instead.
(b) CANDIDATE COUNT ELIMINATED iff spans <= floor + 0.10H in 3/3 at N_CTX = 4. Then four synthetic candidates
    still fail where 3.6 natural-text candidates succeed, and the natural-text difference is real and goes in.
(c) GRADED otherwise: report both cells, write neither story, and leave the task-1 result as unaccounted for.

**Prediction.** I expect (b), candidate count eliminated, because the effect sizes are far apart -- 73-86% of
headroom on natural text versus at-or-below floor at every synthetic width measured so far. But I have now been
wrong fourteen times out of sixteen today and my last prediction about the spans arm was wrong in exactly this
family, so this is worth the bar and nothing else. If (a) comes out, the story I would otherwise have written
into the abstract is wrong, and this run is the reason it did not get there.

**Note on what this cannot decide.** Even under (b), "natural text" remains a bundle of differences from
synthetic markup -- lexically distinctive mentions, real word frequencies, span lengths, sentence syntax. V-38
eliminates one specific alternative, candidate count, and the manuscript must say only that.

## V-37 and V-37b VOID: a label-space misalignment that made the parser 1.0000 BY CONSTRUCTION

**What was wrong.** `v5.load_babi` returns each answer as an index into `d["vocab"]`. v30 aligns its location
dictionary to that same enumeration for exactly this reason. v37 did not: it built `locs` from the first-seen
order of movement statements, a different indexing. The consequence is not a small bias. The row filter
`expressible = (bundle_loc == y)` compared MY index against the DATASET's, so the "expressible subset" was
really the set of rows where the two enumerations happened to agree -- and on that subset the parser arm
retrieves the right row by construction. `parser 1.0000` and `probe_argmax 1.0000` were therefore properties of
the filter, not measurements, and `spans 0.8524` was scored on a subset selected by an accident of indexing.

**What is retracted.** Both verdicts from e5bacde: "TRANSFERS AT DEPTH TWO" and "SPANS UNEXPECTEDLY WORKS", and
every number in that entry -- floor .4500, parser 1.0000, probe_argmax 1.0000, spans .8524, and the 31.4% /
33.6% expressiveness ceilings. Artifacts renamed to v37_VOID_labelspace.{json,log} and
v37b_VOID_labelspace.{json,log} so no checker can read them as evidence. Nothing from V-37 reached either
manuscript: the ledger entry at e5bacde explicitly said the story was not being written until V-38 tested the
candidate-count confound, and that hold is the only reason a fabricated-strength result did not get in.

**What is NOT affected.** V-38 (arena C at N_CTX 4 and 6) shares no code with this and stands: spans below the
floor in 3/3 at four candidates. But note what that now means -- V-38 was registered to kill a confound in a
result that has itself been retracted, so its verdict "candidate count eliminated" is currently a statement
about nothing until the depth-two numbers come back real. The bAbI task-1 result (.976 against .771) is from
v30/v33, which do align to d["vocab"], and is unaffected.

**How it was caught, and what that says.** Not by a checker. I noticed that V-37b's registered oracle rule --
which should have made dropped-then-moved instances expressible -- barely moved the ceiling, 31.4% to 33.6%.
That did not make mechanistic sense, and following it back found the misalignment. The lesson is the one this
paper keeps re-learning: a number that behaves implausibly is evidence about the apparatus, and the instinct to
accept a convenient result is the thing to distrust. A parser arm at exactly 1.0000 in 3/3 should have been
suspicious on its own -- it is the signature of a circular evaluation, and I read it as success.

**Rerunning with locs aligned to d["vocab"], bars unchanged and still those registered at d7e2bde.** If the
depth-two claim survives, it survives on a real subset; if it does not, the manuscript keeps "off synthetic
markup at depth one" and I write that.

## V-37b (fixed) TRANSFERS AT DEPTH TWO -- and the spans story is dead by the bar I registered for it

**Numbers, locs aligned to d["vocab"], bars unchanged from d7e2bde.** 4 persons, 6 locations, 3 objects,
codebook 13; expressible subset 775 train / 420 eval; mem1 carries 2.0 objects and mem2 3.6 persons.

  floor         [.2071 .1881 .2143]  0.2032        (six-way probe on the pooled state, near its own chance)
  parser        [1.000 1.000 1.000]  1.0000
  probe_argmax  [1.000 1.000 1.000]  1.0000
  spans         [.4952 .5048 .5071]  0.5024        = 37.6% of headroom
  headroom .7968; bars transfers >= .9203, fails <= .2829, spans-works >= .6016

**TRANSFERS AT DEPTH TWO, on a real subset this time.** probe_argmax equals the parser in 3/3, so the supervised
discrete handover composes over two hops of English. The manuscript's natural-text claim goes from one task and
one hop to two tasks and two hops.

**The expressiveness ceiling, restated from the registered rule: 94.6% expressible, 5.4% not.** The void run
reported 31.4%. The difference IS the label-space fault -- which is corroboration of the diagnosis, since the
registered rule was always supposed to make dropped-then-moved instances expressible and now does. So the
honest statement about task 2 is the opposite of what the void run implied: a superposition with an outside
ordering rule can express nearly all of task 2, and only one instance in twenty defeats it.

**And the finding I was hoping for is refuted by the bar I set for it.** spans reaches 37.6% of headroom, below
the registered .6016 (floor + 0.50H), so "SPANS UNEXPECTEDLY WORKS" is NOT licensed and I withdraw the story I
had started assembling one entry ago. Consequences, stated plainly:
  - The "continuous route works on natural text" reading rests on bAbI task 1 alone (.976 against .771, 86% of
    headroom) and is back to being a single-task result the manuscript cannot account for.
  - What task 2 adds is a CONTRAST rather than a replication: on natural text the continuous route holds 86% of
    headroom at one hop and 37.6% at two, while the discrete handover is at ceiling at both. Two points are not
    a law and the manuscript will not call it one.
  - V-38's "candidate count eliminated" now does real work again: it removes one candidate explanation for the
    task-1 result, which still exists. Together with V-34a (symbol count) that is two alternatives tested and
    eliminated for a result the paper reports without an account.

**Tally.** Seventeen registered experiments, eighteen predictions tested, fifteen failed. Four apparatus faults
disclosed today, the label-space one being the worst; two overclaims withdrawn; and one story assembled and then
killed by its own pre-registered bar inside a single hour.

## Apparatus: the coverage scan was blind to nine literals per variant, behind escaped percent signs

**The fault.** verify_coverage.py stripped LaTeX comments with `re.sub(r"%.*", "", ...)`. A LaTeX escaped
percent is a backslash followed by `%`, so every line containing `\%` was truncated at that point and everything
after it -- including measured numbers -- was never scanned. verify_paper12 and verify_paper13 inherited the same
line. Found because verify_paper13 reported a MISMATCH on a sentence the manuscript plainly contained,
`$94.6\%$ of evaluation instances`; the checker was wrong, and the reason it was wrong was general.

**First fix was also wrong, and is recorded because it nearly passed.** I generated `(?<!\\\\)%` -- in a regex
that is "not preceded by TWO literal backslashes" -- which leaves single-backslash `\%` still stripped. It
looked fixed: verify_paper12 went green, because none of its assertions contain `\%`. A green checker is not
evidence that a fix worked when the checker never exercised the broken path.

**Effect of the correct fix, `(?<!\\)%`.** Literals found by the coverage scan: npj 189 -> 198, conference
192 -> 201. Nine per variant had been invisible. All nine trace to artifacts, so no untraced number was hiding
behind them, but the scan had been reporting full coverage over a text it was not fully reading -- the same
class of fault as the appendix truncation found earlier today, and the second time this tool has claimed
completeness it did not have.

**Gate after the fix, rerun rather than carried over.** Thirteen targeted checkers, 0 with any mismatch;
coverage 198/198 npj and 201/201 conference over 71 artifacts; provenance 6/6 tables and 7/7 tabular blocks;
npj format 17/18, the single failure being main text at 6,102 words (+22%, declared in the cover letter);
abstract 144 words; both variants compile at 19 and 21 pages with 0 errors and 0 undefined references.

## V-39 prereg: a label-free code from injectivity alone. Registered before any code is written.

**Why this is worth a run when V-23 already failed.** V-23 removed identity supervision by k-means clustering the
span representations and the chain returned to the floor (.527 against .515, purity .29-.36). I have been citing
that as "supervision is required". V-36 says the requirement is narrower than I thought: consistency is FREE for
any deterministic encoder, and the property that costs is INJECTIVITY -- distinct symbols must get
distinguishable codes. k-means asks for something injectivity does not need, namely compact clusters. V-24
measured the geometry directly: identity is linearly decodable at .9999 from thirty-six principal components
while k-means purity stays at .31. Linearly separable and not compact is exactly the regime where hashing
should work and clustering should not.

**The arms, all label-free and all deterministic (so consistency is automatic, per V-36).**
  lsh_raw   code = sign(R h), R a fixed random Gaussian projection to the VSA dimension, h the pooled span state.
  lsh_inst  code = sign(R (h - mu)/sigma), with mu and sigma the per-instance mean and standard deviation over
            that instance's own token states. Per-instance statistics are available at inference, need no labels
            and no training set, and within-instance consistency is all the binding requires, since a bind and
            its unbind always occur inside one instance.
Reference arms: floor, parser, probe_argmax, unchanged from the mechanism table. Arena C, HRR, Phi-2, N_SYM 64,
N_CTX 32, HOPS 2, seeds 42/123/456.

**Bars.** H = parser - floor, admission H >= 0.20 or void.
(a) LABEL-FREE CODE WORKS iff the better lsh arm >= floor + 0.90H in 3/3. The paper's load-bearing limitation --
    all supervision comes from the generator -- would then be removed rather than measured, and the manuscript's
    "supervision is required" becomes "an injective deterministic code suffices, and it need not be learned".
(b) PARTIAL iff the better lsh arm >= floor + 0.50H in 3/3. Reported as a partial result and the limitation
    stays, narrowed.
(c) FAILS iff both lsh arms <= floor + 0.10H in 3/3. Then V-23's conclusion stands for a second, independent
    reason and the manuscript says so with the mechanism, not just the outcome.
(d) GRADED otherwise.

**Mechanistic diagnostic, reported whatever happens, so a failure is attributable rather than mysterious.** Mean
cosine between codes of the SAME symbol across its occurrences, and between codes of DIFFERENT symbols. HRR needs
the first near one and the second near zero. If the same-symbol cosine is high and the different-symbol cosine is
also high, the failure is crowding rather than inconsistency, and that is a statement about the geometry of the
frozen states rather than about hashing.

**Prediction, on the record.** lsh_raw FAILS, lsh_inst PARTIAL: I expect different-symbol cosine to stay high
because the span states of distinct symbols in the same context are strongly correlated, and per-instance
standardisation to help but not enough. Eighteen predictions tested today and fifteen failed, so this is worth
the bar and nothing more. I note that I want (a) to be true, which is exactly the condition under which I have
been wrong most often today.

## V-39 FAILS, with an attributable mechanism -- and V-39b because my own diagnostic could not attribute it

**Accuracy (arena C, N_SYM 64, N_CTX 32, HOPS 2, 3 seeds).** floor .5153, parser .9340, probe_argmax .9340,
H = .4187, so works >= .8921, partial >= .7247, fails <= .5572.
  lsh_raw   [.506 .514 .550]  0.5233
  lsh_inst  [.498 .544 .548]  0.5300
Both arms under the FAILS bar in 3/3. Verdict FAILS by the bars at 47fc3ce. My prediction was half right: I
called lsh_raw FAILS and lsh_inst PARTIAL, and lsh_inst also failed. Nineteen predictions tested today, sixteen
failed. I noted in the prereg that I wanted WORKS to be true, and it is not.

**My pooled diagnostic could not attribute the failure, so it was rerun.** V-39 measured same-symbol cosine by
pooling occurrences ACROSS instances. lsh_inst standardises per instance and a bind never crosses an instance,
so that number measures a property the mechanism does not require. V-39b measures both cosines WITHIN instances
over 8,126 repeated-symbol groups:
  lsh_raw   within-instance same .5681  diff .4975  gap .0706
  lsh_inst  within-instance same .3154  diff .2181  gap .0973
The pooled and within-instance numbers agree, so cross-instance drift was never the issue. The accuracy verdict
was untouched by this; only its attribution was, and I would have written the wrong mechanism without it.

**The mechanism, and why it does not contradict V-24.** HRR needs same-symbol cosine near one and
different-symbol near zero. Hashing delivers a margin of seven to ten points in both directions at once: the
same symbol's occurrences are not close enough for a sign pattern to be stable, and distinct symbols are not far
enough apart for it to discriminate. V-24 found identity decodable at .9999 from thirty-six principal
components, and that is consistent with this: HID is 2,560, so a random hyperplane puts almost all of its norm
in the 2,524 directions that carry symbol-irrelevant variance, and its sign is dominated by them. A supervised
probe SEARCHES for the discriminating hyperplane; a random projection does not. So "identity is linearly
decodable" and "an unsupervised hash cannot read it" are the same fact stated from two sides, and the paper can
now say why label-free codes fail rather than only that they do.

**What goes in the manuscript.** V-23's conclusion now has a second, independent reason, and a mechanism instead
of an outcome: it is not that the code is hidden (V-24) and not that clustering was the wrong algorithm (V-39) --
it is that the discriminating directions are a thin subspace of a wide state, and finding them is what the
supervision buys. That is a sharper limitation than the one currently written, and it points at the one
label-free route this run does not test: hashing INSIDE the unsupervised principal subspace. Registered as V-40
before writing any of it.

## V-40 prereg: hashing inside the unsupervised principal subspace. Before any code.

**The one label-free route V-39 leaves open, and why the mechanism points at it.** V-39's failure is attributed:
identity occupies a thin set of directions in a 2,560-dimensional state, so a random hyperplane's sign is
dominated by the symbol-irrelevant remainder. That diagnosis has a direct consequence -- restrict the hash to
the principal subspace first. PCA needs no labels, so the route stays label-free, and V-24 already measured that
thirty-six principal components carry identity at .9999 under a SUPERVISED read.

**The trap I am registering against in advance.** Supervised decodability from a subspace does NOT imply
unsupervised separability within it. V-24's .9999 was a trained probe on those coordinates; a random hyperplane
inside the same subspace still has to beat the within-subspace nuisance variance. So the honest prior is that
this narrows the gap without necessarily closing it, and PARTIAL is the outcome I expect.

**Arms, all label-free, all deterministic, no training set of labels anywhere.** PCA is fitted on a HELD-OUT
arena built with a different seed (seed + 9000) so no fitting touches the evaluated rows, and the fit uses only
span representations, never a symbol id.
  pca_hash_36    project onto the top 36 principal directions, whiten within the subspace, map to the VSA
                 dimension by a fixed random Gaussian, take the sign.
  pca_hash_128   the same at 128 components, in case 36 is too tight for a sign code.
Reference arms: floor, parser, probe_argmax, unchanged. Arena C, HRR, Phi-2, N_SYM 64, N_CTX 32, HOPS 2, seeds
42/123/456.

**Bars.** H = parser - floor, admission H >= 0.20 or void.
(a) LABEL-FREE CODE WORKS iff the better pca_hash arm >= floor + 0.90H in 3/3. The paper's load-bearing
    limitation is then removed rather than measured.
(b) PARTIAL iff >= floor + 0.50H in 3/3. The limitation stays, narrowed, and the manuscript reports that
    restricting the hash to the principal subspace recovers part of the gap.
(c) FAILS iff both arms <= floor + 0.10H in 3/3. Then three independent label-free routes have failed -- k-means
    (V-23), raw hashing (V-39), subspace hashing (V-40) -- and the limitation is stated as a measured property
    of the frozen geometry rather than as a gap in our effort, which is what it currently reads as.
(d) GRADED otherwise.

**Diagnostic, reported whatever happens.** Within-instance same-symbol and different-symbol code cosine, as in
V-39b, plus the same two numbers for the SUPERVISED probe_argmax codes as an upper reference. That third pair is
the one I have never measured and it is what tells us how large the gap between found and hashed directions
really is.

**Prediction on the record.** PARTIAL for pca_hash_36, and the supervised reference showing same-symbol cosine
near one. Nineteen predictions tested today and sixteen failed; the last one in this exact family was wrong in
the optimistic direction, so I weight that.

## V-40 FAILS -- and the three failures together give the limitation its real shape

**Accuracy (arena C, N_SYM 64, N_CTX 32, HOPS 2, 3 seeds; PCA fitted on 25,600 held-out span vectors, top-36
variance share .820, top-128 .986).** floor .5153, parser .9340, probe_argmax .9340, H .4187.
  pca_hash_36   [.492 .518 .500]  0.5033
  pca_hash_128  [.536 .474 .512]  0.5073
Both under the .5572 fails-bar in 3/3. FAILS by the bars at 8c7082f. I predicted PARTIAL. Twenty predictions
tested today, seventeen failed.

**The diagnostic is the result, and it is not a repeat of V-39's.** Within-instance code cosines, where HRR needs
same near one and different near zero:
  lsh_raw        same .5681   diff .4975      both far too high -- crowding
  lsh_inst       same .3154   diff .2181
  pca_hash_36    same .2434   diff .0905      different-symbol now nearly orthogonal, same-symbol collapsed
  pca_hash_128   same .1769   diff .0760
Restricting the hash to the principal subspace FIXED the crowding: .4975 -> .0905 is the near-orthogonality the
algebra needs. It destroyed within-symbol stability in the same move, .5681 -> .2434. Whitening equalises
variance across directions, so the positional and contextual variation of one symbol's own occurrences is
amplified exactly as much as the between-symbol signal.

**What the paper can now say, which it could not before.** The directions that separate symbols also carry the
within-symbol variation, and no unsupervised reweighting we tried separates the two: k-means asks for compact
clusters that do not exist (V-23, purity .29-.36), raw hashing has its sign dominated by 2,524 irrelevant
directions (V-39), and subspace hashing trades crowding for instability (V-40). What the supervision buys is
knowing WHICH variation to discard. Three independent routes, three distinct failure modes, one mechanism. That
replaces a sentence which currently reads as an admission that we did not try hard enough.

**A registered item I did not execute, recorded rather than dropped.** The V-40 prereg said the diagnostic would
include the SUPERVISED codes' cosines as an upper reference. The loop only ran the PCA arms, so that pair was
never measured. It is also tautological: probe_argmax's code IS a codebook row, so the same-symbol cosine is one
whenever the head agrees with itself and the different-symbol cosine is the near-orthogonality of two random
rows, and probe_argmax reproduced the parser exactly in all three seeds, so head agreement is essentially total.
The reference is 1.0 and about 0 by construction. I registered a measurement that turned out to be a definition,
and I am writing that down instead of striking the line.

**Standing tally after twenty registered experiments today.** Twenty predictions tested, seventeen failed. Five
apparatus faults disclosed, the label-space circularity being the worst. Three overclaims withdrawn, one of
which had reached the abstract and one of which was a tautology presented as a measurement. One story assembled
and killed by its own bar within the hour.

## V-41 prereg: can instance-local GROUPING replace global identity? Before any code.

**Why this and not a real-text corpus tonight.** I probed three parquet-native corpora and all three load
(wikimedia/wikipedia streaming, rajpurkar/squad, hotpotqa/hotpot_qa). Building an arena from any of them exposed
the actual blocker, which is not download access: real text has an OPEN entity vocabulary and most entities occur
once, while every identity head in this paper is a fixed-class classifier over a closed set that recurs thousands
of times. bAbI works because four names repeat. A "real corpus" built by forcing the vocabulary closed would be
synthetic wearing a costume, and a head facing unseen entities at test time must fail. So the honest next step is
to remove the closed-vocabulary requirement, not to disguise it.

**The opening V-36 gives.** V-36 established that ANY injective assignment of codebook rows works -- rows are
arbitrary and a permutation is an isomorphism. So the head does not need to NAME a symbol. It only needs to
decide which mentions refer to the same thing, after which rows can be assigned by order of first appearance
inside the instance. That reduces global identity supervision to a mention PARTITION, which is the signal V-35
already measured tolerance for, and which is obtainable from text rather than from a generator.

**Setup.** Arena C, HRR, Phi-2, N_SYM 64, N_CTX 32, HOPS 2, seeds 42/123/456, everything else as the mechanism
table. New arm:
  group_argmax  a matching head scores pairs of span representations; spans are grouped by agglomerating
                positive pairs; each group is assigned the codebook row of its order of first appearance in that
                instance. The head is trained on PAIRWISE same/different labels only. It is never given, and
                cannot output, a global symbol id -- the number of classes it would need does not exist in its
                architecture.
Reference arms: floor, parser, probe_argmax, unchanged.

**Bars.** H = parser - floor, admission H >= 0.20 or void.
(a) GROUPING SUFFICES iff group_argmax >= floor + 0.90H in 3/3. The closed-vocabulary requirement is then not a
    requirement of the mechanism, and open-vocabulary text becomes reachable in principle -- which is the single
    largest structural limitation left in the paper.
(b) PARTIAL iff >= floor + 0.50H in 3/3.
(c) FAILS iff <= floor + 0.10H in 3/3. Then global identity is doing work that grouping cannot, and the paper
    states the closed-vocabulary requirement explicitly as a scope limit rather than leaving it implicit, which
    it currently does.
(d) GRADED otherwise.

**Diagnostic, reported whatever happens.** Pairwise grouping F1 on evaluation spans, and the number of groups
recovered against the true number. This makes a failure attributable: a low chain with high F1 means the
row-assignment scheme is at fault, and a low chain with low F1 means the grouping is, and V-35's tolerance curve
says which side of the cliff the F1 lands on.

**Prediction on the record.** GROUPING SUFFICES on arena C, because the markers are lexically identical so
same-symbol pairs should be easy, and because V-36 says the row assignment cannot matter as long as it is
injective. I expect the hard case to be bAbI, where the same name appears in different syntactic positions, and
that is the next run rather than this one. Twenty predictions tested today and seventeen failed; the last time I
predicted a label-free or supervision-weakening route would work, it did not.

**Note on what this does NOT do.** Even under (a), grouping is still supervised -- by pairwise labels rather than
by names. It is weaker and text-obtainable supervision, not no supervision. V-39 and V-40 already tested no
supervision and it failed. The manuscript must not blur the two.

## V-41 GRADED: instance-local grouping reaches 16% of headroom, and under-splits systematically

**Numbers (arena C, N_SYM 64, N_CTX 32, HOPS 2, 3 seeds; matching head trained on pairwise same/different labels
only, frozen before evaluation; codebook 256 rows since row identity is arbitrary per V-36).**
  floor         [.512 .530 .504]  0.5153
  parser        [.932 .932 .938]  0.9340
  probe_argmax  [.932 .932 .938]  0.9340
  group_argmax  [.572 .598 .572]  0.5807      = 16% of headroom
  H = .4187, so suffices >= .8921, partial >= .7247, fails <= .5572.

**Verdict GRADED by the bars at 4efecad, and I hold to that.** Every seed sits above the FAILS bar and far below
PARTIAL, so the prereg licenses NEITHER reading. I do not get to write "grouping cannot replace identity" and I
do not get to write that it works. What I can report is the measurement and the attribution.

**The attribution, which is the useful part and was registered in advance.** Pairwise F1 on evaluation spans and
recovered group count against the true count:
  seed 42   F1 .4002   35.3 groups vs 58.1 true symbols
  seed 123  F1 .4497   38.6 groups vs 58.1 true symbols
  seed 456  F1 .4150   35.8 groups vs 58.1 true symbols
The head recovers about three fifths of the groups that exist, in all three seeds. That is systematic
UNDER-SPLITTING: distinct symbols are being merged. Training-side F1 was already only .63-.65 with positives at
1.387% of all pairs, so this is not an inference-time threshold artifact -- the head never learned to separate
them. V-35 and V-36 say exactly what under-splitting costs: merging is the non-injective failure and it is the
expensive one, twelve points for merging one symbol of four on natural text. Here roughly twenty-three of
fifty-eight are merged, and the chain lands sixteen per cent up the headroom.

**Why this is a stronger statement than V-39/V-40, and a different one.** V-39 and V-40 removed supervision
entirely and failed. V-41 KEPT supervision and only weakened its form -- pairwise same/different instead of
global names, which is the form obtainable from text rather than from a generator. So the finding is not "labels
are needed"; it is that the specific weaker form we tried does not, in our hands, produce an injective enough
partition on this arena. The route is not closed by this run, and the manuscript will say that.

**What goes in the manuscript, and what does not.** Goes in: the numbers, the under-splitting diagnostic, and an
EXPLICIT scope statement the paper currently leaves implicit -- every identity head here is a fixed-class
classifier over a closed, recurring symbol vocabulary, and that is a requirement of the implementation, not an
incidental choice; open-vocabulary text needs a mechanism this paper does not supply. Does not go in: any claim
that grouping fails in general, and any suggestion that this closes the route.

**Prediction refuted.** I predicted GROUPING SUFFICES on arena C, reasoning that lexically identical markers make
same-symbol pairs easy. They are not easy from pooled state representations: 1.4% positive rate makes the
pairwise problem badly imbalanced and the head collapses toward merging. Twenty-one predictions tested today,
eighteen failed.

**Apparatus notes.** My first launch of this run died mid-flight with no treatment number produced; the dead
artifacts are quarantined as v41_run1_died.log and v41_run1_partial.json so no checker can read them, and the
relaunch (cuda:2) produced everything above. GPU 1 was not used at any point.

## V-42 prereg: the grouping decision rule was specified against the wrong objective. Before any code.

**This is a SECOND attempt at V-41's question, registered after seeing V-41's result, and I say so up front.**
V-41's GRADED verdict stands exactly as reported at f25d34e whatever V-42 returns. Nothing about V-41 is
relabelled retroactively; V-42 is a separate entry with its own outcome.

**What was wrong with V-41, and why this is a specification error rather than a fishing trip.** V-41 chose the
grouping threshold to maximise pairwise F1. F1 weights a false merge and a false split equally. My own earlier
results say they are not equal: V-36 prices a single merge of two symbols at twelve points on natural text
because merging is the non-injective failure, while V-35's SPLIT family -- over-splitting -- was consistently the
cheaper corruption at equal rate. So V-41's selection criterion was chosen against an objective the mechanism
does not have, and it duly picked an operating point that merged: 35 to 39 recovered groups where 58 exist, in
three of three seeds. Fixing the criterion is correcting a specification, and it is the only change I would have
made had I derived the criterion from V-35 and V-36 in the first place.

**Two changes, both derived from that.**
  (1) Balanced pair sampling in training. Positives were 1.4% of all pairs in V-41, and a head trained on that
      imbalance collapses toward calling everything the same thing.
  (2) The threshold is chosen to maximise CHAIN ACCURACY ON TRAINING INSTANCES, not pairwise F1. This uses
      training data only, optimises the quantity the paper actually measures, and is asymmetric in the right
      direction by construction, since over-splitting costs the chain less than merging.
Everything else is V-41 unchanged: arena C, HRR, Phi-2, N_SYM 64, N_CTX 32, HOPS 2, seeds 42/123/456, the
matching head trained on pairwise same-or-different labels only and architecturally unable to emit a global id,
frozen before evaluation, q_vec raising if any path tries to read an id.

**Bars: identical to V-41's, so the two runs are directly comparable.** H = parser - floor, admission H >= 0.20.
(a) GROUPING SUFFICES iff group_argmax >= floor + 0.90H in 3/3. The closed-vocabulary scope condition just
    written into the manuscript would then have to come back out, and I would rewrite it rather than keep a
    limitation I had disproved.
(b) PARTIAL iff >= floor + 0.50H in 3/3. The scope condition stays but is narrowed, and the paper reports that
    the decision rule, not the representation, was the binding constraint.
(c) FAILS iff <= floor + 0.10H in 3/3.
(d) GRADED otherwise, and the manuscript keeps V-41's text with V-42 reported alongside it.

**Diagnostic, reported whatever happens.** Chain accuracy, pairwise F1, recovered groups against true count, and
-- new, because V-41 could not distinguish them -- the merge rate and the split rate separately: the fraction of
same-symbol pairs wrongly separated, and the fraction of different-symbol pairs wrongly joined. If the fix works
the second number should fall and the first should be allowed to rise.

**Prediction on the record.** PARTIAL. The asymmetry argument is sound, but V-41's TRAINING pairwise F1 was
already only .63 to .65, which is evidence about the representation rather than about the threshold, and a better
operating point on a weak score cannot manufacture separability that is not there. I want SUFFICES, and wanting
an outcome has been the reliable predictor of my being wrong today: twenty-one predictions tested, eighteen
failed.

## V-43 prereg: does the handover extrapolate to chain depths it was never trained on? Before any code.

**Why this experiment.** The paper's positive core is that a supervised discrete handover recovers 99-100% of the
parser-over-floor gap. What it has never shown is the property that would make a symbolic route worth its cost:
COMPOSITIONAL EXTRAPOLATION. The algebra binds and unbinds one hop at a time, so a code learned at one depth
should compose at greater depths with no retraining, while anything learned from pooled states has no such
structure and must degrade. V-19 swept depths one to four but trained and evaluated at the SAME depth every
time, so extrapolation is untested.

**Stated honestly in advance: half of this is true by construction and I will not present that half as a
discovery.** The identity head maps a span to a symbol and never sees the chain, so it is depth-agnostic
trivially. What is NOT by construction is (i) whether HRR retrieval survives the extra hops with a code of that
quality, and (ii) whether the learned baselines fail where it holds. The claim only means something as a
CONTRAST, so the contrast is part of the bar rather than a remark afterwards.

**Setup.** Arena C, HRR, Phi-2, N_SYM 64, N_CTX 32, seeds 42/123/456. Everything trained at HOPS = 2 and then
evaluated, with no retraining and no refitting of any parameter, at HOPS = 2 (control), 3, and 4. Arms:
  probe_argmax   the supervised discrete handover -- head trained at depth 2 only
  floor          a linear probe on the pooled frozen state, trained at depth 2 only
  parser         exact codebook rows, which learn nothing and therefore mark what the algebra alone can do
Each depth has its own freshly generated evaluation arena.

**Bars.** Per evaluation depth d, H_d = parser_d - floor_d, and admission H_d >= 0.20 or that depth is void.
(a) EXTRAPOLATES iff, at BOTH d = 3 and d = 4, probe_argmax >= floor_d + 0.90 H_d in 3/3 seeds AND
    probe_argmax_d >= 0.90 x probe_argmax_2 in 3/3. Both halves required: clearing the headroom bar while
    collapsing in absolute terms would not be extrapolation, and holding absolute accuracy on a depth whose own
    floor has risen would not be either.
(b) THE CONTRAST HOLDS iff, at both d = 3 and d = 4, the depth-2-trained floor probe is <= floor_d + 0.10 H_d in
    3/3 -- i.e. the learned-from-states route really does fail to transfer. If the probe transfers too, the
    symbolic route's advantage here is not compositional and I say so.
(c) FAILS iff probe_argmax <= floor_d + 0.10 H_d in 3/3 at either depth.
(d) GRADED otherwise.
A positive result requires (a) AND (b). (a) alone is reported as "holds but without a contrast", which is weaker
than what this paper needs and I will label it that way.

**Prediction on the record.** (a) holds, (b) holds. This is the first time today I am predicting a positive
outcome for a reason that is structural rather than hopeful: the head is per-span and the algebra is per-hop, so
neither has a depth parameter to be wrong about, while a probe on a pooled state at depth 4 is being asked about
a sequence twice as long as any it saw. Twenty-one predictions tested today, eighteen failed, and I note that
the three that held were the ones where I could name the mechanism in advance rather than hope for it.

**What a negative would mean.** If probe_argmax degrades across depth while parser does not, the code's quality
is depth-sensitive in a way the paper currently denies, and the mechanism section needs a caveat. If parser
degrades too, that is a capacity limit of HRR at this dimension and belongs in the capacity discussion, which
already predicts monotone decay with binding count (V-14: 1.000 down to .934).

## V-43: the handover composes at a depth it never trained on -- and my contrast bar was circular

**Numbers (arena C, N_SYM 64, N_CTX 32, HRR, Phi-2; everything trained at HOPS=2, nothing refitted at 3 or 4;
decision thresholds fitted on the training depth only).**

  depth   probe_argmax            parser                  probe trained at depth 2, evaluated here
  2       .948 .938 .942  .9427   .948 .938 .942  .9427   .488 .498 .496  .4940
  3       .872 .850 .858  .8600   .872 .850 .858  .8600   .524 .444 .450  .4727
  4       .590 .572 .578  .5800   .582 .574 .586  .5807   .478 .556 .548  .5273

**THE POSITIVE RESULT.** At depth 3 -- a chain length the identity head never saw -- probe_argmax equals the
parser to four decimals in all three seeds. The head was trained on depth-2 spans, nothing was refitted, and the
chain still tracks exact codebook rows exactly. The algebra's own ceiling falls over the same interval, .9427 to
.8600, and the handover falls WITH it rather than away from it. That is the compositional property a symbolic
route is supposed to buy, measured rather than asserted, and it is the first result today that came out the way
I predicted for a structural reason: the head is per-span and the algebra is per-hop, so neither carries a depth
parameter that could be wrong.

**Depth 4 is VOID by the registered admission gate and I make no claim there.** parser .5807 against a
transferred probe at .5273 leaves headroom of .053, far under the .20 admission, so no arm comparison is
possible. This is HRR capacity running out, in the direction V-14 already measured (parser decaying monotonically
with binding count, 1.000 to .934 there). Honest ceiling, not a failure of the handover.

**And a bar of mine that cannot be read: (b), the contrast, is CIRCULAR as I coded it.** The prereg said the
contrast holds iff the depth-2-trained probe lands at or below floor_d + 0.10 H_d. But in the code floor_d IS
that same transferred probe -- I never measured a probe trained AT depth 3 or 4. So the test compared the probe
against the mean of itself, which asks whether the seeds agree, not whether the learned-from-states route fails
to transfer. The contrast is therefore NOT established by this run and I am not reporting it as established.
What the numbers do show, without the bar: a depth-2-trained probe sits at .4727 and .5273 on depths 3 and 4,
which is chance on a balanced task. What they cannot show is whether a probe trained AT those depths would do
better -- if it would not, the arena is simply unsolvable from pooled states there and the contrast is about the
task rather than about transfer.

**The missing control is cheap and is registered next as V-44** -- a probe trained at each evaluation depth,
which is what "floor" was supposed to mean. Until it runs, the manuscript may state the depth-3 extrapolation
result and may NOT state the contrast.

**Tally.** Twenty-two predictions tested today, eighteen failed. Six apparatus or specification faults disclosed,
this being the sixth and the second one where a bar I wrote could not answer the question I wrote it for.

## V-44 prereg: the control V-43 was missing -- a probe trained AT each evaluation depth. Before any code.

**What is being fixed.** V-43's contrast bar was circular: it defined floor_d as the depth-2-trained probe and
then tested that probe against the mean of itself. The quantity that was supposed to sit there is a probe trained
AT depth d, which is the only thing that says whether a learned-from-states route can do the task at that depth
at all. Without it, "the transferred probe is at chance" is ambiguous between "transfer fails" and "the task is
not solvable from pooled states here".

**Setup.** Identical arenas to V-43 (arena C, N_SYM 64, N_CTX 32, HRR, Phi-2, seeds 42/123/456, evaluation
arenas at seeds 4242+d so the same instances are scored). For each depth d in {2, 3, 4}, a fresh linear probe on
the pooled frozen state is trained on a depth-d TRAINING arena and evaluated on the depth-d evaluation arena.
Nothing else is rerun; V-43's probe_argmax and parser numbers are reused as banked, because this run changes
only the floor.

**Bars.**
(a) THE CONTRAST HOLDS iff, at d = 3, probe_argmax >= floor_d^same + 0.90 x (parser_d - floor_d^same) in 3/3
    AND the depth-2-transferred probe from V-43 is at least 0.05 below floor_d^same in 3/3 -- i.e. training at
    the evaluation depth genuinely helps the probe, so its failure after transfer is a failure OF TRANSFER.
(b) THE CONTRAST IS ABOUT THE TASK, NOT TRANSFER iff floor_d^same is within 0.05 of the transferred probe in 3/3
    at d = 3. Then the arena is not solvable from pooled states at that depth regardless of training depth, the
    comparison says nothing about compositionality, and the manuscript reports the extrapolation result with
    that caveat attached and no contrast claim.
(c) ADMISSION: parser_d - floor_d^same >= 0.20 at d = 3, else that depth is void for the contrast.
(d) Depth 4 is expected to stay void on admission and is reported, not scored.

**Prediction on the record.** (b), the deflationary outcome. A pooled mean over a 768-token sequence carrying
thirty-two role-filler pairs per level almost certainly cannot express a three-hop lookup at any training depth,
so I expect the same-depth probe to sit near chance too and the contrast to dissolve. I would rather register
that expectation now than discover it after writing a compositionality claim into the paper. If (a) comes out
instead, the contrast is real and the manuscript gets the stronger sentence.

**Either way the depth-3 extrapolation result from V-43 stands.** It does not depend on this run: probe_argmax
equalling parser to four decimals at an unseen depth is a statement about the handover and the algebra, not about
any probe. What this run decides is only whether the paper may ALSO say the learned alternative cannot follow.

## V-42 GRADED: the criterion was wrong, correcting it changed the operating point, and the chain did not move

**Numbers (arena C, N_SYM 64, N_CTX 32, HOPS 2, 3 seeds; same head architecture as V-41, negatives sampled down
to the positive count, threshold chosen on TRAINING chain accuracy).**
  group_argmax  [.606 .552 .590]  0.5827      (V-41, F1-selected threshold: [.572 .598 .572] 0.5807)
  floor .5153, parser .9340, H .4187; suffices >= .8921, partial >= .7247, fails <= .5572.
Verdict GRADED: seed 123 at .552 sits below the FAILS bar while the other two sit above it, so neither reading is
licensed. I hold to that.

**The criterion fix worked, and that is what makes this informative.** Thresholds moved from .40/.42 (V-41) to
.50/.60/.50, and the head accepted a WORSE pairwise F1 in exchange -- .63-.65 down to .46-.48 -- exactly the
asymmetric trade the prereg said to make. The diagnostic confirms it did what it was meant to do:
  seed 42   F1 .4633  groups 50.0  merge_rate .0132  split_rate .4141
  seed 123  F1 .4814  groups 60.9  merge_rate .0076  split_rate .5111
  seed 456  F1 .4753  groups 50.3  merge_rate .0126  split_rate .4086
Merging is essentially gone: V-41 recovered 35-39 groups against 58.1 true symbols, V-42 recovers 50-61, and the
merge rate is about one per cent. And the chain is unchanged, .5827 against .5807.

**So my specification-error explanation for V-41 is refuted by my own fix.** The threshold was indeed chosen
against the wrong objective, and correcting it did move the operating point, and the chain did not follow. What
binds is the representation, not the decision rule -- which is what V-41's TRAINING pairwise F1 of .63-.65 was
already saying and what I registered as the reason to expect only PARTIAL.

**A reconciliation the paper needs, because V-35 will otherwise be misread.** V-35 found over-splitting CHEAPER
than merging at equal rate. V-42 avoids merging only by over-splitting 41-51% of same-symbol pairs, and gains
nothing. Both are true because the two "splits" are different operations:
  V-35's split is LABEL NOISE at training time. The head is a deterministic function of the state, so identical
    mentions still receive identical codes at inference; the noise is averaged away, and one mention in ten
    mislabelled costs only .946.
  V-42's split is a DECISION at inference. The head genuinely assigns two occurrences of one symbol to different
    groups, so the key used to unbind is not the key that was bound, and there is nothing to average over.
The manuscript must say this, or "over-splitting is the cheap error" reads as licence to split freely, which this
run shows it is not.

**Prediction outcome.** I predicted PARTIAL; it came out GRADED, with the mean unmoved. Twenty-three predictions
tested today, nineteen failed.

## V-45 prereg: the compositional contrast, on a substrate where the baseline actually works. Before any code.

**What V-44 left open.** V-43 showed the handover composes at an untrained depth. V-44 then removed the stronger
reading: on arena C a pooled-state probe cannot do the task at depth three at ANY training depth, so its failure
after transfer says nothing about compositionality -- there was never a route to fail. The contrast needs a
substrate where the learned baseline demonstrably works at the training setting and then loses it. bAbI task 1
is that substrate: the six-way pooled-state probe scores .771 there, which is real purchase, not chance.

**The axis.** Story length. bAbI task 1 instances vary in how many statements precede the question. Longer
stories mean more distractor locations in the bundle and a longer sequence for a pooled mean to summarise. Train
on SHORT stories, evaluate on short (control) and LONG (held out by length, never trained on).
  short   instances with at most 6 statements
  long    instances with at least 10 statements
Buckets are by statement count only; if either bucket has fewer than 150 evaluation instances the run reports
that and is void, because a contrast measured on a handful of stories is not a contrast.

**Arms, all trained on the SHORT bucket only and evaluated on both, nothing refitted.**
  floor          six-way linear probe on the pooled frozen state
  parser         exact codebook rows -- learns nothing, marks what the algebra alone does at each length
  probe_argmax   the supervised discrete handover
The recency rule is supplied from outside the algebra at both lengths, as in V-30, since a superposition cannot
express recency and this run is about length rather than about that limit.

**Bars.** Per bucket, H = parser - floor, admission H >= 0.20 or that bucket is void.
(a) THE BASELINE HAS PURCHASE (required before any contrast may be claimed) iff floor on the SHORT bucket is
    >= 0.70 in 3/3. If the probe is near chance even on short stories, this substrate is no better than arena C
    for this purpose and I say so and stop.
(b) EXTRAPOLATES iff probe_argmax on LONG >= floor_long + 0.90 H_long in 3/3 AND >= 0.90 x its own SHORT
    accuracy in 3/3.
(c) THE CONTRAST HOLDS iff the probe's LONG accuracy is at least 0.10 below its SHORT accuracy in 3/3 -- it had
    the ability and lost it with length.
(d) A POSITIVE RESULT REQUIRES (a) AND (b) AND (c). (b) without (c) is reported as "extrapolates, no contrast",
    the same outcome V-43 ended with, and is labelled that way rather than dressed up.
(e) FAILS iff probe_argmax on LONG <= floor_long + 0.10 H_long in 3/3.

**Diagnostic, reported whatever happens.** Bucket sizes; mean statements and mean distinct locations per bucket;
per-span identity accuracy of the head on the LONG bucket, so that a failure separates "the head stopped
recognising symbols in longer contexts" from "the algebra ran out of capacity at more bindings".

**Prediction on the record.** (a) holds, (b) holds, (c) holds. The head is per-span and cannot see story length;
the algebra binds one statement at a time and its capacity decays gradually, as V-14 measured; a pooled mean over
a longer story is being asked to summarise strictly more distractors with the same width. Twenty-three
predictions tested today, nineteen failed, and the ones that held were those where I could name the mechanism in
advance -- as here.

**What a negative means.** If (c) fails because the probe holds up on long stories, then pooled states carry this
task robustly and the paper's "why prefer a symbolic route" section is weaker than currently written, and I would
have to say so. If (b) fails, the handover is length-sensitive and the extrapolation claim from V-43 narrows to
depth rather than generalising to context size.

## V-45 RECONCILIATION: the .771 is SOURCED (it is V-30's floor) and the discrepancy has a named cause -- the two
## harnesses compute "pooled" differently. Zero GPU; everything below is read from committed code and the ledger.

**The source.** The V-45 prereg's premise figure ("the six-way pooled-state probe scores .771") is V-30's floor,
this ledger, 2026-08-21 entry "V-30: MECHANISM FAILS ON NATURAL TEXT": bAbI task 1, 900 train / 500 eval
instances, ALL story lengths mixed, phi-2 frozen states, 3 seeds -> .780 .782 .752, mean .7713 (prereg lineage
0c17441). The V-45 verdict's "unsourced" flag is hereby lifted; the number is real and ledgered. What was wrong
was citing it as if it measured the arm V-45 built.

**The named confound: same word, different operator.**
  v30.py pooled() (lines 121-123): idx = am.sum(-1)-1; return H[arange, idx]  -- the LAST-TOKEN hidden state.
    On a causal LM this position summarises the entire prefix, and it sits nearest the final statement, so it
    carries recency structurally.
  v45.py pooled() (lines 27-29): (H*m).sum(0)/m.sum()  -- a masked MEAN over all tokens. Recency-blind, and the
    signal is diluted across the whole story.
The V-45 prereg even argued from "a pooled mean over a longer story" while citing a number measured on
last-token pooling. Both floors are honest implementations of the phrase "probe on the pooled frozen state";
they are not the same measurement, and .77 vs .34-.36 on the same substrate is the size of that gap.

**Secondary difference, disclosed:** V-30's probe trained on 900 mixed-length instances; V-45's on 540
short-only. Plausibly smaller, but not separable from the pooling change without a run, and no run is licensed
here.

**What this does and does not change.** V-45's verdict STANDS AS MEASURED: for the harness as built, bar (a)
failed 3/3 and no contrast is claimed. What changes is the reading: "the .771 did not reproduce" overstated it --
V-45 never re-measured V-30's floor; it measured a different floor arm that shares a name. The two results are
consistent: last-token probe .7713 (V-30), mean-pooled probe .34-.36 (V-45), same frozen states.

**Manuscript instruction.** Wherever the paper cites the .771 floor it must say LAST-TOKEN (final-position)
probe, not "pooled mean"; and the V-45 natural-data paragraph, if kept, must describe its floor as mean-pooled
and cite this reconciliation rather than saying the earlier number failed to reproduce.

**What would be licensed next (NOT run now).** A fresh prereg naming this confound could re-run the V-45
length-contrast with V-30's last-token floor. Registered expectation if it ever runs: the last-token floor
clears the 0.70 admission on short stories, restoring bar (a) -- that is a prediction on the record, not a
result. Under discipline 2 this entry changes no code and launches nothing.

(a) BASELINE HAS PURCHASE iff the last-token floor >= 0.70 on SHORT in 3/3. If (a) fails, the V-30/V-45 gap
    is NOT explained by the pooling operator alone and the 900-mixed vs 540-short training cut becomes the
    live suspect; I say so and stop -- no training-set enlargement without a fresh prereg.
(b) SYMBOLIC ROUTE EXTRAPOLATES iff probe_argmax on LONG >= floor_long + 0.90*H_long in 3/3 AND >= 0.90x its
    own SHORT accuracy in 3/3 (H as defined in V-45: headroom above the measured floor).
(c) CONTRAST HOLDS iff the last-token floor loses >= 0.10 absolute short->long in 3/3.
(d) A POSITIVE RESULT REQUIRES (a) AND (b) AND (c). (b) without (c) is reported verbatim as "extrapolates,
    no contrast" -- the V-43 outcome, not dressed up.
(e) FAILS iff probe_argmax on LONG <= floor_long + 0.10*H_long in 3/3.

**Predictions on the record, mechanisms named.** (a) HOLDS -- the last-token state of a causal LM summarises
the entire prefix and V-30 measured .7713 on mixed lengths; residual risk is the smaller short-only train set.
(This repeats the expectation already registered in the reconciliation entry.) (b) HOLDS -- the symbolic route
measured 1.000 at both lengths in V-45 and nothing in this change touches it. (c) HOLDS -- the last-token
state is recency-carrying; in longer stories the last mention of the queried entity sits on average further
from the final position and must survive more intervening bindings at fixed width (V-14's gradual capacity
decay is the mechanism). Confidence is lowest on (c), disclosed: the same recency structure that gives (a)
its purchase could keep recency-dominated instances easy at any length, in which case (c) fails and the floor
is reported as length-robust.

## V-46 prereg: two floors that cannot both be right. Before any code.

**The discrepancy.** The manuscript quotes .771 as the bAbI task-1 floor -- a six-way linear probe on the pooled
frozen state, from V-30 (.780/.782/.752). V-45 ran the same probe architecture for the same number of epochs and
got .3506 on short stories and .2150 on long ones. A mixture of .35 and .22 cannot be .77, so at least one of
these numbers does not mean what I have been taking it to mean, and .771 is load-bearing: it is the reference
against which the natural-text headroom, the twenty-three-point coverage cost and the .976 anomaly are all
stated.

**What I should have measured in V-45 and did not.** The MAJORITY-CLASS rate per bucket. Short stories average
3.13 distinct locations out of six, so .3506 may simply be the label prior, meaning the probe learned nothing --
which would be a fact about my bucketing, not about length. Omitting a prior baseline is the exact defect this
paper's audit half is about, and I omitted it.

**Setup, three cells, everything else identical to V-45's code path.**
  (1) ALL-LENGTH: no bucketing, n_train 2000 as in V-30, probe trained and evaluated on all lengths.
  (2) SHORT-ONLY and LONG-ONLY: V-45's buckets, rerun so the comparison is within one code path.
  (3) For every cell and every bucket: the majority-class rate on the evaluation set, and the probe's TRAINING
      accuracy, so underfitting and label-prior effects are separable.
Seeds 42/123/456 throughout.

**Bars.**
(a) REPRODUCES iff the ALL-LENGTH floor is within 0.05 of .7713 in 3/3. Then .771 stands, V-45's low floors are
    an effect of restricting to short stories, and that effect itself has to be reported: it would mean the probe's
    apparent competence on bAbI comes from the long stories, which is the opposite of what a length-extrapolation
    story would want.
(b) DOES NOT REPRODUCE iff the ALL-LENGTH floor is more than 0.10 below .7713 in 3/3. Then the manuscript's .771
    is wrong or means something else, every claim scaled against it must be rechecked, and I go find which.
(c) GRADED in between: report both and reconcile before any manuscript change.
(d) Independently: if the majority-class rate is within 0.03 of the probe accuracy in any cell, that cell's probe
    is reported as having learned nothing beyond the prior, whatever the bar above says.

**Prediction on the record.** (a) reproduces, and the majority-class rate on the short bucket is close to .35 --
i.e. both numbers are right and my short-bucket probe learned nothing beyond the prior. That would mean V-45's
bar (a) failed for a reason I created by bucketing, and that the length-extrapolation result stands but still
without a contrast. I have been wrong nineteen times out of twenty-three today, and this is a prediction I would
rather have checked than assumed -- which is the whole point of the entry.

**Consequence either way.** The positive half of V-45 is untouched: the handover reaches 1.0000 on ten-statement
stories with a head trained only on six-statement ones, span identity 1.0000, three of three. What V-46 decides
is whether the paper's bAbI floor is what the paper says it is.
