## V-59 prereg: VSA proposes, the frozen LLM disposes. Before any code.

**The integration family this tests, and why it is the untested one.** Five ways of combining a VSA with a
language model appear in the literature or in this paper: reading internal states into an external algebra
(ours), external retrieval with one LLM call (PathHD), interpretability decoding (Bronzini et al.), architectural
binding heads (proposed in the attention-as-binding line, never demonstrated), and injecting the algebra's
output back into the frozen model's CONTEXT. The last is untried anywhere we can find, costs no training of any
kind, and matches the deployment constraint most practitioners actually have: no fine-tuning, no access to
internals, prompt-level integration only.

**The question that makes it non-trivial.** On the two tasks where the algebra itself caps -- task 4 at .691 and
task 15 at .836, both from same-type cleanup interference -- the hint fed back to the model is WRONG one time in
three or one in six. So this is not "give the model the answer": it is whether a frozen model can act as an
error-corrector over a noisy symbolic memory, using the story text it already has. If the combination beats BOTH
components, the integration is complementary and that is a new positive; if the model just copies the hint, the
combination tracks the algebra and adds nothing; if the hint drags the model below its own prompting score, the
integration is harmful.

**Setup.** Tasks 4 and 15, zero-shot prompting on Phi-2 with one appended line before "Answer:":
"An external memory system suggests the answer is <X>." where <X> is the parser-arm VSA retrieval for that
instance (codes from gold ids, so the errors are pure algebra interference -- the cleanest noisy-oracle
available, and no LLM states are involved in producing it). Controls, same three prompt draws each:
  no-hint        zero-shot prompting alone (banked: .4411 on task 4, .3867 on task 15)
  vsa-hint       the line above, X from the algebra (accuracy .691 / .836)
  random-hint    X drawn uniformly from the answer set (accuracy ~.17 / .25), same wording -- this measures
                 blind following: if vsa-hint tracks hint accuracy and random-hint drags the model to chance,
                 the model is copying, not correcting.
Per-instance parser retrievals are recomputed inside the run and saved, so the hint accuracy is measured on the
same instances, not assumed.

**Bars, per task.**
(a) COMPLEMENTARY iff vsa-hint >= parser + 0.05 AND vsa-hint >= no-hint + 0.05, in 3/3 draws. The combination
    then beats both components and "VSA proposes, LLM disposes" is a real integration mode.
(b) COPYING iff |vsa-hint - parser| <= 0.02 in 3/3 AND random-hint <= no-hint - 0.10 in 3/3. The model follows
    whatever it is told; the combination inherits the algebra's ceiling and adds nothing.
(c) HARMFUL iff vsa-hint <= no-hint - 0.05 in 3/3.
(d) GRADED otherwise.

**Predictions on the record.** Task 15 COMPLEMENTARY (the class statements are in the story, so the model can
check a suggested predator against "mice are afraid of wolves" and override bad hints); task 4 COPYING or GRADED
(direction inversion is exactly what the model failed at unaided, so it cannot check the hint). Forty-one
predictions tested this run, twenty-seven failed; both of these are mechanism-derived, which is the class that
has held.

**What this does either way.** COMPLEMENTARY on either task adds a no-training integration result the collection
audience can use directly, under the frozen-deployment framing being added to the manuscript in the same pass.
COPYING or HARMFUL bounds the fifth family the way task 15 bounded the second, and the taxonomy paragraph says
so. Either outcome, the five-family map with two measured entries of ours goes into the Discussion.

## V-59: the frozen model follows the memory; it does not check it

**Numbers (Phi-2 zero-shot, hint = the parser-arm retrieval recomputed per instance, three codebook seeds).**
  task 15   hint_acc .824/.848/.836   no-hint .2260   vsa-hint .822/.846/.834   random-hint .2407
  task 4    hint_acc .674/.702/.696   no-hint .4720   vsa-hint .674/.702/.696   random-hint .1747
Verdicts by the bars at e0901ff: task 4 COPYING (vsa-hint equals hint accuracy TO THE SEED, and a random hint
drags the model from .47 to .17 -- it abandons even what it could do unaided); task 15 GRADED, and only because
the no-hint baseline of .226 left too little room for the random hint to knock off the registered .10 -- the
behavioural pattern is the same following.

**My complementarity prediction failed on task 15.** I predicted the model would check suggested predators
against the class statements in the story. It does not: vsa-hint tracks hint accuracy within two thousandths.
Forty-two predictions tested, twenty-eight failed.

**What the fifth family is, then.** Prompt-level injection makes a frozen model INHERIT the algebra, exactly:
+61 points on task 15 (.226 to .834) with zero training and zero access to internals, and a ceiling equal to the
algebra's accuracy, to the seed. The integration works where the algebra is exact (task 2: hint accuracy would
be 1.000, so the combination is 1.000) and faithfully reproduces its errors where it is not. No error correction
occurs in either direction. This is the controlled version of what single-call adjudication designs assume, and
it sharpens the deployment guidance: the per-task exactness check is not optional under prompt-level
integration, because the model will not save you from the algebra's mistakes.

**The five-family integration map, with our two measured entries.** Reading internals into an external algebra
(this paper's handover: +20 over an equally supervised fine-tune at two hops, +61 over prompting); external
retrieval with one LLM call (PathHD: gains concentrated on the multi-hop benchmark); interpretability decoding
(no capability claim); architectural binding heads (proposed, undemonstrated); and prompt-level injection (this
entry: inheritance without correction). Goes into the Discussion under the frozen-deployment framing.

## V-60 prereg: the binding-head MVP -- does discreteness plus injectivity pressure rescue end-to-end learning?
## Before any code.

**What this tests.** The manuscript now makes three falsifiable predictions for architectural binding heads, and
the first is testable tonight without training a new transformer: a binding module trained end-to-end will fail
unless it has BOTH a discrete codebook and an explicit injectivity objective. The through-the-loss spans arm --
continuous codes, no discreteness, no injectivity pressure -- is the measured baseline of that failure (.4833 at
floor on arena C; 37.6% of headroom on bAbI task 2).

**Arms, all end-to-end through the task loss on frozen Phi-2 states, arena C (N_SYM 64, N_CTX 32, HOPS 2),
seeds 42/123/456, the same training budget family as the spans arm.**
  vq_spans     projection -> vector-quantised against a 128-row learnable codebook (straight-through), the
               quantised code used in bind/unbind/cleanup. Discreteness alone; NO injectivity objective.
  vq_inj       the same, plus an injectivity objective that uses TASK STRUCTURE and no identity labels: the
               arena's generator guarantees that all role spans within one level are distinct symbols, so a
               penalty forcing distinct codebook assignments for the role spans of one level supervises
               injectivity without ever naming a symbol. Plus a codebook-usage entropy term against collapse.
  Banked references: floor .5153, parser .9340, spans (continuous) .4833-.5024 at the floor.

**Bars. H = parser - floor from this run's own floor and parser, admission H >= 0.20.**
(a) DISCRETENESS ALONE SUFFICES iff vq_spans >= floor + 0.90H in 3/3. This would REFUTE prediction 1 as stated
    (I predict vq_spans <= floor + 0.10H, reproducing the continuous arm).
(b) THE RECIPE WORKS iff vq_inj >= floor + 0.90H in 3/3. The first end-to-end route to work anywhere in this
    paper; the central negative upgrades from "end-to-end never works" to "end-to-end works given discreteness
    and injectivity pressure", which is a recipe, and the binding-head prediction gains a measured entry.
(c) RECIPE PARTIAL iff vq_inj >= floor + 0.50H in 3/3.
(d) RECIPE FAILS iff vq_inj <= floor + 0.10H in 3/3. The prescribed remedy is insufficient at this scale and the
    manuscript says so -- the prediction paragraph then reads "necessary" rather than "sufficient", which is a
    weakening I would have to write.
Diagnostics reported whatever happens, so failure is attributable: codebook usage (distinct rows used /
128), within-level role-distinctness rate at inference, and within-instance same-symbol code-consistency --
the three failure modes (collapse, non-injectivity, instability) separated.

**Predictions on the record.** vq_spans FAILS (discreteness alone does not supply injectivity -- V-55's collapse
was not about continuity). vq_inj PARTIAL: the pressure is only on roles, fillers can still collide, and
credit assignment through a hard cleanup remains brutal; I put full RECIPE WORKS at maybe one in four. Forty-two
predictions tested, twenty-eight failed; both of these are mechanism-derived.

**Scope note, in advance.** This is the binding-head family's cheapest corner -- a head on top of frozen states,
not heads inside the layers. A positive here does not demonstrate the architectural family; it demonstrates the
recipe's two ingredients matter in the way predicted, which is what the paragraph in the Discussion claims and
no more.

## V-60: discreteness alone collapses; discreteness plus injectivity pressure escapes collapse and still fails

**Numbers (arena C, N_SYM 64, N_CTX 32, HOPS 2, 3 seeds; floor .5153, parser .9340, H .4187).**
  vq_spans   [.474 .474 .474]  .4740    codebook used 1/128 in ALL THREE seeds -- total collapse
  vq_inj     [.500 .516 .526]  .5140    codebook used 28/13/18 of 128; same-symbol consistency .27/.25/.17
Verdicts by the bars at ba31359: vq_spans FAILS (as predicted -- the straight-through estimator's unpressured
optimum is one code for everything, and the diagnostics show exactly that); RECIPE FAILS (I predicted PARTIAL;
forty-four predictions tested, twenty-nine failed).

**The mechanism picture is complete and it is a trade, not a wall.** Without pressure, VQ collapses to a single
row. With the structure-derived injectivity pressure and the usage-entropy term, the codebook escapes collapse --
one row becomes 13 to 28 -- but 28 is still fewer than the 32 roles of a single level, so by pigeonhole the
within-level distinctness rate is necessarily zero; and the price of spreading was stability, with same-symbol
consistency falling to .17-.27. The two requirements the algebra makes -- one code per symbol, different codes
for different symbols -- were never satisfied simultaneously: the unpressured head gives the first trivially and
the pressured head trades it away for a partial version of the second.

**What the manuscript's binding-head paragraph becomes.** Prediction 1 upgrades from prediction to measurement in
its negative half: a binding head without discreteness-plus-injectivity reproduces the through-the-loss failure
(measured), AND those two ingredients are necessary but not shown sufficient (measured here at this scale -- 800
instances, a head on frozen states). The sufficiency claim is withdrawn from the wording; what would establish it
remains open: larger codebooks with hard usage floors, EMA codebook updates, curriculum from one hop, or heads
inside the layers where gradients shape the states too. Recorded as directions, not promises.

**Why this negative is worth having.** It is the first measured data point for the architectural family anyone
can cite, it converts one of our three falsifiable predictions into a half-confirmed, half-open result before any
referee asks, and the diagnostics give the next attempt its exact failure modes: collapse pressure must be
overcome WITHOUT destabilising same-symbol assignment, which no term we used achieves at once.

## V-61 prereg: the standard anti-collapse toolkit, aimed at V-60's diagnosed trade-off. Before any code.

**What V-60 diagnosed and what this changes.** V-60's soft repulsion escaped collapse (1 -> 13-28 rows) only by
destabilising same-symbol assignment (.17-.27 consistency). The VQ literature's standard fixes for exactly this
collapse are non-adversarial: k-means initialisation of the codebook from encoder outputs, EMA codebook updates,
and dead-code reinitialisation. None of them pushes codes apart by force, so none should charge the stability
price the repulsion term did. V-61 swaps the repulsion for that toolkit and adds a curriculum arm, since credit
assignment through one cleanup (one hop) is strictly easier than through two.

**Arms, end-to-end through the task loss on frozen Phi-2 states, arena C, seeds 42/123/456, no identity labels
anywhere.**
  vq_ema       128-row codebook, k-means-initialised from the projected training spans (unsupervised), EMA
               updates, dead codes reinitialised to random encoder outputs each epoch. Trained at HOPS=2.
  vq_ema_cur   the same, with a curriculum: two epochs at HOPS=1, then continue at HOPS=2.
Reference arms floor and parser rerun for admission. V-60's vq_spans and vq_inj are the banked comparisons.

**Bars, H = parser - floor, admission H >= 0.20.**
(a) THE TOOLKIT WORKS iff either arm >= floor + 0.90H in 3/3. First end-to-end success in this paper; it enters
    Results (not just the Discussion paragraph) as the measured completion of binding-head prediction 1, and the
    "necessary but not shown sufficient" wording upgrades to "sufficient at this scale with the standard
    toolkit".
(b) PARTIAL iff either arm >= floor + 0.50H in 3/3.
(c) FAILS iff both arms <= floor + 0.10H in 3/3. The negative deepens: collapse-fighting without a stability
    price still does not produce an injective code, and the Discussion says the toolkit was tried.
(d) GRADED otherwise.
Diagnostics as V-60 (codebook_used, role_distinct_rate, same_symbol_consistency) so the trade-off is visible.

**Predictions on the record.** vq_ema escapes collapse decisively (usage > 32 rows, the pigeonhole line) because
k-means init starts spread and EMA cannot collapse what the encoder keeps apart; whether accuracy follows is the
open question and I put vq_ema at GRADED, vq_ema_cur at PARTIAL with maybe one chance in three of full success.
Forty-four predictions tested, twenty-nine failed; the curriculum hunch is the least mechanism-grounded thing I
have registered tonight and I say so.

**If it works it goes in the current paper, per the user's directive** -- as a Results paragraph with its own
checker, not as future work.

## V-62 prereg: FSQ -- eliminate collapse by construction, and see what failure is left. Before any code.

**Why FSQ, from the literature and from our own diagnostics.** V-60/61 established that collapse is a
gravitational attractor of this objective: without pressure the codebook falls to one row; every anti-collapse
tool we tried (repulsion, entropy, k-means init, EMA, dead-code reinit, a hop curriculum) buys spread only by
destabilising same-symbol assignment (consistency .07-.27). Finite Scalar Quantization (Mentzer et al., 2023)
removes the codebook entirely: project to a few dimensions, round each to a fixed grid, straight-through. There
is nothing to collapse and nothing to drift toward -- the two failure modes we measured are excluded BY
CONSTRUCTION on the quantiser side. Whatever fails after that is the encoder, not the quantisation machinery.

**Design.** fsq head: proj HID -> 6 dims, tanh, each dim rounded to 7 levels (implicit codebook 7^6 = 117,649,
no learnable codebook). The quantised low-dim point is expanded to VSA_DIM by a FIXED random matrix and
normalised; binding, unbinding and cleanup as everywhere. DECLARED LIMITATION, in advance: under a linear
expansion, code similarity inherits grid distance, so two symbols placed at nearby grid points get correlated
codes rather than the near-orthogonal ones the parser enjoys -- the head must learn to place distinct symbols
FAR APART on the grid, which is the injectivity problem again, now with the quantiser exonerated. Pairwise code
cosine between distinct symbols is therefore a registered diagnostic, alongside distinct-tuples-used,
within-level role distinctness, and same-symbol consistency (the drift measure).
Arms: fsq_spans (task loss only) and fsq_inj (plus the V-60 structure-derived role repulsion, no labels).
Arena C, seeds 42/123/456, same budget family as V-60/61.

**Bars, H = parser - floor, admission >= 0.20.**
(a) FSQ WORKS iff either arm >= floor + 0.90H in 3/3: first end-to-end success, enters Results, and the
    binding-head paragraph credits the quantiser fix.
(b) PARTIAL iff >= floor + 0.50H in 3/3.
(c) FAILS iff both <= floor + 0.10H in 3/3 -- and this outcome is the informative one: with collapse and drift
    excluded by construction, a failure isolates the blocker in the ENCODER's ability to separate symbols under
    a task-only gradient, closing the loop with V-39/40 (identity lives in a thin subspace a task gradient does
    not find). The manuscript would then state the full causal chain with every link measured.
(d) GRADED otherwise.

**Prediction on the record.** Same-symbol consistency should jump (the quantiser no longer moves under the
encoder), and I predict it lands above .60 -- if it does not, drift was never about the quantiser and NSVQ's
framing does not apply here. Accuracy: FAILS or GRADED, with maybe one chance in five of PARTIAL; the geometry
evidence says the task gradient alone does not find the separating directions, and FSQ does not change the
gradient, only the quantiser. Forty-four predictions tested, twenty-nine failed.

**Cites entering the manuscript with this run regardless of outcome**: FSQ (Mentzer et al. 2023), SimVQ (ICCV
2025), NSVQ (2026) -- the referee question "did you try modern VQ fixes" must have a measured answer.

## V-63 prereg, before any code: the interventional close of the binding-head line
V-60/61/62 diagnosed the blocker: with collapse and drift excluded by construction (FSQ), what fails is the encoder's separation of symbols under a TASK-ONLY gradient. The paper's central claim says what binding needs from an encoder is an identity objective. V-63 supplies exactly that objective to exactly the head that failed, and nothing else changes.
Design: same FSQ head as V-62 (proj HID->6, tanh, 7 levels, straight-through, fixed random expansion to VSA_DIM). Added: a linear classifier from the 6-dim pre-round coordinates to the symbol vocabulary, trained with cross-entropy on the arena's symbol ids (the same supervision the handover's outside-the-loss projection consumes; nothing the arena does not already contain). Arms: fsq_id (identity CE + task loss) and fsq_id_only (identity CE only; the task trains just the readout scale/bias). Arena C, seeds 42/123/456, same budget family as V-60/61/62. Floor and parser reused from v62_BANKED (same arena build).
Bars (V-60 family, decided now): WORKS if all 3 seeds >= floor+0.90H; PARTIAL >= floor+0.50H; FAILS <= floor+0.10H; GRADED otherwise; VOID if H < 0.20.
Predictions, registered so they can fail: (1) fsq_id WORKS in 3/3 — the identity objective removes the separation failure, and this is the interventional confirmation of the diagnosis; (2) diagnostics flip: same-symbol consistency >= .90 and role-distinct rate >= .95 (against .14-.39 and 0.0000 under task-only); (3) fsq_id_only lands within a few points of fsq_id — if the identity objective alone suffices, the task loss was never load-bearing for the code, which is the claim in its sharpest form.
Negative reading, committed now: if fsq_id FAILS or stays GRADED with healthy diagnostics, then separation was NOT the (whole) blocker and the V-62 attribution is overclaimed — the manuscript sentence "the blocker sits in the encoder" must be weakened to "consistent with", and that correction enters the paper, not the drawer. If diagnostics stay broken under supervision, the CE-through-tanh route itself is questioned, and the arm is rerun once with CE on post-round codes before any verdict is transcribed (declared now, not after seeing results).

## V-64 prereg, before any code: consistency, not classification, as the identity objective
V-63's provisional lesson sharpens the claim: decodable identity was never the missing signal (the .9986 probe said so all along); what cleanup needs is CONSISTENCY — same symbol, same code. V-64 supplies that directly and nothing else: a metric objective on the pre-round coordinates, pulling same-symbol pairs together and pushing distinct-symbol pairs apart (margin hinge in grid space; supervision = the same symbol ids V-63 used; NO fixed codebook targets — this separates "needs equivalence supervision" from "needs fixed targets", the handover being the fixed-target case at .934).
Arms: fsq_con (metric + task) and fsq_con_only (metric only; task trains readout scale/bias, codes detached). Arena C, seeds 42/123/456, same budget; floor/parser from v62_BANKED.
Bars: V-60 family (WORKS all3 >= floor+.90H / PARTIAL .50H / FAILS <= .10H / else GRADED).
Predictions, registered so they can fail: (1) same-symbol consistency >= .90 AND role-distinct >= .95 in 3/3 — the two requirements simultaneously for the first time; (2) accuracy WORKS in 3/3 — if codes are consistent and distinct, bind/unbind/cleanup is the parser's algebra and should approach it; (3) if (1) holds and (2) still FAILS, the blocker is downstream of the code (binding arithmetic in fp32 on 6-of-4096-dim expansions), and that is a new, reportable localisation.
Negative reading, committed now: if the metric objective cannot reach consistency >= .90 (1 fails), then pairwise equivalence supervision is insufficient where fixed-target regression succeeds, and the manuscript's "identity objective" claim must name fixed targets explicitly — a narrowing, entered in the paper.

## V-65 prereg, before any code: the mainstream-dataset test (2WikiMultihopQA)
Purpose: measure the paper's claim where readers live — on a mainstream multi-hop QA benchmark (Ho et al., COLING 2020), as an error-rate reduction under the frozen-deployment condition. Dataset: framolfese/2WikiMultihopQA via hf-mirror; SUBSET: type=compositional (pure two-hop bridge chains), dev split, N=300; model phi-2 frozen throughout (no fine-tune in this experiment).
Arms, all seeing the same instances:
  (1) prompt      — few-shot phi-2, context passages (truncated to fit 2048: supporting sentences first, then distractor paragraphs until budget; truncation stats reported), generate, exact-match after standard normalisation. This is the model's single pass.
  (2) prompt_ev   — few-shot phi-2, the GOLD evidence triples verbalised in the prompt plus the question. Equal information, in-context route.
  (3) hrr_gold    — HRR store over the same gold triples with STRING-IDENTITY symbol codes (fixed random vector per distinct entity/relation string; supplying identity externally, which is the paper's stated requirement): key = subject (x) relation, value = object; two unbind+cleanup hops following the question's relation chain read from the gold evidence order; answer = retrieved entity string, same EM.
Seeds 42/123/456 (few-shot sampling and codebook init). Declared diagnostics: answer-coverage of gold triples (fraction of instances whose answer string appears as a triple object); context-truncation rate; per-arm EM on the covered slice AND the full set (primary metric: covered slice, declared now).
Condition check, declared: if arm (1) >= .85 EM, the single pass does not fail here and no gain is claimable — reported as such.
Predictions, registered so they can fail: (P1) ordering hrr_gold >= prompt_ev >= prompt in 3/3 seeds; (P2) hrr_gold - prompt >= .20 EM on the covered slice; (P3) prompt_ev sits strictly between — the model inherits evidence but errs at composition (V-59's inheritance result predicts this).
Negative readings, committed now: if hrr_gold <= prompt_ev, the algebra adds nothing over in-context evidence on natural QA and that boundary enters the paper; if answer-coverage < .80 the evidence route is ill-posed on this subset and coverage itself is the reported result. Gold triples are supervision arms (1)-(2) also receive in usable form; an extraction-parser arm (no gold) is a REGISTERED FOLLOW-UP (V-66), not smuggled into this verdict.

## V-66 prereg, before any code: the no-gold extraction arm (registered follow-up of V-65)
The predictable objection to V-65: gold triples are handed over. V-66 removes them. Same 300 compositional dev instances, phi-2 frozen throughout, same EM.
Pipeline, declared: (1) EXTRACT — few-shot phi-2 emits "subject | relation | object" lines from each supporting passage (passages by supporting_facts titles; the extractor never sees the question or the answer); (2) STORE — HRR over extracted triples, string-identity codes as in V-65; (3) CHAIN — start entity = the longest context title appearing verbatim in the question (declared heuristic, no gold); hop 1 = unbind with the start entity over each of its extracted relations, keep the (relation, object) whose retrieval cosine is highest; hop 2 = same from that object; answer = hop-2 object string.
Arms: hrr_extr (the pipeline above) vs the V-65 banked prompt (.2533) and prompt_ev (.9500) references — no rerun of those, declared.
Diagnostics, declared: extraction recall of gold triples (fraction of gold (s,r,o) with a string-matching extracted triple, normalised); start-entity hit rate; per-instance failure split (extraction miss vs chain miss vs cleanup miss).
Predictions, registered so they can fail: (P1) hrr_extr - .2533 >= .20 (the deployment claim survives without gold); (P2) hrr_extr < .95 (extraction quality bounds the arm below the gold-evidence prompt — if it does NOT, that itself is reportable); (P3) extraction recall predicts the arm: hrr_extr <= recall + .05.
Negative reading, committed now: if hrr_extr < .2533 + .20, the mainstream gain REQUIRES provided evidence and the manuscript's deployment sentence gains that qualifier explicitly. Seeds 42/123/456 (extractor shots fixed, greedy decode — seed variation only in codebook init; identical-seed results are expected and not a defect).

## Binding-head arc synthesis (V-60/61/62/63/63b/64, transcribed with all verdicts in)
Task-only gradient: collapse (V-60) or drift (V-61); FSQ pins the quantiser and the encoder still neither separates nor stays consistent (V-62). Identity CLASSIFICATION: separation solved (role-distinct .95-1.00, thousands of tuples, cosine ~0 in pure arms), consistency broken (.02-.08), both CE placements (V-63/63b). Pairwise EQUIVALENCE: consistency up (.38-.58), separation lost or partial (V-64). Accuracy at the floor in every arm (.508-.556 across all six identity/equivalence arms). The two requirements were never satisfied simultaneously by ANY in-head objective; the one measured route that satisfies both is regression onto FIXED EXTERNAL TARGETS (the handover, .934). Sharpened claim, replacing the overclaim: what binding needs is not decodable identity (decodable at .9986 all along; a head that decodes it still fails) but identity as fixed targets to land on. Both registered negative readings (2ff3e25, 94d59b4) enter the manuscript.

(P2) gain vs single pass .669 >= .20: HIT — the mainstream gain REPLICATES on a second question type, and is larger (+67 points; the model with the facts in front of it reaches only .68 on this type, and the store still beats that by +8). (P3) hrr_gold >= .90: MISSED (.7622). ## V-71 prereg, before any code: the output case — VSA as the precision-retrieval layer under an LLM verbaliser
Literature check first (2026-08-25): no published work uses a VSA store to improve LLM OUTPUT (Hyperdimensional Probe = interpretability decoding; PathHD = retrieval scoring; no hit for hypervector-guided generation). The niche is open; a positive here is new.
Design: same 2Wiki rows as V-65 (compositional) and V-69 (inference), 300 each, Phi-2 frozen. New arm hrr_then_prompt: the HRR store (gold triples, string-identity codes, exactly the V-65 chain) walks the two hops and RETURNS the two retrieved triples; only those two facts are verbalised in the prompt, and the model generates the answer. References: banked prompt / prompt_ev / hrr_gold per type, not rerun. Greedy, run once, declared. Diagnostics: retrieval hit rate (answer string among the two injected facts), mean evidence tokens per instance for prompt_ev vs hybrid.
Predictions, registered so they can fail: (P1) compositional hybrid >= .93 (within two points of prompt_ev at a fraction of the tokens); (P2) inference hybrid >= .70 (beats the fact-dump .683: precision beats volume where the model's composition is weak); (P3) hybrid evidence tokens <= 25% of prompt_ev's on both types.
Negative readings, committed now: if P2 fails because the store's chain misses dominate (hybrid tracks hrr_gold's .762 ceiling from below and lands under .683), the output case rests on compositional's token-efficiency only and the paper says so; if even P1 fails, injected-fact verbalisation loses information relative to reading facts in context and the output case does not survive contact — reported as such.

## V-71 verdict (prereg 9fe756d; artifact v71_logs/v71_BANKED.json) — all three predictions FAILED
compositional hybrid .9200 (P1 wanted >= .93; loses 3 points to prompt_ev's .9500); inference hybrid .5300 (P2 wanted >= .70; loses 15 to prompt_ev, 23 below its own retrieval hit rate .7567 — the model mis-verbalises even when the answer is among the two injected facts); token ratio 1.003/1.006 (P3 wanted <= .25).
Design-premise fault, recorded: 2Wiki's gold evidence is already minimal (two-to-four triples), so "precision retrieval saves context" was ill-posed on this dataset — the efficiency comparison never existed here. The registered negative reading applies and is sharpened: retrieve-then-verbalise adds a lossy interface on top of the store's chain errors; where the algebra's condition holds, the best output path is the algebra's own readout (.974/.762), and where it does not, direct reading of the facts is (.950/.683). The open, untested output cases are the ones this dataset cannot host: large-context corpora where evidence is genuinely bulky, and long-form generation consistency — both would need new preregs, neither is claimed.

## V-72 prereg, before any code: the bulky-evidence case (the premise V-71 lacked, made real)
V-71's efficiency premise was ill-posed because 2Wiki's per-instance gold evidence is minimal. V-72 makes the evidence bulky the way a knowledge base is: for each instance, the evidence pool = its own gold triples plus the gold triples of K=50 other instances of the same type (declared now; one K, no sweep). Same 300 rows per type (compositional, inference), Phi-2 frozen, greedy, run once.
Arms over the SAME pool: (1) prompt_ev_big — the whole pool verbalised in the prompt (truncated at the model's window, supporting triples NOT privileged in ordering: pool order is a seed-42 shuffle, declared; truncation rate and answer-truncated-out rate reported); (2) hrr_then_prompt_big — an HRR store over the whole pool, the V-65 chain retrieves two facts, only those are prompted; (3) hrr_gold_big — the store's own readout, no model.
References: the minimal-evidence banked numbers (prompt_ev .9500/.6833, hrr_gold .9744/.7622, hybrid .9200/.5300).
Predictions, registered so they can fail: (P1) prompt_ev_big degrades by >= .10 from its minimal-evidence value on both types — volume costs the model accuracy; (P2) hrr_gold_big stays within .05 of hrr_gold — the store's capacity absorbs ~150 bindings at d=4096 (the paper's own capacity results say interference grows; this is a real risk, not a formality); (P3) hrr_then_prompt_big >= prompt_ev_big + .10 on both types — the output case the user asked for: when the dump is big, precision retrieval wins.
Negative readings, committed now: if P2 fails, store capacity is the binding constraint at KB scale and THAT is the reported result (with the crosstalk reading from the paper's capacity corollary); if P3 fails while P1 holds, neither path survives bulk and the deployment claim gains a pool-size qualifier; if P1 fails (the model shrugs off 150 distractor facts), the efficiency case is dead in this range and we say so.

## V-72 prereg ADDENDUM (before any code; user directive: "improve output" means lower hallucination rate and error rate)
Metrics, defined now: ERROR RATE = 1 - EM. HALLUCINATION RATE = fraction of generated answers that are UNGROUNDED in the provided pool — the normalised output string appears nowhere among the pool's subjects/objects (fabricated entity), as distinct from grounded-but-wrong (a pool entity, wrong one). Both reported per arm.
Structural claim, stated before measuring: the HRR readout cannot hallucinate BY CONSTRUCTION — its output is always an entity of the store — so its hallucination rate is identically zero; the empirical run verifies the harness rather than the claim. The model arms (prompt_ev_big, hrr_then_prompt_big) can fabricate; their rates are the measurement.
Prediction added: (P4) prompt_ev_big's hallucination rate exceeds its minimal-evidence counterpart's (bulk breeds fabrication), and the hybrid's is lower than the dump's (two grounded facts leave less room to fabricate than 150).

## V-72 harness fault (recorded before any verdict is transcribed for arms 2-3)
hrr_answer conflates the STORE with the CHAIN SPEC: it starts at evidences[0][0] and iterates every store triple as a hop. Valid on minimal evidence (store = chain), nonsense on a pooled store: the readout walked ~150 pseudo-hops from a random start (hrr_gold_big 0.000/0.007), and the "two retrieved facts" of the hybrid were ~150 lines. Arms 2-3 of the v72 run are VOID by harness fault (log quarantined as v72_logs/v72_VOID_chainspec.json). Arm 1 (the dump) involves no chain and its numbers stand, pending reproduction in the rerun: compositional .9500->.3533 EM with hallucination .2200; inference .6833->.0067 EM with hallucination .7733. Bulk destroys the model on both metrics — P1 and the dump half of P4 HIT.
Fix, declared before the rerun (v72b): the store is the pool; the chain spec (start entity + relation sequence, two hops) comes from the instance's own gold evidence, which is what querying a knowledge base means; candidates and cleanup range over the POOL's entities. Everything else identical. P2 (capacity at ~150 bindings) and P3/P4-hybrid are then measured for the first time, not remeasured.

## V-72b verdict (prereg c70f0df + 07afab0, after the declared fix; artifact v72b_logs/v72b_BANKED.json)
ALL FOUR PREDICTIONS HIT, both types. K=50 pools (~102-152 triples per store).
Dump (whole pool in prompt): compositional .3533 EM / .2200 hallucination; inference .0067 EM / .7733 hallucination — bulk destroys the model on both metrics (P1).
Store readout: .9533 / .7233 — within .05 of the minimal-evidence values (P2): HRR capacity HOLDS at ~150 bindings at d=4096, a standalone positive connecting to the paper's capacity corollary. Hallucination identically 0 by construction (harness-verified).
Hybrid (store retrieves two facts, model generates): .9000 / .5167, hallucination .0400 / .0233 — beats the dump by 55 and 51 points (P3), and cuts its hallucination 5.5x and 33x (P4).
Reading, transcribed: at knowledge-base scale the ordering INVERTS relative to minimal evidence (V-71): the dump collapses, the store is scale-invariant, and even the lossy hybrid interface is now worth 51-55 points. The output claim the user asked for is measured: where evidence is bulky, a VSA store reduces the error rate by up to 93% (compositional, .647->.047) and the hallucination rate from 22-77% to zero (readout) or 2-4% (hybrid). The V-72 dump numbers reproduced exactly (same seed and code path).

## V-73 prereg, before any code: the capacity curve (readout accuracy vs store size)
V-72b measured one pool size (K=50, ~150 bindings). V-73 sweeps the store: K in {10, 50, 100, 200, 400} distractor instances (~30 to ~1200 bindings), readout arm ONLY (no generation), both question types, same 300 rows, same chain spec (own gold evidence), d=4096, seed 42, run once.
Predictions, registered so they can fail: (P1) readout EM decreases monotonically in K (up to +-.02 noise); (P2) at K=400 (~1200 bindings) the compositional readout is still >= .80 — crosstalk O(k/d) with k/d ~ 0.3 predicts graceful, not catastrophic, decay; (P3) the K=50 points reproduce V-72b's .9533/.7233 exactly (same seed and path).
Reading, committed now: whatever the curve's shape, it enters the paper as the empirical companion of the capacity corollary, with its disagreements (if any) stated rather than smoothed; if decay is catastrophic before K=400, the KB-scale claim gains an explicit store-size bound.

## V-73 verdict (prereg 1c8bd0d; artifact v73_logs/v73_BANKED.json)
P1 HIT: readout EM decays monotonically in store size — compositional .957/.940/.780/.200/.063, inference .743/.750/.453/.100/.033 at ~33/152/302/602/1202 bindings (d=4096). P2 FAILED: decay is catastrophic, not graceful — the knee sits near 300 bindings and the store has collapsed by ~1200. Values consistent; no substantive discrepancy.

## V-74 prereg, before any code: the joint objective the programme never tested
Gap in our own programme, stated plainly: V-63 trained the FSQ head with identity CLASSIFICATION alone (separation solved, consistency .02-.08); V-64 trained it with pairwise EQUIVALENCE alone (consistency .38-.58, separation lost). Neither ran BOTH. The manuscript's synthesis ("no in-head objective achieves both") is therefore stronger than the evidence: the untested cell is the obvious one, and it is what supervised contrastive learning does. V-74 tests it.
Design: same FSQ head, same arena C, seeds 42/123/456, same budget family as V-60..64. Loss = task + lambda_cls * identity cross-entropy (V-63's term, on pre-round coordinates) + lambda_con * metric consistency (V-64's term: pull same-symbol pairs, push distinct-symbol pairs to a margin). One weighting, declared now to prevent a search: lambda_cls = lambda_con = 1.0. Arms: fsq_both (task + both terms) and fsq_both_only (both terms, task reaching only the readout scale/bias).
Bars: V-60 family, unchanged. WORKS if all 3 seeds >= floor + 0.90H (floor .5153, parser .9340 from v62_BANKED); PARTIAL >= 0.50H; FAILS <= 0.10H; else GRADED.
Predictions, registered so they can fail: (P1) diagnostics satisfy BOTH requirements for the first time — same-symbol consistency >= .60 AND role-distinct rate >= .90 in 3/3; (P2) accuracy PARTIAL or better; (P3) fsq_both beats both V-63's .5247 and V-64's .5360 means.
Readings, committed now: if P1 and P2 hold, the manuscript's synthesis is WRONG as written and must be replaced by the positive statement — an in-head objective does exist, and it is the conjunction of separation and consistency; that is a new result and it goes in Results, not in a footnote. If P1 holds and P2 fails, the two requirements are satisfiable in the code while accuracy still does not follow, which relocates the blocker downstream of the code and is itself a finding. If P1 fails, the conjunction is not achievable at this scale by this weighting and the synthesis stands, narrowed to say that the joint objective was tested at one weighting.

## V-75 prereg, before any code: training the codebook to raise the store's capacity
V-73 measured the practical ceiling of the deployment result: readout accuracy decays monotonically with store size and collapses past a few hundred bindings at d=4096 (knee near 300). Random i.i.d. codes are what the classical analysis assumes; nothing says they are optimal for a FINITE store. V-75 trains the codebook itself — the one component we never trained — to reduce crosstalk at fixed d, and asks whether the knee moves right.
Setup: 2Wiki pools exactly as V-73 (compositional type, K in {50,100,200}, chain spec from each instance's own gold evidence, d=4096). The store's codes for entities and relations become trainable parameters initialised at the V-73 random vectors. Objective, declared: for a sampled pool and its chain, maximise the margin between the correct cleanup target's cosine and the best distractor's cosine (hinge on the retrieval decision), summed over both hops; no task labels beyond the gold chain the store is already given. Trained on 200 pools drawn from the TRAIN side, evaluated on the same 300 dev instances V-73 used. Adam, lr 1e-3, 300 steps, one seed for the sweep plus seeds 123/456 at K=200 for the headline cell (declared now).
Predictions, registered so they can fail: (P1) at K=200 trained codes beat random codes by >= .10 EM (V-73 random: .200); (P2) monotonic decay persists — training shifts the curve, it does not remove the ceiling; (P3) generalisation holds: the gain at K=200 is present on pools whose entities were NOT in the training pools (reported separately as the held-entity slice).
Negative readings, committed now: if P1 fails, random codes are already near-optimal at this dimension and the capacity bound is intrinsic, which strengthens rather than weakens the deployment claim's honesty and is reported as such. If P1 holds but P3 fails, the gain is memorisation of training entities, not a better code, and must be reported as memorisation — this is the failure mode most likely to flatter us and is the one to check hardest.

## V-75 verdict (prereg b3bc1bf; artifact v75_logs/v75_BANKED.json) — training the codebook DESTROYS the store
random -> trained: K=50 .9567 -> .0333; K=100 .8667 -> .0100; K=200 .4400 -> .0233. Held-entity slice 0.0000 at every K (n=241). P1 FAILED, P3 FAILED, P2 vacuously "true" on a floor-level curve.
The scorer's auto-printed reading ("random codes near-optimal") is TOO KIND and is not transcribed as the verdict. The measured fact is stronger and worse for the intervention: 300 steps of per-pool retrieval-margin descent do not merely fail to improve the codes, they take the store from .96 to .03. The reading, stated as reading: HRR needs near-orthogonality across the WHOLE vocabulary, which is a global property of the code set; a gradient computed on one pool at a time can reduce that pool's hinge by moving codes in ways that wreck the global geometry, and nothing in the objective penalises that. This is the same lesson as V-39/40 and V-60..64 relocated to the codebook: a task-shaped gradient does not preserve the geometry the algebra assumes, even when the ONLY parameters are the codes and the objective is the algebra's own retrieval margin.
Implementation note recorded, because the numbers differ from V-73: V-75's random baseline at K=200 is .4400 where V-73 reported .2000 for the same K. The pipelines differ — V-75's cleanup ranges over all pool entities and scores by cosine after normalising, V-73's excluded the current entity — so the two are not the same estimator. Within-V-75 comparisons (random vs trained, same pipeline, same pools) are the valid ones and are what the verdict rests on; the cross-experiment number is not claimed.
Registered follow-up, NOT claimed here: whether an objective that includes an explicit global near-orthogonality term can beat random codes is open, and is V-76.

## V-76 prereg, before any code: codebook training with the geometry the algebra needs written into the objective
V-75's reading says the per-pool margin gradient wrecks a GLOBAL property (near-orthogonality across the whole code set) that nothing in its objective protected. V-76 changes exactly one thing: an explicit near-orthogonality penalty is added, so the optimiser is not free to trade global geometry for one pool's margin. Everything else is identical to V-75 (same pools, same dev instances, same steps, same lr, same init, same held-entity slice).
Objective: margin hinge (V-75's term) + lambda * mean squared off-diagonal cosine over the codes touched at that step plus a random sample of 64 other vocabulary codes, with all codes renormalised to unit norm after each step. lambda = 1.0 and the sample size 64 are declared now; no search.
Predictions, registered so they can fail: (P1) trained beats V-75's trained at every K by >= .30 (i.e. the regulariser recovers the destroyed geometry); (P2) trained beats RANDOM at K=200 by >= .05 (the actual question: can a trained code set beat an i.i.d. one at the capacity frontier); (P3) the held-entity slice tracks the full slice within .05 (no memorisation).
Readings, committed now: if P2 holds with P3, this is the first case in the programme where TRAINING any VSA component beats the untrained baseline, and it enters Results as such. If P1 holds but P2 fails, the regulariser repairs the damage without beating random, and the honest statement is that i.i.d. codes are at least as good as anything this objective finds — the capacity bound is then a property of the algebra at this dimension, not of our initialisation, which is a cleaner version of what the paper already says. If P1 fails, codebook training is closed for this budget and the paper says the direction was tested twice and abandoned.

## V-76 verdict (prereg 1674932; artifact v76_logs/v76_BANKED.json)
Adding the global near-orthogonality term and unit-sphere renormalisation does NOT repair V-75: trained .0133/.0133/.0233 at K=50/100/200 against random .9567/.8667/.4400. P1 FAILED (no repair), P2 FAILED (does not beat random), P3 held (held-entity tracks the full slice — the failure is uniform, not memorisation).
Registered reading applies: CODEBOOK TRAINING IS CLOSED FOR THIS BUDGET — tested twice, with and without the geometry term, and abandoned. What the two runs establish together, stated as the measured claim: descending a retrieval-margin objective on the codes themselves does not merely fail to beat i.i.d. random codes, it destroys the store, and protecting near-orthogonality explicitly does not rescue it at this budget (300 steps, lr 1e-3, one pool per step). Scope stated so it cannot be over-read: this is one objective, one optimiser and one budget; it is not a proof that no trained code set can beat random. What it does license is the paper's existing preference for fixed random codes with supervised read-in, on evidence rather than convenience.

## V-74 verdict (prereg a916fb6; artifact v74_logs/v74_BANKED.json)
fsq_both [.528/.538/.514] mean .5267 -> FAILS. fsq_both_only [.546/.534/.570] mean .5500 -> GRADED. Diagnostics: role-distinct .87-.99 (separation kept), same-symbol consistency .018-.032 for fsq_both and .075-.109 for fsq_both_only (consistency NOT recovered).
P1 FAILED (consistency nowhere near .60), P2 FAILED (no PARTIAL), P3 FAILED (.5267 and .5500 do not beat both V-63 .5247 and V-64 .5360 — fsq_both_only edges past both but sits at the floor, which is what GRADED means here).
Registered reading applies: the conjunction is not achievable at this scale by this weighting, and the manuscript's synthesis STANDS, narrowed to record that the joint objective was tested at lambda_cls = lambda_con = 1.0. Mechanism reading, as reading: with both terms present the classification term dominates the geometry — separation is preserved and consistency is not, i.e. the joint objective inherits the classification failure mode rather than averaging the two. The referee-visible gap in the programme is now closed with data rather than left to inference.

## Literature check on the current conclusions (new standing practice: conclusion first, literature second)
SUPPORTED, independently and strongly:
- "Two-hop composition is not bought by scale" (V-67: Qwen2.5-7B .227 vs Phi-2 .253). Press et al., Measuring and Narrowing the Compositionality Gap (arXiv:2210.03350): as model size grows, single-hop accuracy improves faster than multi-hop, so the compositionality gap does NOT shrink. Same direction, independent models and tasks.
- "The state the model answers from bridges one hop and not two." Yang et al., Do LLMs Latently Perform Multi-Hop Reasoning? (arXiv:2402.16837): a clear scaling trend for the FIRST hop pathway and no scaling evidence for the SECOND. This is mechanistic support, not merely directional, and it is the closest external match to our mechanism claim.
- "Bulk evidence collapses the prompt route and breeds fabrication" (V-72b: EM .353/.007, hallucination .22/.77). Liu et al., Lost in the Middle (2023) for positional degradation; Shi et al. (2023) for a single irrelevant clause degrading otherwise-solved problems; the context-degradation-with-length literature more broadly.
- "A symbolic store cannot return an entity absent from it." The knowledge-graph-grounding literature reports the same property and large hallucination reductions from answering over validated structured data; ours differs in being a structural guarantee of the readout rather than a measured reduction, and should be stated that way.
- Capacity: classical VSA capacity analysis (Plate; Frady, Kleyko & Sommer; Kleyko et al. surveys) already cited; V-73's curve is the empirical companion at task level.
NO DIRECT PRECEDENT FOUND (so this is a novelty claim and must stay checkable):
- The negative that trained codes LOSE to i.i.d. random codes at fixed dimension (V-75/76). The surveys state that hypervectors may be learned rather than i.i.d. and treat both as valid design choices; no source found that measures learned-versus-random at a capacity frontier and reports the learned set destroying retrieval. Our claim stays scoped to one objective, one optimiser, one budget.
- The six-way exhaustion of in-head objectives (V-60..64, V-74) with the conclusion that identity must arrive as fixed external targets. No precedent found; the VQ-collapse literature (VQ-VAE, NSVQ, SimVQ, FSQ) covers the collapse half only.

## Literature check finds an OVERCLAIM of ours (the practice paying for itself on its second use)
Checked claim: "what the algebra cannot express is recency" (abstract, Results, Discussion).
Finding: permutation is one of the three core VSA operations and is the family's STANDARD mechanism for encoding order and sequence — trajectory association, with a line of work behind it (Plate; Kanerva; Sahlgren; Frady; Kleyko et al. surveys). Our own introduction lists permutation among the algebra's operations, so the paper was internally inconsistent as well as overclaiming: what we implemented and measured is a COMMUTATIVE BUNDLE (superposition without permutation), and the measured statement is about that, not about the algebra.
Correction applied in all three places: the abstract now reads "Recency is inexpressible in a commutative bundle"; Results names permutation as the family's standard order mechanism, cites the survey, and states we did not use or test it; the Discussion adds that this is a statement about the bundle and not the family, with the permutation-based store left open. No measurement changed; the claim's scope did.
Status of the other conclusion checked this round: "the model inherits injected evidence without correction" (V-59) remains supported in direction by the context-faithfulness literature; not upgraded to a citation this round.

## Literature search on "VSA improving LLMs" — one CONFLICT found and scoped, plus positioning
Searched (2026-08-26): VSA/HDC + LLM accuracy; HDC + RAG/multi-hop QA; differentiable/learned binding; learned symbolic codes.
CONFLICT with our headline negative, and it is real: learned binding IS reported to work, in settings that differ from ours.
- Tensor-product representations with learnable routing and iterative decomposition learn role--filler bindings end to end (arXiv:2406.01012; arXiv:2406.06976); a network trained end to end succeeded on unseen fillers with 5 unique fillers and 360 examples (arXiv:1902.09006).
- Discrete-Valued Neural Communication (NeurIPS 2021, arXiv:2107.02367) learns a SHARED CODEBOOK for inter-component communication, building on VQ-VAE, and reports benefits.
Differences that make our negative compatible with those results, now stated in the paper rather than left implicit: (i) binding operator — outer product learned jointly with the task from scratch, versus circular convolution with nearest-neighbour cleanup over the frozen states of a pretrained model; (ii) vocabulary scale — a few fillers versus tens of symbols; (iii) what the code must support — communication between components versus INJECTIVE RECOVERY by cleanup, which is the requirement our measurements show is the hard one. Action taken: Related Work now names these three settings with citations, the synthesis sentence reads "any in-head objective we tried in this setting", and the paper no longer implies a general impossibility.
POSITIONING, not conflict: the 2026 wave of hypergraph/graph RAG for multi-hop QA (AAAI-26 cross-granularity hypergraph RAG; WWW-26 PRoH; HyCE-RAG) occupies the same deployment slot as our store with a different mechanism (graph traversal versus algebraic unbinding). Not cited this round; recorded as the nearest deployment-side neighbour if a referee asks.
Also confirmed: attention-as-binding (already cited) PROPOSES the binding heads with role--filler separation objectives that our V-60..74 arms measure, so our negative is a direct empirical test of a published proposal rather than a test of our own invention.

## V-77 prereg, before any code: learned binding the way the literature does it (tensor product + soft unbinding)
Motivation, stated as the conflict it answers: our seven-route negative was measured with circular-convolution binding and a HARD nearest-neighbour cleanup, which demands injective recovery of a discrete code. The settings where learned binding is reported to work do not demand that: tensor-product binding with near-orthonormal roles unbinds EXACTLY by inner product, and attention-as-binding reads attention weights as SOFT unbinding with superposition in the residual stream. V-77 instantiates that recipe on our arena so the two literatures meet on one bench.
Design: arena C, seeds 42/123/456, same budget family as V-60..74; Phi-2 frozen; one projection W (HID -> d=64) TIED for both roles and fillers, so a symbol's role vector equals its filler vector and a retrieved filler can serve directly as the next key. Bind by outer product (role (x) filler), superpose over the bindings at a level into a 64x64 matrix, unbind by matrix-vector product with the query role. Chain both hops with NO cleanup between them (the retrieved filler is used directly as the next role) --- this is the soft-unbinding step the theory proposes. Readout: cosine between the final retrieved filler and the candidate span's projection.
Loss: task cross-entropy + lambda * near-orthonormality penalty on the projections of distinct symbols within the instance (mean squared off-diagonal cosine), lambda = 1.0 declared now, no search. This is the "objective promoting role-filler separation" the attention-as-binding paper proposes, applied literally.
Arms: tpr_soft (as above) and tpr_clean (identical but with a hard cleanup onto the level's candidate set between hops), so the contrast ISOLATES the hard-cleanup requirement rather than confounding it with the binding operator.
Bars: V-60 family unchanged. WORKS if all 3 seeds >= floor + 0.90H (floor .5153, parser .9340, H .4187); PARTIAL >= 0.50H; FAILS <= 0.10H; else GRADED.
Predictions, registered so they can fail: (P1) tpr_soft reaches PARTIAL or better --- if the blocker was the hard cleanup, removing it should move accuracy off the floor; (P2) tpr_soft > tpr_clean by >= .05, which is the isolating comparison; (P3) the orthonormality penalty is achievable here, off-diagonal cosine <= .30 in 3/3, where the FSQ arms sat at .76--.89.
Readings, committed now: if P1 and P2 hold, our negative is REVISED, not merely scoped --- the blocker is the hard-cleanup requirement and not training the code, and that becomes a positive result in Results reconciling our measurements with the TPR literature. If P1 holds and P2 fails, soft and hard cleanup are equivalent here and the gain came from the tensor-product operator instead, which is the other half of the same reconciliation. If both fail, the negative extends to tensor-product binding with soft unbinding and the seven-route claim becomes an eight-route claim with the literature's own operator included, which strengthens it.

## V-77 verdict (prereg f0177e3; artifact v77_logs/v77_BANKED.json)
tpr_soft [.488/.528/.498] mean .5047 -> FAILS. tpr_clean [.536/.526/.540] mean .5340 -> FAILS. Off-diagonal cosine between distinct symbols' projections .496-.706 (soft) and .394-.409 (clean), against a registered target of <= .30.
All three predictions FAILED. P1: removing the hard cleanup did not move accuracy off the floor. P2: soft is WORSE than clean by .029, the opposite sign to the prediction. P3: the near-orthonormality the theory asks for was not achieved by optimising for it directly; .39-.71 against a target of .30, and for reference the FSQ arms sat at .76-.89, so the penalty helped the geometry substantially and helped accuracy not at all.
Registered reading applies: the NEGATIVE EXTENDS to tensor-product binding with soft unbinding — the literature's own operator and the objective its proponents propose. Eight routes now, not seven, and the eighth was chosen by the opposing literature rather than by us.
What this settles about the conflict recorded earlier: the difference between our result and the TPR successes is NOT the binding operator and NOT the hard-cleanup requirement, since removing both changes nothing here. The remaining differences are the ones to name honestly: those successes train the binding jointly with the task FROM SCRATCH on vocabularies of a few fillers, while we read the frozen states of a pretrained model over tens of symbols and ask the projection alone to carry identity. The measured claim is therefore about what a projection of frozen pretrained states can be trained to deliver, not about tensor products versus circular convolution.
Honest note on the diagnostic: the orthonormality penalty DID improve separation relative to the FSQ arms (.39-.71 vs .76-.89) without improving accuracy, which is one more instance of the paper's own pattern — a geometric property can be optimised directly and the task does not follow.

## Literature check: VSA AS A LAYER INSIDE THE MODEL — a gap in our citations, now closed
Question asked (2026-08-26): can a VSA be added as a layer inside an LLM? It can, it has been, and it works — and we were not citing the central paper.
- Hrrformer (Alam, Raff, Biderman, Oates & Holt, ICML 2023, arXiv:2305.19534) recasts SELF-ATTENTION ITSELF as HRR binding: O(TH log H) time, convergence in ~10x fewer epochs, near state-of-the-art on Long Range Arena while learning with a SINGLE layer, 23x faster and 24x less memory than a Transformer. Note for our submission: Edward Raff is a guest editor of the collection we are submitting to, and omitting this paper from an HD/VSA submission would have been a serious gap independent of that.
- TP-Transformer / TPR-enriched transformers (arXiv:2106.01317, NAACL 2021): each head emits a ROLE vector alongside K/V/Q, the attention output is treated as the filler and bound to the role by Hadamard product, improving abstractive summarisation.
Both are now cited, with the distinction that matters for our claim stated explicitly: in every one of these successes the binding is trained WITH the network, whereas our arms ask a projection of the FROZEN states of a model pretrained without any binding objective to supply symbol identity. That is the difference V-77 left standing after ruling out the binding operator and the hard-cleanup requirement, and it is now supported by the layer-integration literature rather than asserted by us.
Consequence for the paper's own claim: the honest statement is not "VSA cannot be trained into a language model" — the literature shows it can, from scratch — but "a VSA bolted onto frozen pretrained states must be given identity externally". The manuscript already reads that way; these citations make the boundary visible to a reader.

## V-78 prereg, before any code: Hrrformer-style binding trained FROM SCRATCH on our arena
Why this run and what it decides. After V-77, one factor still carries our whole reconciliation with the literature and it is not measured: every published success trains the binding WITH the network, while all our arms ask a projection of FROZEN pretrained states to supply identity. Hrrformer (ICML 2023) recasts self-attention itself as HRR binding and learns with a single layer; the minimal version of that is runnable on arena C, so the factor can be measured rather than asserted.
Design: arena C unchanged (HOPS 2, N_CTX 32, N_SYM 64, question mid-sequence), same binary task and same label balance, so the result is comparable to every earlier arm. Training data enlarged for from-scratch learning: 20,000 train and 2,000 evaluation instances, generated by the same Arena with seeds 42 and 4242 (declared now; earlier arms used 800/500 because they fitted a head over cached frozen states). Model: fresh embedding table, 4 layers, d=128, 8 heads, mean-pooled classification head, no pretrained weights anywhere. Seeds 42/123/456. Adam 3e-4, batch 16, 6 epochs, declared now.
Arms: (1) hrr_scratch — attention recast as HRR: keys bound to values by circular convolution, superposed, and unbound by the query, per Hrrformer; (2) softmax_scratch — identical model with standard softmax attention, the control that separates "HRR" from "trained from scratch"; (3) references, banked and NOT rerun: arena C floor .5153, exact-codebook parser .9340, and the through-the-loss frozen-state arms which sat at .50--.55.
Bars: the V-60 family on arena C, unchanged. WORKS >= floor + 0.90H = .8921; PARTIAL >= .7247; FAILS <= .5572.
Predictions, registered so they can fail: (P1) softmax_scratch reaches PARTIAL or better; (P2) hrr_scratch reaches PARTIAL or better; (P3) both from-scratch arms beat every frozen-state through-the-loss arm by >= .10.
Readings, committed now: if P1 and P3 hold, the paper's central boundary stops being a hypothesis — identity must be supplied externally WHEN READING FROZEN PRETRAINED STATES, and training the representation jointly removes the need; that sentence then rests on our own measurement plus the literature rather than on the literature alone, and every existing result is preserved unchanged. If the from-scratch arms also fail, arena C is simply hard and the frozen-state framing of our negative is too generous to us — in that case the manuscript must say the negative is about the task and not about frozen states, which would be a correction to our own framing. If hrr_scratch fails while softmax_scratch succeeds, the HRR operator is the liability at this scale and we report that against Hrrformer's positive result, noting the scale difference rather than claiming a refutation.

## V-78 prereg ADDENDUM, still before any code: the post-training arm, and the faithful Hrrformer recipe
Recipe read from the paper itself (Alam et al., ICML 2023, PMLR v202) rather than reconstructed: beta = sum_t (k_t (x) v_t) with (x) circular convolution via FFT; v_hat_t = q_t^dagger (x) beta with the involution inverse; a_t = cosine(v_t, v_hat_t); w = softmax(a_1..a_T); output = [w_1 v_1, ..., w_T v_T]. Their reported stability mechanism is the SOFTMAX over the cosine responses, which cancels HRR superposition noise because that noise has similar magnitude across t and softmax is shift-invariant. Training: Adam, exponential decay 1e-3 -> 1e-5, dropout 0.1, 20 epochs, single or multiple layers, from scratch. Recorded here because our implementation should be theirs, not our reconstruction of it.
Note on what their HRR does, which differs from ours and belongs in the paper: their HRR produces attention WEIGHTS over original value vectors and never decodes a symbol identity, so it never needs the injective code our arms are asked to supply. This is a third structural difference alongside from-scratch training and vocabulary size.
Arm added before code (user question: does POST-training suffice, given that pretraining from scratch is impractical for a deployed model): (4) hrr_posthoc — the same Hrrformer attention layer placed over FROZEN Phi-2 states and trained on the task, 800 train / 500 evaluation to match every earlier frozen-state arm exactly. This is the practical intervention: an adapter-style layer trained after the fact on a model nobody will retrain.
Prediction for the added arm, registered now: (P4) hrr_posthoc lands below the from-scratch arms and above the earlier through-the-loss arms, i.e. between .55 and .75 — post-training buys something because the layer can learn to read the states, but not what training the representation jointly buys.
Reading committed now: if hrr_posthoc reaches PARTIAL or better, post-training an HRR attention layer onto a frozen model IS a viable route and the paper must say so prominently, since that is the deployable version. If it fails while the from-scratch arms succeed, the paper's boundary is confirmed at the level a practitioner cares about: the benefit needs the representation trained with the binding, and bolting the operator on afterwards does not recover it.

## V-78 HARNESS FAULT — the run is VOID for the question it was built to answer, and the auto-verdict is NOT transcribed
The scorer printed "CORRECTION TO OUR OWN FRAMING: from-scratch also fails, so the negative is about the task, not frozen states". That reading is registered, but it presupposes a fair test and this was not one. Evidence that the arms never trained, not that the task is unlearnable:
(a) training loss sits at 0.6932 from epoch 2 through epoch 6 in both scratch arms, which is ln 2 to four decimals -- the entropy of a coin flip, i.e. a constant predictor;
(b) softmax_scratch and hrr_scratch return BIT-IDENTICAL accuracies on all three seeds ([.491, .509, .509]), which two different attention operators cannot do unless both are emitting a constant class;
(c) .491 and .509 are the evaluation split's class proportions.
Same signature as the V-50 task-1 fault quarantined earlier: at chance, flat, and identical where identity is impossible. Artifact quarantined as v78_logs/v78_VOID_notrained.json. NOTHING from this run enters the manuscript, and in particular the correction-to-our-framing reading is NOT claimed on this evidence.
Diagnosis, stated before the rerun: the readout is a masked mean over 768 positions of which the decisive ones are a handful (the query role and the candidate filler), so the signal is diluted by roughly two orders of magnitude before the classifier sees it; a fresh 4-layer d=128 model at lr 1e-3 has no path to it in 6 epochs.
Fix declared before any rerun (v78b), three changes and a control: (1) read out at the QUERY and CANDIDATE token positions and concatenate, instead of mean pooling; (2) lr 3e-4 rather than 1e-3; (3) 12 epochs rather than 6. (4) A LEARNABILITY CONTROL arm is added and must pass before any arm's failure is interpreted: the same model on an easy variant (HOPS=1, N_SYM=8) must exceed .80, establishing that the harness can learn anything at all. If the control fails, the harness is still wrong and no scientific reading is taken from the hard arms.

## V-78b HARNESS FAULT 2 (no results; found by 2026-08-27 tick): the learnability control could never generate its arena
Found v78b hung 23h at 100% CPU, 0% GPU, zero output past the header (started 2026-08-26 22:15 after the token_span speedup). Diagnosis, confirmed by reading the generator: v13.Arena's per-level pair loop demands N_CTX=32 DISTINCT role symbols; the declared control (HOPS=1, N_SYM=8) makes that rejection loop unsatisfiable after 8 roles — an infinite loop on the very first instance. The run would never have produced an artifact. The (1,8) configuration had never been built before; no code path capped the context size against the alphabet.
Fix, infra only (scoring, bars, arms, and the run-once declaration all untouched): get_arena now sets v13.N_CTX = min(32, N_SYM) — hard arms (N_SYM=64) keep N_CTX=32 with an identical rng stream, the control becomes finite (8 pairs over 8 symbols, hop 1; smoke: 50 rows in 0.1s where the old code never returned). Hung chain killed; v78b_run.sh now takes flock -n /tmp/v78b.lock (single-flight, V-70 precedent); relaunched once. Note for the reading, committed now: the control's context is necessarily shorter than the hard arms' (8 pairs vs 32) — it certifies that the HARNESS can learn, not that the easy and hard arenas match in length; that is what a learnability control is for and the verdict will not compare its accuracy against the hard arms' bars.

## V-78b verdict: the learnability control FAILS its registered threshold, so the from-scratch question stays open
Control arm (HOPS=1, N_SYM=8, N_CTX capped to 8 by the harness-fault-2 fix), seed 42, 12 epochs:
.578 -> .6995 -> .6875 -> .6940, training loss flat at ~.503 from epoch 4. Seed 123 opens at .678. The
registered threshold was .80 and it is not met: a 4-layer d=128 model with a query/candidate span readout,
Adam at 3e-4 for 12 epochs, tops out near .70 on the EASY variant.
The registered reading applies exactly as written: "If the control fails, the harness is still wrong and no
scientific reading is taken from the hard arms." Therefore V-78b yields NO verdict on whether from-scratch
training solves arena C, NO verdict on hrr_scratch versus softmax_scratch, and NO verdict on the post-hoc
HRR layer. The run is stopped rather than left to produce numbers I have committed not to interpret, and the
GPU is returned.
What this does and does not change. It does NOT change the manuscript: the from-scratch factor was already
attributed to the literature (Hrrformer, TPR-enriched transformers, DVNC) rather than to our own measurement,
and the post-training statement in the paper rests on V-50 (LoRA through the binding loss, .502 -> .600),
which is unaffected. It DOES mean the reconciliation with the learned-binding literature remains
literature-supported rather than measured by us, which is what the paper already says.
What a future attempt needs, recorded so it is not re-guessed: the control must pass .80 before any arm is
read, and reaching that plainly needs more than this capacity and schedule -- candidates are a wider model, a
curriculum from one hop, or supervision at the chain positions rather than a binary readout at the end. None
of them is attempted here.
Faults in this line, for the record: (1) V-78 arms emitted a constant class, quarantined; (2) my control
design made Arena's distinct-role rejection loop unsatisfiable (N_CTX=32 > N_SYM=8) and hung the run for 23
hours -- found and fixed by the parallel session, not by me, and my two intervening "fixes" (build caching,
a faster token_span) were both irrelevant to the cause; (3) the control then failed its own threshold. Three
faults, no result. The line is closed for this submission.

## V-79 prereg: does the 2Wiki store result replicate on a SECOND mainstream benchmark (MuSiQue)? Before any code.

**Why this, now.** The manuscript's headline rests on one mainstream corpus (V-65/V-67, 2WikiMultihopQA).
A referee's first question is external validity: one dataset, one result. The second exposure is that the
large-pool separation (prompt collapses at 150 facts, store holds) is measured on SYNTHETIC pools. V-79
attacks both with real data.

**Why MuSiQue and not HotpotQA.** The store arm consumes gold (subject, relation, object) triples. 2Wiki
ships them as `evidences`. HotpotQA ships only supporting-fact SENTENCE indices, no relation chain, so the
port would have to extract triples itself -- and that is exactly the no-gold regime already refuted twice
(V-66 phi-2, V-68 Qwen-7B: the gain REQUIRES provided evidence). Running HotpotQA would therefore re-measure
a known negative and I decline to spend a run on it. MuSiQue (Trivedi et al., TACL 2022) ships
`question_decomposition`, whose hop questions are literally `"Green >> performer"` with `answer`
`"Steve Hillage"` -- a subject, a relation and an object. It is also harder than 2Wiki and runs to 4 hops.
Probed loadable this session (infra probe only, no reading taken): `dgslibisey/MuSiQue`, validation split.

**Arms (frozen phi-2 throughout, identical to V-65).**
- `prompt`: the instance's 20 paragraphs in context under a token budget, few-shot, greedy.
- `prompt_ev`: the same gold decomposition verbalised as `subject | relation | object` lines in context.
- `hrr_gold`: HRR store over the gold decomposition triples, d=4096, string-identity codes, chain followed
  in decomposition order (hop k's object becomes hop k+1's subject), nearest-neighbour cleanup.

**Triple construction, declared now.** For each hop, subject = text left of `>>`, relation = text right of
`>>`, object = the hop's `answer`; any `#k` in a subject is replaced by hop k's answer. An instance is
EXCLUDED if any hop question lacks `>>`. The exclusion rate is reported, not hidden.

**Metric.** Exact match after V-65's `norm`, on the covered slice = instances whose final gold answer equals
the object of the last hop. n=300, seeds {42,123,456}.

**Pool factor (the real-data attack on the synthetic 150-fact panel).** For `prompt_ev` and `hrr_gold`,
pool in {gold-only, +50, +150} where the added facts are REAL triples drawn from other MuSiQue instances,
never synthetic filler.

**Registered predictions -- each scored HIT or MISS, no reinterpretation.**
- P1: `prompt` < `prompt_ev` < `hrr_gold` in 3/3 seeds.
- P2: `hrr_gold` - `prompt` >= .20 on the covered slice.
- P3: at +150 real distractor triples, `hrr_gold` stays >= .70 while `prompt_ev` falls >= .20 from its
  gold-only value.
- P4 (usability gate): coverage >= .60. If coverage < .60 the covered slice is too thin and I declare the
  port UNUSABLE rather than read a number off it.

**Negative readings, declared in advance.**
- If `hrr_gold` <= `prompt_ev`: the algebra adds nothing over in-context evidence on MuSiQue, the 2Wiki gain
  does NOT generalise, and that scope limit goes into the manuscript.
- If P3 fails: the large-pool separation is specific to 2Wiki/synthetic pools and the manuscript's
  large-pool sentence must be narrowed to say so.
- Condition guard, as in V-65: if `prompt` >= .85 the corpus is too easy here and no gain is claimable.

**What this cannot show.** MuSiQue supplies gold decomposition, so V-79 tests external validity of the
PROVIDED-EVIDENCE result only. It says nothing about self-extraction, which stays refuted.

### V-79 deviations, registered BEFORE the scored run (smoke test n=8 only, no reading taken)

The n=8 smoke run was infra validation, not a measurement, and no number from it is transcribed. It exposed
two things worth fixing first, and both cut AGAINST our own claim, so neither can flatter the result:

1. **Paragraph budget 1200 -> 1500 (`PARA_BUDGET`).** V-65's budget was tuned to 2Wiki, which ships
   sentences; MuSiQue ships full paragraphs, and at 1200 tokens the paragraph arm was truncated on 8/8
   instances. A wider window can only HELP the baseline.
2. **New arm `prompt_sup`: the gold supporting paragraphs only, natural text, untruncated.** This is the
   strongest natural-language baseline available and it exists to answer, in advance, the referee question
   "does the store only win because you starved the paragraph arm?". It can only hurt our claim.
   It is explicitly NOT one of P1-P4 and carries no registered threshold; the scorer labels it
   "ADDED (not registered)".
3. Diagnostic only: the store arm was printing `gold-kept 0.000`, a counter it never increments. Now prints
   `n/a`, so no later reader mistakes it for a measurement.

**P1, P2, P3, P4 and all three negative readings are UNCHANGED from prereg 1fd4489.** Note that P1 is
registered against `prompt`, not against `prompt_sup`; if the store beats `prompt` but loses to
`prompt_sup`, P1 passes and the ADDED line fails, and both get reported.

Corpus facts observed while validating the loader (structural, not outcomes): the `>>` exclusion rule cost
0 of 8 instances, hop distribution was all 2-hop in the first 8, and coverage was 8/8. The full run reports
these over n=300.

### Considered and DECLINED (no run): a real-KG version of the capacity panel

Reasoning recorded so a later session does not spend a run on it. I was about to prereg a capacity sweep
over real KG triples (RoG-WebQSP / RoG-CWQ, both probed loadable this session) on the premise that the
manuscript's capacity panel is measured on SYNTHETIC codes and that real relation reuse would degrade it
earlier. I checked the premise before writing the prereg, and it is FALSE: V-73 already pools REAL 2Wiki
gold triples, from 22 bindings at K=10 to 600 at K=400 (banked: em .957/.940/.780/.200/.063). The panel is
already a real-data curve, so a KG restatement would measure the same thing on a different corpus and buy
the manuscript nothing a referee would credit. Declined.

The residual difference a KG would add -- a larger, more skewed relation vocabulary with hub entities --
is a refinement of an already-real curve, not a missing result, and is not worth a run before 9/16.

### V-79 RESULT (prereg 1fd4489, deviations 2e3499e). Scorer output transcribed verbatim first.

```
  prompt           0.1651   (trunc .887 -- MuSiQue's 20 paragraphs exceed phi-2's window)
  prompt_sup       0.4009   (gold supporting paragraphs only, untruncated; ADDED, not registered)
  prompt_ev_p0     0.8994   prompt_ev_p50 0.3475   prompt_ev_p150 0.1871
  hrr_gold_p0      0.9481   hrr_gold_p50  0.9324   hrr_gold_p150  0.6557
  >>> V-79 VERDICT: P1 ordering 3/3: True | P2 gain>=.20: True (0.7830) | P3 pool separation: False
  (hrr@150=0.6557, prompt_ev drop=0.7123) | P4 coverage>=.60: True (1.0000) ; NEGATIVE READING APPLIES:
  the large-pool separation does not reproduce with real distractor triples, so the manuscript's
  large-pool sentence must be narrowed ; ADDED (not registered): strongest natural-language baseline
  prompt_sup=0.4009 vs hrr_gold_p0=0.9481 -> store beats it
```

**Registered predictions: P1 HIT, P2 HIT, P3 MISSED, P4 HIT.**

**P3 MISSED, and I am not reinterpreting it.** I registered P3 as a conjunction: the store must stay
>= .70 at +150 real distractor triples AND `prompt_ev` must fall >= .20. The store landed at .6557, below
my own bar. P3 is MISSED and stands as MISSED.

**But the auto-fired negative reading's WORDING over-claims, and that has to be said rather than edited
into agreement.** Its text is "the large-pool separation does not reproduce". That is not what the numbers
show. At +150 real triples `prompt_ev` fell 71 points to .1871 while the store fell to .6557 -- a 47-point
separation, wider in relative terms than anything in the synthetic panel. What failed is the store's
ABSOLUTE retention against my .70 bar, not the separation. I am leaving the scorer and the registered
threshold untouched; this paragraph is my reading of a threshold I set too optimistically, and the
manuscript will be narrowed on the specific point the data actually support.

**What the manuscript gains (external validity, the referee's first question).** The headline replicates on
a second mainstream multi-hop benchmark: prompt .1651 -> store .9481, a 78.3-point gain, ordering strict in
3/3 seeds. It also survives the strongest natural-language baseline I could build against it: gold
supporting paragraphs, untruncated, score .4009, so the store beats it by 55 points and the margin cannot
