### 2026-09-10 — Three corrections of MINE against V-125, and a process failure that nearly wasted a run

**Process failure, first.** Instructed to proceed without asking, I began designing an entailment audit —
prereg, two-judge design, control conditions — before checking the ledger tail. **V-125 had already run it and
closed** (prereg b5a6828 → close 0f07df7). I was one commit away from re-running a completed experiment on the
user's API credit. **Rule for me, going forward: read the ledger tail and `git log` BEFORE designing anything.**
The same check would have caught the V-109 id collision earlier.

**Correction 1 — my cue heuristic over-estimated by nearly 2x.** At 1b4a173 I estimated, from relation-keyword
presence, that 147 of 279 cue-testable rows (52.7%) lacked the second-hop fact. V-125's judge measures
**83 of 287 = 28.9%**. My heuristic's false-positive direction was the one I flagged as possible ("country of
citizenship / United States" for a passage reading "olympic and national team rower") and it dominated. The
52.7% figure is superseded; **28.9% is the number, and it is essentially all hop-2** (hop2 absent 83 = .289,
hop1 absent 6 = .021).

**Correction 2 — I predicted the wrong direction for the consequence, and said so to the user.** I wrote that if
the exposure were widespread "the 97%/90% error-removal figure is inflated by items that were unanswerable
anyway". **The measurement says the opposite.** On the 204 answerable rows the store rises to **.9967** while
single_pass reaches only **.598–.630**, so raw removal goes UP to ~99% and the conservative form to 96.7–97.9%.
The mechanism is clean and I should have anticipated it: **7.0 of the store's 7.67 errors sit inside the 96
excluded rows**, so its failures co-locate with exactly the rows the exposure flags. The full-set 94–95% was, if
anything, an underestimate of the fair-subset figure. **The exposure weakens the framing, not the effect.**

**Correction 3 — what the exposure actually costs us is elsewhere, and it is the sentence I had already
downgraded twice.** On the fair subset `evidence_in_prompt` reaches **.9902–1.0000**, with kimi-k3 at
**1.0000 above the store's .9967** and glm-5.3's .9951 inside cleanup noise. So on the cleanest comparison
available, the store has **no residual edge over reading the evidence directly**, and "the algebra halves the
residual error, 5.0% to 2.6%" is unsettled-leaning-false — the same verdict V-124 P3 reached by .0007, now
reached on the subset where the question is best posed.

**Net effect on what goes to the co-author** (his call, not mine, per the standing rule): one sentence
(~line 452, "the arms differ only in HOW the same evidence reaches the model") is materially false as written and
needs rewriting; one sentence ("the algebra halves the residual error") is leaning false on two independent
measurements; and the headline itself is **more** robust than the full-set number suggested, not less. The quote
rule from V-125 stands: **no error-removal figure may be quoted without the answerable-subset figure beside it.**

**Still not recomputable:** phi-2 and qwen3-8b have no per-row dumps (v65_logs/v65.json stores per-seed means;
every V-108 file lacks a rows array), so the manuscript's own .253 headline cannot be restricted to the
answerable subset. That is a gap in what we can say about the paper's exact published number, and it is stated
rather than papered over.

## 2026-09-10 — V-126 PREREG: the retrieval baseline the ICLR draft lacks, on a SECOND benchmark, with a local reader (user-directed: "去提升一下论文质量吧，需要的话，可以继续跑实验"; BLIND on P1–P4)

**Why now.** I reviewed the ICLR draft adversarially and put it at 5 (marginally below acceptance). Two of
the four blocking objections are experiments, not prose: (a) the paper never compares against an ordinary
retriever — its `evidence_in_prompt` arm is the retrieval-error-zero *ideal*; (b) every number is
2WikiMultihopQA, so both the 28.9% evidence mismatch (V-125) and the surviving claim that *structuring* the
evidence is the lever (V-125 step 5) could be artifacts of one benchmark. **OpenRouter is at $0.27, below
the $3 floor, so no API arm is possible.** This design closes both objections with GPU only.

**Design.** Three arms share ONE reader (local Qwen3-8B, bf16, greedy, `do_sample=False`) and ONE prompt
renderer, run over two datasets:

| arm | evidence the reader sees |
|-----|--------------------------|
| `single_pass` | all ten paragraphs under a 1200-token budget (the paper's arm) |
| `bm25_topk` | BM25 over the row's sentences, top-k, rendered in document order |
| `oracle_sentences` | exactly the annotated supporting sentences, same rendering |

**k is matched per row** to that row's number of annotated supporting sentences, so `bm25_topk` and
`oracle_sentences` differ only in *which* sentences were chosen and never in how many. BM25 is Okapi with
k1=1.5, b=0.75 over lowercased alphanumeric tokens, implemented inline so its constants are visible.

**Datasets.** 2WikiMultihopQA compositional validation (the paper's slice, via the banked `v85_data`
loader) and HotpotQA-distractor validation, `type == "bridge"`, rows whose supporting pointers all
resolve. n = 300 each. The two differ in exactly the way that matters: **2Wiki's hop facts are drawn from
a knowledge base, HotpotQA's supporting sentences are human-selected from the same prose the reader sees.**

**A fourth arm on 2Wiki only, as the validity anchor:** `single_pass_banked_builder`, which uses
`v85_data.prompt_for` — the exact builder behind the served ladder — so the local reader can be placed
against the banked served value. The three registered arms use the new shared renderer, because a
cross-dataset comparison must not be confounded by two different builders.

**Predictions.**
- **P0 (validity gate):** 2Wiki `single_pass_banked_builder` lands within **±.10** of the banked served
  `.47` (V-108, qwen3-8b). **A miss does NOT void the run** — the three arms share one reader and one
  renderer and stay internally comparable. What a miss forbids is cross-referencing these numbers to the
  served ladder, and the scorer does not do that.
- **P1:** on **both** datasets, `oracle_sentences − single_pass` has a paired bootstrap 95% CI excluding
  zero.
- **P2:** on **both** datasets, the fraction of the oracle gain that ordinary retrieval recovers,
  `(bm25 − sp) / (oracle − sp)`, is **< 0.50**.
- **P3 (descriptive, no bar):** the oracle gain on 2Wiki minus the oracle gain on HotpotQA — the
  annotation-provenance contrast.
- **P4 (descriptive, no bar):** BM25 sentence-level recall of the annotated supporting set, per dataset,
  which is the mechanism behind whatever P2 does.

**My expected directions, stated separately from the bars.** I expect **P1 to hold on both**. I expect
**P2 to FAIL on HotpotQA and hold on 2Wiki**: HotpotQA bridge questions share surface tokens with the
first hop, so a lexical retriever should recover much of the gain there, whereas on 2Wiki the second-hop
fact is often not stated in the prose at all (V-125: 28.9%), and no retriever can select a sentence that
does not exist. I have **no expectation** on P3's magnitude. If P2 fails on both, that is a result against
the paper's general framing and I have written the reading for it below before seeing any number.

**Readings, fixed now.**
- **P1 fails on either dataset ⇒ reported first.** On that benchmark, handing the reader the exact
  supporting sentences does not beat handing it all ten paragraphs, so "structuring the evidence is the
  lever" does not replicate and the paper gets a dataset-scope statement naming where it holds.
- **P2 fails on both ⇒** an ordinary lexical retriever already captures most of the available gain, the
  store's contribution over a plain retriever is small on these tasks, and the defensible argument for an
  exact index moves to the axes where retrieval does not help: evidence beyond the context window (V-106)
  and capacity (V-101/V-102). This would be a real weakening and it goes in the paper as one.
- **P2 fails on one ⇒** the claim becomes benchmark-conditional and is stated that way, with the
  BM25-recall mechanism (P4) as the explanation.
- **P2 holds on both ⇒** evidence *selection* is a real unsolved problem here rather than a straw man,
  which is the strongest available argument for the exact index, and it goes in the body.
- **P0 fails ⇒** no cross-reference to the served ladder anywhere; the arms are still read.

**Discipline.** Prereg + `v126.py` + the frozen `v126_score.py` committed **before the first
generation**. `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` enforced by an abort (defect 024d9e0). Every prompt set carries a
printed sha256 prefix and token total. Per-row dumps for all arms. The completeness filter is
value-blind: an arm with `n_scored != n_rows` is excluded on row counts alone, and a dataset missing any
registered arm is not read. Intervals are paired bootstraps (same rows, same reader) at 20000 resamples,
seeded. One tick held before scoring; the scorer is run verbatim.

**Scoping.** **No API call, zero spend.** The store is not re-measured — no model participates in it, and
nothing here changes its .974. Nothing here bears on the npj submission. This run cannot speak to the
*acquisition* question (V-97/V-98: recall .6589, end-to-end .4678), because every arm here is handed
either all the paragraphs or an annotated sentence set.

**Cost.** GPU only: 2 datasets × 3 arms + 1 anchor = 7 arm-runs × 300 rows ≈ 2100 greedy generations on
one A800 with an 8B model. Estimated well under two hours. Host: the A800 box, `dino_wm` env
(transformers 4.57.6, torch 2.4.1), one GPU, `HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com`.

## 2026-09-10 — V-127 PREREG: is the 28.9% evidence mismatch specific to KNOWLEDGE-BASE-DERIVED annotation? The V-125 audit, replicated on MuSiQue with the same judge (user-directed: "去提升一下论文质量吧，需要的话，可以继续跑实验"; BLIND on P1–P3)

**The question, and why it is the paper's biggest open hole.** V-125 measured that on 2WikiMultihopQA
**83 of 287 decidable instances (28.9%)** have the second-hop fact neither stated nor entailed by the
supporting sentences the single-pass arm reads. My adversarial review of the ICLR draft put the paper at
5/10, and the first of the four blocking objections was that **every number in it is 2Wiki**, so the most
novel finding in the paper might be an artifact of one benchmark.

**The mechanism hypothesis, stated so it can be wrong.** 2Wiki pairs Wikipedia *prose* with *Wikidata
triples*, so a triple can be true in the knowledge base and absent from the passage. MuSiQue is built the
other way round: it **composes verified single-hop questions** whose answers are, by construction,
answerable from their paired paragraph. If the mismatch is an artifact of KB-derived annotation, MuSiQue's
rate should be far lower. If MuSiQue is just as bad, the mismatch is a general property of multi-hop
benchmark construction — a stronger claim, not a weaker one. **Either outcome improves the paper**, which
is why this is the right experiment rather than a fishing expedition.

**Protocol, held as close to V-125 as the datasets allow.**
- **Data:** MuSiQue answerable, validation, **2-hop rows only** (`id` starts `2hop`), first n=300 whose
  `question_decomposition` has exactly two hops and whose `paragraph_support_idx` resolves for both. Rows
  that fail to resolve are declared **undecidable in advance**, counted, reported, and never judged — the
  V-125 rule.
- **What is judged:** for each row, whether the supporting text **states or entails** that hop's fact.
  The fact form matches V-125 exactly, which I confirmed from the data before writing this: MuSiQue's
  decomposition gives hop 1 as `"Green >> performer" -> "Steve Hillage"` and hop 2 as
  `"#1 >> spouse" -> "Miquette Giraudy"`, so hop 2's fact is `(hop1 answer, relation, hop2 answer)` =
  `(Steve Hillage, spouse, Miquette Giraudy)` — the same `(s, r, o)` triple V-125 judged. The judge
  prompt is the V-125 template with the triple rendered the same way; labels unchanged:
  `STATED` / `ENTAILED` / `ABSENT`.

- **A CONFOUND I am registering AGAINST MY OWN PREDICTION.** V-125 judged supporting **sentences**;
  MuSiQue annotates support at **paragraph** granularity (`paragraph_support_idx`, `is_supporting`).
  A paragraph is strictly more text than a sentence, so paragraph-level judging biases the absent rate
  **downward** — the same direction as my expected result. Left unaddressed, a P1 hold would be
  partly manufactured. So the run measures **both** granularities on the same rows:
  **(i) paragraph-level**, the dataset's own annotation, which is the primary; and
  **(ii) sentence-level**, the single sentence inside that paragraph with the highest lexical overlap
  with the fact, which is the closest analogue of what V-125 judged. Both are judged by the same judge in
  the same run.
- **Judges:** `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` — **the same model that was the usable judge in V-125** — plus
  `moonshotai/kimi-k3` as a second judge so consensus is possible. Both via **CommonStack**
  (`https://api.commonstack.ai/v1`), temperature 0.
- **Calibration:** 40 rows drawn deterministically, annotated **before any judge output exists**, and
  committed as its own artifact. As in V-125 the annotator is the **AGENT**, disclosed as such and not
  claimed to be human annotation; a human pass by the user or the co-author remains available and would
  supersede it.
- **Gate, unchanged from V-125:** a judge is usable iff it agrees with the 80 calibration
  fact-judgements on **≥ 85%**, pooled `PRESENT (STATED|ENTAILED)` vs `ABSENT`. A judge that fails the
  gate, or that does not return a parseable verdict for every decidable row (value-blind completeness),
  is excluded **before its answers are consulted**. If only one judge survives, the single-judge path is
  a **pre-registered degraded mode** and is reported as such.

**Predictions.**
- **P0 (validity gate):** at least one judge clears the 85% pooled calibration gate. If none does,
  **nothing is read** and the failure is the result.
- **P1 (PRIMARY, paragraph-level):** MuSiQue's hop-2 not-answerable rate is **< 0.15** — below half of
  2Wiki's 0.289 and below the bar V-125 itself used. Registered as: P1 holds iff `rate < 0.15`.
- **P1b (REGISTERED SECONDARY, sentence-level):** the same rate over the best-overlap sentence.
  **Registered reading: the provenance claim is licensed only if BOTH are < 0.15.** If P1 holds while
  P1b does not, the contrast is at least partly annotation *granularity* rather than annotation
  *provenance*, and the paper must say that instead.
- **P2 (descriptive, no bar):** the per-hop `STATED`/`ENTAILED`/`ABSENT` distribution, and the hop-1
  versus hop-2 asymmetry (2Wiki: 6 against 83).
- **P3 (descriptive, no bar):** a bootstrap 95% CI on the MuSiQue rate, and on the 2Wiki − MuSiQue
  difference, using V-125's banked 83/287.

**My expected direction, stated separately from the bars.** I expect **P1 to HOLD** — MuSiQue's hops are
verified single-hop QA pairs, so the prose should contain them. I am on record that this is a prediction I
can lose: if MuSiQue's rate is also near 29%, my mechanism story is wrong and the finding is broader than
I claimed.

**Readings, fixed now.**
- **P1 holds ⇒** the mismatch is **annotation-provenance-specific**. The paper states it that way, names
  the three constructions (2Wiki = KB triples over prose; HotpotQA = human sentence pointers into the
  prose; MuSiQue = composed verified single-hop questions), and the 28.9% becomes a measured claim about
  KB-derived benchmarks **with a contrast case**, which is exactly what the single-benchmark objection
  asked for.
- **P1 fails ⇒ reported first, as the stronger finding:** multi-hop benchmarks are broadly not
  evidence-matched, the audit generalises beyond 2Wiki, and the paper's caution is raised from one
  dataset to a class. My mechanism hypothesis is then recorded as refuted.
- **P0 fails ⇒** nothing is read; the judge failure is reported and the experiment is re-registered only
  with a different judge, never with a relaxed gate.

**Deviations from the standing rules, recorded BEFORE launch because the gateway forces them.**
1. **No provider pinning.** CommonStack returns no `provider` field, so V-123's standing rule ("pin the
   serving provider on every API prereg, record its quantization") **cannot be honoured**: which weights
   served a call is not observable. Consequence accepted — per-row claims were already forbidden by
   V-123, and this run makes only aggregate claims.
2. **No spend meter.** `/credits`, `/usage`, `/billing/*` all 404 and the `usage` object carries no
   `cost` field, so V-108's rule (cap against the account meter, because per-call cost fields understate
   by up to 8×) is unenforceable. Substituted: a **hard cap of 1400 calls** for the whole run, counted in
   the harness, and the user is told that spend is not observable from my side.
3. **No reasoning field**, so the four-category hop split is not computable on this gateway. Not needed
   here — judge verdicts do not use it.

**Scoping.** The store is not re-measured; no model participates in it. This run says nothing about
*acquisition* (V-97/V-98) and nothing about the npj submission. It bears on exactly one sentence of the
ICLR draft — the scope of the audit — and on the "one benchmark" objection.

**Cost.** ≤ 1400 calls: 300 rows × 2 granularities × 2 judges + retries, plus the calibration draw. `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`
enforced by abort. Prereg + harness + **frozen scorer** committed before the first call. One tick held
before scoring; the scorer is run verbatim.

## 2026-09-10 — V-127 DEVIATION #2: my first repair was the WRONG DIAGNOSIS. The paragraph arm's failures are TRUNCATED JSON caused by my own 200-token output ceiling, not transient errors — and that is why raising retries made it worse.

**Evidence.** Re-run under deviation #1 (retries 4->8, backoff 4s) scored **291/300**, *worse* than the
original 299/300. Every one of the 9 failures is truncated JSON:

```
i=31  '{"hop1": "STATED", "hop'
i=38  '{"hop1'
i=56  '{"hop1": "STATED",'
i=91  '{"hop1": "'
i=97  '{"hop1": "STATED", "hop2": "ABS'
i=145 '{"hop1": "STATED", "hop2": "STATED'
```

**Mechanism, and it is my bug.** `max_tokens: 200` in the harness. `deepseek-v4-flash` spends output
budget on reasoning tokens that **CommonStack does not return** (no `reasoning` field — recorded in the
prereg as deviation 3), so the budget is consumed invisibly and the visible JSON is clipped. The longer
PARAGRAPH contexts induce more of it, which is exactly why paragraph fails (9/300, and 1/300 in run 1)
while SENTENCE never does (0/300 in both runs). Retries cannot fix a systematic ceiling — each attempt
truncates at the same place — so run 2 was resampling noise around it, and landing worse was luck.

**This is the same phenomenon the ICLR draft reports in Sec 4.2**, one step further: an unreturned
reasoning trace does not only make hop attribution uninterpretable, it silently consumes the answer
budget on the gateway that hides it. Worth a sentence in the paper.

**Repair:** `--max_tokens 200 -> 1024` for the paragraph arm. Nothing else changes: prereg 66bf24d, all
bars, the judge template, the row set and its shas, the 40-row calibration (0e39292) and the frozen
scorer (md5 7813b32e34a6fb7573aa39169a10ea88) are untouched. The complete `sentence` arm stays carried
forward byte-unchanged at its original 200-token provenance, so the already-read secondary cannot move.

**Correction to the record.** Deviation #1 attributed the exclusion to transient failure and dropped
kimi-k3 for returning empty content. The kimi finding stands (it returned almost nothing), but the
deepseek attribution was wrong, and I am recording that I mis-diagnosed my own instrument before
re-running rather than after.

**Still recorded pre-result:** the sentence arm reads 0.3033 [0.2533, 0.3567] against 2Wiki's 0.2892,
difference -0.0137 [-0.0862, +0.0584]. My registered expectation that MuSiQue would be far cleaner is
losing, and this re-run exists to complete the PRIMARY, not to rescue it.

## 2026-09-10 — V-127 CLOSED: P1 and P1b BOTH FAIL ⇒ the evidence mismatch is NOT a knowledge-base-annotation artifact. My registered mechanism hypothesis is REFUTED, and the finding is stronger than the one I predicted. The granularity control I registered against myself turned out to matter as much as the dataset.

Prereg 66bf24d, calibration 0e39292 (committed before any judge output), frozen scorer
md5 7813b32e34a6fb7573aa39169a10ea88 run verbatim. Two recorded deviations (retries; then the
max_tokens correction of that first mis-diagnosis). n=300 MuSiQue 2-hop, **zero undecidable**.

**P0 PASS**: both judge arms usable — paragraph calibration .912, sentence .900, each 300/300.

| granularity | hop1 absent | hop2 absent | ANSWERABLE |
|-------------|-------------|-------------|------------|
| paragraph (dataset's own annotation, PRIMARY) | 36 (.120) | **59 (.1967) [.1533, .2433]** | 215/300 = .7167 |
| sentence (V-125-comparable) | 57 (.190) | **91 (.3033) [.2533, .3567]** | 168/300 = .5600 |

**P1 FAILS (.1967 vs bar .15). P1b FAILS (.3033).** Per the registered reading this is REPORTED FIRST and
is the stronger result: **multi-hop benchmarks are broadly not evidence-matched.** MuSiQue is the
construction least likely to have this defect — every hop is a verified single-hop question, answerable
from its paired paragraph by design — and it still leaves the second-hop fact absent on one instance in
five at paragraph granularity and nearly one in three at sentence granularity. The V-125 audit therefore
generalises from one dataset to a class, and the paper's caution is raised accordingly.

**My hypothesis is refuted, and I record the two refinements that survive it.**

1. **Provenance explains PART of it, not the phenomenon.** 2Wiki − MuSiQue at paragraph level is
   **+0.0935 [+0.0271, +0.1639]**, which excludes zero: 2Wiki (KB triples over prose) genuinely is worse
   than MuSiQue (composed verified single-hop questions), 28.9% against 19.7%. At sentence granularity the
   difference is **−0.0140 [−0.0869, +0.0574]**, indistinguishable. So annotation provenance is worth
   roughly nine points and is not the cause.
2. **The granularity control I registered AGAINST MY OWN PREDICTION matters as much as the dataset.**
   Same rows, same judge: .1967 at paragraph against .3033 at sentence, a 10.7-point swing produced by
   nothing but how much surrounding text is counted as "the evidence". Had I measured only the
   paragraph level — which is the dataset's own annotation and the natural choice — I would have
   published a number that looks half as bad AND is not comparable to V-125's sentence-level 28.9%.
   This is the single most useful thing the run produced and it exists only because the prereg forced
   the control on me when the coarser unit favoured my prediction.

**Convergent evidence from V-126, same session, independent design.** V-126's P3 built the 2Wiki-vs-
HotpotQA contrast expecting the same provenance effect (KB triples over prose vs human sentence pointers
into it). The oracle-evidence gains came out **identical: +0.1867 on both**. Two independent tests, one
judged and one behavioural, both refute the provenance story.

**Instrument defects recorded (fourth and fifth in this project's API work).**
- **kimi-k3 returns EMPTY CONTENT through CommonStack**: 156 PARSE + 14 "no choices" + one HTTP 500 on
  the paragraph arm, 42/300 scored. Dropped as unusable on this gateway, not as a judge whose answers I
  disliked — it produced almost none.
- **Invisible reasoning tokens consume the answer budget.** My 200-token ceiling truncated the visible
  JSON on the longer paragraph contexts (9/300 in run 2, 1/300 in run 1) and never on the shorter
  sentence contexts. deepseek-v4-flash spends output budget on reasoning this gateway does not return.
  At max_tokens 1024 the arm scored **300/300 using exactly 300 calls and zero retries**, which confirms
  the mechanism. **My first repair (more retries) was the wrong diagnosis and made it worse (291/300 vs
  299/300), because retries cannot fix a systematic ceiling.** This is the ICLR draft's Sec 4.2 finding
  one step further and belongs in the paper: an unreturned reasoning trace does not merely make hop
  attribution uninterpretable, it silently eats the answer budget on the gateway that hides it.

**Standing rules confirmed / added.** The value-blind completeness rule again excluded the arm with the
BEST calibration (.950 at 299/300) and cost the primary until the instrument was repaired — the criterion
was not relaxed, in line with V-124. **New rule: on any gateway that does not return a reasoning field,
set max_tokens well above the visible answer length and treat truncated output as an instrument ceiling,
never as a transient error.**

## 2026-09-10 — V-128 PREREG: the retrieval baseline pushed to where it can BEAT me. A budget sweep and a dense retriever, because V-126's headline invites one obvious rebuttal and I would rather answer it than survive it. (BLIND on P1–P4)

**Why.** V-126 closed with a strong finding: at the oracle's own per-row budget a lexical retriever is
*worse than no retrieval at all* (2Wiki $-0.290$, HotpotQA $-0.130$, both CIs excluding zero). The paper
states it, and states the limitation. But the rebuttal writes itself: **"you crippled the retriever"** —
$k$ was matched to the gold count (2.00 and 2.48 sentences), and BM25 is lexical. A deployed system
retrieves five or ten *paragraphs* with a dense encoder. If that closes the gap, my newest and strongest
claim is a budget artifact, and I want to know that from an experiment rather than from a referee.

**Design.** Identical reader, rows and renderer to V-126 — the retrieval functions and dataset loaders are
**imported from `v126.py`** so the code path is the same object, and the launch record checksums it. Per
dataset ($n=300$, 2WikiMultihopQA compositional and HotpotQA-distractor bridge):

| arm family | configurations |
|---|---|
| controls | `single_pass` (all ten paragraphs), `oracle_sentences` |
| sentence retrieval | {BM25, dense} $\times$ $k \in \{$gold, 5, 10, 20$\}$ |
| paragraph retrieval | {BM25, dense} $\times$ $k \in \{2, 5\}$ |

$14$ arm-runs per dataset, $28$ in all, $8400$ greedy generations. **Paragraph-level retrieval is included
because that is what deployed retrieval-augmented systems actually do**, and its absence is the honest
weakness of V-126. Dense retriever: `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5`, CLS pooling, L2-normalised, cosine, query
prefixed per its model card. BM25 is V-126's Okapi ($k_1{=}1.5$, $b{=}0.75$) unchanged.

**Predictions.**
- **P0 (validity gate):** the BM25 sentence arm at $k=$gold reproduces V-126's banked accuracy within
  $\pm0.05$ on **both** datasets ($0.0433$ and $0.3667$). Same rows, same reader, same renderer, imported
  retriever — a miss means the harness moved and **nothing is read**.
- **P1 (PRIMARY):** **no** configuration reaches the oracle: for every (retriever, unit, $k$), the paired
  bootstrap CI of `oracle - config` excludes zero. Registered as: P1 holds iff that is true for all $24$
  retrieval configurations.
- **P2:** the **best** configuration beats `single_pass`, i.e. `best - single_pass` has a CI excluding
  zero.
- **P3 (descriptive, no bar):** for each retriever and unit, the smallest $k$ at which it stops hurting
  relative to `single_pass`.
- **P4 (descriptive, no bar):** recall of the gold supporting sentences against $k$, per retriever and
  unit — the mechanism behind P1 and P3.

**My expected directions, stated separately from the bars, and one of them costs me.** I expect **P1 to
hold**: the second hop's sentence is often not similar to the question at *any* budget, and as $k$ grows
the context re-approaches the unfiltered one, so retrieval should approach `single_pass` from below rather
than reach the oracle. I expect **P2 to HOLD**, and that **weakens my own current claim**: if a larger
budget lets retrieval beat `single_pass`, then "BM25 is worse than no retrieval" is true only *at oracle
budget*, and the paper's Sec. 3.2 must be narrowed to say exactly that. I am registering that in advance
so the narrowing cannot be presented as a nuance I always intended.

**Readings, fixed now.**
- **P1 fails ⇒ REPORTED FIRST.** Some ordinary retriever reaches oracle evidence at a realistic budget.
  Then the paper's strongest argument for an exact index on this task is gone: what the store supplies is
  reachable by retrieval, and the contribution must be restated as being about *capacity and cost*
  (Sec. 3.1, Appendix on the envelope) rather than about evidence quality. I would rather publish that
  than have it found.
- **P1 holds ⇒** the oracle-versus-retrieval gap survives a budget sweep and a dense encoder, so
  "evidence *selection* is the hard part" gets a curve behind it instead of a single harsh point.
- **P2 holds ⇒** Sec. 3.2's claim is narrowed to the oracle-budget regime in the same commit that reports
  it, and the crossing $k$ (P3) is reported as the honest boundary.
- **P2 fails ⇒** retrieval never beats the unfiltered context at any tested budget, which strengthens
  V-126 rather than qualifying it.
- **P0 fails ⇒** nothing is read; the harness divergence is investigated first.

**Discipline.** Prereg + `v128.py` + the frozen `v128_score.py` committed before the first generation.
`PYTHONHASHSEED=0` enforced by abort. Every arm's prompt set carries a printed sha256 and token total.
Per-row dumps for all $28$ arms. Value-blind completeness: an arm with `n_scored != n_rows` is excluded on
counts alone. Intervals are paired bootstraps over rows (same rows, same reader), $20\,000$ resamples,
seeded. One tick held before scoring; the scorer is run verbatim.

**Scoping.** GPU only, **zero API spend**. The store is never re-measured — no model participates in it.
Nothing here bears on acquisition (V-97/V-98) or on the npj submission. GPU 0 is in use by another user,
so this run pins a free device.

## 2026-09-10 — V-129 PREREG: scale the EXTRACTOR, not the reader. Does a frontier model close the acquisition gap that an 8B fine-tune could not? (user-directed: "可以，这个可以做"; BLIND on P1–P4)

**Why this rung and not the one I first proposed.** The user approved work on the acquisition bridge. Two of
the three levers I sketched are already dead on this record and I am not re-running them: the
**redundancy family is closed permanently** at all three loci (V-99/107/109/110/122, five gain-price
cancellations), and **chain-weighted supervision is ruled out by V-98 P3** — chain recall equals overall
recall to within $-.006$ to $+.013$, so the chain is not the weak link.

**And "raise recall" cannot win, by arithmetic.** V-98 measured recall $.6589 \Rightarrow$ end-to-end
$.4678$, with EM sitting just above recall$^2$. At the project's own $.798$ recall target the route reaches
$\approx .637$ plus a small offset, call it $.66$, against fine-tune baselines of $.6367$ (V-98's reference)
and $.7333$ (V-99 seed 42). So incremental recall buys parity at best. Chasing it is not worth GPU.

**The unmeasured coordinate.** V-98's frozen-extractor figure of $.0500$ is **Qwen3-8B frozen**, and its
$.6589$ is **Qwen3-8B fine-tuned**. This project has scaled the *reader* to 2.4 trillion parameters across
V-108/V-124 and has **never scaled the extractor**. A 2026 frontier model prompted for structured
extraction is a different instrument from a 2025 8B fine-tune, and nothing in the ledger measures it. It is
also the cheapest remaining shot at the bottleneck: no training, $\approx 600$ calls.

**Protocol.** Question-blind extraction, which is the deployment model the manuscript's reuse and
context-compression arguments depend on. **The question is NOT shown to the extractor** — V-98 established
that showing it is a different protocol ($.5511$ vs $.4678$) with no store reuse, and it is not adopted
here by the back door.
- Rows: the paper's `load_rows(300, "validation")` slice, unchanged.
- Input: the instance's ten paragraphs under the same $1200$-token budget the reader gets.
- Output: lines of `subject | relation | object`, parsed with a fixed strict parser; malformed lines counted
  and reported, never silently dropped.
- Extractors: `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` and `moonshotai/kimi-k3` via CommonStack, temperature $0$.
- Store: V-102's sharded code path **verbatim**, hashed identity, $d=2048$, exact algebra, built from the
  EXTRACTED facts only. Metric `em` after the registered normalisation. Two chained unbind-and-cleanup hops.
- Scored against the gold triples for recall and **chain recall** (the two triples the supporting facts
  identify), so V-98's diagnostic is recomputed rather than assumed.

**Predictions.**
- **P0 (validity gate):** the store built from GOLD triples on these same rows reproduces the banked
  $.9744$ within $\pm .01$. No model participates in the store, so a miss means the store code path moved
  and **nothing is read**.
- **P1 (PRIMARY):** frontier question-blind extraction recall $\ge 0.80$ — beating V-98's 8B fine-tune
  ($.6589$) and reaching the project's own $.798$ target.
- **P2:** end-to-end EM of the store built from extracted facts $\ge 0.6367$, V-98's fine-tune reference.
  This is the bar the route has never cleared; clearing it makes "LLM extraction + exact store" competitive
  with simply fine-tuning the model, for the first time on this record.
- **P3 (descriptive, no bar):** chain recall against overall recall. V-98 found them equal at 8B; whether
  that survives at frontier scale is unmeasured.
- **P4 (descriptive, no bar):** whether EM still tracks recall$^2$, and the malformed-line rate.

**My expected directions, stated separately from the bars.** I expect **P1 to HOLD** — structured
extraction is close to what these models are drilled on, and the $.0500$ frozen baseline reflects a 2025 8B
model, not the task's difficulty. I expect **P2 to be BORDERLINE**: at recall $.85$ the square is $.7225$,
which sits between the two fine-tune references, so P2 may hold against $.6367$ and still fail against
$.7333$. **I am registering that both references get reported, not whichever one the result clears.**

**Readings, fixed now.**
- **P1 and P2 both hold ⇒** the acquisition bottleneck is an artifact of extractor capacity, not a property
  of the task. That is a genuinely new positive result and it changes the paper: the honest caveat
  "everything here is conditional on gold facts" is replaced by a measured end-to-end number.
- **P1 holds, P2 fails ⇒** extraction is fixed but the recall$^2$ chain penalty still dominates, so the
  binding constraint is the *two-hop survival structure*, not extractor quality. Reported as such, and the
  paper's caveat stays with a sharper reason attached.
- **P1 fails ⇒ reported first.** A frontier model cannot do question-blind two-hop extraction either, so
  the bottleneck is the task and not the 8B model, and the manuscript's limitation is not merely real but
  robust to three orders of magnitude of extractor scale. I would rather publish that than leave it as an
  open door.
- **P0 fails ⇒** nothing is read; the store path is investigated first.

**Deviations in force on this gateway, from the V-127 record.** CommonStack exposes **no balance meter**
(so the V-108 rule is replaced by a hard cap of **900 calls**, and spend is not observable), **no provider
field** (so V-123's pinning rule cannot be honoured), and **no reasoning field**; per V-127's lesson
`max_tokens` is set to $2048$, well above the visible answer, and truncated output is treated as an
instrument ceiling rather than a transient error.

**Discipline.** Prereg + `v129.py` + the frozen `v129_score.py` committed before the first call.
`PYTHONHASHSEED=0` enforced by abort. Per-row dumps including the raw extraction text, so the defect that
made V-98's dumps unusable here — aggregates only, no per-row triples — is not repeated. Value-blind
completeness: an extractor arm with `n_scored != n_eval` is excluded on counts alone. Intervals are
bootstraps over rows, seeded. One tick held before scoring; the scorer is run verbatim.

**Scoping.** The store is re-measured **only** on gold triples as the P0 gate; its banked $.974$ is not
restated as a new result. Nothing here bears on the npj submission. If P1 and P2 hold, the natural
follow-up is V-106's evidence-scale sweep rebuilt on extracted facts — **named here, not run**, because
designing it after seeing this outcome is the hindsight this discipline exists to prevent.

## 2026-09-10 — DEFECT, MINE, IN THE HEADLINE CLAIM: the ICLR paper's "The store" paragraph describes a DIFFERENT SYSTEM from the arm that produced .974. Six specifics wrong, and the one that matters is the cleanup candidate set: 2-3 in-instance entities, not 200,003 codebook rows.

**How it surfaced.** V-129's P0 gate re-read the store on gold triples with `v102.sharded_two_hop` and got
**.9767** against the banked **.9744**. The gate is +-.01 so it passed, but the SEED-LEVEL number did not
match (banked seed-42 is .9700), and chasing that 2-row difference instead of accepting the pass is what
found this.

**What the paper says** (ICLR draft, `\paragraph{The store.}`): a fixed random codebook of `n = 200003`
rows; bipolar `{+-1}^d`; `m = sum phi(s) (*) phi(o)` with `(*)` the elementwise **self-inverse** product;
**`d = 2048`**; cleanup `argmax_e <phi(e), phi(s)(*)m>`; an abstain floor at `0.5/sqrt(n)`; and explicitly
"**the construction discards the relation**, so this is a subject-to-object associative memory rather than
a full triple store".

**What actually produced .974** (`hrr_answer`, v65.py, copied verbatim into `v125_answerable_recompute.py`):

| paper | reality |
|---|---|
| elementwise self-inverse product | **circular convolution** (`irfft(rfft(a)*rfft(b))`) |
| relation DISCARDED | relation **bound in AND used at query**: `bind(bind(vec[s],vec[r]),vec[o])`, query `unbind(mem, bind(vec[cur],vec[r]))` |
| fixed codebook, n=200003 | **per-instance Gaussian draws**, `rng.standard_normal(VSA_DIM)/sqrt(VSA_DIM)`, fresh vectors per row |
| d = 2048 | **d = 4096** (`VSA_DIM = 4096`) |
| cleanup argmax over entities | argmax over `cands = {e for e in ents if e != cur}` where `ents` is only THIS instance's evidence entities |
| abstain floor 0.5/sqrt(n) | **no abstain floor in the function at all** |

**Verified, not inferred.** At `d=4096`, `hrr_answer` reproduces the banked per-seed EMs to the digit:
**.9700 / .9767 / .9767, mean .9744** = the paper's .974. At `d=2048` (the paper's stated dimension) the
same function gives .9633/.9667/.9633. So the stated dimension is wrong too, and my first comparison run
was wrong for the same reason -- I coded it from the paper instead of from the arm, which is the same
mistake one level down.

**The substantive part is the cleanup set.** Measured over all 300 rows x 2 hops: candidate-set size
**min 2, max 3, mean 2.04**. The paper implies the store selects the answer from a 200,003-row codebook.
It actually selects from two or three entities that came out of the same instance's own gold triples. That
is a materially easier problem, and it changes what ".974 from an exact algebra" is evidence OF. Any
reviewer who opened the code would find this, and would be right to distrust the rest.

**Every one of the six wrong specifics is an accurate description of `v102.sharded_two_hop`** -- a
genuinely different store used in V-101/V-102/V-106. I wrote the Setup paragraph from the wrong module and
never checked it against the arm whose number I was quoting. The prereg discipline did not catch it because
no prereg ever asked "does the Setup text describe the arm that produced the headline".

**The remedy, and it is not a softening.** The store the paper DESCRIBES is the harder one and it scores
HIGHER: `sharded_two_hop`, full 200,003-row codebook, relation discarded, gold triples, 300 rows =
**.9767 / .9833 / .9733, mean .9778**. So the paper is re-based onto implementation B, which makes the text
accurate and the number slightly stronger. Re-describing A instead would mean publishing a 2-3 candidate
cleanup as if it were the paper's central instrument, which it should not be.

**Downstream quantities that referenced .974/.9744 and must be recomputed, not edited:** the +.42 to +.48
single-pass gaps; the raw 94-95% and conservative 84-91% error-removal figures; V-125's .9967
answerable-subset store readout and the 7.0-of-7.67 error-location split; V-106's store arm (already
`sharded_two_hop`, so unaffected in kind but its reference line moves); and V-129's own P0 gate value.
`make_figures.py` recomputes all of these from banked dumps, so the fix is mechanical once the store
reference is changed -- but it is a recompute, not a find-and-replace.

**Outward consequence, USER-only.** The npj manuscript carries the same .974 from the same v65 arm and is
dated 9/16. The co-author cannot judge this without being told. Reporting it is the user's call, not mine,
but it must reach him before submission.

**New standing rule.** A paper's method description must be generated from, or gate-checked against, the
arm that produced the number it accompanies. Add a gate: for every headline figure, assert that the module
which produced it is the module the text describes.

## 2026-09-10 — STORE RE-BASE MEASURED (defect remedy, banked as `store_rebase.json` with per-row hits): the implementation the paper DESCRIBES is harder AND scores higher on every quantity. The counter-finding it strengthens is the one that costs us.

Remedy for the defect entry above. `v102.sharded_two_hop`, gold triples, 300 rows, d=2048, full
200,003-row codebook, relation discarded, three codebook seeds. Per-row hits banked so every downstream
figure is RECOMPUTED, not edited.

| quantity | superseded (`v65.hrr_answer`, d=4096) | re-based (`v102.sharded_two_hop`) |
|---|---|---|
| per-seed EM | .9700 / .9767 / .9767 | **.9767 / .9833 / .9733** |
| mean EM | .9744 | **.9778** |
| answerable subset, n=204 | .9967 | **1.0000** |
| store errors, full 300 | 7.67 | **6.667** |
| store errors inside the answerable subset | 0.667 | **0.000** |
| share of errors OUTSIDE the subset | 7.0/7.67 = 91% | **6.667/6.667 = 100%** |
| cleanup candidate set | mean 2.04 (max 3) | **200,003** |
| relation available to the algebra | yes | **no** |

**Three consequences, and the third is against us.**

1. **The paper gets more accurate and slightly stronger at once.** The described instrument solves the
   harder problem (a 200,003-way cleanup with the relation thrown away, rather than a 2-3-way choice among
   entities it was handed) and still reads higher. Nothing needs softening.

2. **V-125's error-localisation finding sharpens from strong to exact.** Every single store error now sits
   on a row the entailment audit flagged as not evidence-matched: 6.667 of 6.667. The store and the reader
   fail on the *same* rows, and on the fair subset the store does not fail at all.

3. **It strengthens the counter-finding that limits the paper's thesis.** The store is now **1.0000** on
   the answerable subset — and `evidence_in_prompt` already reached **1.0000** there too (kimi-k3, V-125
   step 5). They are TIED AT CEILING. So "the exact algebra has no residual accuracy advantage over simply
   reading structured evidence" is not merely still true, it is now true at the ceiling with no room left
   to argue about. The contribution is *structuring*, and this re-base removes the last wiggle room.

**Downstream recomputes owed** (mechanical, from `store_rebase.json` + banked dumps, via
`make_figures.py`): the +.42/+.48 single-pass gaps; raw 94-95% and conservative 84-91% error removal; the
ladder table's store row and Fig. `fig_appendix`d seed panel; V-125's subset table and the store-error
panel of `fig_subset`; and V-129's P0 gate reference. Nothing is hand-edited.

**Robustness note.** Four network failures this session came from re-streaming
`framolfese/2WikiMultihopQA` on every run; the 300-row slice is now cached to `rows300.json` by
`cache_rows.py`. The slice is deterministic under PYTHONHASHSEED=0, so caching changes nothing measured.

## 2026-09-11 — V-129 VOID (instrument defects; P1/P2 NOT READ, no value entered the record)

V-129's P0 gate passed (store on gold triples $.9767$ against the then-banked $.9744$; the re-based
reference is $.9778$ and it passes that too). P1 and P2 are **not read**, because three defects in the
instrument — not in the extractors — make the numbers uninterpretable in either direction:

1. **Exact-string recall.** `recall_of` matches normalised `(subject, object)` strings, and the extractors
   obey the instruction to use surface forms as written in the passages, which are not the gold's Wikidata
   labels: `Polish-Russian War (film)` against gold `Polish-Russian War`; `actress Małgorzata Braunek`
   against `Małgorzata Braunek`. The recorded recall ($.4583$ deepseek-v4-flash, $.5450$ kimi-k3) is a lower
   bound of unknown looseness, so the P1 bar cannot be applied to it.
2. **Query-key mismatch in the store.** The store is keyed by the same exact strings, and the query uses
   `head_entity(row)` from the gold, so the end-to-end EM ($.0100$ / $.0200$) measures whether the
   extractor happened to spell the head entity exactly as Wikidata does — not whether it extracted the
   fact. The store readout on the extracted facts is therefore not the quantity P2 names.
3. **Truncation.** $17/300$ rows hit `max_tokens=2048` (paragraph sets with many relations); per the V-127
   rule these are an instrument ceiling, and $17$ is above the completeness tolerance of zero.

**What survives:** nothing quantitative. The per-row dumps (raw extraction text included) are kept, and
they are what exposed the defect — V-98's aggregates-only dumps could not have. The prereg's readings are
not applied to a void run. **Re-registration is named, not designed:** an extraction run needs an entity
normalisation / linking step that maps extracted surface forms to the store's query key, registered before
the call, and a token budget sized to the longest paragraph set. It takes a new ID when designed.

**Second-order finding, descriptive.** The defect is the paper's own $\varphi$-is-a-hash point turned on the
acquisition side: `cosine('Polish-Russian War', 'Polish-Russian War (film)') = 0.0107`, indistinguishable
from random ($0.0221$). Any extractor feeding this store must produce the store's exact keys, and that
linking step is a component the paper's caveat did not name.

## 2026-09-11 — V-130 PREREG: structured PLAIN TEXT at scale versus the store, with FRONTIER readers (user-directed: "给100个结构化信息，plain text形式 llm 依然错，vsa 形式则正确 — 去验证一下"; BLIND on P1–P4)

**The user's question.** Plain text can be structured too. Hand a model $100$ structured facts as text and
it still errs; hand the same $100$ facts to the store and it does not. Is that so?

**What the record already says, and what it cannot say.** V-106 measured exactly this axis: the same pooled
gold facts, rendered as `subject | relation | object` lines in the prompt versus loaded into the store,
$K \in \{8, 64, 128, 512, 1024\}$, $n = 120$. Prompt $.9500 \to .5417$, store $.9361 \to .9083$, LoRA
$.9167 \to .4250$. At $K = 128$ the prompt reads $.8500$ against the store's $.9194$. So the user's
hypothesis is **already confirmed for one reader** — Qwen3-8B. Nothing on the record says whether the
collapse of structured plain text at scale is a property of *reading structured text* or of an *8B model*.
The paper's ladder scaled the reader to $2.4$T on $K \approx 8$ in-instance facts only; the evidence-scale
axis has never seen a frontier reader. That is the unmeasured coordinate, and it is the one the user's
question actually turns on.

**Protocol.** V-106's harness with the reader swapped.
- Rows: V-106's $120$ evaluation rows from its $400$-row pool, same seed ($42$), same `pooled()` call, so
  the pooled fact sets are those V-106 used. Cached to `rows400.json` if the mirror allows; otherwise
  streamed as V-106 did.
- $K \in \{8, 64, 100, 128, 512, 1024\}$ — V-106's grid plus the user's $K = 100$.
- Renderer: V-106's `facts_prompt` **verbatim** (few-shot + `Facts:` block + "Answer with the entity
  only"). Every reader receives the byte-identical prompt; the arms differ only in who reads.
- Readers: **Qwen3-8B frozen, local GPU** (the P0b gate, re-run rather than copied), and
  `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, `zai-org/glm-5.3`, `moonshotai/kimi-k3` via CommonStack at temperature
  $0$, `max_tokens = 1024` per the V-127 rule. Scored on the first output line after the registered
  normalisation, as V-106 scored the 8B; an echoed `Answer:` prefix is stripped.
- Store: V-102's `sharded_two_hop` **verbatim**, $64$ facts per shard, $d = 2048$, codebook seeds
  $\{0, 1, 2\}$ with V-106's exact seed offsets, per-row per-seed hits banked. Shard count is
  $\lceil K/64 \rceil$, identical to V-106's $\lfloor K/64 \rfloor$ at every V-106 grid point and $2$ at
  $K = 100$ so the per-shard load never exceeds the operating point.
- Completeness is value-blind: any reader-$K$ cell with `n_scored != n` is excluded on counts alone.
  Intervals are paired bootstraps over rows ($20{,}000$, seeded), store per-row accuracy being the mean
  over seeds.

**Predictions.**
- **P0a (validity):** the store reproduces V-106's store row within $\pm .01$ at the five shared $K$.
  Same code, seeds and pool — a miss means the pool or the store path moved and **nothing is read**.
- **P0b (validity):** the re-run Qwen3-8B prompt arm reproduces V-106's prompt row within $\pm .05$ at
  the five shared $K$. This is what certifies the renderer copy and the fact pool; a miss voids the run.
- **P1 (PRIMARY):** at $K = 1024$, for **every** complete frontier reader, store $-$ reader $\ge .05$ with
  the paired CI excluding zero. This is the user's hypothesis at frontier scale.
- **P2:** at the user's $K = 100$, for every complete frontier reader, store $-$ reader has a paired CI
  excluding zero (any positive gap).
- **P3 (descriptive, no bar):** per reader, the smallest $K$ at which the store leads by $\ge .02$ (V-106
  P4's rule), and the reader's drop from $K = 8$ to $K = 1024$.
- **P4 (descriptive, no bar):** prompt tokens and latency per query at $K = 1024$ against the store's.

**My expected directions, stated separately from the bars and against the user's hypothesis.** I expect
**P0a and P0b to hold**. I expect **P1 to FAIL** for at least one frontier reader: $1024$ clean
pipe-delimited lines are about $11{,}600$ tokens, a tenth of these models' context, and locating two
matching lines in clean structured text is close to what they are drilled on; I expect frontier accuracy at
$K = 1024$ in the $.85$–$.95$ band, i.e. the 8B collapse is a capacity effect that parameter count buys back.
I expect **P2 to FAIL** by a wider margin — a tie at $K = 100$. **I am registering this so that a P1 hold is
read as the user being right and me wrong, not as a result I steered toward.**

**Readings, fixed now.**
- **P1 holds ⇒** the user's hypothesis holds at frontier scale: structured plain text at $K = 1024$ still
  loses to the store for every reader we can reach. V-106's evidence-scale advantage is not an 8B artifact,
  and the paper's Sec 3.1 may cite it for the full ladder. This would be the first store-over-frontier
  accuracy result on the record.
- **P1 fails ⇒ reported first.** At least one frontier reader reads $1024$ structured facts as well as the
  store. V-106 becomes a small-model finding, in the same class as V-108's "algebra halves the residual",
  and the paper's evidence-scale claim is restricted to the 8B reader in the same commit that reports this.
  The cost claim (P4) survives regardless; the accuracy claim does not.
- **P2 holds ⇒** even $100$ structured facts are beyond exact reading for every frontier model; the user's
  intuition is right at the point they named.
- **P2 fails ⇒** $100$ structured facts are within what a frontier model reads exactly; the store's
  advantage, where it exists, begins higher, and P3 says where.
- **P0a or P0b fails ⇒** nothing is read.

**Deviations in force on this gateway (V-127/V-129 record).** No balance meter (hard cap $2{,}600$ calls;
spend not observable), no provider field (V-123's pinning rule cannot be honoured, so per-row claims carry
the $\pm .05$–$.19$ band; the bars read aggregates), no reasoning field (`max_tokens = 1024`).

**Discipline.** Prereg + `v130.py` + the frozen `v130_score.py` committed before the first call.
`PYTHONHASHSEED = 0` enforced by abort. Per-row dumps with raw output for every reader and per-seed hits for
the store. Hold one tick before scoring; run the scorer verbatim. This run takes a new ID; V-129 is void
above and is not reused.

**Scoping.** All arms receive gold triples: this measures the *use* of structured evidence at scale, not
its acquisition. Nothing here bears on the npj submission.

did not, and that is recorded as such.

**What this does NOT touch.** Every arm received gold triples. The acquisition limit (V-98/V-129-void) is
unchanged. The K≈8 in-instance ladder (V-108/V-124, single_pass .49–.55 vs store .978) is a different
axis — there the model reads *prose* and must compose; here it reads *already-structured* lines. Put
together, the two axes say the same thing the paper already says: the lever is structuring the evidence,
and once the evidence is structured a frontier reader needs no algebra to use it, at any scale we tested.

**Literature check (mandate).** Consistent with Liu et al. 2023 ("Lost in the Middle"), which found
position-dependent degradation in 2023-era models over multi-document contexts, and with the 2024–26
needle-in-a-haystack results on which frontier models saturate for clean retrieval targets; no conflicting
result found for pipe-delimited fact lists specifically. Recorded as "consistent, extends to the structured
case".

## 2026-09-11 — CORRECTION to the 2026-09-10 defect entry (795059b): v102.sharded_two_hop is NOT an elementwise self-inverse store and does NOT clean up over 200,003 rows

Reading `v102.py` line by line while auditing the npj Methods' "every measurement uses circular-convolution
HRR" sentence: `bind(a, b) = irfft(rfft(a) * rfft(b))` — **circular convolution**, the same operator as
`v65.hrr_answer`; `unbind(ab, a) = bind(involution(a), ab)` — correlation; `codebook()` returns **unit-norm
Gaussian** rows, not bipolar; and `sharded_two_hop` cleans up with `cosine_similarity(OV, hat)` where `OV`
is the stack of **object vectors present in that shard** — the cleanup candidate set is the K stored objects
(the whole pool at the pooled settings), not the 200,003-row codebook, and there is no abstain floor.

So the 795059b entry was right that the ICLR Setup paragraph described the wrong module, and right about
the remedy (re-base on v102 — the measured .9767/.9833/.9733 stand), but wrong about **what v102 is**:
it attributed to v102 an elementwise product, a 200,003-way cleanup and an abstain floor that exist in
neither implementation. Those three specifics were the manuscript's own text, and I repeated them into the
ledger as if they were the code. What actually separates v102 from v65: a fixed 200,003-row codebook
indexed by a hash of the normalised string (v65: fresh per-instance vectors), d=2048 (v65: 4096), relation
discarded (v65: bound and queried), sharding. The npj manuscript, which uses v65 and says "HRR, circular
convolution", is unaffected.

ICLR Setup paragraph rewritten to match the code (paper repo, this date; no number changes). **Rule
reinforced:** a method description is gate-checked against the module by READING THE MODULE, not by
reading the manuscript's account of it — 795059b failed its own new rule in the same entry that stated it.

## 2026-09-14 — V-132 AMENDMENT to V-131's validity gate. Written AFTER seeing the P0 miss, its diagnosis, and Parts B and C — disclosed as such, and the bars are carried over unchanged.

**This is not a blind prereg and does not pretend to be.** V-131's data exist and I have read them. What
follows changes the *validity gate* and nothing else. Every bar below is copied verbatim from V-131, where it
was fixed and committed (6a2a52d) before the first call. A reader who distrusts this amendment can apply
V-131's gate as written and discard everything; the record supports that reading too.

**What happened.** V-131 P0 required the Part-A re-run to reproduce V-65's banked per-seed EMs within
$\pm.01$ on all three arms. Two reproduced **to the digit**: `prompt_ev` $0.9500 \times 3$ and `hrr_gold`
$0.9700/0.9767/0.9767$. The third, `prompt`, came back $0.2400$ against a banked $0.2533$ — four rows,
$0.0133$, over the tolerance. Per V-131 the gate fails and nothing is read from any part.

**The diagnosis, and why it is not an excuse.** `v65.build_context` contains
`sup = set(zip(titles, sent_ids))` and then iterates that set to order the *supporting* sentences at the head
of the context. Iterating a set of `(str, int)` tuples is order-randomised per process unless
`PYTHONHASHSEED` is fixed, and **the banked V-65 run predates the standing PYTHONHASHSEED=0 rule adopted at
V-123**. So the banked $0.2533$ is one draw from a permutation distribution, not a point.

Three things make this a diagnosis rather than a story told after the fact:
1. **Only the arm with the set survived as a suspect.** `prompt_ev` builds its body from the
   `r["evidences"]` *list* and `hrr_gold` cleans up over `sorted({...})`; both are order-deterministic, and
   both reproduced exactly. The single arm containing a bare set iteration is the single arm that moved.
   Had the cause been a library, a driver or a dataset change, it would not have partitioned the arms that way.
2. **The effect was already measured on this project, before this run.** The companion study records context
   assembly order as worth about $\pm 0.03$ — larger than the $0.0133$ observed here.
3. **It was checked, not asserted.** `v131_hashdiag.py` re-ran the `prompt` arm alone under
   `PYTHONHASHSEED` $\in \{0,1,2,3,4\}$: five processes gave $0.2400$, $0.2667$, $0.2667$, $0.2467$ and $0.2767$ — a spread of $0.0367$ that contains both the banked $0.2533$ and the `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` re-run's $0.2400$, and matches the $\pm 0.03$ the companion measured independently. The diagnostic also records each run's opening context block: under seeds $0$--$3$ it begins *Polish-Russian War (film): …*, under seed $4$ *Xawery Żuławski: He is the son of actress …* — the permutation is directly visible, not inferred.

**The amended gate.**
- **G1 (unchanged, and it passed):** arms whose code path is order-deterministic — `prompt_ev` and
  `hrr_gold` — must reproduce their banked per-seed EMs within $\pm.01$. They reproduced exactly.
- **G2 (new, replacing the blanket tolerance for one arm):** the `prompt` arm is gated against the
  *measured* permutation spread from `v131_hashdiag.py` rather than a point: the re-run and the banked value
  must both lie inside it. A value outside that spread would still void the run.
- **G3 (new, and this is the part that costs us):** V-131 said a P0 miss voids *every* part. Parts B and C
  never touch `v65.py`, so that clause was over-broad. It is narrowed to Part A. **Note the direction: the
  narrowing admits Part B, and Part B fails its own bar against our manuscript.** Letting it in retracts one
  of our headline claims. This amendment cannot be read as chosen for the outcome, because the outcome is
  against us.

**Bars, carried over from V-131 verbatim, unchanged.**
- **P1 (PRIMARY):** at its best of the grid, the LoRA fine-tune still trails the handover's $1.000$ by
  $\ge 10$ points, in $3/3$ seeds of that configuration.
- **P2:** the paired bootstrap interval for `hrr_gold` $-$ `prompt_ev` on the $300$ rows excludes zero.
- **P3:** with no truncation, the MuSiQue single pass still trails the store's $0.9481$ by $\ge 20$ points.
- **P4 (descriptive):** the three arms on V-125's $204$ answerable rows.

**Readings, also carried over verbatim** — including the one that strikes our own sentence if P1 fails, and
the one that restates "halves the residual error" as unresolvable if P2 fails.

**One reading added, forced by the diagnosis and applying whatever the bars say.** The npj manuscript quotes
2Wiki single pass as $0.253$ with no band. That number carries the same context-assembly permutation
distribution the companion measured at $\pm 0.03$, now confirmed on this arm. Every sentence deriving from
it — the $97\%$ error removal, the $+0.72$ gap, the "$70$ of the $72$ points" decomposition — must carry that
band or be restated over the measured spread. This correction is independent of P1–P4 and is owed regardless.

**Scoring.** The frozen `v131_score.py` is run verbatim, unchanged, with its P0 block satisfied under G1–G3.
No bar, no bootstrap seed and no artifact is touched.

## 2026-09-14 — V-131 CLOSED under the V-132 amended gate (both scorers run verbatim, outputs banked). **P1 FAILS and P2 FAILS — two of the manuscript's own sentences are retracted. P3 holds. P4 is descriptive and partly rescues what P2 loses, on a subset.**

**Gates.** The frozen `v131_score.py` was run first, verbatim, and records what it was written to record:
`prompt_ev` and `hrr_gold` reproduce V-65 **to the digit**, `prompt` misses by $0.0133$, gate fails, nothing
read. `v132_score.py` (generated from it by replacing only the P0 block; all four bar lines byte-identical)
then applied G1/G2/G3: G1 passed exactly, G2 passed — the five-seed spread $[0.2400, 0.2767]$ contains both
the re-run's $0.2400$ and the banked $0.2533$ — G3 passed, per-row dumps complete on all nine arm-seed cells.

**P1 (PRIMARY) FAILS — reported first, as registered.** Twelve configurations $\times$ three seeds, all
completed. Best on test (a disclosed handicap in the comparator's favour): rank $16$, six epochs,
lr $10^{-4}$ → $0.9722$ ($0.9714$, $0.9738$, $0.9714$). The handover's lead is $0.0286$, $0.0262$, $0.0286$
— **$2.6$ to $2.9$ points, not the manuscript's twenty.** The re-run of the manuscript's own point (rank $8$,
two epochs, $10^{-4}$) gives $0.7952$ against its banked $0.8008$, so the grid is comparable and the
difference is tuning, not drift. Six of twelve configurations diverge to $0.16$–$0.41$, so the tuned result
is a real optimum and not a monotone effect of capacity.
**What this costs: the two-hop margin was an under-trained opponent.** Under the paper's own registered
ten-point bar — the one it applies to the one-hop case and reports failing there — the two-hop comparison now
fails too. The capability claim on natural text is withdrawn; what survives is narrower and still true: the
handover sits at $1.000$ in $3/3$ with a linear head, while a fine-tune tuned over twelve configurations
still misses about twelve of $420$ instances.

**P2 FAILS.** Paired bootstrap over the $300$ rows: `hrr_gold` $-$ `prompt_ev` $= +0.0244$, $95\%$ CI
$[-0.0044, +0.0544]$, $26$ discordant rows. **The store and the in-prompt evidence arm are not
distinguishable at this sample size**, so "it halves the residual error, $5.0\%$ to $2.6\%$" is restated as
unresolvable. This was my registered expectation and it retracts a sentence I defended through four audit
passes. For contrast, the headline gap is intact and enormous: store $-$ single pass $= +0.7344$, CI
$[+0.6822, +0.7856]$.

**P3 HOLDS.** MuSiQue read by Qwen3-8B at a $32$k window, truncation rate $0.000$ (phi-2: $0.887$): the
single pass rises from $0.1651$ to $0.2877$ and still trails the store's $0.9481$ by $0.6604 \ge 0.20$. The
separation is a property of the method, not of phi-2's window. Two secondary numbers move and must be
reported with it: the gold-paragraph baseline rises $0.4009 \to 0.5283$, and the $+150$ pooled prompt rises
$0.1873 \to 0.5786$ with **every gold fact kept** (phi-2 kept $46$–$51\%$) against the store's $0.6556$ —
**the pooled separation falls from $47$ points to $7.7$.**

**P4 (descriptive, no bar) — and it is the one good surprise.** With phi-2 per-row hits finally banked, the
gap V-125 recorded as `"phi2_v65": per-seed means only, ABSENT` is closed. On its $204$ answerable rows:
single pass $0.2990$, evidence-in-prompt $0.9559$, store $0.9967$. Error removal $96.6\%$ full,
$99.5\%$ answerable. And `hrr_gold` $-$ `prompt_ev` there is $+0.0408$, CI $[+0.0131, +0.0719]$, which
**excludes zero**. So the algebra's residual advantage is measurable exactly where the arms receive matched
evidence, and vanishes into the noise when the $96$ mismatched rows are mixed back in. This is reported as
descriptive: P4 carried no bar, the subset was defined by another study, and it does not reinstate P2.

by iterating a `set`, so the manuscript's $0.253$ single pass is one draw from a permutation distribution
measured here at $[0.2400, 0.2767]$. Every sentence derived from it — the $97\%$ error removal, the $+0.72$
gap, the "$70$ of the $72$ points" decomposition — carries that band and must say so.

(exact rows work, task-gradient codes never do, the $0.10$ cross-talk tolerance, injectivity), the arena
results where the fine-tune is at chance by construction, the capacity and sharding sweeps, and the store's
structural inability to name an absent entity. The spine holds; three specific comparisons shrink.

## 2026-09-15 — V-133 CLOSED: chain depth does NOT widen the algebra's lead, and an instrument error of mine

**Question, user-directed.** V-131 left the algebra's accuracy contribution unresolvable at two hops
(+0.024, CI crossing zero) because both arms sit near ceiling there. Does the gap open at three, four, five,
six hops with a reader of at least 30B? Prereg `9bcb703`, amendment `cf5d8d4`, closed here.

**Instrument.** Synthetic typed chains, `k = 2..6`, **fact count held constant at 120** so depth is the only
quantity that varies. Every chain node carries exactly one edge with the queried relation and three decoy
edges with other relations, so the relation must be used; background distractor subjects are never queried
nodes, so the path is unique; an independent path-follower re-derives every answer from the shuffled list
(**750/750**, unique-relation **750/750**, P0(a) PASS). Reader: **Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, local, greedy,
row-replicable** — chosen over API frontier models precisely because V-123 bars per-row claims there.

**P1 VOID (amendment cf5d8d4).** The `direct` arm — instructed to answer with the entity name only — floors
at two hops at *every* fact load calibrated (n=40 × 6 loads: .675 at K=24, .450 at 48, .200 at 120), while
the store clears its half of the anchor everywhere. Raw generations are clean single-entity strings, so this
is neither the prompt nor the extractor: **a 32B cannot compose two relation-typed lookups in one forward
pass.** An arm pinned at the floor has no dynamic range, so `gap(6) − gap(2)` against it measures its floor,
not depth. Declared void rather than scored. The amendment removes the reading I expected to HOLD and leaves
the run resting on P2, which I expected to FAIL, so it cannot be outcome-motivated in my favour.

**P2 FAILS, and fails in the informative direction.** `gap(6) − gap(2)` vs chain-of-thought = **−0.2333,
CI [−0.3178, −0.1511], EXCLUDING ZERO** against a `+0.20` bar. Depth does not widen the gap; it **inverts**
it. **P3 HOLDS** (store .7267 ≥ .70 at k=6, d=4096, unsharded).

**Mechanism (P4).** Per-hop survival `acc(k)^(1/k)`: the store declines .980 → .948 as k grows while the
reader holds ~.986 and even rises. **The reader's failures are not per-hop** — it carries a roughly fixed
~10% misreading rate independent of chain length — **while the algebra's are**, because every hop spends one
cleanup and a cleanup that misses never recovers. That is the opposite of the intuition motivating the run.

**MY INSTRUMENT ERROR, found after scoring, and it ran AGAINST the algebra.** Both V-133 and the V-134 smoke
used the **unsharded** store; the manuscript deploys a **sharded** one (V-102, prereg cc5ae08). Gate: at
S=1 the sharded code reproduces the unsharded to the digit. Recomputed at S=2 (the published ~64-facts-per-
shard rule), language-model arms untouched:

| k | store registered | store sharded | cot | gap registered | gap sharded |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | .9600 | .9889 | .9200 | +.0400 | +.0689 |
| 4 | .7978 | .9089 | .9333 | −.1356 | −.0244 |
| 6 | .7267 | .8511 | .9200 | −.1933 | −.0689 |

`gap(6) − gap(2)` moves **−.2333 → −.1378**, so P2 still fails and the conclusion stands, but **I had told
the user the algebra loses badly at depth and that was wrong**: with the paper's own implementation it stays
within seven points of a 32B-with-scratchpad at every depth while making no model call. Both columns banked
(`v133a.json`, `v133a_sharded.json`).

**"Plain prompt" settled by measurement, not assertion.** The user twice asked why the comparator is
chain-of-thought. A third arm with **no instruction about format or reasoning at all**: accuracy
**.9067 / .8933 / .9133 / .9200 / .8800** at k=2..6, **100% of outputs reasoned**, **0% wrote an `Answer:`
line**. So chain-of-thought is not an enhancement I granted the reader — **reasoning is its default, and
`direct` is the handicap I added**. Against this honest baseline the store leads +.082 at two hops, is level
at four and trails slightly at five and six. First run of this arm scored 0.0000 at every depth: that was my
`Answer:`-locator failing on "So, we end at Garion.", **a parser artefact, not a result** — fixed, full text
now banked, and both a strict and a vocabulary-anchored rule reported.

**What this closes.** The manuscript states as open: *"whether the gain grows with hops is testable only
where the comparator has real purchase ... on natural text that question remains open."* It is now answered
on a controlled task with a competent comparator: **it does not grow.** The manuscript's own
"The gap does not grow with depth" paragraph is therefore confirmed rather than contradicted, and its
depth claims are accurate as written.

**Also measured, and it bears on Theorem (capacity).** At **constant k = 160 facts and constant d = 4096**,
single-hop readout ranges **0.632 → 0.957** depending only on how densely the entity vocabulary is shared:

| entities V | facts per entity | readout |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 20 | 8.0 | .632 |
| 40 | 4.0 | .816 |
| 160 | 1.0 | .912 |
| 640 | 0.2 | .957 |

The theorem predicts one number for every row (`SNR = d/(k+O(1))`, cross-talk terms *independent*). Two
decompositions rule out simpler stories: concentrating either vocabulary alone costs ~3 points, and
subject/object overlap alone at a large vocabulary ~5; it is the **interaction — node degree in a
shared-vocabulary graph — that costs up to 32**. Every number already in the manuscript stays valid, since
2Wiki and MuSiQue gold triples have low degree, but the capacity story as written does not transfer to a
dense knowledge graph, and the sentence "the readout is set by facts per shard, not by the total" inherits
the gap. **My first diagnosis of this effect ("entity re-use costs 15 points") was imprecise and is
withdrawn in favour of the decomposition above.**

**Discipline.** Prereg and frozen scorer committed before any instance existed (`9bcb703`). Frozen scorer run
verbatim first — it gated on P0(b) and took no reading. Amended scorer generated by a script that replaces
only the P0 block and **asserts every bar line and every scoring function byte-identical**
(`make_v133_amended_score.py`), both outputs banked. Zero API spend; all compute local.

**STATE.** V-134 (knowledge in weights vs algebraic memory) and V-135 (evidence volume) are in flight under
preregs `9444197` and `f51acda`, both with frozen scorers committed before data. Manuscript edits: **none
made** — the user asked for review without changes, and the depth claims reviewed as accurate.

## 2026-09-15 — V-134 CLOSED: knowledge in weights vs an algebraic memory. Both bars FAIL; the direction is real but small.

**Question, user-directed** ("我希望可以拉开微调的差距"). V-133 had shown depth does not widen the algebra's
lead over prompting. V-133's task cannot address fine-tuning, because the facts sit in the context there and
a fine-tune need only learn to walk a table. V-134 moves to the axis where the two genuinely differ — **where
the knowledge lives**. Prereg `9444197`, amendment `cf5d8d4`/`913c2aa` (sharded store), frozen scorer run
verbatim.

**Instrument.** 4 independent knowledge bases, 40 entities x 4 relations = 160 facts each. One LoRA per KB
(r=32, 12 epochs, all attention + MLP projections) trained on **single-hop material only** — statements and
one-hop QA, no chain of length >= 2 ever appears. Then k-hop questions with **no facts in context**. Against
the same facts in a **sharded** HRR store (S=3 by the published ~64-facts-per-shard rule). Every LLM arm gets
a scratchpad, because V-133 established that an arm denied one floors and stops being an opponent.

**P0 gate PASSES on all three clauses**, which is what makes the negative readable: memorisation
`lora_weights` **0.9656** at one hop (bar .80), `base_nofacts` **0.0000** at every depth so answers are not
guessable, scratchpad truncation **0.0156** (bar .02).

| k | store | lora_weights | ctx_cot | store − lora |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | .8510 | **.9656** | .8750 | −.1146 |
| 2 | .6969 | .6219 | **.9250** | +.0750 |
| 3 | .5719 | .4437 | **.8281** | +.1281 |
| 4 | .4813 | .3094 | **.8187** | +.1719 |

**P1 FAILS**: store − lora at k=2 = **+.0750**, CI **[−.0948, +.2344]**, against a +.30 bar and a
CI-excludes-zero requirement. **P2 FAILS**: gap(4) − gap(2) = **+.0969**, CI **[+.0021, +.1917]** — the CI
*does* exclude zero, so the growth is real, but the magnitude is well under the +.15 bar.

**What is nonetheless established, and it is the one positive here.** At one hop the fine-tune **beats** the
store (.9656 vs .8510): it recalls the base better than the store stores it. The store then overtakes it and
the gap widens monotonically with depth, and that widening is statistically real. So **latent composition
over memorised facts degrades faster than algebraic composition** — which is exactly the opposite of what
V-133 found against *in-context* reading, where the reader's per-hop reliability was flat. Knowledge in
weights composes badly; knowledge on the page does not. My registered expectation (P1 holds, large) is
**refuted**; the registered direction survives at a third of the registered size.

**P3 scope, binding.** `ctx_cot` beats the store at **every** depth (.875/.925/.828/.819 against
.851/.697/.572/.481). This run therefore licenses "an algebraic memory composes better than the same base
model with the facts in its weights" and **not** "the algebra beats putting the evidence in the prompt".

**My own design defect, recorded.** The bootstrap clusters by KB and there are only four of them, while
between-KB spread at k=2 runs +.288 to −.159 — larger than the effect. P1's CI is consequently ±.16 wide and
would have struggled to exclude zero at any plausible effect size. **V-134 is underpowered at the KB level by
my design, not by the data**, and the failure of P1 must be read with that attached. A properly powered
re-run needs many more KBs and a fresh prereg; it is named here, not launched.

**Store dimension is not the lever** (d = 2048/4096/8192 at k=4: .4646/.4813/.4938), consistent with the
saturation already reported in the manuscript.

**Discipline.** Prereg and frozen scorer committed before any KB, LoRA or query existed. Pilot ran against
the hypothesis (unsharded store, lora ahead at k=2) and the full run was **not** cancelled on that basis.
Sharded-store amendment justified independently of outcome and paired with an opponent-strengthening change
(2 -> 12 LoRA epochs). Zero API spend.
